quest:1001.text: Buzzbox 411. Along Darkshore’s coast, Buzzbox 411 needs thresher eyes to return to service. This Alliance errand comes through an eccentric, intoxicated gnome inventor, Wizbang Cranktoggle, who works through a mechanical relay network. After you help repair Buzzbox 827 farther south, gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle’s voice crackles through the mechanical transmitter again. From somewhere safely out of sight, he directs adventurers north along Darkshore’s mist-laden beach to a damaged terminal called Buzzbox 411. His transmissions break with hiccups and muttered praise for crawler wine. He says local aquatic predators carry what his coastal apparatus needs to keep working. To restore Buzzbox 411, thresher eyes must be fed into its waiting hatch. Darkshore threshers, aggressive marine beasts, prowl the shallows off Auberdine, and their eyes have the properties Wizbang says are needed to recalibrate the device. The eyes jolt the apparatus back into operation, and the line opens for another assignment, delivered in an even slurrier voice.

quest:1002.text: Buzzbox 323. Wizbang Cranktoggle’s field research reaches Buzzbox 323, the third stop along Darkshore’s coast. You gather six Moonstalker fangs and place them in the machine north of Auberdine. Wizbang Cranktoggle’s voice crackles through the speaker after you operate Buzzbox 411 farther south. Heavy drinking muddles his directions, but he points you north of Auberdine, to Buzzbox 323 near a road bridge. His research calls for six Moonstalker fangs from the fierce hunters roaming Darkshore’s forests. Buzzbox 323 chatters with static and faint muttering before you begin. Place the requested fangs in its intake hopper, and the machine rattles violently, grinding the teeth into dust. Wizbang’s boozy voice returns through the transceiver to celebrate your delivery and point you toward the next machine in his scattered network.

quest:1003.text: Buzzbox 525. Along Darkshore’s coast, Buzzbox 525 waits for the last of Wizbang Cranktoggle’s strange requests. The gnome’s scattered machines call for animal remnants and ever stranger materials. After Buzzbox 323 is serviced, its rattling speakers carry Wizbang Cranktoggle’s garbled instructions. His words slur through drunken chuckles and rambling directions, sending his helpers far south along Darkshore’s main road. He asks them to hunt grizzled thistle bears and place four thick scalps in Buzzbox 525’s compartment. The machine is concealed behind a fence in the brush beside the road.

quest:1008.text: The Zoram Strand. Naga now threaten Ashenvale from the Zoram Strand. Shindrell Swiftfire of Astranaar sends Alliance champions to scour the northwestern coast, where an ancient ruined city lies. Stopping the naga protects the forest from a haunting echo of the night elves’ distant past. At Ashenvale’s northwestern edge, the Zoram Strand meets the Veiled Sea. Its shore lies northwest of Astranaar, where the forest canopy gives way to the coast. The beach was quiet for ages, its stones left from a civilization shattered ten millennia ago. Now Wrathtail naga have come out of the dark tides in force. They have made a hostile beachhead on the borders of night elven territory, and threaten to press inland. The city of Zoram lies shattered beneath the surf, submerged during the Great Sundering. For ages, it remained abandoned and nearly forgotten by the kaldorei. The naga’s sudden arrival among its ruins stirs bitter memories among Astranaar’s defenders. Sentinels such as Shindrell Swiftfire know the invaders as twisted cousins, born of their own ancient catastrophe. They will not let the depths claim the shore again.

quest:102.text:
Patrolling Westfall. Gnoll packs threaten the people still living on Westfall’s grasslands. From Sentinel Hill, Captain Danuvin calls on volunteers to hunt them, fearing they work with thieves in the Deadmines. Sentinel Hill is Westfall’s main defense, held by local volunteers instead of royal troops. With Stormwind sending no soldiers to protect the outer farmlands, the people formed the People’s Militia. Captain Danuvin once farmed in Westfall. Now he leads the militia and refuses to abandon his homeland.

The militia depends on travelers passing through to help hold its perimeter against dangers gathering across the plains. Gnolls threaten the refugees and squatters struggling to survive in Westfall. Danuvin’s scouts believe the packs work with bandits based in the Deadmines. So he sends hunters to collect gnoll paws. He hopes to curb the packs’ growing patrols and break any cooperation between the beasts and the outlaws.

quest:103.text: Keeper of the Flame. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the coast. He seeks oil to keep the beacon burning after murlocs killed the living keepers, guiding ships safely past the reefs. Westfall Lighthouse stands on a rocky islet off Westfall’s southwest shore. Its light once guided sailors through the Great Sea’s shallow waters. That duty ended when Old Murk-Eye led a murloc attack and killed the keeper and his family. Captain Grayson died in the waters by these rocks and now watches over the tower as a ghost. He could not stop the slaughter in life, but he will not let the lighthouse go dark. No living keeper remains to tend the flame, so Captain Grayson needs an unusual fuel. Harvest Watchers roam Westfall’s abandoned farmlands, carrying flasks of machinery oil inside their rusted bodies. Grayson sends you ashore to recover the oil from these broken constructs. With it, the beacon can keep burning and guide captains past the reefs.

quest:1061.text: The Spirits of Stonetalon. Unrest stirs among the spirits of Stonetalon, and Zor Lonetree sends Horde champions west to learn why. From Orgrimmar, they travel past the Crossroads and report directly to Seereth Stonebreak near Greatwood Vale. In Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree listens to the natural world and feels deep distress from the Stonetalon Mountains. The elemental spirits of its rocky peaks are furious as logging tears into their forests. Horde shamans hear that unrest and fear the devastation in the western highlands will upset Kalimdor's spiritual balance. The Venture Company, an unscrupulous goblin syndicate, is cutting timber in Greatwood Vale. Its commercial crews use aggressive machinery, saws, and muscle to butcher the ancient woodland instead of harvesting sustainably. The Horde sent Seereth Stonebreak, a young shaman, to watch the forest from the frontier and rally defenders against the ravagers.

quest:1062.text: Goblin Invaders. At the Barrens and Stonetalon border, Seereth Stonebreak sends the Horde to strike Venture Company loggers in Windshear Crag. Their work lays waste to the mountains' ancient woodlands. The Venture Company has cut deep into the Stonetalon Mountains, tearing through crags and valleys. Its loggers strip hillsides of timber and burn the underbrush, leaving scorched ground behind. For tauren and their allies, this is more than the destruction of forests by a mining and lumber company. The primal spirits bound to Stonetalon howl in torment. Seereth Stonebreak, stationed along the mountain border, sees that the goblins' relentless assault has left the spirits blind with agony and fury. The Venture Company's executives and hirelings care only for profit, and reason will not sway them. Seereth sends travelers past Greatwood Vale and into Windshear Crag to kill fifteen loggers. The Horde means to meet the company's greed with force, halting the deforestation and buying time for tauren elders to soothe the land's agitated spirits.

quest:1063.text: The Elder Crone. Seereth Stonebreak sends word from Stonetalon to Thunder Bluff. Enraged by goblin deforestation and mining, the mountain's elements need spiritual guidance, so Seereth sends emissaries to seek counsel from Magatha Grimtotem on Elder Rise. Goblin deforestation and mining have enraged the elemental spirits of Stonetalon Mountains. Seereth Stonebreak sees that force alone cannot ease the land's spiritual anguish and turns to elder shamans for wisdom. Seereth knows few tribal leaders by name, but knows of Magatha Grimtotem, an elder famed for her knowledge and commanding presence. Magatha Grimtotem holds court atop Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, where shamanic and spiritual affairs gather. The Grimtotem tribe's relationship with Cairne Bloodhoof's leadership is tense and often confrontational. Even so, Magatha is a formidable elder whose counsel carries great weight across the Horde. You bring Stonetalon's troubles to her, seeking her guidance.

quest:1064.text: Forsaken Aid. In Thunder Bluff, Magatha Grimtotem sends you to seek help for Stonetalon's blighted spirits. She turns to Apothecary Zamah, the Forsaken emissary in the Pools of Vision, to bring tauren and undead knowledge together. Magatha Grimtotem sees practical value in the Forsaken alliance. When word reaches Thunder Bluff of corrupted elemental spirits and suffering land in the Stonetalon Mountains, she turns to the undead for help. She believes those who understand disease can help cure it, so she sends you to the Royal Apothecary Society instead of seeking traditional druidic remedies. Apothecary Zamah represents Undercity interests on Kalimdor from the Pools of Vision beneath Spirit Rise. Tauren shamans, priests, and seers use the cavern as a sacred retreat, and Zamah's presence brings Forsaken work into their midst. Magatha sends a serpent messenger ahead of you to alert Zamah, opening a direct line to the Forsaken's alchemical researchers.

quest:1065.text: Journey to Tarren Mill. Apothecary Zamah seeks a way to drive the Venture Company from Stonetalon Mountains without open war. She sends you across the sea to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, where the Royal Apothecary Society works in Lordaeron. In Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah is a link between the Forsaken and the Earth Mother's children. The Venture Company is logging and mining the sacred lands of Stonetalon Mountains, and the tauren have found that ordinary methods will not stop them. Zamah turns to her peers in the Royal Apothecary Society for a chemical deterrent. She hopes their alchemy can drive the company out without a drawn-out war. You cross the sea from Kalimdor by zeppelin toward Lordaeron and the Undercity. From Tirisfal Glades, the road leads south through Silverpine Forest and into the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Tarren Mill lies near human farmsteads and ruins. Once a human hamlet, it is now a Forsaken stronghold and a place where the Royal Apothecary Society carries out its research.

quest:109.text: Report to Gryan Stoutmantle. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle gathers Westfall's defenders against threats to the farms. Guards along the Elwynn border and farmers driven west both send capable travelers toward Sentinel Hill. Those who answer join a defense built from local volunteers. No royal battalions come to their aid. From the stone tower atop Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle organizes farmers, retired veterans, and mercenaries into the People's Militia. You join their bitter guerrilla war to keep Westfall's farmlands from falling into lawlessness.

quest:1097.text: Elmore's Task. Smith Argus sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind, where Grimand Elmore awaits help with a delivery. The weaponsmith needs it carried to his kin in Khaz Modan, and Argus trusts you with the road ahead. Smith Argus watches for travelers he can trust with work beyond wolves and kobolds. Grimand Elmore has sent word from Stormwind and asks for help carrying a delivery to his kin in Khaz Modan. The city gates open the way to Elmore's call. Stormwind and Ironforge rely on open trade and goodwill to keep both realms supplied and united. Argus says Elwynn Forest needs defenders, yet promises to the dwarves matter too. In northeastern Stormwind, the Dwarven District leads you to Elmore's shop. There, a journey beyond the forest begins.

quest:1099.text: Goblins Win!. In Thousand Needles, a goblin race ticket pays off when the goblins come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The goblin race ticket is the stub that counts when the goblins win. Hold on to it, and a goblin prize box is yours once the result is in. The gnome ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

quest:11.text: Riverpaw Gnoll Bounty. In western Elwynn, Riverpaw Gnoll Bounty calls for help against gnolls pressing the border. Deputy Rainer offers a reward at Westbrook Garrison for painted armbands taken from Riverpaw packs in the woods and by the water. Westbrook Garrison guards Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Its depleted forces struggle to contain the growing Riverpaw presence. The gnolls camp south of the guard tower and farther east around Stone Cairn Lake. From those camps, they threaten travelers and nearby homesteads. Deputy Rainer cannot spare regular infantry to sweep the woods, so he offers a bounty on the raiders. He requires painted armbands from slain gnolls as proof of each kill. Wandering adventurers and recruits are hired to thin the pack before the Riverpaws overrun the western marches.

quest:111.text: Speak with Gramma. Tommy Joe Stonefield asks Gramma Stonefield for a way to reach Maybell Maclure. Their families keep them apart, and he hopes to meet her without drawing their kin into conflict. Tommy Joe and Maybell hide their love from their families. He turns to Gramma Stonefield, hoping she can find them a chance to meet in secret. Their kin must not discover the romance and turn old hostility into violence. Gramma Stonefield knows the families cannot truly unite while their bad blood remains. Still, she will not let that end the young couple's hopes. She begins seeking small chances to bring Tommy Joe and Maybell together.

quest:112.text: Collecting Kelp. In Goldshire, Maybell Maclure seeks to visit Tommy Joe Stonefield unseen. William Pestle needs rare crystal kelp to brew her an invisibility liquor. The feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families keeps Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield from meeting openly. Maybell wants to see the one she loves without bringing their kin into an armed clash. So she seeks a way to cross the valley unseen. William Pestle, an herbalist and apothecary at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, plans to brew an invisibility liquor, but its rare ingredients are not in the inn's cupboards. William Pestle needs crystal kelp as the catalyst for his brew. Its fronds usually grow far out in saltwater oceans, but tribal murlocs have carried stashes inland to their crude camps along Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. Their peculiar instincts draw them to haul the marine plants to the freshwater shore. You need to recover enough fronds from the murlocs before returning to Goldshire with them.

quest:1138.text: Fruit of the Sea. Along Darkshore, Auberdine fisherman Gubber Blump asks you to gather crab meat. He keeps to the docks and dreams of dishes for his catch. Gubber Blump fishes from Auberdine's long wooden piers, thinking of crab meat. He calls crabs the ocean's true bounty and imagines them baked, barbecued, or boiled. His recipes include whipper root crab and Ironforge surprise crab. Gubber cannot leave his fishing rod, so he asks you to gather ingredients from Darkshore's beaches. Reef crawlers and encrusted tide crawlers move among the breakers, offering meat for a coastal cook. Mind their claws as you gather the fine crab chunks.

quest:114.text: The Escape. Maybell Maclure seeks a way to leave her family and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. You bring her William Pestle's Invisibility Liquor, brewed with crystal kelp gathered across the region. The Maclures and Stonefields have feuded for generations, leaving no room for courtship. Gramma Stonefield asks William Pestle, an alchemist at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, for help. Crystal kelp from nearby lakes gives Pestle what he needs to brew Invisibility Liquor. The brew can hide Maybell's escape from the Maclure homestead.

quest:1141.text: The Family and the Fishing Pole. Gubber Blump and his heirloom Fishing Pole await a catch on Auberdine's docks. Hostile murlocs keep the town's small fishing boats ashore, so Gubber seeks help catching native Darkshore grouper from the coast. Gubber Blump takes pride in a family known for its skill with a fishing line. Night elves make up most of Auberdine, though dwarves and gnomes have settled around its docks and port. Gubber spends his days gazing over the Veiled Sea instead of digging into stone, hoping to bring in the local catch. Darkshore grouper thrive along the coast and make versatile food, but they can put up a lively fight on the line. Local fishermen usually row small boats into deeper waters to catch them. Now aggressive murlocs prowl the coast, and small boats no longer go out. Gubber fears the creatures are eating the local fish, so he asks travelers to fish from shore. Gubber gives a Blump Family Fishing Pole to anyone who brings him a hearty catch. He believes anyone who can land a batch of feisty groupers is worthy of his family's legendary anglers, including his cousin Graun Blump. For Gubber, handing over a family rod is the highest mark of respect.

quest:116.text: Dry Times. Barkeep Daniels needs drink for Lakeshire's inn while Blackrock orcs keep the town under siege. The roads are unsafe, and the usual supplies have stopped coming. Blackrock orcs descend from Stonewatch Keep, pressing Lakeshire hard. With supply lines cut and roads unsafe, the inn is running low on drink. Barkeep Daniels turns to travelers who can cross the blocked roads and bring supplies back for frightened villagers and the town guards. Daniels needs drink from across Stormwind's lands. You can find Merlot in the capital, Sweet Rum at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Moonshine in Darkshire in Duskwood, and Thunderbrew Lager from Grimbooze Thunderbrew in the hills of Westfall.

quest:117.text: Thunderbrew. In Westfall, Grimbooze Thunderbrew gathers fresh hops for his next batch. Without them, his ale may turn thick as stew, so he shares kegs with those who bring what he needs. Far from Dun Morogh, Grimbooze keeps his family's brewing tradition alive. He insists on proper hops for his current brew, or it may turn to thick stew instead of refreshing ale. Grimbooze praises hops, barley, yeast, and malt in cheerful rhymes. Fresh hops let him finish fermentation on the spot. In return, he shares whole kegs of Thunderbrew Lager, known for its forceful taste.

quest:1174.text: Gnomes Win!. In Thousand Needles, a gnome race ticket pays off when the gnomes come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The gnome race ticket is the stub that counts when the gnomes win. Hold on to it, and a gnome prize box is yours once the result is in. The goblin ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

quest:118.text: The Price of Shoes. Verner Osgood has run out of iron in Lakeshire, where the guard's gear needs constant repair. He sends you west across Elwynn Forest to ask Smith Argus in Goldshire for horseshoes. Lakeshire faces gnolls, orcs, and murlocs, while Stormwind sends little help. The garrison fights each day to keep the town from falling, and battle quickly wears down its gear. Verner Osgood spends nearly every waking hour repairing dented breastplates, reshaping dulled swords, and keeping the guards clad in iron. The work has exhausted his supply of raw materials. Without iron, even ordinary work in a frontier town can stop. Horses without shoes cannot carry messengers swiftly or haul supplies along Redridge's rocky paths. Verner swallows his pride and sends you west along the Three Corners road to Goldshire. Smith Argus there still has regular access to the kingdom's mineral stores.

quest:119.text: Return to Verner. Smith Argus has finished fifty horseshoes, and you carry them from Goldshire to Verner Osgood in Lakeshire. Redridge needs them for its hard-pressed mounts. You carry the crate east across the border into Redridge. There, supply shortages and gnoll attacks threaten the town. The fifty iron shoes keep horses and draft animals working on rugged mountain roads, which Redridge needs to face those dangers. Verner Osgood is relieved when the horseshoes arrive. Then he finds the bill Smith Argus attached to the crate. Verner is annoyed that the Goldshire smith expects payment. With dangers pressing around Redridge, there is little time to argue over the charge.

quest:12.text: The People's Militia. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle puts the People's Militia to the test against outlaws in Westfall's northern fields and mines. Local volunteers defend the region from the Defias Brotherhood while Stormwind's throne is distracted and its army absent. Gryan Stoutmantle founded the People's Militia, and he does not take just anyone. Anyone seeking its badge must prove they can fight and protect innocent settlers. He calls for decisive action to reclaim Westfall from the outlaws, vagrants, and thieves overrunning the region. Before Gryan Stoutmantle trusts new recruits with deeper operations, he sends them against Defias forces near the northern homesteads. Defias Trappers and Smugglers work openly near Jangolode Mine, Molsen Farm, and Furlbrow's Pumpkin Patch. They pillage stores and ambush travelers. Driving them out disrupts their foraging and shows Stoutmantle's scouts you have the grit for a long fight against crime.

quest:120.text: Messenger to Stormwind. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea for help to Stormwind. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs press around the town, and he has no garrison troops to spare for the journey. He entrusts a traveler with The State of Lakeshire for General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind City. Gnolls contest every road from Lakeshire, while Blackrock orcs raid from the north. The town's guardsmen are stretched beyond their limits. Magistrate Solomon cannot spare fighting men for the days-long ride to the capital, so a traveler carries his official plea for regular troops to the city gates. General Marcus Jonathan commands Stormwind's defense. Solomon's report reaches him, and he respects the magistrate's leadership and recognizes the urgency. Yet army protocol bars Jonathan from mobilizing troops without a royal directive. Redridge's defense must wait until he consults the young King Anduin and the regency council.

quest:1205.text: Deadmire. In Dustwallow Marsh, Deadmire suffers in the waterways north of the Stonemaul Ruins. Melor Stonehoof sends hunters from Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff to track the ancient crocolisk and bring back a tooth as proof. The hunt teaches tracking and mercy. On Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof teaches promising trackers the spiritual traditions of the hunt. Tauren hunters seek reverence and a bond with the natural world, not slaughter or trophies. Melor sends you east to Dustwallow Marsh to find Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk whose long life has become a burden. North of the Stonemaul Ruins, Deadmire prowls the waterways as a massive, pale crocolisk. His strength and fury still come in sudden bursts, but age has worn down his body with grinding bones and unrelenting pain. Melor asks you to grant him a swift, honorable end and bring back one tooth as a token of his release.

quest:121.text: Messenger to Stormwind. In Stormwind, you carry General Marcus Jonathan's reply to Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten the town. The capital sends no troops while its leaders delay, leaving the settlement exposed. You brought Magistrate Solomon's plea for reinforcements to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind. Now you carry his first reply back to Redridge while he waits for the throne's approval. Without royal permission, the General cannot commit the army. Lakeshire's citizens still have no city guards, and each day brings the settlement closer to falling to the Blackrock clan.

quest:122.text: Underbelly Scales. Verner Osgood needs black dragon whelp underbelly scales to settle his trade debt with Smith Argus of Goldshire. You gather them from young drakes wandering the crags south of Lakeshire. The scales settle Verner’s account and leave enough raw hide to craft a piece of gear. Verner Osgood runs a forge on the outskirts of Lakeshire and often trades with craftsmen beyond the Redridge Mountains. Smith Argus of Goldshire sent him a shipment of horseshoes, but Verner is short on coin. Argus demands valuable dragonhide in payment: the highly prized, softer underbelly scales of the black dragon whelps nesting in the region. Without them, collectors may come from Elwynn Forest to claim the debt. Black dragon whelps in the Redridge Mountains alarm the local defenders. Gnolls and orcs contest the roads, while the Black Dragonflight nests in the high peaks and its brood wanders the skies south of Lake Everstill. The young predators’ underbelly scales are tough yet pliable. Armorers, smiths, and leatherworkers across the kingdom prize them, if they dare to harvest them.

quest:123.text: The Collector. In Elwynn Forest, gold shipments leave the abandoned mines under cover of gnoll raids. An intercepted dispatch names their overseer as 'The Collector' and points to an organized operation near Stormwind's garrison. Riverpaw gnolls in western Elwynn Forest carry a parchment called the Gold Pickup Schedule. It sets dates and times for gold taken from local mines. The intercepted note directs each shipment to an overseer known only as 'The Collector.' At the Lion's Pride Inn, Marshal Dughan learns that gold is still being mined and moved. Official mines across Elwynn have been closed for months because of gnoll attacks, kobold infestations, and roaming bandits. Gnolls with shipping schedules point to an organized criminal network stealing the kingdom's wealth.

quest:125.text: The Lost Tools. Blackrock fire has sunk Foreman Oslow's tools in Lake Everstill. With Lakeshire under pressure, local hands must maintain its defenses, and the tools shipped from Goldshire are needed to rebuild the shattered bridge. The Great Bridge no longer connects Lakeshire to Elwynn Forest. A replacement shipment of stonemasonry and carpentry tools came overland from Goldshire, but the wagons could not reach town. The crew loaded the supplies into a rowboat to cross Lake Everstill. A Blackrock orc catapult struck the boat, destroying it and sending Oslow's heavy ironbound toolbox to the lake floor. Lake Everstill holds dangers below its surface. Aggressive murloc tribes prowl the shallows, while predatory threshers hunt in the murky depths. Foreman Oslow needs his tools to resume repairs on the bridge and keep Lakeshire from falling further into ruin.

quest:129.text: A Free Lunch. Darcy asks you to carry a prepared meal from Lakeshire to Guard Parker on the southern road. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the approaches, and the town's guards are stretched thin. Darcy, the cook in Lakeshire, has packed a meal for Guard Parker but cannot carry it beyond town herself. Redridge gnolls and roaming orc warbands make the roads outside the gates too dangerous for a civilian. She asks passing travelers to take the food along the road toward Darkshire, where Parker keeps watch. Guard Parker watches the road south of Lakeshire, along the route toward Duskwood. Redridge's guards have too few reinforcements from the Stormwind army to face the growing gnoll packs and the Blackrock clan in the mountains. Sentries like Parker keep watch alone in hostile country, and a hot meal from town can lift their spirits.

quest:13.text: The People's Militia. Westfall's volunteers face a growing Defias threat. Led by Gryan Stoutmantle, The People's Militia now confronts thieves who have moved beyond highway robbery to ransack Moonbrook and the Gold Coast Quarry. The Militia calls for harsher retaliation. Defias attacks have spread from the roads to Westfall's economic centers. Defias Looters and Pillagers, who hurl fire, occupy Moonbrook and the Gold Coast Quarry. They strip the Alexston Farmstead as well. Gryan Stoutmantle sees what their hold on these places could mean: Westfall may become impossible to reclaim without a formal royal army. Stormwind has sent Gryan Stoutmantle neither soldiers nor supplies. So he calls on the Holy Light and the resolve of Westfall's remaining farmers. Volunteers carry the fight into Defias strongholds, wearing down the Brotherhood. Driving out the looters will deny them resources and show fearful residents that defenders still fight for Westfall's peace and prosperity.

quest:130.text: Visit the Herbalist. Guard Parker sends you to buy flowers for Darcy before you return to the Lakeshire inn. He wants the gift to stay secret. At his post on Lakeshire's southern approach, Guard Parker watches for blackrock orcs and gnolls. You bring him a warm meal from Darcy at the Lakeshire Inn. Grateful for her kindness, Parker asks you to stop at the herbalist shop on the west end of town and buy flowers for her. Parker asks you to keep the order private when you visit Martie Jainrose, the herbalist. Lakeshire is a small town, and he does not want Martie to know who sent the flowers or who will receive them. At the shop, Martie teases you, guessing you have already found a sweetheart in town. With orc incursions and brigands troubling Redridge, a small gesture of romance brings some welcome relief.

quest:131.text: Delivering Daffodils. In Lakeshire, you carry flowers from Martie Jainrose to Darcy, and an awkward rivalry comes to light. First, you bring lunch to Guard Parker, who asks you to collect a bouquet for Darcy at the Lakeshire Inn. Guard Parker thanks you for bringing his lunch and asks you to fetch flowers from Martie Jainrose for Darcy, the cook who prepared his meal. Martie arranges a bouquet of daffodils, her own favorite flowers, without knowing who will receive them.

quest:132.text: The Defias Brotherhood. At the edges of Redridge and Westfall, Wiley the Black warns Gryan Stoutmantle. His intelligence shows the Defias threat reaches beyond banditry, and Gryan needs to learn how far it extends. Wiley the Black says sharing what he knows could cost him his life. His sealed note describes how the Brotherhood has coordinated groups across the countryside, though those groups are usually hostile to one another. Wiley warns that the Defias has drawn an alarming network around itself. The red-masked outlaws have enlisted gnoll packs, kobold diggers, and goblin engineers instead of working alone. Their brutal muscle, burrowing labor, and mechanical cunning point to an enterprise beyond what the People's Militia first expected. Gryan Stoutmantle has little love for Wiley. He openly laments that he did not leave the rogue to rot when he had the chance. Yet Westfall cannot afford pride. The People's Militia must take useful intelligence wherever it can find it.

quest:1338.text:
Stormpike's Order. In Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike sends a shield order south to Stormwind City. He asks you to carry it to Furen Longbeard, the armorsmith he trusts. Stormpike trusts no other smith with his shield. He offers good pay to place the commission in Furen Longbeard’s hands, though Stormwind City lies far south of Loch Modan. Stormpike wonders why Furen works so far from Ironforge and the Great Forge, where many dwarves make their home. He suspects Stormwind’s humans pay the smith a king’s ransom.

When the order reaches Furen at his anvil, he takes pride in hearing from the prestigious Stormpike clan. He eagerly prepares to forge the shield.

quest:1339.text: Mountaineer Stormpike's Task. At his post in Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike needs a runner for urgent business beyond the valley. Mountaineer Kadrell sends you to find him, since Stormpike cannot leave his watch. The northern guard tower is Stormpike’s post, and his watch keeps him from leaving Loch Modan. The Mountaineers are stretched thin by troggs and roaming wildlife. So Kadrell directs capable travelers to guards who cannot abandon their duties. Stormpike needs a messenger for business far beyond the region’s borders. You find Stormpike atop the northern guard tower, looking out over the valley. He belongs to the prominent Stormpike clan and has affairs beyond Thelsamar’s frontier defenses. Carrying his message and supplies takes you across regional borders on his behalf. Your road leads from the loch onto the highways of Khaz Modan.

quest:135.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, Gryan Stoutmantle suspects the Defias Brotherhood has ties to Stormwind's old Stonemasons Guild. He sends you there with Wiley's Note. Wiley's mention of the Stonemasons catches Gryan's attention. The guild rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War, but many believe it scattered or dissolved. If the Defias are linked to the guild, Westfall's rural insurgency may be more than a band of outlaws. Gryan cannot test his suspicions from Sentinel Hill, so he sends you to Master Mathias Shaw, head of Stormwind's covert intelligence wing, SI:7. Shaw works from the Barracks in Old Town, gathering whispers and secrets from across the realm. He may untangle the Defias Brotherhood's origins.

quest:1358.text: Sample for Helbrim. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim awaits a wolf heart from across the sea. Apothecary Zinge sends it from the Undercity to support the Forsaken's research in central Kalimdor. Apothecary Zinge sends a Wolf Heart Sample from the Undercity to Apothecary Helbrim in the Barrens. The Royal Apothecary Society's experiments reach beyond the ruins of Lordaeron. After Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine sent tainted organs, Zinge sought to extend their research across the world. Now a courier carries the sample overseas to Helbrim, an alchemist stationed in the Barrens' dry savanna. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim studies how Kalimdor's native beasts react to compounds from the Plaguelands. The wolf heart could show how those toxins affect local creatures. Helbrim believes that dissecting and testing it alongside them will help the Forsaken master poisons and unnatural afflictions.

quest:1359.text: Zinge's Delivery. Apothecary Renferrel sends Zinge's Delivery from the Sepulcher to the Undercity. The wolf hearts he sends from Silverpine Forest carry toxins that should have killed the beasts, and Apothecary Zinge receives them for study by the Royal Apothecary Society. Apothecary Renferrel found a strange trait in the wolves roaming Silverpine Forest's ruined woods. Their hearts held such powerful toxins that they should have killed the beasts. Renferrel preserved several tissue samples and packed them for colleagues at the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Apothecary Zinge receives the preserved organs at the Undercity's underground headquarters of the Royal Apothecary Society. The society seeks potent plagues and new alchemical compounds, so poisons that sustain their hosts draw its attention. Zinge welcomes the samples as the start of further laboratory trials across the Forsaken alchemical network.

quest:136.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. Along Westfall's shore, Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure begins with a battered parchment map. It sends you searching for his personal footlocker, then onward toward his hidden plunder across the region. Captain Sanders was an old seafarer who met a watery grave off Westfall's western coast. He left cryptic instructions so his hard-won fortune would not be lost to the Great Sea or taken by scavengers. You can retrace the trail he left behind. Shipwrecks and the restless spirits of drowned sailors mark the western shore.

quest:138.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. Along Westfall's shore, Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure sends you inland. You leave the coast and follow the next mark in his scattered trail. Captain Sanders left riddles across the countryside instead of marking one cache by the beach. The solved cipher points beyond rocky bluffs toward Westfall's main roads. Among the roadside ruins, an old chimney marks the next stop. A discarded, weathered barrel nearby holds another message, and the ruined farmstead gives Sanders a landmark for his trail.

quest:139.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A broken barrel on Westfall's western shore begins Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure trail. Its clue points north to an old jug beside a coastal windmill, one step closer to the late pirate's riches. Captain Sanders left clues that point only to the next hiding place. No single parchment shows where his plunder lies, so the trail stays unresolved until you find each message. The parchment sends you due north from the barrel to the sea cliffs. An isolated windmill stands on the bluffs, with another clue in an abandoned jug beside it. Murlocs and Defias scavengers roam the coast, making the way perilous.

quest:14.text: The People's Militia. In southern Westfall, volunteers of The People's Militia press their fight against the Defias. The seasoned brigands hold the Dagger Hills, and Gryan Stoutmantle leads a campaign to clear the roads and farms. Complete the patrols, and you earn full induction at Sentinel Hill. The Defias Brotherhood has brought great hardship to Westfall's northern farmlands. Those who escaped Gryan Stoutmantle's first sweeps fled south to the rocky Dagger Hills. From there, Defias Highwaymen, Pathstalkers, and Knuckledusters still raid homesteads and waylay travelers. You join hardened recruits sent into the hills to break the brigands' hold over southern Westfall. After returning from the fight against the Scourge in Lordaeron, Gryan Stoutmantle found Westfall abandoned by Stormwind's royal garrison. A criminal syndicate went unchecked, and hunger drove farmers from their land. So he rallied local volunteers to take up arms. Complete this final patrol, and Stoutmantle blesses you in the Light as he formally inducts you into the militia. The fight against the Brotherhood deepens.

quest:140.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A whiskey-soaked clue sends you west from Westfall's shore and out across the Great Sea. Captain Sanders' trail ends at a remote islet, where his hidden prize waits. Captain Sanders left clues along Westfall's coast for you to piece together. The last parchment came from the dregs of his favorite whiskey jug. It gives the final bearing: head west to the water's edge, then swim into the waves.

quest:141.text: The Defias Brotherhood. From Stormwind, Mathias Shaw sends Gryan Stoutmantle a confidential report at Sentinel Hill. Shaw investigated the former Stonemasons Guild to help Stoutmantle uncover the Defias Brotherhood's origins.

quest:143.text: Messenger to Westfall. Magistrate Solomon sends a plea from Lakeshire to Westfall for help against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls. With Stormwind's forces absent, he hopes Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia can lend aid. Blackrock orcs and gnolls besiege Lakeshire, and the Stormwind Army has not arrived in force. Magistrate Solomon knows the town guards and irregulars cannot hold the Redridge Mountains alone. With no royal reserves in sight, he writes a formal plea for help. Word has reached him of a citizen defense group forming west of Elwynn Forest, so he sends his appeal there. Gryan Stoutmantle is a veteran commander rallying volunteer fighters under the People's Militia banner. Solomon sends his dispatch across the kingdom, hoping Westfall's volunteers can reinforce Lakeshire's borders until the Crown's armies mobilize. But Westfall is fighting its own desperate struggle against the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:144.text: Messenger to Westfall. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon receives a hard answer from Westfall. He asked Gryan Stoutmantle for soldiers to defend Redridge, but Westfall faces troubles of its own. Magistrate Solomon faces growing troubles in the Redridge Mountains without Stormwind's royal garrison. So he writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall, and asks the southern frontier for help. Solomon hopes the volunteers at Sentinel Hill can spare fighters to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. He does not know how hard pressed the western plains are. Gryan Stoutmantle refuses, though the answer weighs heavily on him. Westfall fights the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls because the House of Nobles and the crown have abandoned the kingdom's breadbasket. The People's Militia formed to help the people survive. Its ranks lose good men each day, and Stoutmantle cannot spare a single fighter for Redridge.

quest:145.text: Messenger to Darkshire. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Darkshire for aid. Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten Redridge, and Solomon turns to his neighbor for military support. A courier must cross Duskwood's shadowed roads to deliver the letter to Lord Ello Ebonlocke, Darkshire's mayor. Redridge faces growing pressure from Blackrock orcs and gnoll packs, and Lakeshire's guards are stretched thin. Stormwind's royal court has ignored Magistrate Solomon's pleas, while Westfall is caught up in its own insurrection. With little help nearby, Solomon writes to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke in Duskwood, hoping Darkshire can lend or hire its Night Watch to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. Solomon's letter must travel south through Duskwood, a forest under supernatural gloom. He warns you to keep to the roads, since the wilderness between Lakeshire and Darkshire is perilous. The letter is bound for Town Hall, where Lord Ebonlocke can receive it. Whether Duskwood can spare any forces is another matter.

quest:1453.text: Reclaimers' Business in Desolace. Roetten Stonehammer sends travelers from Ironforge across the sea to Desolace for paid work with the Reclaimers. At Nijel's Point, Kreldig Ungor needs help recovering lost treasures and relics. Beyond the sea, Desolace is a harsh stretch of Kalimdor ruled by warring centaur clans. The Reclaimers seek profit among its forgotten ruins and barren lands. For those willing to face the danger, the journey may pay well. The route runs west through the Stonetalon Mountains and into northern Desolace. High among the cliffs, Nijel's Point is an Alliance outpost where Kreldig Ungor welcomes new hands. The Reclaimers recover heirlooms, magical artifacts, and family treasures lost across the war-torn world. For the right price, Kreldig and his associates retrieve those valuables from the wild.

quest:146.text: Messenger to Darkshire. In Darkshire, Lord Ello Ebonlocke answers a plea for help from Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls press against the town, but the plea cannot be granted. Magistrate Solomon of Redridge asks his old peer in Duskwood for troops. Blackrock orcs and gnolls are closing in on his town. Lord Ello Ebonlocke answers in anger. Darkshire struggles against the living dead, ravenous beasts, and cursed magic on every side. Ebonlocke says the Night Watch exists because Stormwind abandoned Duskwood. Without its defenders, Darkshire would fall before a patrol could cross the forest.

quest:1462.text: Earth Sapta. At Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather prepares another Earth Sapta when a young shaman loses the brew before completing the rite. The draught opens a novice’s sight to the spirits of stone and lets the trial continue. Young shaman begin by learning to sense forces beyond ordinary sight. To meet Mulgore’s earth elementals, an initiate drinks a sapta, a ritual brew made with natural essences of stone and soil. The Earth Sapta lifts the veil between the physical and spiritual realms, letting a novice see and commune with the spirits of the land. A novice may lose or spill the brew before reaching the stone monument for communion. Seer Ravenfeather waits at Camp Narache and prepares another vessel when a pupil needs one. With the draught restored, the novice can continue the rite and face the spirits.

quest:1463.text: Earth Sapta. In the Valley of Trials, an initiate who loses the Earth Sapta can ask Canaga Earthcaller for another. The replacement gives the young shaman a chance to commune with the spirits of the land, along with a warning to guard sacred draughts carefully. A misplaced Earth Sapta can interrupt an initiate's communion with the spirits of stone and soil. Prepared through specific rituals, the elemental brew thins the veil between the physical realm and the spirits. When an initiate loses or spills it while traveling through Durotar, Canaga Earthcaller prepares another in good faith, but warns the novice to guard sacred gifts with greater care. Canaga Earthcaller watches over fledgling shamans emerging from the Den in the Valley of Trials. He understands that young orcs and trolls are prone to the chaos of early trials, but stresses that elemental spirits do not take kindly to negligence. Accepting a second sapta offers a small lesson in humility: power granted by the earth must be guarded and respected.

quest:147.text: Manhunt. In Elwynn Forest, Marshal Dughan sends you to find the Collector, a Defias bagman. He works from the overrun Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and sends stolen gold from the forest's mines to the Brotherhood. Marshal Dughan sends you to Brackwell Pumpkin Patch after Elwynn's gnolls are found carrying a schedule for gold pickups. Defias bandits and gnolls have taken over the once quiet homestead. The Collector hides among its overgrown vines, skimming ore from the kingdom's mines and arranging shipments for the growing rebellion.

quest:1470.text: Piercing the Veil. In Deathknell, Venya Marthand tests a novice warlock's resolve. The newly risen Forsaken must gather skulls from nearby mindless skeletons to earn the knowledge to summon and bind an imp. In Deathknell, Venya Marthand teaches newly awakened Forsaken warlocks that strength comes from knowledge and mastery of chaotic powers. She sends novices to gather skulls from the Rattlecage Skeletons near Deathknell's abandoned smithy. The trial tests whether they have the focus to command powers beyond this world and subdue nether beings. Venya accepts the skulls as proof that a novice can overcome mindless undead and face the bleak truths of warlock craft. She then teaches the rituals to summon and bind an imp. Though small, the demon brings cunning and fire, making it a dangerous ally.

quest:1471.text: The Binding. In the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Forsaken warlocks seek to summon, conquer, and permanently command a voidwalker. Carendin Halgar oversees the rite that grants them this power. Forsaken warlocks must prove they can master a voidwalker before they may summon one. Unlike minor imps, which dark magic easily draws into pacts, creatures of the Void despise reality and possess formidable physical might. In the Magic Quarter, mentor Carendin Halgar provides the mystic runes required to tear a voidwalker from the Nether into the physical realm. Beneath Carendin Halgar's dais, a glowing summoning circle is etched into the floor. When the runes are activated, an unbound voidwalker appears in fury. You cannot subdue it through diplomacy; you must break it with arcane force and raw will. Only after the creature is thoroughly crushed does Carendin reveal the true summoning formula, which binds its essence to you indefinitely.

quest:1473.text: Creature of the Void. In the Undercity, a lost grimoire holds the key to summoning a voidwalker. Forsaken warlocks must recover Egalin's Grimoire from the Scarlet Crusade in western Tirisfal Glades to learn how to summon and bind one. Carendin Halgar guides Forsaken summoners in the Temple of the Damned. When an acolyte can wield more than the power of petty imps, Halgar points them toward the voidwalker, a creature forged from pure shadow and chaos. Forsaken warlocks rely on the careful research of Egalin, Halgar's former master, who wrote the rituals for subduing these beings of the void. Egalin's Grimoire holds the methods for channeling the volatile magic needed to master a voidwalker. Perrine, a Scarlet Crusade zealot stationed in an outpost tower to the west, stole the book. The Crusade may see it only as blasphemous contraband to seize and hoard, but recovering it gives the Forsaken the ritual secrets they need before they try to tear open the veil.

quest:1478.text: Halgar's Summons. A formal summons calls promising Forsaken warlocks to advanced training in Undercity. Carendin Halgar expects those who have reached a threshold in their craft to join him in the Magic Quarter, where dangerous Nether beings await. Word of a warlock's control over basic fel energies travels from Brill or the Tirisfal wilderness to Undercity. Ageron Kargal, a senior practitioner who spots talent, sends notice to those who show promise. Carendin Halgar's summons marks a rare privilege and a perilous step in a warlock's training. Basic imps and petty curses no longer suffice. Carendin Halgar oversees warlock rites in Undercity's Magic Quarter, near the Temple of the Damned. Forsaken darkcasters lack the living's moral restraint, but planar summonings still demand discipline. Halgar tolerates neither hesitation nor sentimentality. Those called to him are expected to show deference and be ready to face the hostile horrors of the Twisting Nether.

quest:1485.text: Vile Familiars. Near the Den, Vile Familiars threaten every warlock who seeks the power of demons. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength against them and bring back their heads. This is the humble, dangerous first step toward mastering fel power under the Horde’s watchful eyes. Warlocks live uneasily within Thrall’s new Horde. Demonic corruption and blood pacts once brought ruin to the orcs, leaving deep scars and distrust. Fel magic is tolerated in Durotar, but its practitioners are neither loved nor welcomed. Many warlocks live in seclusion, practicing in shadowed places like the Den, away from prying eyes. There, they teach the few initiates daring enough to follow their path. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength before he teaches you the dangerous rites for bending an imp to your will. Vile Familiars skulk near a cave northeast of the Den and hurl bolts of flame at those who approach. Slay these lesser demons and bring back their heads to show you can overcome the fiery creatures you hope to control. Only then can you face the danger of the magic you seek to command.

quest:1492.text: Wharfmaster Dizzywig. At Ratchet's pier, a crate of alchemy supplies waits for passage across the sea. Wharfmaster Dizzywig arranges its journey to the Old World aboard a ship bound for Blackwater Cove. A crate of potions and reagents waits at the Barrens port, bound for colleagues in the Old World. Caravans that might have carried it have already departed, so you are asked to take the secure shipment to Ratchet's water's edge. The port offers a route across the Great Sea between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Wharfmaster Dizzywig handles cargo on Ratchet's wooden piers. He tracks shipments in ledgers and manifests, then finds space aboard vessels sailing east across the Great Sea. This crate is booked for a ship bound for Blackwater Cove.

quest:1498.text: Path of Defense. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek prepares young Horde warriors to defend those who cannot defend themselves. He sends them to Thunder Ridge to prove their endurance against its electric beasts. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek teaches young warriors that defense is part of the Horde's duty. The post lies on the border between the Barrens and Durotar. Uzzek says a warrior's highest calling is to stand between danger and those unable to defend themselves, taking the blows so the Horde can endure. Uzzek sends the novices to Thunder Ridge, north across the Southfury River in Durotar, to test their stamina and resolve. Thunder lizards and lightning hides roam the canyon. The initiates must survive the beasts' jolts and harvest their singed scales to show they have the fortitude to hold the front line.

quest:1499.text: Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Ruzan sends warlock initiates against vile familiars. After you slay them, you report to Zureetha Fargaze, who oversees the effort to curb the Burning Blade. Warriors and scouts in the Valley of Trials answer directly to Zureetha Fargaze, who sends them to curb the Burning Blade Coven. Warlock initiates first answer to Ruzan, their shadowy mentor. He demands proof that you can master lesser demons before sending you back to aid the Horde's defense. Your work serves both the warlocks and the safety of the Den. Zureetha Fargaze watches the northern cavern above the Valley of Trials. Vile familiars hide within, the weakest pets of the Burning Blade cultists. Their presence in the sacred training grounds insults the orcs and threatens the Valley. When you report your success, you show that those who practice fel magic remain ready to defend Durotar from corruption.

quest:15.text: Investigate Echo Ridge. Kobolds gather in force at Echo Ridge Mine, so Marshal McBride sends you north. The mine supplies ore and raw materials to Northshire Abbey and the Stormwind guard stationed there. Scattered vermin have troubled the valley's forested edge near Northshire. Now the scouts report a more organized gathering. At the entrance, you face kobold workers and see how deeply they have settled into the mine. The kobolds have seized the tunnels and stopped the digging. Their presence strains the Northshire brotherhood's defenses. McBride asks you to cull ten workers, but the infestation reaches farther into the shafts than a surface patrol can reach.

quest:1501.text: Creature of the Void. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye sends a young warlock after the stolen Tablet of Verga. The rogue Burning Blade cultists took it to their cavern at Skull Rock, and its runes are needed to summon a voidwalker. Gan'rul Bloodeye trains Horde warlocks in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. Thrall's new realm regards fel magic with deep wariness because of the orcish clans' dark history. Gan'rul says few true warlocks remain in the Horde, but their perilous skills are essential to its survival. To serve the Warchief, an initiate must learn more than the chaotic fire of an imp; they must command beings of pure shadow and endurance. The runes needed to summon a voidwalker are inscribed on the Tablet of Verga. The Burning Blade, a fanatical shadow cult, stole the relic and hides in a cavern at Skull Rock, right beneath the Warchief's nose. Gan'rul sends you into the cultists' den to recover the tablet and strike a bloody blow against the renegades who stain the name of all practicing warlocks.

quest:1502.text: Thun'grim Firegaze. Atop Thorn Hill, Thun'grim Firegaze keeps to a reclusive life and a solitary forge. After their first lessons in defense, Horde warriors cross the Barrens to find him and seek steel fit for their growing skill. After you show skill in the defensive arts under veteran trainers like Uzzek, you are sent to sharpen your fighting with suitable steel. Ordinary armories can carry a frontline fighter only so far. True mastery calls for a personal weapon from a smith of renown. In the Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze is that smith, an aging orc who has left settlement life behind to keep an isolated forge high above the plains. Thun'grim Firegaze lives atop Thorn Hill, a jagged rise east of the Crossroads where wild raptors and hostile quilboar roam. He spends his solitary hours shaping metal, far from the protection of town walls. Decades of gazing into blistering forge flames have ruined his eyesight, though his instincts remain sharp. When you climb the heights and disturb his solitude, Firegaze knows why: a warrior has come seeking forged steel.

quest:1503.text: Forged Steel. Thun'grim Firegaze waits in the eastern Barrens for the steel stolen from his camp. He offers to forge a weapon for the warrior who brings it back. Thun'grim Firegaze keeps a smithy in the eastern Barrens, far from Orgrimmar. Years at the forge have dimmed his sight. The nearby Razormane quilboar used that weakness to steal an iron chest from his camp. Some snorted and made noise on one side to draw his gaze while others slipped in from the other and carried off his forged steel bars. Thun'grim is angry at the theft, but doubts the Razormanes can use the steel. Quilboar craft with stone, tusks, and thorny roots, not refined metal. The heavy chest remains near a broken wagon in their camp, untouched and useless to them. For Thun'grim, its steel is the stock he needs to forge weapons for young Horde warriors.

quest:1504.text: The Binding. In Orgrimmar, The Binding marks young Horde warlocks' final initiation ritual. Gan'rul Bloodeye directs each petitioner to use glyphs from the Tablet of Verga in Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle. You face your first true test of will when you summon a voidwalker. An imp is child's play by comparison. Warlocks do not make pacts with these creatures or commune with them. You pull them across dimensions by force and bind them to serve. Gan'rul Bloodeye directs you to use glyphs from the Tablet of Verga and call the voidwalker into Neeru Fireblade's ritual circle, to break it there in single combat. Defeating the voidwalker in physical and magical combat is only half the struggle. Gan'rul Bloodeye warns that a bound voidwalker never truly accepts its enslavement. Even while it guards its master in battle as a durable, shadowy bulwark, it waits for a lapse in your concentration. If your hold over your servant ever falters, it will consume the soul of the one who bound it.

quest:1506.text: Gan'rul's Summons. Ophek brings Gan'rul's Summons to young Horde warlocks in Razor Hill. Gan'rul Bloodeye calls them to the Cleft of Shadow to advance their training. There, they take the first step toward summoning a voidwalker. In Durotar, novice warlocks do not go unnoticed for long. When a practitioner shows enough mastery over an initial imp, word reaches the deep caverns beneath Orgrimmar. Ophek carries messages for the senior dark casters from his post in Durotar. He finds warlocks with an urgent demand to leave their work and report to the Cleft of Shadow. Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the training of young orc warlocks within the Horde. From the hidden caverns beneath Orgrimmar, he hones their lethal fel power while keeping these dangerous arts from the Warchief's disapproving gaze. A call to his circle means simple fire spells and imps are no longer enough. The apprentice is ready to bind a creature from the Twisting Nether.

quest:151.text: Poor Old Blanchy. On Westfall's road, Poor Old Blanchy waits with the stranded Furlbrows, worn out and hungry. Their wagon broke as they fled, and Verna asks you to find oats at nearby abandoned farms to feed the mare. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow are stranded beside Westfall's main road. Bandits and rogue mechanical harvest golems have driven families like theirs from their homes. The Furlbrows tried to carry their belongings to safety, but their wagon broke down, leaving them marooned in open country. Old Blanchy has plowed and hauled for the Furlbrow family through many seasons. Now the delay has left the gentle mare exhausted and starving. Verna asks you to search nearby overrun farmsteads for sacks of oats. Hostile threshers and gnoll scavengers threaten there, but the grain could give the faithful mare a decent meal.

quest:1516.text: Call of Earth. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller sets novice Horde shamans a test of endurance and patience. They hunt felstalkers to prepare a ritual sapta. A shaman begins by learning to bond with each element. For orcs and trolls, that path starts with earth, the bedrock of life, endurance, and patience. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller guides new shamans and teaches them that earth demands respect and steadfastness before it grants protection. The Burning Blade cult festers in ravines north of the Valley of Trials. Its dark magic summons felstalkers, corrupt hounds from beyond this plane. Hunting them tests whether a shaman can defend the land from unnatural decay. Canaga uses their hooves to brew an Earth Sapta, a sacred draft that opens mortal eyes to the elemental plane.

quest:1517.text: Call of Earth. At Spirit Rock, Canaga Earthcaller guides young shaman through their first communion with the elements. They drink an Earth Sapta on sacred ground to see the Minor Manifestation of Earth. A sapta is a mystical draught known to only a few shaman masters. Made with elemental magic, it bridges mortal perception and the spiritual plane, granting Sapta Sight to the strong-willed. Because it binds the drinker's spirit directly to an element, tradition forbids drinking it outside consecrated holy ground. To commune with earth, you leave the Valley of Trials and climb the Hidden Path into Durotar's southern crags. Spirit Rock waits at the trail's end, an elevated sanctuary overlooking the rugged wasteland. Drink the sapta there, and you can perceive what ordinary eyes cannot: an elemental presence among the stone. The Minor Manifestation of Earth asks no bloodshed or submission. It asks only that you stand humbly before the world. Fire, water, and air bear turbulent, volatile, often chaotic spirits, while earth teaches steadiness. Mountains offer endurance, and plains teach boundless patience.

quest:1518.text: Call of Earth. In Durotar, a young shaman communes with a manifestation of the earth spirit. The initiate returns to Canaga Earthcaller with rough quartz and receives a first elemental totem. A novice shaman seeks communion with the earth through patience and humility, not brute strength. The Minor Manifestation of Earth grants the initiate a piece of rough quartz. The small stone proves the spirit has accepted the initiate’s pledge and remains a seed of power. You complete the trial by bringing the quartz to Canaga Earthcaller in the Valley of Trials. Canaga shapes it into an Earth Totem, the focus through which you channel the ground’s steadfast protection and strength. The rite begins your path through the four elemental disciplines and lays the foundation for a lifetime of communion with the natural world.

quest:152.text: The Coast Isn't Clear. Shipwrecked sailors struggle to reach Westfall's western shore as murlocs close in. Captain Grayson calls on you to clear the beaches so survivors can land safely. Reefs, squalls, and jagged rocks drive ships onto Westfall's shoals. Survivors cling to wreckage and crawl onto the sand, hoping help will come. They find murloc tribes along the shore instead, and the murlocs show no mercy to castaways. Captain Grayson watches from a lonely outcropping southwest of the mainland. Though dead, he remains bound to the lighthouse and to his duty toward passing ships and lost sailors. Coastrunners hold the northern shore. Farther south, Tidehunters, Warriors, and Oracles gather.

quest:1520.text: Call of Earth. At Kodo Rock, you seek communion with earth through a sacred tauren rite. Drinking an Earth Sapta lets you see a Minor Manifestation of Earth. Shamanic elders brew a sapta to bind an initiate’s mortal spirit to a primal element. Ancestral magic guards the brewing secrets, known to only a select few among the tauren. Drink the draught at a sacred site, and your mind opens beyond the physical world. The veil parts, and the elements can be witnessed in their raw form. East of Camp Narache, Kodo Rock rises as a stone pillar and holy sanctuary. Drink the sapta there, and a Minor Manifestation of Earth appears before you. Along the shaman’s path, other aspects of nature are volatile, fiery, or raging. Earth asks for quiet humility instead. Honor the land, and its spirit grants you the mountain’s enduring strength and the plains’ calm patience.

quest:1521.text: Call of Earth. After the first communion with the land spirits in Mulgore, a young tauren shaman returns to Camp Narache with a gift from the earth. Drinking the Earth Sapta lets the initiate speak directly with a spirit manifestation and receive raw stone, binding them to the first of the four elements. After drinking the Earth Sapta, you meet the Minor Manifestation of Earth atop the crags near Red Cloud Mesa. The spirit gives you a plain Rough Quartz. It represents your pact with the element and the endurance of stone. The spirit reminds you that patience and strength are the virtues the earth demands, and promises harmony with the land through mutual respect. At Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather shapes the gifted quartz into your first Earth Totem. The totem is more than a mark of status: it is a lasting physical and spiritual anchor. Through this carved focus, you channel the earth’s grounding, protective magic and take your first true step along the fourfold elemental path.

quest:1524.text: Call of Fire. In the Barrens, an aspiring shaman begins the second trial in the search for communion with fire. Kranal Fiss sends the initiate across the Southfury River to a secluded mountaintop shrine in Durotar, carrying the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame. Kranal Fiss entrusts the shaman with the Torch of the Dormant Flame. Raw mystical strength alone cannot meet fire’s demands; the trial calls for temperance, focus, and respect. The torch is both ritual instrument and proof to the shrine’s keeper that the bearer has been judged ready to attempt the trial. The shrine lies across the Southfury River, among Durotar’s southern crags. A weathered stone carved with a fire rune marks an obscure path that climbs toward one of the region’s highest peaks. At the summit, the Shrine of the Dormant Flame is watched by Telf Joolam, a troll hermit. He turns away curious travelers and treasure hunters, keeping the sacred brazier from ordinary eyes until a petitioner arrives with the unlit torch.

quest:1525.text: Call of Fire. Telf Joolam sends a shaman across Durotar and the eastern Barrens for a Fire Sapta's ingredients. The draught prepares an initiate to perceive and speak with fire spirits. A Fire Sapta opens a shaman’s senses to the Eternal Flame. Like the draught for earth, it lets a shaman see and speak with spirits hidden from mortal sight. Telf Joolam sends initiates across Durotar and into the eastern Barrens to gather ingredients bound to heat and flame. Razormane quilboar spellcasters in the eastern Barrens carry fire tar, made in their earthy rituals. Burning Blade cultists carry the other needed ingredient in Dustwind Cave, in the ravines northeast of Razor Hill. The cultists use fire for destruction and demonic chaos, while the reagents in their pouches hold a natural tie to the element.

quest:1526.text: Call of Fire. Atop Durotar's peaks, a shaman faces the trial that attunes them to fire. Telf Joolam guides the initiate to drink fire sapta, confront a Minor Manifestation of Fire, and claim its glowing ember to light the ceremonial torch. Fire spirits hide from untrained eyes on Durotar's summit. To see them, you drink fire sapta, a draught made from reagents gathered across the barrens and coast. It sharpens your senses to the unseen, revealing minor spirits and manifestations among the summit crags. A Minor Manifestation of Fire waits atop the mountain. Once the sapta takes hold, the spirit knows you can see it and awaits your challenge. Fire answers strength and decisive action, so you strike without delay. The longer the fight lasts, the more fiercely the elemental fire burns.

quest:153.text: Red Leather Bandanas. At Sentinel Hill, Red Leather Bandanas mark the Defias fight. Scout Galiaan seeks the red masks worn by outlaws as the People's Militia struggles to track them across Westfall. Across Westfall, a red bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. Cutpurses, looters, and traitors from many walks of life join the gang, then rally beneath the same crimson sign. At Sentinel Hill, Scout Galiaan and the People's Militia collect the cloth as proof that bandits have fallen. The bandanas also help them follow the Defias as its fronts shift across the countryside. Stormwind has denied Westfall proper military support, leaving the People's Militia to chart Defias activity with seasoned observers like Scout Galiaan. From Sentinel Hill, Galiaan watches outlaw patrols and tracks their movements. Passing adventurers and militia volunteers take on the dangerous work of bringing down the highwaymen who drove honest farmers from their land.

quest:155.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the People's Militia seeks the Defias Brotherhood's hidden base. A captured brigand will guide you there in exchange for protection, leading through Moonbrook to Edwin VanCleef's inner sanctum. The Defias Traitor fears execution or assassination by his former brothers. So he bargains with the People's Militia: escort him safely through hostile territory, and he will reveal where Edwin VanCleef and his ringleaders hide. The thieves' network silences those who speak out, and the turncoat needs armed protection along the road.

quest:1578.text: Supplying the Front. In Loch Modan, Mountaineers need fresh arms as trogg attacks threaten their defenses. Tormus Deepforge sends apprentice smiths east to supply them. Excavations have opened ruins and caverns across the border. Troggs now strike the Mountaineers without warning. Their lines need fresh blades, belts, and fittings to hold against the attacks. Tormus sends apprentices east while veteran smiths stay at Ironforge’s city forges. His colleague Thorvald Deepforge keeps a field armory in the southern guard tower. There, sturdy copper axes and copper chain belts prove a smith’s reliability and earn advanced smithing techniques.

quest:1579.text: Gaffer Jacks. In Auberdine, Wizbang Cranktoggle needs his lost gaffer jacks back. The gnome inventor tossed a box of hardware into the sea during his voyage from Ironforge, and anglers can search for it along Darkshore's coast. Wizbang Cranktoggle crossed the Great Sea from Ironforge to find quiet in Darkshore. The gnome inventor drank too much on the voyage. Leaning over the rail in a drunken haze, he lost a crate of specialized metal parts called gaffer jacks in the water near Auberdine. Wizbang says gaffer jacks are essential precision tools. Without them, he cannot properly tune his stintle pegs or continue his delicate tinkering. Unwilling to wade into the cold surf himself, he asks local anglers to cast along Darkshore's shore and fish up the scattered parts.

quest:1580.text: Electropellers. In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle asks anglers to recover his lost electropellers. He lost the prototype parts in freshwater streams after a mishap with an explosive duck decoy. Wizbang Cranktoggle spends an evening searching inland Darkshore for a place to test his latest invention. The gnome tinkerer, stationed in Auberdine, has built a self-propelled, exploding duck decoy. After drinking too much, he blacks out and wakes hours later back in town with singed hair and an empty pack. His bag of electropellers has fallen into one of the coastal rivers. Wizbang asks local fishermen to dredge Darkshore's freshwater streams because he does not want to brave the wilds himself. Anglers fishing the Wildbend River and Cliffspring River can snag the buoyant metal parts alongside local fish. With the components recovered, the gnome can resume his erratic waterfowl experiments.

quest:1581.text: Elixirs for the Bladeleafs. Syral Bladeleaf seeks help keeping her family’s busy trade supplied in Dolanaar. Her husband spends nearly all his time brewing, and fresh elixirs could ease his workload while earning the brewer uncommon herbs. Dolanaar draws travelers, sentinels, and druids moving through Teldrassil. Syral Bladeleaf and her husband have built a flourishing herb and alchemy trade to serve them. Demand keeps her husband bent over vials and cauldrons for nearly all his hours, leaving the couple little time together. Syral turns to passing herbalists and brewers to ease her husband’s workload. She asks for Elixirs of Lion's Strength and Minor Defense, offering freshly gathered, uncommon herbs in exchange. For a fledgling alchemist practicing beneath the Great Tree, the exchange brings a bundle of herbs and a chance to turn common forest flora into coveted regional flora.

quest:1582.text: Moonglow Vest. In Darnassus, Lotherias needs leather gear for young adventurers setting out across Kalimdor. She offers the pattern for a Moonglow Vest in return for shipments of embossed leather goods. In Darnassus, leatherworkers work to outfit sentinels and young scouts. Night elves and allied wanderers leave Teldrassil for the wilds of Kalimdor, where sturdy armor is in demand. Lotherias is among the master leatherworkers supplying them with gear. Lotherias asks apprentices to bring matched embossed gloves, boots, and cloaks as proof of their skill. Those who meet her order earn her trust, and she teaches them a night elf pattern for the Moonglow Vest, made to protect while allowing free movement.

quest:1598.text: The Stolen Tome. At Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle seeks a stolen tome from the Defias camp in the vineyards. Powers of the Void could aid her teaching, and bringing it back will prove your skill. Warlocks in Stormwind's lands keep their craft and their research from prying eyes. Northshire Abbey guards forbidden grimoires in its archives. Drusilla cannot risk suspicion from the clerics and paladins by entering the protected wing herself. She covets Powers of the Void and needs another to retrieve it. An abbey novice joined the Defias Brotherhood and stole several valuable texts as he left. He fled to the Northshire Vineyards and took refuge near the Defias campsite. The thieves keep their prize in a field tent, unaware of the danger in the book's dark arts. Recovering Powers of the Void tests your nerve and opens the way to darker knowledge. Returning the tome satisfies Drusilla's ambition and proves you are ready to practice the dark arts. She rewards you with the rites to summon and bind an imp, the first demon an apprentice learns to command.

quest:1599.text: Beginnings. In Dun Morogh, Alamar Grimm tests Alliance warlock novices before teaching them to summon an imp. First, they must take feather charms from Frostmane troll novices. Influential voices have noticed a recruit with promise, and their attention draws Alamar Grimm from his occult research. Though reluctant, the warlock comes to assess the novice. Before teaching a novice to enslave lesser demons, Grimm demands proof of endurance and magical affinity. Frostmane troll novices carry feather charms in a cave southwest of Anvilmar. Subtle primal magic runs through the charms, and taking them proves the novice can overcome a magical foe. The curious specimens also serve Grimm's research. The charms persuade Grimm that the novice has the will to survive. He teaches the summoning of an imp, a warlock's most basic minion. Its chaotic fire magic can overpower a master who lacks discipline.

quest:16.text: Give Gerard a Drink. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works long days in the fields and needs fresh spring water. Passing travelers bring water and trade it for apples. Elwynn's farms supply grain, fruit, and vegetables to Stormwind's townsfolk and garrisons. The work is hot beneath the open sky. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller tends the crops, keeps pests away, and manages the harvest. With little time to reach the town wells, he depends on passing recruits to bring clean spring water so he can keep working. Gerard trades provisions for water instead of coin. Travelers with extra flasks of Refreshing Spring Water can exchange them for fresh apples from his orchard. The kingdom stretches its resources to keep order and feed its army. So barter between smallholders and recruits remains a practical way to get by in rural Elwynn.

quest:161.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII suspects sabotage and sends a powder sample north for examination. A courier must carry it through the Wetlands to demolition expert Ashlan Stonesmirk at Dun Modr. A suspicious barrel near the dam’s eastern ramp held a strange-smelling powder. Hinderweir had seen Dark Iron sappers nearby, and suspects the powder is a refined explosive meant to shatter dwarven masonry. The dam has no specialized equipment to test it. Before he can be certain, he needs a military demolitionist to examine the sample. The road runs through the Algaz Gate and down into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands. Hostile wildlife, aggressive dragonkin, and Dark Iron infiltrators make the way dangerous. Hinderweir urges couriers to keep to the cobbled road to Dun Modr. The pillaged dwarven town stands at the southern approach to the Thandol Span, where an Ironforge regiment still keeps watch.

quest:1618.text: Gearing Redridge. At Lakeshire, a besieged garrison needs sturdy copper equipment from Ironforge. Tormus Deepforge asks aspiring Alliance smiths to forge the gear and help resident smith Verner Osgood defend the region from hostile orcs and gnolls. At Ironforge's Great Forge, dwarven smiths know the Alliance's frontline struggles reach beyond Dun Morogh. In the Redridge Mountains, Lakeshire faces repeated attacks from Blackrock orcs marching from Stonewatch Keep and gnolls roaming the northern ridges. Royal reinforcements from Stormwind are slow to arrive, and local supplies remain dangerously low. Lakeshire's resident blacksmith, Verner Osgood, works nearly alone at his outdoor forge, mending shattered armor and replacing broken weapons. Seeing the strain on his human counterpart, Tormus Deepforge asks developing smiths to bring four Runed Copper Belts and four Heavy Copper Mauls to Lakeshire. In return for bolstering the militia's defensive reserves, Verner teaches traveling craftsmen finer trade techniques.

quest:1638.text: A Warrior's Training. Lyria Du Lac sends young warriors from Goldshire to Stormwind for lessons in battlefield endurance. At the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Old Town, veteran Harry Burlguard puts them through seasoned instruction. When you have shown your skill against threats across Elwynn Forest, Goldshire's trainers have little more to teach. So Lyria Du Lac sends you to Stormwind and the rough district of Old Town. Veteran fighters gather there to share what combat has taught them, far from the royal garrison's rigid ways. Harry Burlguard is an aged battle veteran who keeps his quarters at the Pig and Whistle Tavern. He tests your mettle with drink and practical trials of stamina, not parade-ground drills. Before teaching defensive moves for dangerous campaigns, Harry expects you to match his appetite for drink and face the tavern's local brawlers.

quest:1639.text: Bartleby the Drunk. In the Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby the Drunk faces Harry Burlguard’s test. An aspiring Alliance warrior must take Bartleby’s prized mug before Harry teaches deeper combat skills. Harry Burlguard asks you to prove your backbone before he teaches deeper combat skills in the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Across the room, Bartleby nurses his drinks at the far end of the counter. Harry wants you to take the man’s mug, knowing Bartleby would rather fight than surrender his ale. The challenge tests your resolve. Soldiers, laborers, and rough locals fill the Pig and Whistle, where polished manners count for little. Bartleby mocks newcomers as too prissy for a tavern scuffle instead of answering politely. The exchange leads to a brawl on the floorboards. In Stormwind, a warrior’s training begins with a test of basic barroom fighting.

quest:1640.text: Beat Bartleby. In Stormwind, Beat Bartleby keeps a prized mug from the warrior instructors. He will not give it up, so a recruit must win it in a brawl.
