Then he points you toward the mountain buzzards scavenging around the lodge's nearby crags and hillsides. The hunt tests your speed, patience, and aim against the buzzards' quick flight. Bring down all six before time runs out, and Daryl grudgingly gives up one of his ranged weapons. He offers you further hunting dares, too.

quest:258.text: A Hunter's Challenge. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling dares you to kill five elder mountain boars within twelve minutes. He expects Loch Modan's rough highlands and dangerous wildlife to make you fail. Daryl the Youngling lives among Farstrider Lodge's seasoned huntsmen, but he lacks their quiet patience. He covers his youth with bluster and long hunting tales, including rambling accounts of how he earned his “famous” scar. He refuses to admit that anyone else is skilled. He also keeps getting his fellow hunters' names wrong and sets strict trials for newcomers, hoping to humble them and restore his standing among the lodge's residents. Elder mountain boars roam Loch Modan's crags and hillsides. They are massive and thick-skinned, and grow dangerous when provoked. Daryl gives you twelve minutes to find and kill five. If you finish in time, the loudmouthed youngster retreats awkwardly and pretends he knows nothing of the extravagant wager he made so casually.

quest:26.text: A Lesson to Learn. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends young druids from Darnassus to Moonglade to learn the ways of water. There, they meet an elder of the Cenarion Circle and begin training in their aquatic aspect. Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides young night elf druids as they practice among Darnassus’s boughs. When an initiate shows a firm bond with nature and readiness for greater responsibility, Mathrengyl sends them toward mastery of the waters. Cenarius’s gifts demand focus, and learning to cross the depths without drowning calls for guidance from the Cenarion Circle’s elders. The initiate leaves Darnassus for Moonglade, an ancient sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze waits as an elder mentor of the Cenarion Circle. Starblaze judges whether young shapeshifters are ready for the trials that lead to aquatic form. Mastering water takes both physical resilience and mental resolve.

quest:263.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. At the Southern Guard Tower, Mountaineer Wallbang calls travelers to defend Loch Modan from the Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's reserves sent to distant fronts, the southern pass is thinly held. Wallbang sends seasoned recruits into Stonesplinter Valley against the clan's shamans and bonesnappers. Loch Modan's defenses are stretched thin. Ironforge's regular reserves have been summoned to distant fronts across Azeroth, leaving the Southern Guard Tower short-handed. Mountaineer Wallbang and his few comrades face constant pressure from the Stonesplinter clan. They depend on Alliance travelers passing through to help hold the southern pass. The fight reaches beyond stray scouts to the Stonesplinter clan's strength. Its bonesnappers bring brutal force, while its shamans use earthen magic to rally their kin. Slaying twenty of these foes weakens the clan's incursions into the lowlands. It also serves King Magni Bronzebeard's defense of the realm.

quest:264.text: Until Death Do Us Part. In Silverpine Forest, Until Death Do Us Part brings Clarice Foster’s old grief to Yuriv’s grave. From the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, the Forsaken asks you to leave her keepsake pendant on the tomb of the husband who abandoned her and their children. Clarice Foster remembers her mortal marriage without fondness. As Lordaeron crumbled, Yuriv left her and their children to join a crusade against the rising undead, declaring service to the Holy Light paramount. His devotion saved neither his family nor himself. Clarice was raised into undeath, while Yuriv lies beneath a defaced stone. She wants the last tangible reminder of his broken promises cast away. Yuriv’s tomb lies in the graveyard around the Sepulcher, marked by gashes, rubbish, and weeds. Set Clarice’s pendant on the relief of his sculpted hands, and no grand magic or spiritual closure follows. The gem grows dull, and a cold, silent gust passes over the tombs, leaving the old resentments of Lordaeron’s fallen people.

quest:267.text: The Trogg Threat. At Loch Modan’s Southern Gate, Captain Rugelfuss faces a growing trogg threat with too few defenders. The Ironforge Reserve has been called away to Alliance battlefronts, leaving him to hold the pass while troggs threaten the nearby hills. Dwarven mountaineers and the Ironforge Reserve have gone to reinforce Alliance battlefronts. Captain Rugelfuss now has only a small garrison. Strict orders keep him at the gate, unable to lead an attack into the highlands. Settlers and travelers there remain exposed to ambushes. Troggs in the nearby crags threaten Khaz Modan. Left unchecked, their numbers grow quickly, and they could overrun dwarven outposts. Rugelfuss calls for help to buy time and thin their ranks. Strike at the troggs in their hillside warrens, then bring back their stone teeth as proof.

quest:27.text: A Lesson to Learn. In Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids north to study the waters. Their road leads to Nighthaven in Moonglade, where the Cenarion Circle guides their training. After learning the bear form and its physical might, your studies turn to adaptability. Azeroth's waterways bring hazards that landbound travelers cannot face easily. Turak Runetotem watches his students and sends those devoted to nature north to learn the aquatic form. Turak Runetotem sends you beyond Mulgore for guidance in shaping yourself for the waters. You travel to Moonglade, the sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal, and reach Nighthaven. There, night elf mentors of the Cenarion Circle welcome tauren students. They set factional strife aside to preserve the shared teachings of Cenarius. Dendrite Starblaze waits for you in Nighthaven, where your training begins. The night elf elder says mastery over the waters must be earned. Two trials await: one tests your endurance and composure under water, and the other calls for deep spiritual understanding of the aquatic aspect.

quest:273.text: Resupplying the Excavation. Jern Hornhelm sends you from Thelsamar after a slow wagon carrying blastpowder to Ironband's Excavation Site. Its three dwarven haulers travel south along the Loch's shore. In southern Loch Modan, Ironband's Excavation Site needs blastpowder to break through hard rock. The powder comes first to Thelsamar, where Jern Hornhelm arranges for Huldar, Miran, and Saean to haul three volatile barrels south. The heavy load slows their pack team along the lakeside road, giving you time to catch them and help on the way.

quest:274.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At the Stonewrought Dam, suspicious powder puts Loch Modan and Ironforge in danger. Ashlan Stonesmirk in Dun Modr identifies it as unstable Seaforium, which can explode catastrophically when it touches water. Ashlan Stonesmirk recognizes the silver crystals and distinct odor in samples from the Stonewrought Dam as Seaforium. It stays inert while dry, but moisture makes it react violently. An unchecked explosion could blow Ironforge out of the mountain, Ashlan warns.

quest:2751.text: Barbaric Battlements. In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks someone to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks an aspiring smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge. Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar under the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, and he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk of ending, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward. Orokk will not share his secrets with an untested smith. He asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp beast claws as proof of basic skill at the anvil. To him, blacksmithing is no idle luxury: its highest honor is armor and steel stained with enemy blood. Meeting his demands may persuade the old smith that the Omosh legacy can live on through an apprentice, and earn a chance to learn more of the craft.

quest:2753.text: Trampled Under Foot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh puts smiths through an advanced blacksmithing trial. Forging green iron armor tests their endurance and teaches them to make heavy iron boots, with the Omosh bloodline's secret techniques at stake. Orokk Omosh trains armorsmiths in Orgrimmar through hard physical trials. He sees metalworking as more than heating ore and shaping it; the work honors his ancestral clan and tests a smith's endurance. This is the third trial in his chain, and repeated crafting of tempered green iron armor is meant to build muscle and discipline. Smiths who bring Orokk the requested green iron gear earn rare praise from the gruff armorsmith. He compares an artisan who endures the work to his grandfather, Chief Gorokk of Omosh. In exchange for the armor, Orokk teaches the ancestral design for sturdy iron boots, made so Horde warriors can crush their enemies beneath their heels.

quest:2755.text: Joys of Omosh. After an adventurer's great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith brushes off his tears as soot, then performs the Omosh dance of joy to pass down an unusual piece of family heritage. Near Orgrimmar's scorching forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. The burly blacksmith has received great help from you, and the kindness overwhelms him. He stubbornly blames a stray bit of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping. Before you part, Orokk says he must share one last secret of the Omosh family. He performs the vigorous, exhausting Omosh dance of joy for his apprentice, then teaches the apprentice to strike with an iron fist.

quest:278.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron explosives threaten the Stonewrought Dam, and Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs your help. He asks you to gather rare reagents from Loch Modan so he can make a mixture to neutralize them. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs three ingredients for his mixture. Forest Lurker venom, a tear from a crocolisk in the Loch, and a Mo'grosh crystal each bring a different reaction. Together, they can render the dwarven charges inert. The ingredients lie in dangerous parts of Loch Modan. Forest Lurker spiders and crocolisks threaten travelers, while Mo'grosh ogres guard their mined crystals in a stronghold to the northeast. Reaching the crystals means facing the ogres in their encampments.

quest:280.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron saboteurs threaten the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs the charge disarmed before the loch floods the lowlands. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII saw Dark Iron Insurgents swim toward the Stonewrought Dam with a keg of explosive Seaforium. No Mountaineers were nearby to stop them. The infiltrators fastened the keg against the dam’s underwater foundation. If the dam breaks, the loch will flood the lowlands and cripple dwarven trade and travel.

quest:282.text: Senir's Observations. Grelin Whitebeard sends you east to Kharanos with his report for his brother Senir. Troggs have overrun the tunnel from Coldridge Valley, where Mountaineer Thalos guards the way. Grelin Whitebeard's report tells of Frostmane troll activity around Coldridge Valley. The trolls stole his journal, and you recovered it. Grelin judged the findings too important for an inexperienced apprentice to carry. So he entrusts the report to you, to deliver directly to his brother Senir in Kharanos. Troggs have overrun the eastern tunnel from Coldridge Valley into the rest of Dun Morogh. Mountaineer Thalos guards the entrance to keep civilians from danger. He lets travelers through only when they carry urgent official business.

quest:287.text: Frostmane Hold. Above Iceflow Lake, Frostmane trolls guard a cavern stronghold in the western peaks. Senir Whitebeard, a mountaineer and scout in Kharanos, sends you to scout its depths and bring back intelligence for his reports. Senir tracked the aggressive tribes to their main cavern southwest of Brewnall Village. Armed trolls crowd the entrance. Behind on his official reports, Senir will not enter alone, so he hires you to scout the icy cavern in his place. Above Iceflow Lake, the stronghold is carved into the western peaks and packed with hostile ice trolls. You fight through underground tunnels, kill the Frostmane Headhunters stationed along the ledges, and map the interior. Your findings give Senir the intelligence he needs to complete his report for Ironforge's military commanders.

quest:291.text: The Reports. From Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard sends word to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge about the Frostmane threat to Dun Morogh. He asks you to leave his scout unnamed. The report carries news from deep inside Frostmane Hold, where the trolls threaten Dun Morogh. Senir wants you to take it straight to Barin Redstone and keep the scout from the snowy crags unnamed.

quest:2948.text: Gnome Improvement. In Ironforge, Talvash del Kissel offers to improve a ring he made in Gnomeregan. He needs silver and moss agate for a delicate lattice over its old band. Talvash del Kissel fled Gnomeregan after the trogg invasion and radiation brought the city down. Now the gnome refugee lives in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. The jeweler and tinkerer is short on coin and out of stock, but determined to prove his skills remain sharp in exile. Talvash is glad to see his simple ring design again, cleaned by the Sparklematic 5200. Yet he considers the old band dated. He offers to improve it with silver and moss agate lattice work, showing his skill with metal and gemstones.

quest:2950.text: Nogg's Ring Redo. In Orgrimmar, Nogg works to improve a ring recovered from Gnomeregan. He asks for rare materials and information about Dark Iron dwarves, eager to prove goblin craft superior to gnomish design. You bring a cleaned gold ring from Gnomeregan to Nogg's workshop in the Valley of Honor. The goblin engineer takes one look at its modest gnomish craft and offers a bargain. Bring raw materials and a modest fee, and he will add an intricate lattice of silver and moss agate to the band, meant to amplify the magic within it.

quest:298.text: Excavation Progress Report. At Ironband's Excavation Site, Prospector Ironband needs you to carry his dispatches and powder orders to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar. Ironband's dispatches tell of his dig and renew its supply requests. The work needs picks, workers, and blasting powder to break through bedrock. Ironband relies on runners to keep Jern Hornhelm informed.

quest:2997.text: Tome of Divinity. Azar Stronghammer sends promising dwarven paladins from Dun Morogh to Ironforge for deeper instruction. There, Tiza Battleforge awaits in the Hall of Mysteries, where the trials begin in service to the Holy Light. Dwarven initiates guard Dun Morogh's snowbound villages and roads. When Azar sees that a defender is ready for deeper spiritual instruction, he sends that candidate from field duties to Ironforge. There, the city's holy elders can guide them. The summons takes you through the Mystic Ward to the Hall of Mysteries. Sacred relics and solemn study fill its halls. Tiza Battleforge tests your readiness for self-sacrifice, mercy, and the moral duties of your calling.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. A summons now calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Brother Wilhelm sends for them, and the Tome of Divinity begins the sacred trials that teach mastery of resurrection through the Holy Light. In Elwynn Forest, novice paladins spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows discipline in battle and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. The paladin leaders mark promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind. Their report is due at the kingdom's spiritual heart. In Cathedral Square, Stormwind's Cathedral of Light is the kingdom's foremost sanctuary for its priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Duthorian Rall lives there and oversees those sworn to the Order. Beneath its vaulted ceilings, high-ranking paladins set the formal trials of the Tome of Divinity before each initiate. The trials test compassion, fortitude, and willingness to sacrifice.

quest:2999.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, young dwarven paladins are sent to Tiza Battleforge to learn the Holy Light's deeper duties. Their rite of passage reaches beyond martial training and toward sacred vows. You have defended Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls, proving your discipline in battle. Now Brandur Ironhammer, your trainer, sends you upstairs in the Hall of Mysteries. Senior paladins there prepare initiates for the order's spiritual duties. Tiza Battleforge teaches that the Light asks more than swordplay and hammer blows. It asks for compassion, justice, and self-sacrifice. Seeking her begins your formal study of the Tome of Divinity, a sacred path toward the power to resurrect the fallen.

quest:3000.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, dwarf paladins return for deeper training in the Holy Light. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker sends them home, and Tiza Battleforge guides them toward the sacred trials of the Tome of Divinity. Dwarf paladins keep their spiritual and martial roots in Khaz Modan, even when they serve Stormwind or travel through human lands. When Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker judges that a dwarf has gained enough field training, he sends them home. There they learn the duties expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand. In Ironforge, you are directed to the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Mysteries. Tiza Battleforge waits upstairs, where she mentors young dwarven paladins. She prepares them to bear the burden of the Holy Light through sacred trials recorded in the Tome of Divinity.

quest:301.text:
Report to Ironforge. Jern Hornhelm sends Ironband’s report to Prospector Stormpike in Ironforge. The dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies, and the Explorers’ League must attend to it. The Explorers’ League funds and oversees archaeological expeditions across Khaz Modan, and supplies them. Ironband’s dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies. Its overseers cannot simply requisition more nearby.

At the Thelsamar inn, Jern Hornhelm entrusts you with Ironband’s written report. You carry it over the mountain passes to Prospector Stormpike at the League’s headquarters in Ironforge.

quest:302.text: Powder to Ironband. In Ironforge, the Explorer's League sends blasting powder south to Prospector Ironband's dig in Loch Modan. Prospector Stormpike approves the request, and the shipment goes to Thelsamar before continuing to Ironband's Excavation. The Explorer's League sends blasting powder from Ironforge to Prospector Ironband's expedition in southern Loch Modan. When the dig runs short, word reaches the League's leaders. Prospector Stormpike approves the request and sends the runner to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar, the valley's main supply hub.

quest:3065.text: Simple Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a marked parchment sends you to Frang after you prove yourself against local beasts. The warrior trainer waits outside the Den. After you prove you can face the Mottled Boars, Gornek hands you a parchment marked specifically for you. Durotar is harsh, and the Horde quickly gives its fighters guidance. The parchment directs you to Frang, the veteran warrior trainer outside the Den. Frang shelters in the shade outside the Den and watches recruits arrive from the red scrubland. With a seasoned eye, he judges each new arrival before teaching the fundamentals, whether with a heavy axe or a spear. He prepares each recruit to defend the young Horde's fragile settlements.

quest:307.text: Filthy Paws. In Silver Stream Mine, Filthy Paws supplies wait in danger. The Miners' League stored its equipment there after the ore ran dry, but kobolds now fill the tunnels. Mountaineer Stormpike wants the tools recovered before his warriors attack. Silver Stream Mine lies in northern Loch Modan, east of Algaz Station. Its silver ran out long ago, so the dwarven Miners' League turned the empty shafts into a depot for spare excavation gear, picks, and staging materials. Across Khaz Modan, sturdy tunnels make good storehouses, provided they stay guarded and locked against the wilderness. As dwarven watchfulness across Loch Modan has thinned, kobolds have slipped into the mine. Dark shafts and gleaming iron tools drew the scavengers, and soon the depot became their warren. Mountaineer Stormpike is ready to lead warriors inside and drive them out, but their heavy boots and sweeping blows could smash the crates. You can slip or fight your way in to recover the League's supplies before the assault begins.

quest:308.text: Distracting Jarven. At Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Jarven Thunderbrew watches the cellar stores. His family forbids him to drink from the barrels while on duty, so he asks you to bring him Thunder Ale from upstairs. He hopes a mug will sharpen his wits. Jarven watches the deep stores, with Dun Morogh’s finest stout all around him. His family forbids him to drink from the stock while he is on guard. Yet temptation gets the better of him, and he asks you to fetch a pint of potent Thunder Ale from the taps upstairs. Jarven says a good drink will sharpen his senses and strengthen his watch. Whether a guard ought to drink on duty is another matter. Still, few hardy dwarves can fault a Thunderbrew for wanting a taste of the ale his own kin make.

quest:3082.text: Etched Tablet. Gornek sends a carved tablet to hunters in the Valley of Trials. It bears Jen'shan's mark and calls them to begin training in the wilderness. Gornek brings novice hunters a carved tablet after they prove themselves against the boars near the Den. The stone bears Jen'shan's mark. She is a skilled troll huntswoman stationed nearby, and the message shows that seasoned hunters have noticed the young recruit's grit. The lesson now moves beyond surviving the local dangers and toward disciplined training in the wild. Jen'shan teaches that orcs and trolls have a long history within the Horde. Orcs brought renowned traditions of warriors and shamans, while the Darkspear trolls carried ancient skills in stalking, tracking, and survival. Those skills helped the orcs endure life on Azeroth. As Jen'shan trains new hunters, the two peoples continue to share what they know, bound by respect for the hunt.

quest:3083.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives a coded summons to aspiring rogues. It sends them to Rwag in the Den, where rogue instruction meets the Shattered Hand. Gornek gives an Encrypted Tablet to each initiate who proves their mettle against the local wildlife. Its message is written in cipher, a fitting test and precaution for those trained in stealth, poison, and subterfuge. The summons directs the recruit into the Den to meet Rwag, who trains the Horde’s rogues, thieves, and cutpurses. Inside the Den, initiates find Rwag, an agent aligned with the Shattered Hand. He tells new rogues the guild will not dictate their every breath, but the Hand holds him accountable if an apprentice fails to perform. The fledgling Horde is surrounded by foes and relies heavily on silent scouts and agile cutpurses to gather intelligence and eliminate threats from the shadows.

quest:3084.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, new shamans receive a summons from Shikrik. It calls promising initiates to formal training in the spirits and the elements: earth, fire, water, and air. Gornek gives fledgling shamans a carved stone tablet after they prove their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials. Its runes carry an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer. The summons tells each initiate they are ready to look beyond physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world. Shamanism holds a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. Shikrik teaches that shamans draw power from the four elements and strength from ancestral spirits. They follow Warchief Thrall's example as spiritual guides and sources of wisdom for their communities. Across Durotar, they protect the settlements taking root.

quest:3085.text: Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a message from Ken'jai reaches young priests after their first test. The tablet calls them to learn how Darkspear priests commune with the spirits. After you prove yourself against the boars under Gornek's watch, he gives you an inscribed stone called the Hallowed Tablet. Its message bears Ken'jai's mark. The Darkspear mystic waits outside the Den, where he watches over newcomers drawn to faith and spiritual magic. Darkspear priests among the Horde seek communion with spirits and loa, unlike human and dwarven priests who follow the Holy Light across the sea. Ken'jai welcomes you to Durotar and teaches that your power grows through spiritual discipline. He will instruct you in greater rites as your bond with the spirits matures.

quest:3086.text: Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a Glyphic Tablet sends young Horde mages to Mai'ah. Gornek passes it to them after they prove their strength, and the troll trainer waits outside the Den. You have proved your strength against the Valley of Trials' wildlife, and Gornek gives you an inscribed tablet. Mai'ah, the valley's mage trainer, sent it. She asks you to find her by the Den's entrance when you are ready to begin your arcane studies. Mai'ah speaks plainly about the power mages wield and the danger that comes with it. She warns that their greatest threat is magic's unseen pull toward corruption, not rival warriors or enemy races. Humility and patience matter, she says, because unchecked sorcery can make a mage believe they have mastered more than they have.

quest:3087.text: Etched Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Etched Parchment calls a young hunter to Jen'shan. Gornek delivers it after the initiate's first blooding, opening the way to wilderness training in Durotar. After proving themselves against mottled boars, hunters in the Valley of Trials receive an etched parchment from Gornek. Jen'shan, a skilled Darkspear hunter, sent the note after watching new arrivals from the edges of the encampment. It welcomes the initiate to formal training and recognizes the instincts needed to master Durotar's untamed beasts and harsh land. Reporting to Jen'shan marks the move from recruit to dedicated stalker. She warns that hunting is no easier than the arcane arts or ancestral shamanism. Mastering Durotar's predators, maintaining ranged weapons, and surviving on unforgiving land all demand discipline. Jen'shan sends her apprentices to aid the valley's other inhabitants and test their abilities before returning to learn more advanced survival techniques.

quest:3088.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment sends proven novice orc rogues into the Den. Its cipher points them to Rwag, an agent of the Shattered Hand. Gornek passes the coded parchment to novice orcs who have proved themselves against the local wildlife. Other trainers recruit pupils openly in the clearing, but rogue instructor Rwag sends his summons by cipher. The message directs you beyond the sunlit camp and deep into the cavern called the Den. Inside the Den, you find Rwag keeping watch among the rock. Warlocks lurk deeper in the cave, and he tells you he watches recruits for the Shattered Hand. While orcish society prizes open honor and glory in battle, the Shattered Hand works as the Horde's hidden network of spies, cutthroats, and gatherers of intelligence.

quest:3089.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. At the Valley of Trials, a rune-marked summons calls new shamans to Shikrik. Gornek delivers the parchment, which begins their formal training in communion with spirits and elements. After proving their survival skills against local wildlife, new orc shamans receive a rune-inscribed parchment from Gornek, overseer of the Valley of Trials. Its mystical writing comes from Shikrik, the valley's shaman trainer, who asks to meet the newly arrived initiate. Meeting Shikrik begins a shaman's sacred duty to the Horde. She teaches that shamans serve as conduits for ancestral spirits and wielders of elemental wrath. Under her guidance, new shamans learn to channel spiritual energies, mend wounds, and call upon Kalimdor's natural forces.

quest:309.text: Protecting the Shipment. In southern Loch Modan, Miran carries blasting powder toward Ironband's Excavation Site. Prospector Ironband needs it for his dig, but failed supply lines and threats to the courier wagons have left Miran stranded. Prospector Ironband needs blasting powder to cut through stone at his dig. Miran is stranded on the road under threat, carrying a heavy load. You guide him along the uneven roads to the excavation site so the powder can reach the dig.

quest:3092.text: Etched Note. At Camp Narache, a summons calls a young tauren hunter to train with Lanka Farshot. The message marks the start of study in the ways of the wild. Grull Hawkwind passes the etched message to a young tauren with a gift for marksmanship and tracking. The novice has been training among the bluffs of Red Cloud Mesa. Lanka Farshot has taken notice of the youth's bloodline and raw ability, and calls them to study under his watch. Among the Shu'halo, hunters do more than scout or fight. They feed the tribes with their quarry, guard nomadic camps, and keep close to the beasts of Kalimdor. Lanka's training begins with weapons and the creatures of Mulgore. In time, the novice may learn the ancient art of taming wild companions.

quest:3094.text: Verdant Note. At Camp Narache, a summons calls promising young tauren to seek Gart Mistrunner. Grull Hawkwind delivers the message on Gart's behalf. On the Red Cloud Mesa, Grull Hawkwind gives young tauren a message from a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner. The summons calls those showing natural gifts to take up their responsibilities. It invites them to enter the ancient practice of tauren druidism and turn from simple village errands toward the balance of the plains. Gart Mistrunner warns that ancestral and natural spirits have grown restless across Mulgore. Tauren druids act as living avatars of nature, keeping harmony with the Earthmother's will despite distant rivalries. Night elves practice druidic arts too, but Gart says their pride blinds them to the tauren's deep bond with the natural realm.

quest:3096.text: Encrypted Scroll. At Deathknell, a sealed message sends a newly awakened Forsaken rogue to David Trias. Shadow Priest Sarvis passes it on once the recruit has proved ready. Newly raised Forsaken fight mindless zombies in the cemetery as Deathknell's leaders watch for those drawn to stealth and subterfuge. Once you have proved your readiness, Shadow Priest Sarvis gives promising scouts a sealed parchment. David Trias's discreet seal marks it as an early link to the covert network beneath Forsaken leadership. David Trias watches Deathknell's crossroads and inn for prospects in future covert operations. The Forsaken need disciplined agents, not common thieves or reckless cutpurses, to serve their fledgling kingdom. Trias says capable rogues may draw the notice of the Shadowstalkers, a Forsaken cadre that prizes cunning, precision, and absolute loyalty to the Dark Lady.

quest:3097.text: Hallowed Scroll. In Deathknell, the Hallowed Scroll calls newly risen Forsaken priests to the chapel. Shadow Priest Sarvis gives the summons, sending each novice to Dark Cleric Duesten to learn how the Forsaken wield faith after death. Newly awakened undead stagger from Deathknell’s graves, their minds reeling from plague, death, and freedom from the Lich King's grip. For those who followed the Holy Light in life, death leaves deep confusion. As fledgling undead fight the mindless Scourge at the settlement’s edge, Shadow Priest Sarvis receives messages. A summons marked by Dark Cleric Duesten calls newly risen priests away from their wandering and into the desecrated town chapel. At the chapel, Dark Cleric Duesten teaches a harsh faith. He says the Holy Light abandoned the Forsaken in death, ancestral spirits are hollow tales, and demons have no care for their plight. Forsaken clergy teach that willpower and self-reliance are their only sources of salvation. Under Duesten’s guidance, newly risen priests learn to wield divine discipline and shadow through conviction in their own survival, not devotion to distant gods.

quest:3098.text: Glyphic Scroll. In Deathknell, Isabella summons newly awakened Forsaken mages to her in the ruined church. Her sealed scroll calls them to hone their volatile arcane powers. Isabella calls newly awakened Forsaken mages to the ruined church in Deathknell. After you show an affinity for arcane magic while fighting the mindless Scourge nearby, the scroll bearing her arcane sigil bids you to report to her. Isabella trains local mages, and she knows that untrained magic can endanger the Forsaken as much as their enemies. In Deathknell’s ruined chapel, Isabella teaches new Forsaken mages that undeath has not ended the dangers of arcane magic. Their bodies have lost the frailties of life, but magic remains volatile and corrupting. For the Forsaken, mastering the arcane is more than study. It can help them survive, seek vengeance, reclaim their destiny, and destroy those who threaten their fragile return to Lordaeron.

quest:31.text: Aquatic Form. In Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to master the waters. After proving worthy in Moonglade and attuning to the sea lion aspect, the druid comes home for formal recognition and Aquatic Form. Dendrite Starblaze sends the aspiring tauren druid back to Mulgore after the trials in Moonglade. The Pendant of the Sea Lion bears proof of balance and dedication through Kalimdor's waters. Carrying it shows the initiate has honored the ancient traditions needed to take an aquatic aspect. At Thunder Bluff's heights, the traveler presents the pendant to Turak Runetotem, their mentor. Pleased that the initiate has honored their ancestors and kept the balance of nature, Turak teaches the secret of the aquatic form. The druid can then move beneath rivers and oceans, breathe freely, and navigate the depths as a sea creature.

quest:310.text: Bitter Rivals. Marleth Barleybrew asks you to replace a cask of Thunder Ale at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos with her family's brew. The Barleybrews have long begrudged the Thunderbrews the fame of their distillery. Marleth respects its ale, but she cannot abide Dun Morogh knowing only Thunderbrew. She means to change local tastes with her family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder. Beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, aging casks fill a basement storeroom. A guard watches near the Thunderbrews' prized reserve. Draw him away, then secretly switch the barrels.

quest:3103.text: Hallowed Letter. In Northshire, Marshal McBride gives promising young priests a letter from Priestess Anetta. It calls them to begin formal training in the Holy Light at Northshire Abbey, while trouble still shadows the realm. After proving themselves against the kobold camps around Northshire, novice priests receive a letter sealed by Priestess Anetta. Marshal McBride delivers it as an invitation to study the Holy Light in the abbey's quiet halls. When you bring the letter, Priestess Anetta tells you the realm remains troubled. The Burning Legion's lingering threats still shadow Azeroth, and the continents bear fresh wounds and unrest. To Anetta, becoming a priest means more than study. It is a duty to bring healing and comfort to a suffering world.

quest:3104.text: Glyphic Letter. A summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley from Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, the mage trainer at Northshire, wrote it. He watches new recruits arrive at the abbey, looking for magical discipline and talent. Northshire Abbey has long sheltered the Holy Light. Yet Stormwind's dangers call for practitioners of every discipline. The letter brings you upstairs to Khelden Bremen, who offers no easy praise. He warns that mastering arcane power means defying nature's limits. Such power earns profound respect and deep fear from ordinary folk.

quest:3105.text: Tainted Letter. In Northshire, Tainted Letter draws novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards to learn the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle gives it to Marshal McBride, who carries it to her recruits. After proving themselves against the kobolds, novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride. Priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, but warlocks must keep to quieter paths. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter. It directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties. Drusilla warns that Stormwind's guards watch warlocks closely. She calls them 'pathetic mundanes.' Drawing power from the Twisting Nether and communing with demons both risk corruption. So she urges patience, prudence, and firm self-control when handling those dark energies. Caution, she says, must not extinguish a warlock's ambition.

quest:3106.text: Simple Rune. At Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm brings new dwarven warriors a summons from Thran Khorman. The rune calls them from Coldridge Valley's snowy paths to begin training. Veteran scouts watch recruits clear pests around Coldridge Valley, seeking promising fighters. Sten brings an inscribed stone from Thran Khorman. Its simple rune calls them from the snowy paths into Anvilmar's warm forge-hall, where they can pledge themselves to the warrior's trade. Thran speaks plainly about Dun Morogh's troubles. Gnomes displaced by the explosions that destroyed Gnomeregan seek refuge, while some dwarves take up foreign arcane arts or follow the human faith in the Holy Light. Troggs claw at the mountain borders after being disturbed deep underground. Thran believes firm martial discipline is needed to withstand these threats.

quest:3107.text: Consecrated Rune. At Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner calls fledgling dwarven paladins to join the Knights of the Silver Hand. Sten Stoutarm summons them there. Your rune marks the start of a formal induction, where raw potential must meet discipline. Around Coldridge Valley, local leaders watch for those gifted in divine martial prowess. Bromos Grummner awaits inside Anvilmar to guide new initiates. The Knights of the Silver Hand began among the humans of Lordaeron, yet Ironforge dwarves embraced the Holy Light with fierce devotion. Bromos welcomes you into the brotherhood and reminds you that dwarven paladins share the solemn duty of protecting Azeroth. The order is grounded in sacrifice, tradition, and martial virtue, and asks recruits to take up hammer and faith in equal measure.

quest:3108.text: Etched Rune. In Coldridge Valley, novice dwarf hunters receive a carved summons from Sten Stoutarm. It sends them to Thorgas Grimson inside Anvilmar to learn the hunt. As you help Sten Stoutarm face threats around Coldridge Valley, he gives you the Etched Rune. Dwarven mentors favor carved runes for formal messages, not spoken orders or plain parchment. The stone asks you to take stock of your early work, then report indoors at Anvilmar for deeper instruction in the hunt. At Anvilmar, the Etched Rune marks a hunter's entry into formal discipline. Thorgas Grimson teaches that mountaineering and survival in Khaz Modan demand respect for the harsh land. You learn to read tracks in bitter snowdrifts, care for your weapons and ammunition, and understand the wild beasts roaming the crags. The rune marks your first step from a lone wanderer with a gun to an apprentice among Anvilmar's veteran pathfinders.

quest:3109.text: Encrypted Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm gives young rogues a coded rune and calls them into Anvilmar to meet Solm Hargrin. Sten says someone slipped him the etched stone to deliver. He suspects Solm Hargrin sent it. The rune tests whether a novice can keep a confidence, calling them inside without Solm announcing his need for scouts and scoundrels across the courtyard. Inside Anvilmar, Solm Hargrin welcomes the new rogues to their craft. He offers to teach the maneuvers, strikes, and subtle arts that keep them alive and earn them coin. He also reminds dwarf rogues to look after their displaced gnomish allies, still recovering from Gnomeregan's catastrophic fall.

quest:311.text: Return to Marleth. Marleth waits in Brewnall Village for the Thunder Ale you bring from Kharanos. The barrel will prove her Scalder reached the Thunderbrew cellar. The barrel comes from the Thunderbrew cellar, taken under the distillers’ noses. It proves the switch worked and gives Marleth a trophy from her rival. You carry the heavy keg over snowy ridges to Brewnall Village. Marleth delights in outsmarting Kharanos’s guards and cellar masters. Her caper shows how fiercely dwarven families prize their signature recipes.

quest:3110.text: Hallowed Rune. In Coldridge Valley, a young dwarf priest is called to Anvilmar by Sten Stoutarm. He carries Branstock Khalder’s inscribed prayers and guidance to the novice, who is summoned inside to deepen their bond with the Holy Light. A young priest earns Sten Stoutarm’s notice while helping clear threats outside Anvilmar. Branstock Khalder, the settlement’s spiritual guide, gives Sten a rune inscribed with prayers and guidance for the novice. Then the young priest is called inside Anvilmar’s sturdy halls to begin sacred studies. Dwarven life prizes martial strength and heavy plate, yet the Holy Light remains central to Ironforge society. In Coldridge Valley, holy casters stand with warriors and hunters to protect the enclave from trogg incursions and dangerous wildlife moving through the snow.

quest:3112.text: Simple Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, gnome warriors receive a call to Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm carries Thran Khorman’s summons to trained fighters, who are invited to learn the arts of war and prepare to reclaim Gnomeregan. You help Sten Stoutarm drive off troggs and boars in Coldridge Valley. Thran Khorman, a veteran trainer in Anvilmar, sees promise in the refugee recruit. He calls the recruit to the central hall for martial instruction. Dwarven trainers may tease gnome warriors about their size, but Thran Khorman takes their loss seriously. He asks them to imagine how dwarves would feel if Ironforge fell to the Dark Irons. Thran has pledged to help the exiled gnomes. He teaches them the arts of war until they are ready to reclaim their home.

quest:3113.text: Encrypted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm gives new gnome rogues a folded note for Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. As you help the mountaineers face trogg threats, Sten gives you a parchment entrusted to him. It looks like an official memorandum. The note invites you to meet Solm Hargrin, the rogue trainer stationed inside Anvilmar. Gnome survivors share close quarters with their dwarven hosts after Gnomeregan's sudden fall drove them from their underground home. Solm Hargrin knows rogues draw suspicion when items go missing. So he urges them to stand together quietly and help each other survive.

quest:3114.text: Glyphic Memorandum. In Anvilmar, Mountaineer Sten Stoutarm gives you a memorandum from mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, who invites you to meet him. The summons is for you, a novice mage Sten assists in Coldridge Valley. Read it, then go inside Anvilmar to meet the gnome who wrote it. Your spellcraft studies begin there. Inside Anvilmar, gnome mage trainer Marryk Nurribit offers plain advice before your lessons. Keep out of serious trouble and save coin for training and tavern drinks. Stay clear of fallen Gnomeregan and its radioactive danger. Marryk is ready to teach you the arcane arts.

quest:3115.text: Tainted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm quietly sends you to Alamar Grimm in Anvilmar. Grimm urges you to trust dark power over your dwarven hosts. Warlocks face deep suspicion in Coldridge Valley. As you help Sten Stoutarm with local threats, he reluctantly slips you a note. His warning makes plain how little your kind is trusted here, even under the uneasy truce that allows warlocks to practice in Alliance lands. In Anvilmar, Alamar Grimm speaks of the gnomes’ plight. He believes ordinary magic and tinkering failed Gnomeregan, bringing their people near extinction and leaving them as second-class refugees dependent on dwarven goodwill. He urges you to trust neither the Holy Light nor dwarven politics. Instead, summon fiends and master them, for their obedience is unconditional.

quest:3116.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, Alyissia calls young night elf warriors to defend their people. Conservator Ilthalaine carries her summons as the Kaldorei face changes across Teldrassil and beyond. After you prove your basic survival skills against Shadowglen's restless wildlife, Conservator Ilthalaine gives you an inscribed sigil. The token formally marks your move into combat training. It carries a request from Alyissia, the warrior trainer at Aldrassil, asking you to dedicate your strength to defending your people. Alyissia sets your training against a time of rapid change and danger. In only a few years, the night elves have raised the World Tree Teldrassil, seen a taint spread through forest beasts near and far, and reconnected with ancient lands once thought lost, including Feralas. The Kaldorei need capable defenders against these perils. Alyissia prepares young Kaldorei for more than combat. She urges you not to judge outsiders who arrive on Teldrassil by their race. Some travelers may not act from pure generosity, but allies are vital to the Kaldorei's defense. As you take up the work of protecting your people, she asks you to offer them reasonable trust.

quest:3117.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls young night elf hunters to Aldrassil. Through Conservator Ilthalaine, Ayanna Everstride summons them to meet their trainer and begin learning archery and beastcraft. After young kaldorei hunters help defend Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them an inscribed token. A messenger brought it from their mentor, Ayanna Everstride. The sigil directs each novice up into Aldrassil’s high boughs, where the trainers watch over the canopy. Meeting Ayanna begins a hunter’s training on Teldrassil. She teaches novices marksmanship and how to understand Kalimdor’s wild creatures. A hunter must respect their beast companions and meet the world’s unseen dangers with awareness and humility.

quest:3118.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, a coded summons calls new night elf rogues to begin their training. Conservator Ilthalaine carries it for Frahun Shadewhisper, who also warns of the fragile peace across Kalimdor. While young night elves study nature's balance under Conservator Ilthalaine, those drawn to stealth receive a quieter summons. A runner brings the Encrypted Sigil from Frahun Shadewhisper, Shadowglen's rogue mentor. Its ciphers are meant for initiates of the trade. The bearer is to decipher the message and find Frahun near the roots of Aldrassil to begin instruction. Frahun's message also warns of Kalimdor's uncertain peace. The Third War has ended, but the truce between the Alliance and the emerging Horde remains fragile. Rogue scouts and informers in Shadowglen are urged to sharpen their eyes and ears early. They watch for threats and covert provocations that could renew war across the borders.

quest:3119.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, young night elf priests are called to begin their training in Aldrassil. Conservator Ilthalaine passes along Shanda's message as novices learn to wield Elune's grace. Night elf priests serve Elune as handmaidens and servants of the moon goddess. When a young kaldorei in Shadowglen shows devotion and an affinity for the divine light, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them a hallowed sigil. Shanda, the priest trainer, sent the token by messenger as an invitation to come to Aldrassil and begin spiritual training. Shanda tells the young acolyte that unusual change has reached Teldrassil's sheltered sanctuary. Travelers fill the World Tree's boughs, including members of the wider Alliance who have leave to meet with the kaldorei. The wider world calls, but Shanda urges novices to first attend to the troubles facing Shadowglen before turning to conflicts beyond it.

quest:312.text: Tundra MacGrann's Stolen Stash. Tundra MacGrann needs his winter stores back from Old Icebeard. The yeti carried off the thorium-reinforced meat locker, and MacGrann's injured leg keeps him from reaching the cave. For the cold season, MacGrann had salted away a month's worth of dried meat. He sealed it in a thorium-reinforced locker to keep hungry bears out. Old Icebeard carried off the whole chest instead of trying to open it. While MacGrann was away hunting deer, Old Icebeard dragged the chest to a cave in the jagged hills. MacGrann believes the yeti cannot break through solid thorium, but his injured leg keeps him from retrieving the stores. You can face the beast or slip inside while it prowls the snowdrifts.

quest:3120.text: Verdant Sigil. A summons reaches newly awakened night elf druids in Shadowglen. Conservator Ilthalaine passes the Verdant Sigil to fledgling shapeshifters, directing them to Mardant Strongoak within Aldrassil. The token marks the start of their formal training in nature and the Emerald Dream. When a young night elf shows promise in keeping Shadowglen's balance, the order calls for a formal introduction. A runner brings the Verdant Sigil to Conservator Ilthalaine, who entrusts it to the initiate. The token shows that the circle in Aldrassil has taken notice and invites the young druid to begin formal training. Presenting the sigil to Mardant Strongoak inside Aldrassil brings the initiate into the fold. Deeper communion with the Emerald Dream and mastery of animal forms lie ahead. For now, Mardant becomes their first guide, teaching them to read nature's spirits and channel the raw power of the woods.

quest:313.text: The Grizzled Den. At Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, Pilot Stonegear sends you west to hunt wendigos in the Grizzled Den. Their thick pelts will warm his siege engine, Trollplow. Stonegear tests newcomers before he trusts them with the work. A massive siege tank is hard to operate in freezing mountain air. It takes nerves of iron and a steady constitution. Face the native beasts in the frozen hills to prove you have both. Dun Morogh's bitter cold bites through Trollplow's cramped, iron-plated cabin. Stonegear wants thick wendigo manes for a warm, durable rug on the engine's deck. The hunt also helps keep the local beasts in check.

quest:314.text: Protecting the Herd. At Amberstill Ranch, Rudra Amberstill fears Vagash will take more prized mountain rams. He asks passing fighters to protect the herd and bring proof of the predator’s death. Vagash has taken two prized mountain rams from Amberstill Ranch. The ranch supplies the Bronzebeard dwarves with riding and working beasts, and the herd supports Dun Morogh’s rustic economy. Vagash hunts local livestock in the crags above the ranch. Ironforge’s forces are spread thin across the realm, supporting the Alliance on distant frontiers. With no military patrol on the ridgelines, Rudra Amberstill asks independent fighters to hunt Vagash. He wants one of the beast’s deadly fangs as proof.

quest:315.text: The Perfect Stout. In Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew still pursues The Perfect Stout. He draws on family brewing tradition and exotic local ingredients, and now seeks shimmerweed, a pungent plant cultivated only by the hostile Frostmane trolls atop Shimmer Ridge. He sends daring travelers into their encampment to take the herb from tribal baskets. Brewing is a way of life in Brewnall Village, especially for the Barleybrew family. Rejold Barleybrew believes greatness runs in his blood, but the perfect stout calls for new ideas. He looks beyond hops, malt and mountain spring water to Dun Morogh's untamed plants, hoping they will give his ale an unmistakable bite. East of Brewnall Village, the Frostmane trolls cultivate shimmerweed on Shimmer Ridge. They gather it for tribal and mystic rituals, while dwarves know it for its sharp, distinct flavor. The herb is kept in baskets in the troll village, where Rejold's latest and boldest brewing experiment awaits it.

quest:317.text: Stocking Jetsteam. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz prepares Jetsteam for a long deployment with the Ironforge Siege Brigade. Its crew needs boar meat and bear pelts for the journey. Master engineer Beldin Steelgrill tunes the siege tank at Steelgrill's Depot, just outside Kharanos. Jetsteam is being readied for an operation on behalf of the Siege Brigade. The crew needs a month's provisions to endure Dun Morogh's sub-zero temperatures. Beldin Steelgrill works beneath Jetsteam's hood, so Bellowfiz cannot leave the vehicle to gather food and insulation. The snowy plains south of the Grizzled Den hold boars for meat and bears whose pelts can line the tank's bedding and keep it warm.

quest:318.text: Evershine. At Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, Pilot Bellowfiz needs Evershine from Rejold Barleybrew in Brewnall Village. The strong brew warms him and can fuel his siege engine, Jetsteam. Rejold Barleybrew's brewing experiments go beyond ordinary dwarven ales. Evershine can knock all but the hardiest dwarves flat, yet its heat is prized in Dun Morogh's bitter cold. At Steelgrill's Depot outside Kharanos, Pilot Bellowfiz takes a warming sip of Evershine against the freezing winds. The volatile brew can also feed Jetsteam's furnace. When Bellowfiz is in a tight spot, it gives his siege engine an explosive burst of emergency power.

quest:319.text: A Favor for Evershine. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz needs Evershine for his siege engine, Jetsteam. Rejold Barleybrew will give up a cask only after you drive the predators away from Brewnall Village. Rejold offers his brew if you thin the wild beasts of western Dun Morogh. Ice Claw Bears, Elder Crag Boars, and Snow Leopards roam near Brewnall Village. Their presence endangers the locals and keeps Rejold from freely giving up the cask. Rejold says no self-respecting dwarf cowers before wild animals. Yet watching for predators around the village takes the craftsmen valuable hours. Once the beasts are driven off, villagers can focus on distilling and smithing without keeping watch on the tree line.

quest:3221.text: Speak with Renferrel. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel needs to discuss the tainted wolf hearts. High Executor Hadrec sends you back to the Royal Apothecary Society researcher with your findings. After you help the Deathstalkers across Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec gives you an urgent message from Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel has studied the discolored wolf hearts gathered from local wildlife and needs you at once. Apothecary Renferrel works for the Royal Apothecary Society in a laboratory inside the Sepulcher crypt. He studies how dark magic and disease are changing Silverpine's beasts, bringing alchemical research together with military reports from the front.

quest:3261.text: Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, seasoned Horde hunters seek guidance from Jorn Skyseer. After you hunt local raptors for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker offers deeper lessons. You have hunted the cunning sunscale and scytheclaw raptors stalking the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows martial skill must be joined with understanding of the land's great beasts. With her mentorship complete, she sends you south. Follow the Gold Road south through increasingly rugged plains to Camp Taurajo, a vital tauren settlement near the southern wilds. Jorn Skyseer waits there, an elder tracker ready to teach hunters how to pursue elusive, legendary quarry across the Barrens.

quest:3281.text: Stolen Silver. Gazrog at the Crossroads sends you after payroll silver stolen by raptors. Rumors of their cunning lead you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back. Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and the raptors have taken their wages. You are sent to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. When raptors ambushed the payroll shipment, Gazrog first sought vengeance. But killing the pack would not restore the missing money. The Horde must learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin, and where they took them. Scouts found a raptor nest between two craggy peaks, south of Ratchet and northwest of Northwatch Hold. The creatures dragged the intact lockbox into their territory, where they guard it alongside eggs and fresh kills. Tales of raptor cunning and hoarding now seem true to Gazrog. Ordinary beasts rarely stash metallic valuables.

quest:33.text: Wolves Across the Border. In Northshire Valley, Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where daily needs remain even as guards focus on Defias bandits. Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls, angry at the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have little strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits. Tradesfolk still have daily needs, so Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking. Wolves roam closer to Northshire Abbey as patrols weaken. The Kingdom of Stormwind has too few troops and lacks leadership. Young wolves and timber wolves prowl the abbey’s paths and orchards. Hunting them supplies Eagan’s pantry and makes nearby trails safer for novitiates, laborers, and newly arrived defenders.

quest:3301.text: Mura Runetotem. You carry a snapjaw shell from the Barrens across the sea to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine Forest. Its strange vitality may help the tauren healer aid the Forsaken. Tonga Runetotem notices something peculiar about altered snapjaws while investigating the magically changed wildlife around the Barrens oases. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. He asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, who is stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms. Mura Runetotem is at the Sepulcher, a Forsaken outpost in Silverpine Forest. She made the arduous journey there to help the Horde's newest allies cleanse and renew their ailing, blighted woodland. Mura hopes the shell's inner glow and enduring spark of life will reveal ways to restore vitality to the northern continent.

quest:332.text: Wine Shop Advert. Renato Gallina draws passersby to his family's wine shop in Stormwind. He offers a voucher for a free bottle of vintage wine at their canal-side storefront, a small sign of trade in the rebuilt capital. In Stormwind's Trade District, commerce fills the cobbled streets. Renato Gallina walks among them, promoting Gallina Winery, the small shop he runs with his sister, Suzetta. He hands flyers to thirsty travelers and locals. Each offers a free tasting. The Gallina family offers a bottle of their famous pinot noir. Follow the ticket to the winery entrance near the canals, where Suzetta Gallina hands over the bottle. The family hopes a taste of their signature wine will bring newcomers back.

quest:333.text: Harlan Needs a Resupply. In Stormwind, merchant Harlan Bagley cannot keep sturdy clothes and armor in stock. Demand surges, so he sends an urgent cloth order to Rema Schneider at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, unaware of the conflicts brewing beyond the city walls. Across Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley's shelves empty fast. Citizens and wandering adventurers buy reinforced tunics, traveling clothes, and battle-ready armor. Harlan wonders if they are preparing for a harsh season or winter. The rush leaves his shop short of finished cloth. Harlan sends a runner across the city's waterways to Rema Schneider, a seamstress at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is glad of his trade, yet the sudden demand for protective clothing troubles her. Rumors of tension spread through the kingdom. Rema wonders whether the House of Nobles is hiding talk of open war from ordinary people.

quest:334.text: Package for Thurman. Rema Schneider needs help getting her son’s shears and needles to Larson Clothiers in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter. Thurman is apprenticing there and may fall behind without them. Thurman hurried out of home without his tools. Rema fears he will fall behind at his apprenticeship, so she asks you to carry the shears and needles across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

quest:3361.text: A Refugee's Quandary. Gnomeregan's displaced gnomes flee into Dun Morogh after troggs and radiation drive them from their home. Near Anvilmar, engineer Felix Whindlebolt has lost his tools and belongings to Frostmane scavengers. Troggs overran Gnomeregan, the high-tech city beneath the earth. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his advisors released radioactive gas to kill the invaders. The gas brought disaster instead. Thousands of innocents died, survivors became mindless leper gnomes, and the rest fled across Dun Morogh. Gnome engineers and tinkerers carried away the tools and blueprints they could save. Frostmane trolls prowl the icy mountain passes between Gnomeregan and Coldridge Valley. As Felix Whindlebolt hurried toward shelter at Anvilmar, Frostmane raiders took his tool chest, lockbox, and bucket of bolts. They carried his belongings to camps southwest of town.

quest:3364.text: Scalding Mornbrew Delivery. Nori Pridedrift sends you across Coldridge Valley with hot mornbrew for Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar. The mountain cold can steal its heat before it arrives. After you deliver to Grelin Whitebeard, Nori has another cup to send. He cannot carry it himself before the mornbrew freezes into slush. So he asks you to brave the snow and keep his customer from waiting. Durnan Furcutter waits inside Anvilmar's warm mountain hall and is particular about his refreshments. He will not take chilled mornbrew. A hot cup gives the weary dwarf a needed break from his duties. Nori expects his favorite mug back in one piece.

quest:3365.text: Bring Back the Mug. Durnan Furcutter sends you back across Coldridge Valley with Nori Pridedrift's empty mug. Its return closes the Mornbrew delivery. After warming himself with the Mornbrew, Durnan leaves the tankard in your care. Cold bites hard in Dun Morogh, where hospitality depends on mutual respect. Good dishware should make it back too. Nori Pridedrift values sturdy drinkware. Mugs do not grow on trees, especially among the subzero crags of the dwarven homeland. Bring his mug back in one piece, and you show the local community that you can be trusted.

quest:3376.text: Break Sharptusk!. Brave Windfeather sends you east from Red Cloud Mesa to face the raids on Mulgore. Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the Bristleback quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine, and his death could strike a hard blow against their attacks. Red Cloud Mesa is home to young tauren learning the hunt and the ways of the Earth Mother. East of the mesa, Brambleblade Ravine lies in the hands of the Bristleback quilboar. They see the tauren as invaders taking sacred ground, and their skirmishes threaten the tribes trying to make a stable home in Mulgore. The Bristleback attacks on Red Cloud Mesa follow the command of Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle. Deep in Brambleblade Ravine, he directs his warriors and geomancers against the Shu'halo from a fortified makeshift village. Brave Windfeather knows the raids will continue while Sharptusk lives. She sends you into the ravine to kill him and bring back his severed head as proof. Brave Windfeather teaches that hunting an enemy who can hunt back tests more than skill. For young tauren and their allies, the hunt for Sharptusk demands courage, awareness, and discipline. His death brings justice for fallen kin and marks a hunter's readiness to travel across Mulgore's wider plains.

quest:35.text: Further Concerns. East of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan sends you to check reports of danger. You cross Elwynn Forest to speak with Guard Thomas at the river crossing toward Redridge. Marshal Dughan commands Goldshire's garrison and takes reports of hostile creatures along Elwynn's riverbanks seriously. Bandits and vermin already trouble the forest's center, so he cannot spare guards from town. He sends you east to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry at the bridge toward Redridge. Guard Thomas has held the bridge outpost for more than a week and has seen the danger for himself. Hostile, semi-intelligent murlocs have made camps along eastern Elwynn's waterways. Stormwind's army is absent, and local garrisons guard town walls and supply lines. Rural bridge posts like Thomas's are left isolated as the danger grows.

quest:3519.text: A Friend in Need. Iverron lies bitten and in danger in Shadowglen. The young night elf calls for Dirania Silvershine, whose help may save him from Githyiss the Vile's venom. Iverron lies weakened after a bite from Githyiss the Vile. He ignored warnings and went too near the webwood caverns, where the vicious spider struck. Dizziness and failing strength leave him unable to reach safety alone. Iverron sends passersby toward Aldrassil's central tree to find Dirania Silvershine. She looks out for him and knows the dangers of Shadowglen. His life may depend on her preparing an antidote before the venom proves fatal.

quest:3521.text: Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron's Antidote must be brewed before a scout's poison takes hold. Dirania Silvershine needs wild mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor to make the remedy. Young Iverron was scouting the boughs of Shadowglen when Webwood spiders struck him with their poisonous fangs. Now collapsed and dying, he depends on Dirania Silvershine's herbal knowledge at Aldrassil. His venom spreads fast, so she must prepare a remedy before it takes hold. Dirania balances Teldrassil's restorative plants against the spiders' venom. Hyacinth mushrooms, which thieving grell favor in the south, make an earthy base. Moonpetal lilies from tranquil forest pools bring purifying qualities. She also needs Webwood ichor from spiders near Shadowthread Cave, to tailor the cure to their poison.

quest:3522.text: Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron waits for medicine before its strength fades. Poisoned by Webwood spiders, the night elf scout depends on Dirania Silvershine's brew, which must reach him within five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the cure from fresh venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi. The unstable mixture keeps its strength for only five minutes after it is distilled. Whoever carries the vial must sprint straight from the glade toward the northern heights without hesitation. Webwood spiders around Shadowglen's barrows and caves have poisoned Iverron. He admits he has a habit of stumbling into danger and often depends on Dirania's herbal skill to save him. Even after drinking the antidote, his recovery is fragile. The hostile spiders still guard his way home, and he remains wary of them.

quest:3524.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore, Washed Ashore begins an inquiry into the many sea creatures dying on its shore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde starts it in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where priestesses fear the strandings may be an ill omen. Darkshore has seen great sea creatures beach themselves from time to time, a tragic but occasional sight. Now the strandings come in growing numbers along the coast. The Priestesses of Elune in the Temple of the Moon see more than a natural oddity in these deaths. They fear the pattern may bring ill omens to northern Kalimdor. The Temple of the Moon sends scholar Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to the port town of Auberdine to learn why the great beasts are coming ashore. She gathers biological samples to send by hippogryph to Darnassus for close examination. But Greymist murlocs swarm the carcasses in the surf, scavenging the remains and keeping researchers from the bones without armed protection.

quest:353.text: Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. From Stormwind's Dwarven District, the road reaches an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. In Ironforge, the Stormpike clan is respected for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore entrusts travelers with carrying the weapon north, across the distance from Stormwind to the dwarven borderlands. At Loch Modan's northern guard tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches over lands troubled by wandering troggs and burrowing kobolds. Rumors of unrest and banditry reach the southern human kingdoms, while the dwarven frontier has dangers of its own. Stormpike needs a new blade to help keep the mountain passes secure.

quest:354.text: Deaths in the Family. Coleman Farthing, once a mill worker, seeks vengeance from Brill against the Agamand family. During the Third War, he stayed to defend their estate with his fellow workers, and they died beside their stubborn masters. The Agamands rose again as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential farming family. Their mills and fertile pastures yielded grain through the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crossed Lordaeron, the family refused to flee or abandon its ancestral lands. They believed their stone walls and loyal workers could hold back the horrors advancing from the east. Coleman Farthing and the other workers trusted their lords' assurances and stayed to defend the estate. The Scourge overwhelmed them. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered, then raised into undeath where they fell. Farthing eventually broke free through Sylvanas Windrunner's liberation. The Agamand patriarchs and heirs remained under the Lich King's mental grip, wandering the ruined mills as mindless Scourge sentries. Coleman Farthing now lives in Brill, still bitter toward the masters whose pride cost him his mortal life. Seeking vengeance and closure, he sends Forsaken champions to Agamand Mills to destroy Gregor, Nissa, and Thurman Agamand. He hopes his former masters kept enough awareness behind their rotting faces to feel terror as their unlife came to an end.

quest:355.text: Speak with Sevren. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren calls you north after Coleman Farthing's reckoning at Agamand Mills. The undead there threaten the settlement's northern border. Coleman Farthing wanted revenge on his former neighbors, the Agamands, and sent travelers north to kill the undead around their flour mills. After you delivered the remains, Coleman saw that his private grudge touched a wider danger. The Agamand estate still crawls with aggressive Scourge minions, close to Brill. Magistrate Sevren oversees Brill's civic and military security for the Dark Lady. Reports say you survived deep incursions into the haunted farmlands, and Sevren now directs you toward the source of the infestation: the ancient Agamand family crypt.

quest:356.text: Rear Guard Patrol. At the Bulwark, Deathguard Linnea sends you to guard Tirisfal's eastern flank. Scourge horrors and lingering spirits haunt Balnir Farmstead, where they threaten the road and the supply lines that keep the front supplied. The Bulwark holds back the pestilence and armies of the Western Plaguelands from Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Linnea oversees security behind the frontier. The defenders cannot spare troops to guard against attacks from the rear. Any undead that slip past the choke point must be destroyed before they can cut the supply lines feeding the front. Balnir Farmstead was once a working farm in eastern Tirisfal, but it fell to ruin during the Third War. Blight covers its fields, and its crumbling stables shelter Bleeding Horrors and restless Wandering Spirits. Clearing the farmstead denies the Lich King a place to gather forces inside Tirisfal and keeps the road open for Horde reinforcements.

quest:357.text: The Lich's Identity. Bethor Iceshard seeks to learn who lives alone on Brightwater Lake. He sends an emissary to steal the recluse's spellbook and judge his power and allegiance. A lone lich lives in exile on a small island in Brightwater Lake, north of the Undercity. He has free will, unlike the Lich King's mindless pawns, but paranoia rules his life. He believes any undead who approach are Scourge thralls sent to drag him back into servitude. So he unleashes summoned minions on anyone who sets foot on his shore. Word of the rogue lich reaches Bethor Iceshard, the archmage who oversees the Undercity's mages. Bethor knows Lady Sylvanas Windrunner seeks every scrap of magical mastery and every capable will to strengthen the Forsaken against their many foes. To judge whether the hermit can be recruited, Bethor needs proof of his identity and necromantic skill.

quest:358.text: Graverobbers. At the Mass Grave southwest of Garren's Haunt, Rot Hide gnolls dig up the dead. Magistrate Sevren sends you to stop them and recover their embalming ichor for the Royal Apothecary Society's research. The Plague of Undeath overwhelmed Tirisfal Glades, and the dead outnumbered those who could bury them. Immense mass graves were dug across the north to hold the countless victims. For a time, the buried escaped resurrection. Now the Scourge sends Rot Hide gnolls to the trenches southwest of Garren's Haunt. They exhume the decayed remains to swell the Lich King's armies. Embalming ichor preserves and animates the Rot Hides' rotting frames. Magistrate Sevren sends you to slay the graverobbers and recover the fluid. This stops the Scourge from harvesting bodies and gives Brill's apothecaries valuable specimens. They hope to turn the Lich King's own alchemy against him.

quest:36.text: Westfall Stew. Westfall homesteaders are driven from their farms by banditry. As the Furlbrows prepare to leave, Verna entrusts her cherished recipe to Salma Saldean. Defias thieves and wild mechanical harvest reapers have driven Verna and Farmer Furlbrow from their family acreage. They pack their wagon and prepare to seek refuge behind Stormwind's walls. Before they go, Verna gives her neighbor Salma Saldean the recipe for Westfall Stew. She hopes the farm's home-cooked tradition will live on. Salma Saldean and her husband, Farmer Saldean, still hold their homestead just down the road. Verna's recipe keeps a local farm tradition alive as another family leaves. Salma sets out to gather ingredients to feed those still struggling on the frontier.

quest:360.text: Return to the Magistrate. At Brill, Magistrate Sevren receives a warning from the eastern frontier. Deathguard Linnea sends word that the Lich King's mindless servants still test the Forsaken borders. East of Tirisfal Glades, the road reaches the blighted ruins of the Western Plaguelands, where the Scourge holds sway. The Forsaken built the Bulwark to keep the undead from entering their homeland. Deathguard Linnea watches from a waystation behind the line, gathering reports from the eastern gate. She sends messengers west along the King's Road to Brill before enemy infiltrators can exploit gaps in the defenses. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren hears that Scourge scouts are finding paths around or through the frontline. Each creeping ghoul and mindless skeleton recalls the Forsaken's enslavement, broken when Lordaeron fell. Sevren vows that no matter how ceaseless the Lich King's assault, the free undead will not surrender their new autonomy.

quest:361.text: A Letter Undelivered. A faded, bloodstained letter to Yvette Farthing lies among the skeletal ruins of Agamand Mills. It recalls two lovers parted as the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, and what the Forsaken left behind when they traded life for undeath. Thurman Agamand, eldest son of patriarch Gregor Agamand, wrote the message that never reached Yvette Farthing. When the Plague of Undeath consumed Tirisfal Glades, Thurman refused to leave his ancestral home or his kin. As the Scourge struck, he took up his quill to write to Yvette, whom he had loved before the kingdom turned to ash.

quest:362.text: The Haunted Mills. Coleman Farthing of Brill seeks vengeance on the Agamands, his former landowners. He sends you north to Agamand Mills to destroy their restless remains, beginning with Devlin, the family’s sharp-tongued younger son. Farthing’s hatred reaches back to the family’s failure to protect Tirisfal’s common folk from the Plague. Before the Third War, Agamand Mills fed northern Tirisfal under the rule of a wealthy landed family. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, common folk turned to the nobles for safety and found no shelter. Coleman Farthing survived as undead, but hatred for the family he served still consumes him. He wants their bones gathered, not to end their torment, but to desecrate them beneath his heel. Devlin Agamand was Thurman Agamand’s younger brother. People remembered Devlin as weak, spiteful, and sharp-tongued, unlike his gentle elder brother. When the Plague of Undeath reached the mill estate, Devlin quickly fell to its corruption. Now his mindless corpse chatters without cease along the northern road into the family mills.

quest:363.text: Rude Awakening. Newly awakened Forsaken leave Deathknell's crypts to face an unfamiliar life. Freed from the Lich King's grip, you are sent down the hill, away from the incinerators, to learn what comes next from Shadow Priest Sarvis. In Deathknell's damp, subterranean crypt, the chill greets you as you open your eyes to undeath. Undertaker Mordo watches over the newly buried, sorting those who regain free will from those bound for the burning pits. Many rise to find rot, cold stone, and confusion. By chance, they have slipped the Scourge's grasp. Before reaching the chapel, you must face a grim truth: you were once a mindless tool of the Lich King. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner broke that psychic enslavement, freeing remnants of your former humanity to reclaim independent thought. Leaving the tomb and heading down into Deathknell begins your life in a world where both the living and the Scourge see you as an abomination to be destroyed.

quest:364.text: The Mindless Ones. Newly risen Forsaken face the Mindless Ones on Deathknell's northern edge. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends them to cull Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies, Scourge thralls bound to the Lich King's command. Many who rise from Lordaeron's dirt never recover their minds. The Forsaken broke free of Ner'zhul's domination as his power waned, but countless corpses remain chained to his will. In northern Deathknell, Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies wander, driven to violence. For you, newly risen among the undead, putting them down is the first hard trial.
