You prove your freedom by ending the thrall of those who never escaped. Shadow Priest Sarvis grieves that these legions of dead cannot strengthen the Forsaken's desperate struggle. There is no cure for them. Their minds are broken, and they remain instruments of slaughter. If left to roam, they bring chaos to Deathknell's doorstep and give the Lich King easy fodder. Destroying them is necessary for the settlement and brings a grim end to some of Lordaeron's fallen.

quest:365.text: Fields of Grief. Pumpkins are taken from a human farmstead north of Deathknell for the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill. Deathguard Simmer sends newly risen Forsaken to gather them. Deathguard Simmer sends you from the crypts of Deathknell into a hostile land. He serves Sylvanas Windrunner's forces, where survival means taking what the living possess and putting it to use for the Undercity's darker aims. The farm lies west of the road, north of Deathknell, where mortal human peasants work blighted soil. Simmer says they infest the realm like mold on a corpse. The farmers hold their homesteads under the uneasy protection of nearby Scarlet Crusade towers. Taking their crops strikes at their supplies and provides produce for the Royal Apothecary Society's research.

quest:366.text: Return the Book. Bethor Iceshard sends his enchanted message back to Gunther Arcanus on Brightwater Lake. The stolen spellbook may bring his old Kirin Tor companion into the Forsaken fold. Bethor Iceshard sends an arcane message to Gunther Arcanus through a stolen spellbook. Once Bethor learns the necromancer on Brightwater Lake is his old companion, he enchants the tome's pages. The spell leaves Bethor's own magical mark, showing he is active in Lordaeron and free of the Lich King's control. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Bethor Iceshard, Gunther Arcanus, and Thule Ravenclaw studied and became friends in the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. When the Lich King rose, Thule betrayed his companions and joined the Scourge willingly. Bethor and Gunther fell to the Plague. Bethor later broke free alongside Queen Sylvanas. Believing Gunther dead or enslaved, Bethor now learns his old friend has also won his own freedom and seeks to bring him to the Forsaken.

quest:367.text: A New Plague. In Brill, A New Plague begins with blood taken from darkhounds. Apothecary Johaan gathers the samples for the Royal Apothecary Society, acting on Lady Sylvanas Windrunner’s command. Apothecary Johaan works in Brill for the Royal Apothecary Society, under orders from the Dark Lady. Sylvanas Windrunner has charged her alchemists with making a disease unlike any Azeroth has known. The original Plague of Undeath served the Lich King, slaughtering humanity and binding their souls. This new plague is meant to annihilate Arthas Menethil and lay waste to his Scourge legions. Johaan needs grim experiments to develop a weapon against the undead. He believes the blood of native beasts may hold useful chemical properties, beginning with darkhounds roaming Tirisfal Glades. You gather vials of their tainted blood so Johaan can isolate elements and test whether the beasts' resilience and predatory nature can help create a lethal contagion.

quest:368.text: A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan gathers scales from the Vile Fin murlocs along Tirisfal's coast. The errand supports the Royal Apothecary Society's work on a contagion meant to spread beyond isolated victims and reach larger populations. Apothecary Johaan's research in Brill needs more than a poison that harms one target. He is working on a disease that can spread on its own and endure in the wild. For those studies, he looks to the shoreline wildlife of Tirisfal Glades. The resilient biology of the coastal Vile Fin murlocs offers promising material for his work. Aggressive Vile Fin murloc tribes trouble the northern and western shores of Tirisfal Glades. Their scales contain organic compounds adapted to damp, harsh conditions. Johaan wants to add those slick, resilient scales to his developing brew, hoping they will strengthen the Royal Apothecary Society's new plague and help it endure in the wild.

quest:3681.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Master Brandur Ironhammer sends promising human paladins south for deeper training. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Master Duthorian Rall guides their study of the sacred Tomes of Divinity. Stormwind calls promising holy warriors south to the Cathedral of Light. Senior priests and paladin mentors await them there, keeping the Silver Hand's traditions alive in the Church of the Holy Light among human lands. Master Brandur Ironhammer knows when a student is ready for deeper study of the faith. You can reach Stormwind's Cathedral District by the Deeprun Tram or across the mountain passes. There, Duthorian Rall prepares initiates to study the sacred Tomes and learn the rites of redemption.

quest:369.text: A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan studies how an ancient plague survived in spider venom. He seeks a potent new biological agent for the Forsaken. Apothecary Johaan studies old texts in Brill for the Royal Apothecary Society. He finds records of an ancient pestilence that killed thousands. The texts say the pathogen survived across generations in the venom of Tirisfal Glades' local spiders. Johaan needs that venom as a biological reagent. Apothecary Johaan sends agents to eastern Tirisfal Glades for a viable sample. Venomweb Vale lies south of the Scarlet Monastery, where vicious night web spiders infest the hollow. Harvesters must enter their dens and gather fresh venom glands for Johaan's experimental brew.

quest:37.text: Find the Lost Guards. Guard Thomas waits at Elwynn's eastern bridge, needing news of two missing Stormwind guards. At the crossing where the King's road nears Redridge, the riverbanks have grown more dangerous. Days ago, Thomas sent Rolf and Malakai north along the river to scout the murloc threat and clear their nests. Now he fears violence has stopped their patrol.

quest:370.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, the Forsaken strike at Scarlet Crusade forces threatening their borders. Executor Zygand sends champions after Captain Perrine and his garrison at a ruined tower southwest of Brill, using intelligence taken in Deathknell. Executor Arren recovered documents from the Scarlet Crusade in Deathknell, revealing troop movements across Tirisfal Glades. Rather than wait for the fanatics to attack newly fortified Brill, Executor Zygand uses the captured intelligence to strike their field commanders first. Captain Perrine commands Scarlet Zealots and Missionaries from a ruined watchtower southwest of Brill. From there, the Crusade watches Forsaken movements and reaches farther into Tirisfal. Perrine's death matters to the defense of the Dark Lady's young kingdom.

quest:371.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Executor Zygand sends Forsaken fighters against the Scarlet Crusade near Balnir Farmstead. Their strike targets Captain Vachon and his friars in southeastern Tirisfal Glades, where Crusader raids threaten the Dark Lady's lands. The Forsaken guard Brill and the Undercity while the Scarlet Crusade holds fortified sites across the countryside. Executor Arren reports active Crusader incursions from a crumbling guard tower in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. The tower stands close to the abandoned Balnir Farmstead. Executor Zygand targets the Crusade's field leaders, knowing coordinated squads pose a greater danger than scattered zealots. You strike at Captain Vachon and the Scarlet Friars who strengthen his men with holy magic. Without their leadership and support, the cell may lose its cohesion and its raids into Forsaken lands may falter.

quest:372.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, Executor Zygand sends Forsaken agents from Brill against the Scarlet Crusade. Captain Melrache and his personal vanguard hold a ruined watchtower past Faol's Rest. The Forsaken are securing the ruins of Lordaeron while Scarlet Crusade forces keep probing Tirisfal's borders. From a watchtower in northern Tirisfal, past Faol's Rest, crusaders lead raids against Forsaken patrols and lands. Executor Zygand chooses to strike at the officers directing those raids instead of waiting for another attack. Captain Melrache commands the northern camp, with two sworn bodyguards always at his side. From the tower, the Scarlet Crusade can watch the coastal roads and nearby woods. Killing Melrache breaks the raiders' coordination near Brill, removes a direct threat to Lady Sylvanas's young kingdom, and drives the zealots back toward their stronger fortifications farther east.

quest:374.text:
Proof of Demise. In Brill, Proof of Demise sends soldiers against the Scarlet Crusade across Tirisfal Glades. Varimathras, Sylvanas Windrunner's dreadlord lieutenant, orders the campaign to thin their ranks and test loyalty to the Forsaken cause. Recruits must take signet rings from fallen crusaders as proof. Across northern Tirisfal Glades, the Forsaken wage a coordinated war against the living. Varimathras surrendered and pledged his blade to Sylvanas Windrunner. He oversees many of the Forsaken's aggressive military maneuvers.

His orders pass to commanders such as Executor Zygand, then to frontline officers like Deathguard Burgess. Burgess makes the order plain: humans are vermin to be purged from Lordaeron, and nearby crusaders are the immediate target. In Brill, words alone do not satisfy the commanders. Soldiers must take Scarlet Insignia Rings from the fingers of slain zealots to prove obedience to the Dark Lady and her lieutenant. The rings bear the Scarlet Crusade's mark, identifying their bearers as sworn enemies of the Forsaken.

Bring back these trophies, and the dead crusaders are proved. The rings also show a soldier's allegiance to the Forsaken leadership.

quest:3741.text: Hilary's Necklace. On the docks at Lakeshire, Hilary loses the necklace her father gave her while fishing. Her friend Shawn asks travelers to retrieve it from Lake Everstill, where their parents forbid them to swim. Hilary and Shawn spend the day fishing along Lakeshire's docks, trying to enjoy an ordinary childhood amid the threats around the Redridge Mountains. Hilary drops her treasured necklace into Lake Everstill. After searching the piers and shore without finding it, Shawn asks travelers for help. Hilary and Shawn's parents forbid them to swim in Lake Everstill. Aggressive murlocs and hungry threshedons lurk beneath the surface. The children cannot reach the necklace in the glinting mud at the lake bottom, so Shawn turns to travelers for help recovering the gift.

quest:375.text: The Chill of Death. In Brill, The Chill of Death weighs on Gretchen Dedmar as she fights the cold of undeath. The Forsaken tailor fears losing her mind and her service to Lady Sylvanas, so she asks for materials to sew a warm blanket. Gretchen Dedmar feels the Plague of Undeath like an icy serpent moving through her body. The chill drains warmth from her limbs and threatens to leave her mindless, like the wandering corpses in Tirisfal Glades. Her shaking hands make even ordinary work difficult. Gretchen will not abandon her duty to the Forsaken kingdom. When Sylvanas Windrunner first rallied the liberated dead, Gretchen sewed burial shrouds and body bags for fallen soldiers. Sturdy duskbat pelts and coarse thread can help her make a blanket. Its warmth may steady her hands enough to keep serving the Forsaken cause.

quest:376.text: The Damned. New Forsaken in Deathknell turn to Novice Elreth for clothing and battlefield wraps. She trades salvaged armor for the materials needed to make them. Novice Elreth tends the newly risen Forsaken in Deathknell. She assists Shadow Priest Sarvis, cares for battered soldiers, and mends their garments. Supplies run short, so she sends you into the surrounding glades to hunt duskbats and scavenger wolves. Their pelts, wings, and sinew help keep the camp supplied, and Elreth offers salvaged armor in return. Elreth's armor has already belonged to Forsaken who did not survive their awakening. She hopes it serves you better than its previous owner. In Tirisfal Glades, every piece of leather and rusted chain is put to use.

quest:38.text: Westfall Stew. On her farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean cooks Westfall Stew from what the frontier offers. Its ingredients reflect how homesteaders endure bandits, famine, and dangerous beasts. Westfall's settlers face bandits, famine, and rampaging beasts, far from Stormwind's lavish larders. Families like the Saldeans make do with what the land provides. Salma Saldean turns ingredients many city folk might call pests or scraps into a meal that sustains her farmhands. Salma's recipe brings together local okra, stringy meat from circling vultures, and snouts from wild goretusks roaming the plains. It also calls for fresh murloc eyes gathered from coastal raiders. Such fare may turn delicate stomachs in Elwynn, but Westfall cooks swear the blend makes a rich, fortifying meal.

quest:380.text: Night Web's Hollow. Northwest of Deathknell, spiders infest a gold mine the Forsaken need. Executor Arren sends newly risen recruits into the cavern to cull the spiders piece by piece. Raw materials are scarce, and the mine's wealth could sustain the Forsaken settlement and war effort. Executor Arren oversees operations in Deathknell, where the newly risen Forsaken struggle to survive. They face the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders, but defending themselves is only part of the work. A fledgling society also needs raw materials. Precious metals such as gold were scarce in northern Lordaeron even when the Alliance was strong. Arren knows the Forsaken need wealth to arm and equip themselves and establish their society. A natural cavern called Night Web's Hollow lies northwest of Deathknell's cemetery, with a gold vein running through it. Monstrous spiders have overrun its tunnels, leaving thick webs and deadly venom in their depths. Arren has too few seasoned troops for a full purge, so fresh recruits thin the young and adult spiders. Once the danger is reduced, mining crews can burn away the webs and extract the ore.

quest:381.text: The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, Deathknell faces a Scarlet Crusade camp southeast of the settlement. Executor Arren sends the newly awakened Forsaken to ambush its zealots, one of their most fanatical and persistent enemies. After the Night Web spiders are dealt with, Executor Arren turns Deathknell toward a threat drawing near. A detachment of the Scarlet Crusade has made a foothold just southeast of the settlement. Its zealots see no difference between mindless Scourge and free-willed Forsaken. Their presence on Deathknell's border threatens the newly risen dead. Executor Arren orders a strike before the camp can grow into an organized attack on Deathknell. You cut down Scarlet Converts and Scarlet Initiates, then bring back their crimson armbands as proof. The holy fanatics see all dead flesh as an abomination, leaving the Forsaken to claim survival by force.

quest:382.text: The Red Messenger. Executor Arren sends you after a courier bound for the camp outside Deathknell. Dispatched from the Scarlet Monastery, the courier carries word from the crusade to its camp. Intercepting him secures intelligence before the zealots can strengthen their hold in the valley. This is among the Forsaken's first offensive efforts to secure their fledgling sanctuary. Word of the Scarlet courier reaches Executor Arren through his superiors in Brill. The Scarlet Crusade sent an emissary west from its stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery to Deathknell. Crusaders press across Lordaeron, and a courier sent to the edge of the Forsaken's waking grounds signals an organized effort to destroy the newly risen before they can prepare a defense. Meven Korgal, the courier, blended into the small Scarlet camp east of Deathknell without distinctive heraldry. Executor Arren orders a targeted strike to kill Korgal and seize his dispatch. Taking the missives cuts off the local zealots from further tactical coordination with their eastern headquarters.

quest:383.text: Vital Intelligence. In Tirisfal Glades, a new Forsaken carries captured Scarlet Crusade documents from Deathknell to Brill. Executor Zygand awaits the courier there. Executor Arren sends you from Deathknell with captured Scarlet Crusade documents. You have dealt with local threats and intercepted a Scarlet Crusade courier, and are ready for wider service. Leave through Deathknell's sheltered canyon and follow the road east toward Brill, passing Cold Hearth Manor.

quest:384.text: Beer Basted Boar Ribs. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, patrons hunger for Ragnar Thunderbrew's famed ribs. His regular supplier has joined the King's Army, so Ragnar needs fresh crag boar ribs and Rhapsody Malt to keep them on the menu. Tavern keeper Ragnar Thunderbrew has eager customers, but his pantry is bare. The local hunter who supplied fresh meat enlisted in the King's Army to reinforce the Alliance front. Now Ragnar has no fresh ribs for the patrons who favor them. Crag boars roam the snowy foothills around Kharanos, and their meat is tough. Ragnar's recipe also calls for fresh Rhapsody Malt, drawn straight from the distillery's taps. The malt softens the game meat and makes a savory feast fit for a dwarf's praise.

quest:385.text: Crocolisk Hunting. At Farstrider Lodge, Marek Ironheart seeks trackers to hunt Loch Modan's crocolisks. Their hides and meat bring steady trade, though hunting along the lake's shores and rocky islets is dangerous. Crocolisks haunt the shallows and muddy banks, making crossings and fishing perilous. Across Khaz Modan, craftsmen and tailors seek their hides for rugged armor and leather goods. Rustic taverns pay well for the lean tail meat. Loch Modan's crocolisks gather mainly around the rocky islets. Their crushing jaws and sharp teeth make them dangerous quarry. Dwarven veterans like Marek Ironheart carry scars from wrestling them into submission. He warns that one misstep in the water can cost a limb. Skinning and butchering one takes patience, sturdy steel, and a willingness to enter its hunting ground.

quest:3861.text: CLUCK!. In Westfall, a chicken may answer when you call and feed it. Follow its scratched message to the Saldean family, and a warm egg may be yours to hatch. Across Azeroth, ordinary chickens wander farmsteads, though most travelers pass them by. Mimic a chicken's gestures and cluck, and one may stop pecking to regard you. In that brief moment, it scratches letters in the dirt, pointing you toward the farmer who can provide the food it wants. The bird asks for Special Chicken Feed, which the Saldean family keeps for its flock in Westfall. Offer the grain and cheer the chicken on as it eats. In return, it lays a warm egg, ready to be nurtured into a feathered companion.

quest:39.text: Deliver Thomas' Report. In eastern Elwynn, Guard Thomas sends word of two dead guards and rising danger. He asks you to carry the report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, where few hands remain to defend the roads. Guard Thomas watches the bridges into eastern Elwynn, where river traffic meets the wilderness. Aggressive murloc tribes have killed Guards Malakai and Rolf. Thomas has too few guards left to contain them, so he sends you down the road to Goldshire with an urgent report. Marshal Dughan receives Thomas' report in Goldshire, where he already struggles to keep patrols on the roads. Kobolds infest the area, Defias bandits threaten travelers, and Stormwind City has sent no reinforcements. The deaths of two experienced guards deepen his burden. Murlocs may soon threaten Goldshire itself, while the region's defenses grow ever thinner.

quest:3901.text: Rattling the Rattlecages. In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken face a test against the Rattlecage Skeletons. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends them to destroy twelve skeletons and prove they can defend their hard-won freedom. Newly risen Forsaken face a harder trial after culling the mindless zombies in Deathknell. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends recruits against the Rattlecage Skeletons roaming the settlement’s outskirts. The animated bones have no sapience or self-control, yet strike harder and fight more fiercely than the nearby decaying corpses. Surviving their clattering ambushes shows Sarvis that a recruit can withstand immediate pressure. Destroying the skeletons protects Deathknell from the lingering grip of the Lich King and tests which recruits can endure the fight. Those who fail or hesitate risk becoming like the mindless wretches wandering the woods. Overcoming the Rattlecages proves to Sarvis that you have the mettle to face a world that despises your existence.

quest:3902.text: Scavenging Deathknell. In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken gather supplies for the recruits rising from nearby graves. Deathguard Saltain sends them to search the blighted settlement for abandoned boxes and crates, where the Forsaken must find what they need to survive. Newly raised Forsaken wake in Deathknell with little to call their own. Deathguard Saltain sends them to gather what the recruits still climbing from their graves need: clothing and arms. The Forsaken must salvage supplies to outfit those newly risen, with every usable piece put to work. Deathknell holds remnants of its former human inhabitants and supplies abandoned during the kingdom’s fall to the Scourge. Deathguards send newly awakened Forsaken to recover usable goods from boxes and crates scattered through the town. The Forsaken expect no charity from the living and must depend on their own effort to survive.

quest:3903.text: Milly Osworth. Deputy Willem sends you across Northshire Abbey to help his friend Milly Osworth. Her wagon and livelihood are in danger, and Willem's guards cannot leave the abbey grounds to help. After you drive back the Defias thieves pressing into Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem trusts you with a personal favor. His friend Milly Osworth is a civilian caught in the valley's unrest, and helping her falls beyond his guard duties. Milly waits beside her wagon near the stables on the far side of Northshire Abbey. Deputy Willem stays at his post to defend the abbey. With the guard garrison stretched thin, Milly's troubles in the valley go without help.

quest:3904.text: Milly's Harvest. Defias brigands have driven Milly Osworth from the Northshire vineyards. Her gathered grapes remain in buckets and crates among the occupied rows, at risk of theft or ruin. Milly Osworth fled the southeastern fields of Northshire Valley when Defias brigands swarmed the vines. The grapes she had gathered remain in buckets and crates among the occupied rows. Northshire's garrison is stretched thin, and Milly fears boots and fighting will crush any fruit the bandits leave behind. Defias bandits now occupy working vineyards, a sign of how little safety Northshire can offer. Stormwind's attention lies elsewhere, and the valley has too few guards. So farmers like Milly depend on recruits and wanderers to protect their property and secure the food and wine that supply the abbey.

quest:3905.text: Grape Manifest. Milly Osworth needs you to bring her manifest to Brother Neals at Northshire Abbey. It will help the brotherhood replenish its wine stores. Defias thieves and other brigands took the eastern fields. The abbey lost its food and its grapes. Milly has recovered the crop and recorded every bushel in her manifest, including what the occupied fields had yielded. Brother Neals oversees food and drink at Northshire Abbey. In the quiet of the bell tower, he is known to sample Northshire's vintages. Brigands still threaten the gates, yet fresh grapes give the brotherhood a moment to toast the Light and take heart.

quest:3921.text: Wenikee Boltbucket. Near the Mor'shan Rampart, Wenikee Boltbucket may be able to mend a broken samophlange. Sputtervalve tinkered with the device after it was retrieved from the Sludge Fen, and now needs an expert hand before his colleagues in Undermine demand results. Sputtervalve's claims to his fellow engineers in Undermine now hang on a broken machine. An adventurer retrieved the mysterious samophlange from the Venture Company's control console at the Sludge Fen, and Sputtervalve could not resist showing it off. His tinkering damaged the delicate contraption. He needs someone with sharper skill to diagnose the damage and repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket camps beside the road just south of the Mor'shan Rampart. The rampart divides the northern Barrens from Ashenvale. Her inquisitive mind is drawn to intricate machinery, and the broken samophlange quickly captures her attention. Its internal gears hold her curiosity, and she sets to work figuring out how to rebuild it.

quest:3922.text: Nugget Slugs. At the Sludge Fen, Wenikee Boltbucket needs parts for a recovered samophlange. The eccentric tinkerer sends you to the nearby Venture Company drilling crews for spare hardware. Wenikee Boltbucket has a recovered samophlange and wants to learn how the intricate machine works. Its goblin mechanisms need exact parts, so she sends you to the Venture Company crews at the Sludge Fen. Their heavy tool buckets hold the seventeen-point-five gauge nugget slugs she needs.

quest:3923.text: Rilli Greasygob. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob is the specialist Wenikee Boltbucket seeks. She sends you there with a damaged samophlange, hoping his knowledge of its Venture Company origins can explain the device. Wenikee Boltbucket examined the samophlange recovered from the Venture Company drilling site in the Barrens. Her extra gauges showed the apparatus nearing collapse. More levers and dials might destroy it, so she stopped and sent the problem to someone with knowledge of its design. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Wenikee sends you to Nogg's Machine Shop. Rilli Greasygob works there as an engineer and once learned his trade within the Venture Company. He recognizes the machine at once and marvels that anyone survived exploring the company's contested operations in the Barrens.

quest:3924.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob needs help with a broken samophlange. The goblin engineer sends you back into the Barrens for the operating instructions, held by his former Venture Company rival. Rilli Greasygob once worked beside Boss Copperplug in the Venture Company. Copperplug oversaw the samophlange’s inner workings and guarded their secrets closely. He shared no manual with Rilli. Instead, he gave out separate pages only to underlings he trusted, leaving his fellow engineer without the knowledge to understand the device.

quest:398.text: Wanted: Maggot Eye. In Brill, the Forsaken leadership has posted a death bounty for Maggot Eye. The notorious gnoll robs nearby graveyards and farms, supplying bodies to the Lich King's Scourge. Executor Zygand demands proof of the kill to secure the lands around Garren's Haunt. In Tirisfal Glades, the dead do not rest in peace. Maggot Eye faces a severe death sentence for aiding the Lich King. Gnolls are usually seen as savage brutes driven by hunger, but Maggot Eye digs up corpses and gathers remains to strengthen the Scourge army. The Forsaken fight to break free of the Lich King's control, so feeding their dead kin to the Scourge is among the gravest offenses. Executor Zygand oversees local military enforcement in Brill and ordered the bounty to end the grave robberies near Garren's Haunt. To claim the prize, you need Maggot Eye's paw as proof that the beast can trouble Tirisfal no longer.

quest:399.text: Humble Beginnings. In Cathedral Square, Baros Alexston asks you to search his family's burned farm in Westfall. Thieves hold the ruins, and he hopes to recover the compass he treasured as a boy. Baros Alexston once worked the fields of Westfall. Now he is Stormwind City's accomplished architect, advising on stonework and city buildings. Few in the kingdom have made such a journey from farm to city. Yet Baros remains bound to the humble beginnings that shaped him. Lawlessness swept across Westfall and reached the Alexston Farmstead. Bandits and vagrants burned the house, driving Baros's father from his livelihood. Family heirlooms remained behind amid the fire and occupation. Now Baros asks you to search the ruined, bandit-held farmstead west of Sentinel Hill for his first compass, hidden before the home fell.

quest:40.text: A Fishy Peril. In eastern Elwynn, Remy "Two Times" fears a danger is spreading. Fishing has suffered and travelers face attacks, but he doubts the guard understands the trouble. In Goldshire seeking business, Remy grows uneasy as murlocs swim up streams and into inland shallows. He asks passersby to warn the township before the threat spreads further. Marshal Dughan hears the report but doubts it. His garrison is stretched thin, and without confirmed intelligence, he will not send scarce men after rumors of fish-men in the eastern streams.

quest:400.text: Tools for Steelgrill. At Kharanos, Tharek Blackstone sends you northeast with tools for Beldin Steelgrill at the depot. The road leads from town to the mechanics and war machines gathered there. Across Dun Morogh, Beldin Steelgrill is known as the sharpest siege engine mechanic in the mountains. His rough work breaks arclight spanners and other tools faster than Kharanos suppliers can replace them. Tharek Blackstone has a fresh batch of durable gear ready, so a traveler bound northeast carries the heavy crate to the depot. Steelgrill's Depot is crowded with idle war machines and military repairs. Beldin's backlog includes urgent work on Pilot Stonegear's siege engine. He broke his last fang-ratchet only hours before you arrive. The crate is needed to keep Ironforge's tracked armor fleet running.

quest:403.text: Guarded Thunderbrew Barrel. In Kharanos, the Thunderbrew family’s ale waits under guard in the distillery cellar. Jarven watches over the stock. Jarven Thunderbrew keeps watch over the aging casks beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Sentries stand beside the barrels, guarding the brew from tampering or theft. The Thunderbrews keep their recipes close, especially the potent Thunder Ale. Dwarves give brewing the care they give smithing and mining. Troggs creep nearby, and brewing rivals compete across the Alliance. So Jarven watches until the family’s ale is ready to be tapped.

quest:404.text: A Putrid Task. Deathguard Dillinger sends you west from Brill to hold the old bridge against the Scourge. Bring back proof that the dead are destroyed, and Tirisfal's defenders can keep the road clear. Brill guards a crossroads in eastern Tirisfal Glades, where an enemy approach threatens the Forsaken stronghold. Scourge wander west across the waterways and gather around the broken old stone bridge. Without patrols to drive them back, the shambling dead could block travel between Brill and the western farmsteads. For the Forsaken, Scourge on their borders are more than a threat to defend against. Each mindless ghoul and rotting corpse recalls the servitude and torment they escaped under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Deathguards like Dillinger take grim satisfaction in crushing their former captors. They demand severed claws as proof that the mindless dead have been put to rest for good.

quest:405.text: The Prodigal Lich. In the Undercity, Bethor Iceshard needs an agent for a mission involving a wayward lich. After your work in Brill against Scourge remnants and Rot Hide gnolls, Magistrate Sevren sends you south with orders. Magistrate Sevren judges you worthy of greater Forsaken work after your service in Brill. He sends you to Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, who wants an agent tested against the Scourge. Sevren gives you official orders to carry beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, into the corridors of the Forsaken capital. Magistrate Sevren does not know the exact details, but the orders concern finding and recruiting a rogue lich. Liches are among the Scourge's deadliest spellcasters, and dealing with one is perilous. You bring the orders to Bethor atop his arcane sanctum. The icy mage gets straight to business, ready to see whether Brill's magistrate has sent someone strong enough to track such dangerous quarry.

quest:407.text: Fields of Grief. Apothecary Johaan tests his pumpkin weapon in Brill. He has laced pumpkins from Solliden Farmstead with his latest alchemical concoction and sends you to feed one to a captive Scarlet Crusader. Apothecary Johaan believes the Forsaken must use every advantage against the Scourge to the north and human incursions to the south. The Royal Apothecary Society looks beyond blades and dark sorcery, seeking weapons in the ordinary produce of the land. Johaan has tainted pumpkins gathered from the mortal farmers at Solliden Farmstead. He means to prove common crops can be made deadly in service of the Dark Lady.

quest:408.text: The Family Crypt. Scourge forces at the Agamand Mills threaten the Forsaken's hold on Tirisfal. From Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends agents against the undead in the family crypt. The Forsaken hold Tirisfal Glades, but the Scourge still grips much of its countryside. The Agamand Mills once produced flour for Lordaeron; now they are a Scourge stronghold. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren watches the enemy gather with grave concern. Every stretch of land lost to the undead weakens the Forsaken's independence. Captain Dargol, a skeletal commander, has made the Agamand Family Crypt his headquarters. Through necromancy, he raises generations of the Agamand dead as Rotting and Wailing Ancestors to swell his ranks. Magistrate Sevren sends Forsaken agents to purge the crypt, lay the disturbed dead to rest, and sever Dargol's head to disrupt Scourge forces in northern Tirisfal.

quest:409.text: Proving Allegiance. Gunther Arcanus tests whether you serve the free-willed Forsaken or the Lich King. To earn his trust, you are sent to summon and destroy Lillith Nefara, a Scourge operative near his island. Gunther Arcanus has kept to an island in Brightwater Lake since rising into undeath. He fiercely guards his freedom. Bethor Iceshard's enchantments on Gunther's spellbook showed that the emissary carries no Scourge taint. Still, words and charms cannot quiet the hermit's suspicions. An outsider must prove hostility toward the Lich King's minions through decisive violence before Gunther will trust them.

quest:410.text: The Dormant Shade. A dark rite waits at Gunther's Retreat on Brightwater Lake in Tirisfal Glades. Set a mystic candle on an old, blood-soaked table to summon Lillith Nefara, a Scourge agent, and prove to Gunther Arcanus that you oppose the Lich King. On Gunther's Retreat, an island in Brightwater Lake, a battered dinner table lies stained with blood. The table is no ordinary abandoned piece of furniture. It is the focus of a dark conjuration, a rough slab where dried gore marks the place death and dark magic gather.

quest:411.text: The Prodigal Lich Returns. You carry an arcane communion gem to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, after winning Gunther Arcanus's trust and restoring his grimoire. Gunther Arcanus spent years alone on an island in Brightwater Lake. By sheer force of will, he broke free from the Lich King's control, unaware that Sylvanas Windrunner had liberated Lordaeron. Bitter and wary of outsiders, he distrusted the Undercity's emissaries. An adventurer returned his spellbook and showed him their hostility toward the Scourge. Satisfied the visitor was no enemy, Gunther entrusted them with a Nether Gem to contact his former colleague.

quest:412.text: Operation Recombobulation. In Kharanos, Razzle Sprysprocket and Ozzie Togglevolt search for a cure for their kin. Their experimental Recombobulator needs parts taken from hostile leper gnomes outside Gnomeregan. Razzle and Ozzie are building a machine to restore their afflicted kin to health and sanity. Radiation changed most of Gnomeregan's gnomes into sickly, deranged leper gnomes. The inventors hope their Recombobulator can reverse that change. Razzle needs Restabilization Cogs and Gyromechanic Gears for the delicate prototype. The parts must come from hostile leper gnomes outside Gnomeregan's sealed gates. Debris from their altered kin may help undo the tragedy they share.

quest:413.text: Shimmer Stout. At Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew is sending Shimmer Stout to his brother Wellart. The guard watches the pass toward Loch Modan, where a cold post makes a strong drink welcome. Rejold Barleybrew perfected Shimmer Stout with shimmering fronds gathered from Dun Morogh’s icy crags. His family tends the vats and kegs at Brewnall Village, while his brother Wellart chose life as a Mountaineer. Knowing how lonely frontier guard duty can be, Rejold sends a fresh barrel with passing travelers. It is a kindness between brothers and a chance to test the brew. Wellart Barleybrew guards the South Gate Pass into Loch Modan from the southern tower. High in the pass, Mountaineers face bitter winds and occasional beast attacks as they watch over travelers on the mountain road. Wellart is running low on drink and restless for excitement. Shimmer Stout packs quite a punch, he finds, and seems to brighten his vision in the dim mountain night.

quest:414.text: Stout to Kadrell. A cask of Rejold Barleybrew’s new Shimmer Stout is headed east to Mountaineer Kadrell in Loch Modan. You carry it from Dun Morogh’s frozen heights to the warmer valley. From Dun Morogh’s eastern border post, Mountaineer Barleybrew watches the mountain passes and the kin guarding neighboring lands. The Mountaineers’ patrols can be cold and grueling, and a stout heart calls for stout drink. Rejold’s new Shimmer Stout is too good to keep in Dun Morogh. Barleybrew wants an honest opinion from a fellow patrolman, so he sends a cask east with travelers bound for Loch Modan. For young dwarven and gnomish adventurers, the road to Loch Modan is a rite of passage after their early days in Dun Morogh’s snowbound crags. You pass southeast through the South Gate Outpost, then follow long tunnels cut through the mountain bedrock. Beyond them lies Loch Modan’s warmer, wooded basin. Mountaineer Kadrell patrols the road through Thelsamar. He pauses to tap the cask and finds that Barleybrew’s new recipe has an astonishing kick.

quest:415.text: Rejold's New Brew. Back at Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew has perfected his new recipe. He wants you, the trusted friend who secured the Shimmerweed, to taste it. Tharek Blackstone and Pilot Bellowfiz send you back to Brewnall Village. Rejold has finished fermenting his experimental batches and is ready to share them with you. You secured Shimmerweed from the bitter slopes, and now he can offer you the fruits of that effort. Rejold Barleybrew has blended local herbs into his mash to make Shimmer Stout. Before he ships barrels to neighboring outposts and thirsty patrons in Loch Modan, he gives you the honor of the first sip. You risked life and limb for the herbs, and the first taste is yours.

quest:4161.text: Recipe of the Kaldorei. Zarrin teaches a lesson in balance through the Recipe of the Kaldorei. In Dolanaar, young cooks learn to gather only what they need from Teldrassil's woods. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and teaches young adventurers the traditions of his people. The night elves once called themselves the kaldorei, or children of the stars. Zarrin begins their understanding of that heritage with the bond between a hunter, their food, and Teldrassil's boughs, rather than the battlefield. Zarrin teaches restraint through a simple demand: gather small spider legs from the woodland arachnids outside Shadowglen, but take exactly seven. The kaldorei seek harmony with nature by taking only what they need and showing kindness to the wild. Even in troubled times, that balance matters. A spider kabob becomes a lesson in living with care.

quest:417.text: A Pilot's Revenge. Hildelve’s search ends in the crags of Dun Morogh, where Pilot Hammerfoot’s searchers find him frozen beside his journal. His last words call for vengeance. Hildelve’s journal tells of his savage fight with Mangeclaw, the huge Ice Claw bear. He drove the beast away at first, but his wounds were grave. Mangeclaw returned and killed him. Hildelve’s final plea calls for vengeance against Mangeclaw. Bring his journal and a claw torn from the beast to Pilot Hammerfoot. The grim news gives the Ironforge Siege Brigade closure and honors its lost comrade.

quest:418.text: Thelsamar Blood Sausages. At Thelsamar's Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove keeps Thelsamar Blood Sausages on the table. A favorite across Loch Modan, they need fresh ingredients from the valley. Hungry children and miners returning from the Ironband Excavation fill Thelsamar's tavern. Vidra Hearthstove tends the stove, making sausages known across Loch Modan. Her recipe draws on wildlife from the rugged mountain pass. Vidra uses boar intestines for casings and bear meat for the filling. Spider ichor gives the sausages their sharp, pungent bite. Gathering the entrails and venomous fluid takes a steady stomach, though travelers come to appreciate this regional favorite.

quest:419.text: The Lost Pilot. At the wreck, Pilot Hammerfoot fears for Mori Hildelve in Dun Morogh's crags. Hildelve went on foot to seek rare ore for potent blastpowder, but days have passed and roars echo through the peaks. Pilot Mori Hildelve drove his siege engine up Dun Morogh's steep ridges in search of rare ore for high-grade blastpowder. The machine broke on the slope. He left Pilot Hammerfoot at the camp to guard the wreck, then climbed higher into the frozen wilderness on foot. Days passed, and Hildelve did not return to camp. At night, vicious growls echoed from the rocky crags. Hammerfoot's impatience gave way to dread. Hildelve was tough, but the frigid heights offered little shelter from prowling predators without his engine or heavy support.

quest:420.text:
Senir's Observations. Grelin Whitebeard's report reaches his brother Senir in Kharanos, carrying news from Coldridge Valley. Its arrival sends Senir back to watching hostile forces across the snowfields. Mountaineer Thalos guards the gate out of Coldridge Valley. He entrusts passing travelers with Grelin's dispatch. Beyond the gate, violent troggs ambush those crossing the tunnel and make the passage to Kharanos dangerous. Past the tunnel, the main road runs through central Dun Morogh to town. At the Thunderbrew Distillery, Senir Whitebeard warms himself over drinks when Grelin's report arrives. He chuckles at his brother's forceful words. Grelin invokes King Magni Bronzebeard to press for urgent action, Senir says, and that will agitate the stubborn Ironforge Senate.

The bitter cold has kept Senir from filing his own observations. Grelin's dispatch sends him back to watching hostile forces across the snowfields.

quest:421.text: Prove Your Worth. At the Sepulcher, Prove Your Worth begins Dalar Dawnweaver's campaign against the worgen of Silverpine. The Forsaken seek a path south through human and dwarven lands, but feral worgen threaten the road. Their presence leads back to Archmage Arugal. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, seek to secure the lands south of Tirisfal Glades, including human and dwarven enclaves. Silverpine Forest lies in their path, but the route is dangerous. Feral Moonrage worgen prowl the pine-covered hills, threatening Forsaken supply lines and forward bases. Dalar Dawnweaver says the worgen came through the work of Arugal, a disgraced former mage of Dalaran. During the Scourge invasion, Arugal unleashed otherworldly worgen upon Silverpine. He has since claimed Shadowfang Keep, while his feral creations roam the forest. Before Dalar trusts soldiers with a deeper inquiry into Arugal's sorcery, recruits must prove their fighting skill against the nearest Moonrage Whitescalps.

quest:422.text: Arugal's Folly. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver sends Forsaken agents to a nearby farmstead for Arugal's earliest spellbooks. The Forsaken need to understand the magic behind the worgen curse if they are to turn it against Arugal and secure Silverpine Forest. The Remedy of Arugal is the first step in unraveling the threat from Shadowfang Keep. In the Sepulcher's crypts, ambitious Forsaken mage Dalar Dawnweaver holds Archmage Arugal in contempt. He sees him as an ordinary practitioner whose place in the Kirin Tor makes no sense, and whose grasp of magic seems amateurish. Yet the monstrous beasts roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver means to take apart the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

quest:423.text: Arugal's Folly. In Silverpine, Forsaken agents seek shackles worn by Moonrage worgen. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's notes to learn how the renegade mage strengthened his unstable magic. The bindings may help the Forsaken break the worgen threat. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's recovered research with open contempt for his former peer. He says Arugal was never fit to serve Dalaran, much less wield high sorcery in the kingdom's darkest hour. Lacking talent, Arugal turned to enchanted relics and devices to strengthen and bind the worgen he summoned. Dalar needs samples of those objects to study the magic tethering the beasts. Moonrage worgen roam Silverpine with shackles that carry Arugal's binding enchantments. Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls prowl north and east of the Sepulcher. Their heavy metal shackles hold residual arcane energy, making them useful to Dawnweaver as he searches for a way to counter Shadowfang Keep.

quest:424.text: Arugal's Folly. Worgen hold Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine's southeastern hills, keeping the Forsaken from ore needed by Varimathras's forces. Dalar Dawnweaver sends you to slay their corrupted foreman, Grimson the Pale, and carry his head to the Sepulcher. Dalar Dawnweaver learns from the Forsaken Darkstalkers that worgen have reached Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine's southeastern hills. Their feral sorcery spread from Shadowfang Keep, where Archmage Arugal unleashed dark enchantments across the forest. Ore from the mine is needed to arm the Undercity. But worgen now make their lair in its shafts, and the mine lies unusable. Grimson the Pale leads the worgen through the mine's infested shafts. Dalar Dawnweaver orders you to slay the corrupted foreman and bring his head to the Sepulcher. With Grimson gone, the worgen will lose their leader, and Forsaken laborers can claim the mine for Lord Varimathras.

quest:425.text: Ivar the Foul. At the Ivar Patch in northern Silverpine, Ivar the Foul has trapped two Deathstalkers. Rane asks Horde travelers to kill the savage ghoul so Quinn can recover and they can finish their report to High Executor Hadrec. Rane and Quinn Yorick, siblings and Deathstalkers, were sent to survey Silverpine Forest for High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their work ended in violence at a farmstead in the northern forest, where Ivar the Foul ambushed them. Rane and Quinn escaped, but Quinn was badly mauled. An alchemical remedy made from forest beasts has not made him strong enough to travel. Ivar prowls the nearby barn, waiting for Rane's guard to fail. She asks Horde travelers to enter the barn and kill him, so the homestead can be secured.

quest:426.text: The Mills Overrun. In Tirisfal, the Scourge gather at Agamand Mills, close to Forsaken settlements. Deathguard Dillinger sends soldiers from Brill to break their ranks before the ruined mills become a base for attacks deeper into the glades. The Agamand Mills once anchored Tirisfal Glades' agriculture. Since the Third War, their windmills overlook Scourge forces massing on the grounds under the Lich King's thrall. These mindless undead threaten the fledgling Forsaken holdings. If they secure the mills, they will have a base from which to push deeper into Tirisfal and strike at those settlements. Deathguard Dillinger, who helps fortify Brill and patrols the territory, sends recruits against the Scourge. They hunt Rattlecage and Cracked Skull Soldiers, along with Darkeye Bonecasters. Dillinger asks for notched ribs and blackened skulls as proof that the skeletal ranks have been broken apart and driven back toward the Plaguelands before their offensive begins.

quest:427.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal Glades, Executor Zygand directs the Forsaken campaign against the Scarlet Crusade. With intelligence recovered by Executor Arren, you are sent to strike Scarlet Warriors at a guard tower west of the Solliden Farmstead. The attack opens the Forsaken military effort to drive the crusaders from their borders. The Forsaken state under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner faces threats on several fronts. The Deathguard watches the growing armies of the Lich King, while the Scarlet Crusade contests Forsaken dominance over their former homeland. The Crusade condemns all undead as abominations to be purged with fire and blade. Its zealots fail to see that the Forsaken have broken free of the Scourge’s control. Executor Arren secured intelligence documents at Deathknell, giving Executor Zygand the locations of Scarlet encampments and outposts across Tirisfal Glades. With Deathguard garrisons occupied containing the Scourge, independent Forsaken champions are sent to strike the zealots directly. The first target is a guard tower west of Solliden Farmstead, where Scarlet Warriors gather and threaten the western approaches to Brill.

quest:428.text: Lost Deathstalkers. In northern Silverpine, two Forsaken scouts have been missing for weeks. High Executor Hadrec sent Rane and Quinn Yorick to survey haunted farmsteads, and now you must learn what became of them. High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher has heard nothing from Rane and Quinn Yorick for weeks. He sent the two Deathstalkers into northern Silverpine Forest to watch the abandoned farms and track enemy movements. Deathstalkers are the Forsaken’s hidden scouts and killers, serving Lady Sylvanas. Hadrec fears the Scourge or another threat has cut the scouts down. Northern Silverpine lies between Lordaeron’s ruined estates and the shadowed borders of Tirisfal Glades. Undead roam there, beasts prowl, and feral worgen make travel perilous even for seasoned rogues. You must search the decaying farmsteads where Rane and Quinn Yorick began their survey, and recover any intelligence they gathered before danger overtook them.

quest:429.text: Wild Hearts. Rane Yorick seeks help in Silverpine Forest as her brother Quinn lies badly wounded. She needs discolored worg hearts for Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher, whose alchemy may help Quinn recover. Rane Yorick stays beside her severely wounded brother, Quinn, after the Deathstalkers' disastrous mission left them pinned down at a farm in northern Silverpine. The feral ghoul Ivar the Foul mauled Quinn, and he is failing to recover. Ordinary rest cannot mend an undead body torn by such savagery. Rane turns to the Royal Apothecary Society and its grim arts for a way to put her brother back together. The worgs of Silverpine carry the corruption spreading through northern Lordaeron. Their hearts are discolored and hold potent essences. The Royal Apothecaries can distill these blighted organs into concoctions that restore withered Forsaken flesh.

quest:430.text: Return to Quinn. At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick waits for a draught that may let him travel again. Apothecary Renferrel sends you from the Sepulcher with the mixture, while Quinn remains wounded in dangerous country. After you gather wild beast hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Renferrel brews a restorative draught for Quinn Yorick at the Sepulcher. He hands it over without ceremony and returns to his secret alchemical research. You carry the mixture back into the wilderness. At the ruined Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick hides beside his sister, Deathstalker Rane Yorick. The ghoul Ivar the Foul wounded him so badly he cannot cross hostile ground. Quinn drinks the draught as soon as you arrive. It restores enough strength for him to travel in time, though danger still surrounds the farmstead, with Ivar lurking nearby.

quest:431.text: Candles of Beckoning. In Tirisfal Glades, candles from Gunther's island are bound for a grim test. A crate on Gunther's Retreat holds the ritual tapers Gunther Arcanus uses to test allegiance. Gunther asks you to take a candle from the crate on Gunther's Retreat to the old, bloody altar off the island's southern coast. Light it there, and face Lillith Nefara, the Scourge agent. A crate of candles rests on Gunther's Retreat, the island in Brightwater Lake where Gunther Arcanus dwells. For his test in Proving Allegiance, one candle is enough. Lit on the old, bloody altar off the island's southern coast, it awakens Lillith Nefara, the Scourge agent.

quest:432.text: Those Blasted Troggs!. In Gol'Bolar Quarry, troggs wreck the workings while Foreman Stonebrow calls for help. They have broken his equipment and powder barrels. His fading aim keeps him from fighting them himself, so he asks willing fighters to thin the Skullthumpers. Troggs have overrun the lower terraces of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. They broke through the bedrock and flooded the tunnels, ending the dwarven excavation's productive days. Now they smash scaffolding and blow apart powder barrels, leaving the quarry in ruin. From the ridge, Foreman Stonebrow watches his life's work crumble. Age has weakened his hands and spoiled his aim, so he relies on passing wanderers and Alliance recruits to fight in his place. He wants the burly Rockjaw Skullthumpers thinned. Only their complete destruction would satisfy his anger.

quest:433.text: The Public Servant. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Senator Mehr Stonehallow calls for aid against troggs that have halted mining in Dun Morogh. He wants the Rockjaw Bonesnappers driven out so miners can return to work. Mehr Stonehallow serves in Ironforge's Senate and belongs to the Explorers' League. He has come to Gol'Bolar Quarry to direct the response himself. There, he hires travelers and mercenaries to drive the invaders from the mine. Deep digging at Gol'Bolar Quarry broke into sealed hollows underground. Rockjaw troggs poured into the pits, smashed mining equipment, and drove out the workers. Stonehallow wants the Rockjaw Bonesnappers cleared away so Mountaineers can secure the quarry and mining can resume.

quest:435.text: Escorting Erland. In Silverpine, Deathstalker Erland needs help reaching his partner. Wolves have trapped him in a shelter, and he must cross their hunting ground to reach Rane Yorick. Deathstalker Erland is trapped in a shelter by hungry wolves. Even seasoned Forsaken scouts can be outmatched by Silverpine's wilds. The wolves circle the ruined refuge, drawn to the little flesh left on Erland's withered frame. Alone, he cannot break through their pack. Deathstalker Erland needs to reach his partner, Rane Yorick, near the Ivar Patch. The way crosses ground prowled by wolves. Once you guide him past them, Erland runs the last stretch to Rane Yorick's outpost. There, the scouts can bring their intelligence together for the Undercity.

quest:436.text: Ironband's Excavation. Jern Hornhelm has sent you from Thelsamar to find out why Ironband's Excavation is making so little progress. Supplies reach Prospector Ironband's team, and Jern trusts his diligence, but the work remains slow. Jern Hornhelm watches from Thelsamar as provisions and tools cross Loch Modan to the Explorers' League. They arrive steadily, yet the dig makes little progress. Jern suspects something is disrupting the work. He needs you to find out what is holding the team back.

quest:437.text: The Dead Fields. At the Dead Fields, Forsaken forces face a Scourge threat in northern Silverpine. High Executor Hadrec sends champions from the Sepulcher against the Rot Hide gnolls and the banshee who shields them. North of the Sepulcher, an abandoned farmstead lies overrun by Rot Hide gnolls. The fields once held ordinary farms, but now these plague ridden scavengers infest the Silverpine countryside. High Executor Hadrec sent small raiding parties to drive them out. Each attack stalled under a strange magical resistance. Nightlash, a Scourge banshee, directs the Rot Hide gnolls and scatters Forsaken skirmishers with dark sorcery when the gnolls face defeat. Hadrec sends Horde champions to cut down the gnolls and draw Nightlash into the open. He asks for her spectral essence as proof that she is destroyed.

quest:438.text: The Decrepit Ferry. At the Decrepit Ferry, rot hides swarm the dock east of The Sepulcher. High Executor Hadrec sends Forsaken champions to learn why the Scourge has gathered along Lordamere Lake's shore. High Executor Hadrec turns east after the Scourge presence in the Dead Fields is suppressed. The Decrepit Ferry lies among Silverpine Forest's eastern waterways, where mainland Lordaeron once connected to the island estates of Lordamere Lake. Now undead gather around its rotted piers. Hadrec sends scouts to find out what draws the Lich King's servants there.

quest:439.text: Rot Hide Clues. At Lordamere Lake, the Rot Hide Clues begin with an engraved ring on a recently deceased woman's hand. Reporting the grim find to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher reveals that Rot Hide gnolls are taking bodies from Tirisfal's mass graves and carrying them to Fenris Isle. Forsaken scouts find a corpse-laden ferry on the shore of Lordamere Lake. Among the dead is the unwrapped, plague-marked hand of a recently slain woman, with a simple band engraved “For Deliah.” The ferry points to organized transport, not scavengers feeding at random.

quest:441.text: Raleigh and the Undercity. In Brill and the Undercity, a ring draws Raleigh into an old tragedy. Magistrate Sevren sends you to return Deliah's ring to her widowed husband, found after her stolen corpse was bound for Fenris Isle. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren has pieced together clues about a stolen corpse and an engraved ring. The ring belonged to Deliah, and Sevren hopes to learn where it came from and return it to her family. He sends you into the Undercity to find Raleigh, Deliah's surviving husband.

quest:443.text: Rot Hide Ichor. High Executor Hadrec seeks Rot Hide Ichor in Silverpine Forest before the Forsaken attack Fenris Isle. He wants the fluid studied to understand the gnolls that infest the island. Rot Hide gnolls on Fenris Isle are decaying, aggressive, and unlike ordinary wild humanoids. They hold strategic ground across Lordamere Lake. High Executor Hadrec believes the strange fluid in their veins may explain their unnatural resilience. He needs samples before committing Forsaken soldiers to a costly assault. The Royal Apothecary Society works from the Sepulcher, where Apothecary Renferrel studies biological and chemical anomalies. Bring him samples of the putrid fluid, and the Forsaken hope to learn where the gnolls came from, who is engineering them, and what weaknesses they have in battle.

quest:444.text: Rot Hide Origins. In Silverpine Forest, the Rot Hides carry a magic Renferrel cannot explain by alchemy alone. He sends a sample to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, where arcane knowledge may reveal its origin. Apothecary Renferrel has reduced fluid from the Rot Hides of Silverpine Forest to its basic elements. His first tests show the ichor bears both necromancy and warlock magic. Alchemy cannot explain the sorcery behind it, so he prepares a sample for an expert in the Undercity.

quest:445.text: Delivery to Silverpine Forest. You carry Apothecary Johaan’s findings from Brill to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher. The Royal Apothecary Society needs them for its work on the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society answers directly to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and works to concoct a New Plague that can wipe out the living and the Scourge. Its laboratories are scattered across Forsaken territory, so researchers must share their findings to keep their work moving. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan has gathered experimental results for other field researchers. You carry them south to Renferrel at the Sepulcher. Silverpine Forest is the next frontier of Forsaken expansion and research. Apothecary Renferrel works from the Sepulcher, where he oversees biochemical testing amid threats from Moonrage worgen, rogue humans, and the lingering Scourge. He receives Johaan’s notes from Tirisfal Glades and folds their alchemical findings into his own local experiments, advancing the Society’s design.

quest:446.text: Thule Ravenclaw. A courier brings strange Rot Hide ichor to Bethor Iceshard, who recognizes the work of his traitorous former colleague, Thule Ravenclaw. To help the Forsaken resist the gnolls, Bethor prepares a scroll of counter-incantations for Apothecary Renferrel. At the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Bethor Iceshard recognizes the arcane mark in a courier’s sample of Rot Hide ichor. Thule Ravenclaw made the distillation. Before the Third War, Thule was a bright young mage and Bethor’s colleague. When the Lich King rose to power, Thule betrayed his peers and swore himself to the Scourge. As Lordaeron fell, he abandoned his humanity.

quest:447.text: A Recipe For Death. In Silverpine, A Recipe For Death gathers reagents for the Forsaken's New Plague. Apothecary Renferrel sends bear hearts and spider blood from the Sepulcher to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. In Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel sees the danger facing Sylvanas's people. Arthas's legions press them, and remnants of humanity remain their foes. Conventional warfare offers little hope. The Forsaken seek a New Plague that can rot living humans and undead Scourge alike. Renferrel's field research found that arachnid venom from the Skittering Dark, joined with toxins in the hearts of native bears, makes a virulent foundation. The collected organs and blood from Silverpine's wilderness go beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell oversees the Royal Apothecary Society's design. He takes Renferrel's samples to test their contaminable properties and refine formulas that may secure Forsaken supremacy across the continent.

quest:448.text: Report to Hadrec. Apothecary Renferrel sends you to Hadrec as the Scourge threat grows. After Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard investigate the Scourge presence in Lake Lordamere, High Executor Hadrec directs Silverpine's military preparations against Fenris Isle. Apothecary Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard have studied the danger posed by the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. But study alone cannot break the Scourge stronghold rising on Fenris Isle. Ravenclaw is binding the restless dead there, and Renferrel sees that alchemy and magic will not be enough. The Forsaken military must bring its steel and discipline to bear, so Renferrel sends you to the commander. High Executor Hadrec directs Silverpine Forest's strategic operations for the Dark Lady from the Sepulcher's crypts. Bethor's warnings about Ravenclaw reach him, and Hadrec knows a necromancer entrenched on Lordamere's western shore threatens Undercity's flank. He opens the local garrison's armory to equip the vanguard before sending them against the island fortress.

quest:449.text:
The Deathstalkers' Report. Near the northern wilds, the Deathstalkers have found Scourge forces where the Forsaken did not expect them. You carry their report from the wounded scouts to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher, bringing word that Silverpine Forest holds a greater threat than command believed. The Deathstalkers scout ahead for the Dark Lady, slipping into wild country before the main forces. Near the border of Tirisfal and Silverpine, one patrol met fierce resistance while tracking enemy movements.

Deathstalker Quinn barely survived his wounds, while Erland fought his way to safety. Their patrol still gathered intelligence the Forsaken need to hold Silverpine Forest. High Executor Hadrec reads the sealed report and learns that the Scourge hold a stronger presence in Silverpine than Undercity strategists expected. Their forces are more active and aggressive than command believed.

The Forsaken had planned to secure abandoned human hamlets and drive off rogue beasts. Now the Sepulcher's command must prepare for organized Scourge opposition as it fights to claim the region.

quest:4495.text: A Good Friend. At Aldrassil, Dirania Silvershine grows worried when Iverron misses his daily visit. She asks travelers to search the hills near Shadowthread Cave, north of Shadowglen. Dirania Silvershine waits beneath Aldrassil for Iverron, who visits her every day. Hours pass without him, and she asks travelers heading into Shadowglen to look for her friend. Iverron often wanders the hills in northern Shadowglen, near the webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. The spiders make the surrounding slopes dangerous for travelers. Search west of the cave entrance, where Iverron is hiding and needs help.

quest:45.text: Discover Rolf's Fate. Guard Thomas waits for news of Rolf and Malakai, missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks point toward a murloc village. Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints mark the mud and lead east along the water's edge. They run straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

quest:450.text: A Recipe For Death. From the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell sends you to Pyrewood Village in A Recipe For Death. You seek Apothecary Berard's notes on the ancient blight that wiped out Lake Lordamere's aquatic life. Apothecary Berard once stood among the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising researchers. He worked in Pyrewood Village, studying past ecological disasters for the Forsaken's alchemical pursuits. Then Archmage Arugal unleashed shadow magic across Silverpine Forest, and Berard fell under its curse. His mind gave way, binding him as a servant to the mage.

quest:451.text: A Recipe For Death. Apothecary Renferrel sends you to gather rare reagents across Lake Lordamere. Berard's journal names mosses and a strange tumor, which you bring to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. The Royal Apothecary Society needs them for its work on a New Plague. Apothecary Berard's death under Arugal's curse cost the Royal Apothecary Society a skilled researcher. His field journal survived, preserving what he learned about blighted life in Silverpine Forest and Lake Lordamere. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel studied the recovered notes and found Berard's account of promising properties in local freshwater organisms. Now Renferrel asks you to carry forward the work his colleague began. Berard's reagents lie among the Dawning Isles, mist-shrouded islands in the eastern waters of Lake Lordamere. Lake skulkers and lake creepers on the isles carry peculiar moss strains that live in tainted water. Berard also noted a hardened tumor among the fierce Vile Fin murloc tribes that nest along the islets and the lake's southern shoreline near Ambermill.

quest:4512.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle seeks ooze samples from Felwood for his studies. He hopes to learn why the Royal Apothecary Society gathers them and what interests the Undercity's alchemists. Laris Geardawdle studies oozes with the Explorers' League. Most of its scholars seek titan relics or dwarven genealogies, but these living puddles resist ordinary classification. They appear in wetlands, cursed woods, and damp ruins. Laris has seen Forsaken apothecaries collecting slime across Lordaeron, and wants to know what draws them to it. Laris believes oozes may be primordial secretions tied to Azeroth's creation. He thinks they are neither vermin nor magical byproducts. To test his theory, you travel across the ocean to Felwood's blighted canopy. There, you gather Cursed and Tainted Oozes in specially made jars. For Laris and many displaced gnomes, these studies carry personal weight. Since Gnomeregan fell to troggs and radiation, thousands have taken refuge in Ironforge's Great Forge. A discovery for the Explorers' League could answer dwarven skeptics. It could show that welcoming gnomes into the mountain city has become an enduring asset to Alliance science.

quest:4513.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. Laris Geardawdle seeks pure oozes across Kalimdor. His Felwood-tainted samples showed that oozes absorb and reflect their surroundings. Clean specimens may show him how they adapt to the places they inhabit. Laris Geardawdle needs clean samples for his study. The tainted ones showed how oozes take on the traits of their surroundings, but left him without a clear comparison. He seeks samples untouched by demonic taint or urban filth, so he can study ooze life on its own.

quest:452.text: Pyrewood Ambush. Deathstalker Faerleia waits in Pyrewood Village, where Arugal's council keeps the afflicted in line. The Forsaken aim to break his hold on the town and weaken his position in Shadowfang Keep. Deathstalker Faerleia waits inside Pyrewood Village's town hall for the local leaders. Archmage Arugal keeps to Shadowfang Keep, tending his dark sorceries, and leaves the Pyrewood Council to maintain order among the afflicted villagers. Faerleia plans to strike the council in an ambush. Without its mediation, the Forsaken hope the worgen in the surrounding woods and village streets will break free of Arugal's control.

quest:454.text: After the Ambush. Miran needs an escort to carry blasting powder to Loch Modan’s southern excavation site. Dark Iron dwarves ambushed the supply run, and the road is still dangerous. Saean and his conspirators attacked the supply run. Barrels were scattered, and the road became perilous. Huldar remains behind to guard the powder left there. Miran prepares to move ahead with the next load, so the supply line is split. The southern excavation site needs blasting powder to break stone and uncover titan relics. Miran fears another ambush from the ridges. He seeks a companion before loading his cargo and setting out past any traps the Dark Irons may have prepared.

quest:456.text: The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine calls newly awakened night elves to tend Shadowglen’s wildlife. Young nightsabers and thistle boars have grown too numerous, and keeping Teldrassil’s natural harmony calls for stewardship and difficult choices. In Shadowglen, beneath the Great Tree’s sprawling boughs, heavy spring rains have disrupted Teldrassil’s young, fragile forest cycle. Some wildlife populations have grown beyond what the land can sustain. They threaten to strip the glen of resources and bring famine to the ecosystem. Preserving the forest calls for active care. Conservator Ilthalaine watches over Shadowglen’s woods, keeping any one part from overtaking the others. To prevent mass starvation among the animals, he sends young night elves into the grove to thin thistle boars and predatory nightsabers. The work is unglamorous, but vital: kaldorei stewardship means seeking harmony with nature through active balance and difficult decisions.

quest:457.text: The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine sends defenders into Shadowglen to thin its growing wildlife. Mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers threaten the glade's balance. Shadowglen's adult animals now threaten the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine sends young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers. Their appetites can exhaust the land's limited plants and game. North of Aldrassil, younger cubs give way to mottled nightsabers and aggressive boars that root through the soil. For kaldorei, controlled hunting is a grim duty, but it protects the whole forest from collapse.

quest:458.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm hears troubling whispers from the forest spirits. He asks you to find Tarindrella, an elusive dryad whose unexpected return hints at trouble beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Melithar Staghelm receives troubling omens from the woodland spirits while training novices beneath Aldrassil’s boughs. Tarindrella, a dryad regarded as a protector of the wild, has returned to Shadowglen after many years away from Kalimdor’s woodlands. Dryads rarely appear without cause, and Melithar fears the natural order is out of balance.

quest:459.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella seeks the cause of the forest’s sudden unrest and the furbolgs’ disappearance. Grells have turned aggressive, and Fel Moss points to dark magic in Teldrassil’s boughs. Shadowglen’s quiet woods have grown hostile. The furbolgs have left their ancestral dens and gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Feral grells and grellkin now overrun the woodland paths, and Tarindrella has noticed the dark change spreading through Teldrassil. Tarindrella suspects corruption is stirring the forest’s creatures. You slay the grells and bring her samples of Fel Moss, evidence of dark enchantments clinging to Teldrassil’s boughs. With the corruption confirmed, she sends young defenders to Dolanaar to speak with Druid Athridas Bearmantle.

quest:46.text: Bounty on Murlocs. In eastern Elwynn, murlocs are spreading, and the Stormwind Army has set a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a small nuisance now threatens eastern Elwynn, though the western roads remain comparatively secure. Guard Thomas is stationed at the eastern bridge beside the Redridge Mountains. Dangers beyond the bridge and disorder at home both call for his attention. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and bureaucracy weighs on Stormwind's military command. Town garrisons rarely receive the reinforcements they request. So Marshal Dughan and local officers offer public bounties, paying coin for murloc fins to slow the attacks along the waterways.

quest:460.text: Resting in Pieces. On Fenris Isle, Resting in Pieces begins with Alaric's animated, severed head. He asks to be carried across Fenris Keep to an unmarked grave near the stables, where the rest of his remains lie. Alaric once served as Thule Ravenclaw's chief servant and personal bodyguard at Fenris Keep in Silverpine Forest. Thule was a powerful mage aligned with the Scourge. When the Plague of Undeath swept through the region, he promised his sorcery would shield Alaric from it. Instead, the ward trapped Alaric in endless agony and undeath, with his awareness intact in his severed parts. Thule created the rot hide gnolls by infecting local packs with necromantic decay, then turned against his own bodyguard. He cut off Alaric's head and threw it to the savage gnolls as a diversion. The rot hides dragged Alaric's body to a shallow, hastily dug grave outside the keep's stables. They kept his speaking head as a grim plaything until an outsider intervened.

quest:461.text: The Hidden Niche. Alaric's memories lead you back into Fenris Keep. His remains point toward a forgotten alcove where he seeks rest and an old relic waits. Alaric remembers Fenris Keep in its better days. Horde scouts have lifted his bones from a shallow grave outside the stronghold, but he will not go quietly to the Sepulcher. He offers vital knowledge instead: a hidden niche in the keep's southwestern tower holds an item treasured by Thule Ravenclaw and his fellow mages.

quest:4681.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore's misty coast, dead sea creatures have drawn Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde into a troubling inquiry. She serves the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and seeks to learn why marine life is stranding or dying along the shore. Dead sea creatures line Darkshore's beaches and shallows, puzzling the night elves of Auberdine. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde has already examined one stranded creature along the beach. Now she asks you to dive west of the docks, near a sunken vessel, and inspect the bones of a massive sea turtle. The evidence will help her report to the Temple of the Moon.

quest:47.text: Gold Dust Exchange. At Goldshire's crossroads, Gold Dust Exchange brings Remy "Two Times" coin for gold dust from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. Travelers gather the dust and trade it to the nervous broker for pay. Goldshire sits where Elwynn Forest's roads meet. Travelers, merchants, and guards pass through town. Remy "Two Times" is a shady broker with a sharp eye for profit. He repeats his words, and instead of hiring mining crews to dig raw minerals, he offers coin to travelers passing through the Lion's Pride Inn for gold dust taken from kobolds in the region. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. These rat-like tunnelers chip through the dark for candles and shiny baubles, gathering flecks of unrefined ore in their pouches. Driving them back serves the kingdom. Their gold dust also turns the work into a trade for coin.

quest:4722.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s surf-battered shore, a massive sea turtle lies beached as murlocs pick over its carcass. Viable biological samples remain among the scavenged remains, and Auberdine naturalists send them to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for study. Darkshore’s long coast often catches the dead and confused from the Great Sea. Ancient sea turtles drift ashore after death or beach themselves in confusion. Their carcasses quickly draw scavengers, and hostile Greymist murlocs have made crude camps around this turtle’s skeletal frame. They carve away flesh and shell, yet viable bone, shell, or tissue samples may remain intact in the wreckage. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is stationed in Auberdine as a field researcher, documenting unusual marine life and ecological disturbances along the coast. Night elves regard stranded beasts with reverence and scientific curiosity. Suitable remains are cataloged and prepared for shipment to scholars in Darnassus, who seek to understand why so many giants of the open sea are washing ashore.

quest:4723.text: Beached Sea Creature. At Mist's Edge, a giant sea thresher lies stranded while murlocs feed on its carcass. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples for night elf researchers in Darnassus, who seek to learn why deep-sea giants are washing ashore. Enormous thresher remains have appeared along Mist's Edge, where shipwrecks and tide-washed debris are familiar sights. This beast dwarfs the wildlife of Darkshore's shallows, suggesting it came from far beyond the calm waters of the Veiled Sea. Murlocs swarm over the corpse to feed, but they lack the strength and coordination to bring down a creature of this size. Something else killed the predator before the sea carried it ashore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde coordinates efforts in Auberdine to salvage bones and biological samples from Darkshore's stranded sea giants. Night elf researchers in Darnassus hope the remains will show whether illness, disturbances in the deep sea, or arcane corruption drives the giants onto the killing sands.

quest:4725.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's shore, Beached Sea Turtle lies with a broken carriage on its shell. Greymist murlocs have gathered around the great carcass.
