You find a broken carriage strapped across a giant sea turtle's shell on Darkshore's misty shore. Many sea creatures have washed up along this coast, but this turtle was made to carry a load. Its handlers drove it onto the beach, and the carriage now lies abandoned in the tide. Greymist murlocs soon swarm the turtle's remains. They have made a den among the rotting meat and scavenged timber. A marked container lies among their refuse and the broken carriage frame, left by the turtle's former masters.

quest:4727.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s northern shore, Beached Sea Turtle remains untouched by nearby Greymist murlocs. A sample is carried to Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon. Naturalists and priestesses seek to learn why great sea creatures wash ashore and scavengers leave them alone. Greymist murlocs crowd Darkshore’s northern coast and scavenge whatever food washes up from the Veiled Sea. Yet the great turtle’s skeleton lies mostly untouched. Those studying the shore wonder whether the murlocs missed it or avoided it for some unknown reason. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples from beached sea turtles for the Temple of the Moon. The night elf priestesses study the disturbances in Darkshore’s waters. Skeletal fragments may help them learn whether sickness, magic, or dangerous sea predators are killing the ancient creatures.

quest:4728.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a giant sea mammal lies washed ashore beside an abandoned dig site. Its carcass and scattered tools draw murlocs and passing travelers. A giant sea mammal lies on Darkshore's sand, partly gutted and worn by the sea. A rusted wheelbarrow and discarded tools mark the place where an organized study began. The researchers left before they could finish. Dwarven field researchers from the Explorer's League were studying the carcass in Darkshore. Their work stopped when local murlocs swarmed the site to scavenge. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine acts for the Temple of the Moon and accepts salvaged bone samples to help study the unnatural wash-ups along the coast.

quest:4730.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a great sea mammal lies half-devoured on the sand. Murlocs gather around it, and Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples to learn why gentle sea beasts are dying on the shore. Far north along Darkshore's lonely beaches, a great sea mammal lies rotting and half-eaten. Murlocs pick over its bones, more vicious than usual. These beasts were gentle in life, and their deaths trouble the coast as much as the blighted forests inland. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde says these gentle mammals live in the waters around Teldrassil's base. Unlike aggressive threshers, they have never been known to drive themselves onto the rocks. The Temple of the Moon is gathering bone samples to learn what corruption or threat drives them from the deep.

quest:4731.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's coast, a Beached Sea Turtle lies dead beneath the carriage it once hauled. A box marked with strange runes rests in the wreckage. A dead sea turtle lies among the ancient bones scattered along Darkshore's coast. Splintered carriage boards still cling to its broad shell. The turtle was driven onto the rocks while hauling cargo, rather than stranded by sickness or disorientation. A container carved with unfamiliar, serpent-like marks lies in the wreckage, amid scavengers feeding on the remains.

quest:4732.text:
Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore, Beached Sea Turtle remains wash ashore in growing numbers. Their bones give Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine specimens to study as Kalimdor's marine life dwindles. Great sea creatures and turtles lie along Darkshore's shore. Many ancient turtles drift onto the shoals or crawl onto the sand to die. Greymist murlocs gather at the carcasses and strip away the flesh. Soon, only shell and bone remain, beside crude camps they make there. Before the Third War, sea turtles thrived in the sacred waters around Mount Hyjal and the roots of Nordrassil, the World Tree. After Nordrassil's sacrifice against the Burning Legion and Teldrassil's planting off Kalimdor's northern shore, their numbers collapsed.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde and other priestesses of Elune study the remains for the Temple of the Moon. They seek to learn whether dark magic, changing seas, or the loss of the turtles' ancient sanctuary drives them to their deaths.

quest:4733.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore's rocky Twilight Shore, a colossal thresher lies stranded, far larger than any known local specimen. Its death and stranding add to the deep-sea troubles worrying the night elves. You find driftwood and sea debris along the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore, but one inlet holds the remains of an enormous thresher. Tides and scavengers have begun picking it apart, yet its skeleton dwarfs ordinary predators in these coastal shallows. The giant is an outsider to these waters. Sickness or disorientation may have driven it onto the rocks, or some deeper disturbance may lie out in the Veiled Sea.

quest:4740.text: WANTED: Murkdeep!. Auberdine posts an Alliance bounty for Murkdeep, blamed for a Sentinel's death and ships lost off Darkshore. The village council wants the dangerous murloc chieftain dead. Find him south along the misty coast. The Greymist murlocs along Darkshore are usually a nuisance, but Murkdeep has turned against Auberdine. The wanted poster outside the inn names him as the killer of at least one night elf Sentinel. It also suspects him of sabotaging or wrecking two cargo vessels offshore. With ships lost and raids along the coast, the Auberdine Village Council has set a public bounty on the murloc leader. Murkdeep lurks off the southern coast, near murloc huts clustered around a bonfire. Trespassers draw an organized defense: Greymist coastrunners and shore-crawlers surge from the surf to protect their settlement. Murkdeep then emerges alongside his vanguard to strike the intruders. Proof of Murkdeep's death meets a grim need for the Sentinels. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea handles the bounty payout for the council. With Greymist leadership broken, travelers and ships on the foggy Darkshore coast gain a reprieve from sabotage.

quest:475.text: A Troubling Breeze. Athridas Bearmantle waits for word from Starbreeze Village, but the reports have stopped. Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren watches over the sleeping Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, and his silence points to danger in Teldrassil. Athridas Bearmantle depends on regular word from Gaerolas Talvethren, the Great Warden watching over the Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The druids sleep there to keep their sacred pact with Ysera in the Emerald Dream. Their sanctuary matters to the spiritual balance of the young World Tree. Now reports from the east have ceased, and unease spreads through the forest.

quest:476.text: Gnarlpine Corruption. Near Starbreeze Village, Gnarlpine Corruption threatens Teldrassil. Wounded Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren sends word to the night elf leadership in Dolanaar: Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the village and fallen to demonic corruption. Their violence may reach the sleeping druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Near the ruins of Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren lies grievously wounded after an ambush by his former allies. The Gnarlpine furbolgs were long regarded as peaceful neighbors and stewards of the wild, but now they have turned feral. Too injured to carry the warning himself, Gaerolas entrusts you with bringing word to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the madness spreads farther through Teldrassil.

quest:4761.text: Thundris Windweaver. In Auberdine, reports of Blackwood aggression reach the village elder. Terenthis sends you to Thundris Windweaver with news of the furbolgs’ growing hostility. Thundris seeks the cause of the corruption spreading through Darkshore. After scouting corrupted furbolg camps in Darkshore, you carry Terenthis’s report to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Terenthis remains in the wilds to investigate the spreading corruption. As village elder, Thundris oversees the settlement’s daily welfare and considers the spiritual and environmental dangers facing the kaldorei. Your report gives Auberdine’s leadership evidence that the furbolgs are growing more than territorial: an unnatural malice is taking hold of them. Thundris has heard of rising hostility from the forest dwellers near Auberdine. The furbolgs’ aggression is not the only concern. Corruption is spreading through Darkshore’s soil, plants, and waters. Thundris believes the land cannot be healed until the source of the blight is found. He turns to the waterways and enlists capable allies to trace the taint upstream.

quest:4762.text: The Cliffspring River. In Darkshore, foul water now runs down the Cliffspring River toward Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver asks Alliance investigators to take a sample from the pool beneath a road bridge waterfall. He suspects the corruption began beyond the riverbanks. The Cliffspring River runs from the eastern highlands to the coastal shoals of Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Its waters have begun to carry an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Thundris Windweaver fears the foul water will poison the shores and the town's supplies, so he sends scouts upriver to take samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

quest:4763.text: The Blackwood Corrupted. In northern Darkshore, the Blackwood Corrupted are caught in a dark influence. Evidence in the tainted waters of Cliffspring River leads Thundris Windweaver to send you against it. You gather their food and purify it with moonwell water, drawing the demonic handler into the open and breaking his hold on the northern camp. In Auberdine, the night elves have long wondered why the once-peaceful Blackwood furbolgs turned on their neighbors. Their search along Cliffspring River traced the rot to satyr meddling. These ancient servants of the Burning Legion manipulate the tribe with fel magic. Insidious talismans twist the furbolgs' minds and drive them into feral aggression.

quest:477.text: Border Crossings. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends you to intercept Dalaran's supplies and learn why the Kirin Tor support Ambermill. The crates travel through Silverpine Forest toward a Dalaran camp near Pyrewood Village. Dalaran magi send wagons of supplies and arcane goods from the Hillsbrad Foothills through Silverpine Forest. Their shipments support outposts and staging grounds along the way. A camp just north of Pyrewood Village holds Dalaran personnel who watch the road. The human resistance at Ambermill is the main surviving stronghold in eastern Silverpine, and Dalaran has not left it to fend for itself. Shadow Priest Allister and the Forsaken leaders at the Sepulcher want to know why Dalaran commits so much to Ambermill. They suspect the Kirin Tor would not risk lives and supplies deep in Forsaken territory merely for a provincial town. A greater strategic or magical purpose may lie behind that support. Intercepting the crates can show the Forsaken what Dalaran is sending west.

quest:478.text: Maps and Runes. In Silverpine Forest, maps and runes point to Dalaran's interest in Ambermill. A hidden crate holds regional charts and a rune-inscribed pendant, which adventurers recover for Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher. Horde agents find a Dalaran crate hidden along the border routes near Ambermill. Inside are detailed regional charts and an enigmatic pendant inscribed with runes. With human sentries nearby, the scouts retrieve the artifact carefully, wary of Dalaran's arcane reach so close to their borders.

quest:479.text: Ambermill Investigations. In Ambermill, Dalaran wizards are weaving magic that threatens the Forsaken's hold on Silverpine Forest. Shadow Priest Allister sends agents from the Sepulcher to disrupt their spellwork and seize the magical foci. Ambermill is a human town in the hills of eastern Silverpine Forest, held by wizards and defenders pledged to the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. The mages are weaving magical energies in a vast ritual. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister and his companion Dalar recognize the danger. If the Kirin Tor channel their power unchecked, the Forsaken risk being driven from Silverpine entirely. While Dalar scries the forest and traces the flow of magic, Allister sends agents to strike the practitioners in Ambermill. Dalaran conjurers, mages, and their protectors wear enchanted pendants that focus and coordinate their arts. Taking the talismans from slain sorcerers disrupts the ritual and gives the Sepulcher time to find the ringleader directing the arcane weave.

quest:481.text: Dalar's Analysis. In Silverpine, Allister's report sends a Dalaran relic to Dalar for study. A rune-inscribed pendant taken from a supply crate reaches Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. The relic shows that Dalaran's surviving mages are gathering great magical power for a hidden purpose. A supply crate from Dalaran is raided at a camp north of Pyrewood Village. Beneath old maps, Shadow Priest Allister finds a rune-inscribed pendant. Its enchantment is beyond his spiritual knowledge, so he sends it to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. Dalar's skill as an arcane scholar makes him better suited to read Dalaran's magical warding.

quest:4811.text: The Red Crystal. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea asks travelers in Auberdine to investigate a red crystal in Darkshore's eastern mountains. Hostile moonkin are multiplying nearby and seem drawn to it, and the Sentinels need to know if the formation is real. Moonkin were long seen as gentle, mystical creatures bound to the wilds of Kalimdor. Now aggressive packs are multiplying along the slopes east of Auberdine. Some night elves still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea puts the town's safety first as the danger grows. Reports place the beasts at a single spot among the eastern peaks. Scouts and wanderers speak of an unnatural red crystal jutting from a rocky hillside high above Darkshore. Rumors travel easily along the fogbound coast, so Glynda wants someone to see the place firsthand. The crystal is real, and the Sentinels still need to learn why the moonkin gather there and whether it threatens the land.

quest:4812.text: As Water Cascades. Sacred water is brought to bear on the red crystal in Darkshore. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea hopes moonwell water from Auberdine will reveal what lies beneath its opaque surface. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea seeks a safe way to study the red crystal high on Darkshore's eastern cliffs. Moonwell water holds divine, restorative magic, blessed by the night elves' devotion to Elune. Glynda believes water from Auberdine's moonwell may react with the strange stone and pierce its opaque shell without destroying it.

quest:4813.text: The Fragments Within. At the eastern cliffs, you return to the red crystal with water from a moonwell. It may reveal what lies within, and you carry the finding back to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea in Auberdine. Back in Auberdine, you tell Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea what you found. The discovery gives the local night elf leaders more cause for concern, but no clear answers. Glynda will present the findings to the town council. The crystal rests high on the eastern cliffs, far enough from town to bring her some comfort; it poses no immediate danger.

quest:482.text: Dalaran's Intentions. Dalar Dawnweaver sends Shadow Priest Allister a warning from Silverpine Forest. A pendant bound for the Kirin Tor in Ambermill reveals their plan to awaken a dormant ley energy node beneath the town, and the Forsaken at the Sepulcher prepare to answer. Dalar Dawnweaver studies a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate and recalls an old Kirin Tor survey. Ambermill was chosen for a reason: the quiet village sits atop a dormant ley energy node. Dalar realizes the wizards intend to tap it. Awakening such a nexus takes immense magical reserves, and the enchanted pendants the wizards wear are key to channeling and catalyzing its power. The Forsaken cannot tolerate a fortified, power-fueled Kirin Tor outpost threatening the southern approaches to the Sepulcher and Tirisfal Glades. Whatever ritual the magi prepare, raw ley energy would give Dalaran an enormous strategic advantage in Lordaeron. Dalar urgently sends word to Shadow Priest Allister, asking him to devise a way to stall the wizards before their ritual is complete.

quest:483.text: The Relics of Wakening. At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, an urgent effort is underway to save the sleeping Druids of the Talon. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the sacred mounds, threatening the druids whose spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Four ritual relics are needed to bring the sleepers safely back to the waking world. West of Dolanaar, a swarm of corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs has overrun the winding corridors of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Barrow dens are secluded sanctuaries where night elf druids hibernate while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. A foul taint spreading across Teldrassil has driven these former allies mad. They have desecrated the sanctum, leaving the sleepers unaware that danger threatens their physical bodies. Athridas Bearmantle needs four sacred relics for the delicate ceremony that can safely awaken the Druids of the Talon. A druid's spirit needs an anchor when returning from the Dream; without one, a sudden awakening can shatter the mind or strand the spirit. The relics lie in chests across the den: the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. They are the sleepers' only hope before the Gnarlpine butcher or abduct them.

quest:486.text: Ursal the Mauler. In Teldrassil, Athridas Bearmantle seeks to wake the Druids of the Talon from their unnatural sleep. Their kin remain trapped in the Barrow Den, and the corrupted Gnarlpine chief behind the disturbance must be slain. The Druids of the Talon withdrew to the Barrow Den of Ban'ethil to sleep and commune with the Emerald Dream. Their peaceful trance became a prison with no way back to waking. Athridas Bearmantle traced the trouble to the gnarlpine furbolgs, and to their vicious leader, Ursal the Mauler, who meddled with the druids' sacred ritual. The sleepers remain caught between waking and the Dream. Athridas needs more than the Relics of Wakening to reach the druids through the spiritual fog. The source of the interference must be ended. Ursal the Mauler makes his lair in Gnarlpine Hold, the tribe's home in far southwestern Teldrassil. Striking down the furbolg warlord breaks his hold on the sleepers' minds.

quest:487.text: The Road to Darnassus. Along Teldrassil’s western road, corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs threaten the route from Dolanaar to Darnassus. Moon Priestess Amara coordinates scouts and travelers to keep this trade and messenger road clear of ambushes. You travel west from Dolanaar toward Darnassus on Teldrassil’s main overland road. Trade goods, political messages, and travelers use it each day to stay connected with the capital and the boughs of the great tree. Teldrassil is young and wild, so safe roads matter to its kaldorei communities. The Gnarlpine furbolgs of Teldrassil have fallen to a foul corruption. Driven mad by a sickness plaguing the boughs of the World Tree, they attack from hidden dens beneath the ridges. Gnarlpine ambushers stalk the tree line beside the road, preying on couriers and travelers and making the forest passage deadly. Moon Priestess Amara watches over the road outside Dolanaar. She joins the spiritual authority of Elune’s priesthood with the Sentinels’ vigilance, directing capable travelers to strike at ambushers near their dens below the road. The safety of the route to Darnassus’s gates depends on keeping them at bay.

quest:488.text: Zenn's Bidding. Zenn Foulhoof draws newcomers into his schemes north of the road from Shadowglen to Dolanaar. The solitary satyr asks them to gather animal parts, preying on their trust and naivety. Travelers on the path from Shadowglen to Dolanaar may find Zenn Foulhoof beneath the Great Tree. The satyr offers material rewards and secrets for simple work, asking for nightsaber fangs, strigid owl feathers, and webwood spider silk from the surrounding woods. He whispers conspiratorially, urging travelers to keep their bargain between themselves.

quest:489.text: Seek Redemption!. In Dolanaar, you face the Council of the Forest's demand for atonement. Adventurers were duped into doing Zenn Foulhoof's dirty work, and now the council sends you to trick the satyr into eating corrupted fel cones. Just outside Dolanaar, solitary satyr Zenn Foulhoof uses deceit to make passersby do his bidding. Adventurers who unwittingly slaughtered nightsabers, strigid owls, and webwood spiders to satisfy his twisted appetites draw the Council of the Forest's sharp disapproval. The council will not accept harm to nature, especially from its own allies. Syral Bladeleaf, Sentinel Kyra Starsong, or Sentinel Shayla Nightbreeze warns you that you must make amends to remain welcome in Teldrassil. Dolanaar's guardians tell you to turn Foulhoof's wicked gluttony against him instead of facing him with steel. Gather the billowing, corrupted fel cones from the forest floor, then offer the unsuspecting satyr a taste of his own foul medicine.

quest:491.text: Wand to Bethor. At Fenris Keep, the confrontation ends with the Woven Wand bound for Bethor Iceshard. Three apprentice mages made it as a sign of fellowship, but Thule Ravenclaw hid it after choosing the Scourge. Its return brings a piece of Bethor's mortal youth back to the Undercity. Before Lordaeron fell, three young mages joined their training wands into one, the Woven Wand. It marked their friendship and shared hopes in the magical arts. Thule Ravenclaw later gave his loyalty to the Lich King and embraced the Scourge, breaking their fellowship. He came to despise the friendship they had shared, yet could not destroy the wand or leave it with his former companions.

quest:492.text: A New Plague. In Brill, A New Plague reaches its first test on a captive dwarf. Apothecary Johaan sends you to Gallows' End Tavern cellar with the brew he has made from reagents gathered across Tirisfal Glades. Apothecary Johaan has brought his research to a dangerous trial. The Royal Apothecary Society works for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, seeking a plague that kills the living while bypassing undead bodies. Johaan has brewed what he calls a “special drink” and sends you to give it to an imprisoned enemy of the Forsaken. The Deathguard holds captives in a damp cellar beneath Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, where they await interrogation or disposal. One prisoner is a Dwarven Mountaineer, an Ironforge scout caught trespassing in Tirisfal Glades. Defiant and thirsty, he eagerly accepts the drink, unaware of what Johaan has mixed into it.

quest:5041.text: Supplies for the Crossroads. Thork needs supplies back at the Crossroads after Razormane quilboar raids. The stolen crates hold provisions the outpost needs amid conflict across the Barrens. Thork needs provisions restored to the Crossroads after a supply caravan is ambushed. The outpost links Horde travel, trade, and defense across the Barrens, and cargo arrives from Durotar and Mulgore. Without it, shortages of provisions, tools, and arms threaten daily life in the harsh wilderness. Razormane quilboar have taken the crates. These swine-beasts contest Horde control across central Kalimdor. They hauled the cargo to their thorn-bush camps and keep it there. Thork sends trusted warriors into Razormane territory to recover the supplies for the Horde.

quest:5061.text: Aquatic Form. You return to Darnassus with the restored Pendant of the Sea Lion. The rite teaches Alliance druids to attune their spirits to deep waters. For Cenarion Circle initiates, shapeshifting joins the druid’s spirit to the wild aspects of Azeroth. After enduring trials in the dark coastal depths and in Moonglade, young night elf druids receive the assembled Pendant of the Sea Lion from Dendrite Starblaze. They carry the sacred token back to Teldrassil as proof of their respect for the laws of air, water, and breath. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits your return in the Cenarion Enclave. The trials along the coasts of Darkshore and Westfall demand endurance and attunement. Presenting the completed pendant shows Bearwalker that your mind and body are ready to shed their mortal skin and take the swift, breathing form of the sea lion.

quest:52.text: Protect the Frontier. At Elwynn's eastern bridge, Guard Thomas asks you to thin the wolves and bears threatening travelers and workers near Eastvale Logging Camp. The beasts have grown bold, putting roads and logging crews at risk. Goldshire and Northshire Valley have visible Stormwind garrisons. The eastern frontier has far fewer guards. Guard Thomas watches the river crossing, one of the few sentries between the settled heartlands and the wilderness. Travelers help keep the supply roads open. Eastvale Logging Camp sends timber to Stormwind City. Woodsmen cutting trees at the forest's edge face prowlers, gray forest wolves, and young forest bears near the roads and lumber yards. Culling the beasts eases the danger to local workers for a time. Thomas suspects something deeper in the woods is driving them toward settlements.

quest:5261.text: Eagan Peltskinner. Timber wolves threaten Northshire Valley, and Eagan Peltskinner has work for recruits outside the abbey. The local furrier needs hunters to thin the packs and bring back pelts. Deputy Willem often sends abbey recruits to find Eagan Peltskinner on the nearby grounds. Northshire Valley's orchards and fields meet wild woods where timber wolves prowl. Eagan asks newcomers to hunt the aggressive packs and gather pelts for his craft. Timber wolves threaten workers, acolytes, and supplies traveling to and from Northshire. Sending young champions to Eagan helps keep nearby paths safe and leaves Stormwind's few remaining guards free for other duties. Those guards are already occupied by rising tensions across Elwynn Forest.

quest:543.text: The Perenolde Tiara. Count Remington Ridgewell sends mercenaries into the Ruins of Alterac for a lost heirloom. The Perenolde Tiara once adorned Alterac's royal family and now rests with an ogre mage. Alterac's royal family wore an emerald-set tiara made by master dwarven jewelers in Ironforge. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Grand Alliance and joined the Orcish Horde. Alterac was conquered and collapsed. When Alterac City fell, many royal treasures vanished among the snowy rubble of the Alterac Mountains. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage among the Crushridge ogres, holds the tiara in the ruins. He searches the broken stones for baubles and abandoned wealth. Count Remington Ridgewell, a collector of historical oddities in Stormwind City, learns the tiara survived. He hires mercenaries to enter ogre-held territory, defeat Grel'borg, and return the jewel to his gallery.

quest:5481.text: Gordo's Task. Along the road to Brill, Gordo gathers plants for the Royal Apothecary Society. The wandering abomination cannot manage delicate work, so he asks travelers to pick Gloom Weed and bring it to Junior Apothecary Holland. Between Deathknell and Brill, Gordo trudges through the countryside on the Royal Apothecary Society's behalf. Abominations can fight with brute strength and haul heavy loads, but their huge, stitched hands make delicate work difficult. Sent into the meadows to gather ingredients, Gordo finds that his blunt fingers crush more stems than they pluck. He turns to passersby, bullying or bribing them to do the careful work for him.

quest:5482.text: Doom Weed. In Brill, Junior Apothecary Holland seeks doom weed for his research. The plant grows near Tirisfal's northern mass graves, where Rot Hide gnolls prowl. Junior Apothecary Holland researches for the Royal Apothecary Society from Brill. He wants doom weed to advance his experiments, but Gordo cannot tell the right plants from the wrong ones. Holland turns to more capable hands to gather what he needs. Doom weed grows thick around the mass gravesite just north of the Brill graveyard, where death and plague have tainted the soil. Rot Hide gnolls prowl the burial mounds, scavenging among the remains and guarding the overgrown trenches.

quest:5502.text: A Warden of the Horde. In Orgrimmar, Children's Week ends with Grunth's return to Orphan Matron Battlewail. After seeing the world with his guardian, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself. After the adventures of Children's Week, Grunth thanks you for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. He remembers his parents' advice to rise above hardship and hopes to become a hero like you. His final request is to return home and tell the matron about your time together. You return Grunth to Orphan Matron Battlewail at the orphanage in the Valley of Honor. In the new Horde, caring for the young is a profound duty, since war has left countless children without parents. Battlewail praises your compassion as the true measure of a Horde hero. Grunth parts with a beloved pet so you will remember the bond formed during your travels.

quest:5541.text: Ammo for Rumbleshot. Outside Anvilmar, Hegnar Rumbleshot needs ammunition for the riflemen at practice. A courier fled wendigo near the Grizzled Den and left a crate behind. Loslor Rudge at Steelgrill's Depot supplies tradesmen across Dun Morogh, though wildlife often disrupts his shipments. His courier had camped near the Grizzled Den cave system when local wendigo crossed his path. He fled for his life and left the heavy wooden crate in the snow. Hegnar Rumbleshot runs a gun shop beside the main road leading away from Anvilmar. Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar squads gather in the clearing outside his forge to sight their weapons and practice with live fire. Without regular deliveries of powder and lead from suppliers like Loslor, the riflemen's marksmanship practice soon comes to a halt.

quest:5545.text: A Bundle of Trouble. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Supervisor Raelen races to meet a timber shipment deadline for Stormwind. Wolves and bears have driven her woodcutters from the northern woods, leaving the cut bundles behind. Eastvale's timber rebuilds towns and strengthens bridges across the kingdom, yet this vital shipment has fallen behind. The delivery deadline is drawing near, and Supervisor Raelen has little time to spare. North of the camp, wolves and bears drove the woodcutters from the bundles they cut and tied. Raelen cannot wait for guards to clear the woods, so she asks you to bring the timber back before the contract is lost.

quest:5621.text: Garments of the Moon. Laurna Morninglight sends a young priest to aid a wounded Sentinel south of Dolanaar. The duty tests an initiate's devotion and brings formal recognition in the Sisterhood of Elune. The Sisterhood of Elune guides kaldorei in worship and helps defend Teldrassil's borders. Sentinel Shaya is wounded while patrolling the wilderness south of Dolanaar, and priest trainer Laurna Morninglight cannot leave her post to help. She asks a newly trained initiate to tend Shaya's wounds and strengthen her with protective magic. After restoring Sentinel Shaya's vigor, a priest returns to Dolanaar to receive formal robes of office from Laurna Morninglight. The robes mark an acolyte's passage from classroom instruction to practical service that can save lives. For the kaldorei, aiding the Sentinels is both service to Elune and a duty to Teldrassil's safety.

quest:5622.text: In Favor of Elune. Young night elf priests leave Shadowglen for guidance and training in Dolanaar. Priestess Shanda sends them along the forest path to Laurna Morninglight. Priestess Shanda trains initiates serving Elune within Aldrassil's secluded shelter. Their learning begins with simple prayers and defensive invocations under her watchful eye. Shadowglen's cloistered life cannot prepare a priestess or priest for the turmoil gripping the wider world. Once an initiate shows steady faith and discipline, Shanda sends them down the shadowed forest path toward Dolanaar to continue their education. Reaching Dolanaar marks an essential milestone in a night elf's divine vocation. There, respected priestess Laurna Morninglight prepares disciples for the trials facing Teldrassil. The acolyte can receive advanced instruction in moonlit spellcraft and claim their first formal vestments, marking their official standing within the Sisterhood of Elune.

quest:5623.text: In Favor of the Light. At Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta sends you south to continue your training in Goldshire. Priestess Josetta waits at the Lion's Pride Inn to guide your next steps in the Holy Light. Your training carries you beyond Northshire Abbey's cloistered halls and into the lives of Elwynn's people. You leave secluded study for active ministry, where the Holy Light must answer everyday needs beyond the abbey's walls. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Priestess Josetta tends to Goldshire's spiritual needs and guides rising acolytes. She builds on your lessons and teaches you to offer comfort, protect the faithful, and heal the injured. Under her guidance, you learn the duties of the Church's servants across the kingdom, including caring for a wounded guard and receiving ceremonial clerical vestments.

quest:5624.text: Garments of the Light. Priestess Josetta sends you east of Goldshire to Crystal Lake, where Guard Roberts lies wounded. His recovery matters to the town, and the Church of the Holy Light will recognize your service. Josetta asks you to put divine power to use before the Church recognizes a novice priest. Guard Roberts needs healing, giving you a chance to serve someone in need. Tending him is your first step toward formal standing in the Church of the Holy Light. Close Roberts's wounds with restorative prayers, then strengthen him with a blessing of fortitude. He needs healing and resilience to return to his duties. Your care helps a town guard withstand danger, and supports the township. Josetta expects a priest to sustain defenders as well as mend them. Once Roberts has been treated, return to the Lion’s Pride Inn for your first formal robes. They mark the approval and fellowship of Stormwind's priesthood, though further training does not require them. The Church recognizes you as a servant of the Holy Light.

quest:5625.text: Garments of the Light. At Maxan Anvol’s urging, you go south of Kharanos to help a wounded mountaineer before you receive the Garments of the Light. Maxan Anvol, the priest trainer, asks for practical aid before ceremony. Acolytes usually face formal trials to prove they deserve church vestments. But Mountaineer Dolf is wounded, and he needs help now. South of Kharanos, you find Mountaineer Dolf wounded in the line of duty. Restorative prayers mend his injuries. Power Word: Fortitude strengthens him and helps keep an Ironforge defender alive. Once Dolf has received aid, Maxan Anvol presents you with formal garments. The robes give warmth against Dun Morogh’s chill and mark you as a servant of the Light. You are ready to aid wounded wanderers and local guards.

quest:5626.text: In Favor of the Light. Branstock Khalder sends a young priest from Coldridge Valley through the mountain pass to Kharanos for further study. There, Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol prepares the novice for greater duties and a chance to earn their first formal vestments. You leave Anvilmar after showing dedication and understanding of Holy magic. Branstock Khalder sends promising novices beyond the mountains, where priests meet Dun Morogh’s needs and help defend its people. The Coldridge Pass tunnel opens into central Dun Morogh, where Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol guides you beyond basic prayers. He teaches that service to the Holy Light calls for moral character, physical hardiness, and an unyielding will. Prove your resolve under his guidance, and you may receive your first formal garments of office.

quest:5627.text: Stars of Elune. In Darnassus, night elf acolytes are called to the Temple of the Moon after proving their devotion to their people. There, the Sisterhood of Elune teaches them sacred arts of their faith. Night elf priests draw their holy power from Elune, their goddess, while humans and dwarves turn to the Light. When an acolyte serves the realm with steadfast devotion, the Sisterhood in Darnassus takes notice. The acolyte is summoned to the Temple of the Moon and judged ready for deeper communion. There, the priest learns sacred spells passed down through thousands of years of worship. Priestess Alathea calls the initiate to receive instruction in holy mysteries of the night elf faith, including Starshards. These spells channel the radiant wrath and grace of the White Lady. The teaching marks an acolyte's passage beyond basic training, ready to venture beyond Teldrassil's protective canopy in Elune's name.

quest:5628.text: Returning Home. In Goldshire, a novice night elf priest receives a call to return home. The novice has wandered as far as Elwynn Forest, where Priestess Josetta relays an urgent message from Darnassus: return to the Temple of the Moon and continue spiritual training under Priestess Alathea. Night elves are an unusual sight in Elwynn Forest, and a young acolyte among its human settlements draws attention. When you arrive in Goldshire, Priestess Josetta greets you warmly with news. A Sister of Elune has traveled across continents seeking you, bearing an urgent command from the Temple of the Moon. It is time to return to Kalimdor and advance your calling. At the heart of Darnassus stands the Temple of the Moon, center of night elf faith and leadership. Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversee the Sisterhood’s instruction, watching their disciples even when curiosity carries them overseas. When you return, the priestesses welcome you with motherly concern and immediately set you to deeper studies of the Moon Goddess’s celestial mysteries.

quest:5629.text: Returning Home. In Darnassus, Returning Home brings young night elf priests before the leaders of their faith. After proving themselves in Teldrassil’s wilds, they are summoned to the Temple of the Moon to meet Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Priests tending the wounded and cleansing corruption around Dolanaar draw the Sisterhood of Elune’s notice. Trainer Laurna Morninglight intercepts promising initiates with word that Priestess Alathea has asked to meet them. Aid to local settlements matters, but each devotee must also deepen their communion with the Moon Mother and answer the faith’s higher calling. The road leads from Teldrassil’s boughs to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The sanctuary rises above the city in Elune’s gentle glow. It is the kaldorei’s chief house of worship and spiritual capital. An invitation into its halls means an initiate is recognized by the priesthood’s leaders, no longer treated only as a young student. Priestess Alathea greets returning initiates warmly. She says she and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind take pride when initiates venture into the uncertain world and return unharmed. This homecoming begins deeper sacred trials under Alathea’s direct guidance.

quest:5630.text: Returning Home. A summons reaches wandering night elf priests in Dun Morogh, calling them back to Darnassus. Maxan Anvol, the dwarven priest trainer, directs them to report to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon. In Kharanos, Maxan Anvol takes note of the night elf's fortitude amid Dun Morogh's bitter cold, far from Teldrassil's serene forests. The dwarven priest trainer brings urgent word: a priestess of Elune passed through looking for the elf, carrying orders from Darnassus that demand an immediate return. The road leads across the sea to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, among Teldrassil's sacred boughs. Priestess Alathea welcomes the traveler back to the Sisterhood of Elune, relieved to see another devotee return unscathed from foreign lands. She swiftly prepares the priest for the next rites of devotion, beginning with the Stars of Elune.

quest:5631.text: Returning Home. In human lands, a night elf priest receives a summons to return to Teldrassil. Brother Joshua delivers the message from Priestess Alathea, who calls the young priest to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for advanced guidance in Elune’s mysteries. Night elf priests sometimes travel to human lands such as Stormwind to share spiritual fellowship with the Church of the Holy Light. Their deepest ties remain with the Sisterhood of Elune. Brother Joshua tells an acolyte that a night elf emissary has come searching for them. Their early travels are over, and their home temple calls them back for deeper training with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind’s inner circle. Across the sea, Darnassus welcomes the returning priest at the Temple of the Moon. Priestess Alathea greets the acolyte warmly and celebrates their safe passage through a troubled world. Their return brings joy to Alathea and Tyrande, while more demanding spiritual trials await.

quest:5632.text: Returning Home. Priestess Alathea calls promising night elf priests back to Darnassus. The summons brings them to the Temple of the Moon to be recognized by the Sisterhood of Elune and receive advanced guidance. A messenger from the Sisterhood reaches you while you visit Nara Meideros in Stormwind's Park. You have served your people abroad, and the order's leaders now require you in Darnassus. They have watched your spiritual growth and call you back for an evaluation and a rite of recognition. The journey marks your passage from a new initiate to an active servant of the Mother Moon. The summons sends you to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon, Darnassus's highest sanctuary. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversees the Sisterhood, which watches over its members wherever they serve. Your safe return to the temple honors your community and Elune. It also shows that the goddess's grace has guided and preserved you through your early trials in the wild.

quest:5633.text: Returning Home. Night elf priests in Ironforge are called back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. A Sisterhood emissary seeks out acolytes abroad and sends them to Priestess Alathea for urgent training and sacred duties. In Ironforge, night elf priests remain tied to the Sisterhood of Elune, though they are far from Teldrassil. Braenna Flintcrag, a dwarven priest trainer in the Mystic Ward, carries a message from a visiting night elf priestess. The messenger sought young disciples traveling abroad and said their mentors needed them back in the capital at once. At the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, returning acolytes report to Priestess Alathea. Beneath the watchful gaze of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, Alathea welcomes her student and is relieved they crossed the seas safely. Their return begins further devotion and sacred duties, including the Stars of Elune.

quest:5634.text: Desperate Prayer. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena teaches human acolytes a prayer for when their lives are in danger. It calls on the Holy Light to heal a priest's wounds when all else fails. Priests of the Cathedral of Light use their faith to shield companions, heal wounds, and strike at evil. Even the devout may be isolated, cornered, or close to death. In that moment, an acolyte can call to the Holy Light for help, with their own life at stake. High Priestess Laurena guides the clergy in Stormwind's Cathedral Square and decides when an acolyte is ready for deeper teachings. Human initiates who show devotion to the Light across the kingdom receive this lesson as protection and as a charge to keep serving the realm.

quest:5635.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, promising priests from Elwynn Forest come for deeper training in the Church of the Holy Light. After proving their devotion and discipline, they present themselves to High Priestess Laurena at the Cathedral of Light. Priestess Josetta guides novice priests in Goldshire, while local mentors serve Elwynn Forest's outlying settlements. When a disciple proves capable in spirit and deeds, word reaches Stormwind's senior priesthood. A summons to the Cathedral of Light marks a move to deeper duties in the faith and formal training at the spiritual heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind. At the Cathedral, acolytes come before High Priestess Laurena, a senior leader of the Church in Stormwind. She oversees their spiritual grounding and practical training as newly elevated priests. Her instruction prepares them for the Alliance's harsh trials and teaches the Light's miracles, including Desperate Prayer, a plea for salvation known among human practitioners.

quest:5636.text: Desperate Prayer. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight sends human priests home to Stormwind for further training. A fellow priest has crossed continents to summon them to the Cathedral of Light. In Dolanaar, Priestess Laurna Morninglight brings you word from home. A fellow priest has crossed continents to find you, and Laurna urges you to return without delay. She offers Elune’s blessing and good wishes for your faith as you leave Teldrassil. Your path leads across the Great Sea to Stormwind City’s Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena guides the Alliance faithful in their spiritual growth. She summons promising acolytes to deepen their devotion and learn Desperate Prayer, an emergency prayer that can save a life in a darkest hour.

quest:5637.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, High Priestess Laurena calls promising dwarven acolytes to the Cathedral of Light. There they deepen their service to the Light and take on wider duties among the Alliance. Dwarven priests trained in Dun Morogh may outgrow the lessons of local mentors like Maxan Anvol in Kharanos. When an acolyte shows promise, High Priestess Laurena sends a formal summons from the Cathedral of Light. Her attention means the young priest is ready for deeper study and greater duties in the faith. Ironforge keeps its holy traditions in the Mystic Ward, while Stormwind's Church of the Holy Light welcomes humans and dwarves alike. Traveling south by Deeprun Tram brings dwarven acolytes into the wider church community. The journey strengthens the spiritual bond between the allied kingdoms.

quest:5638.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, a summons carries a young priest from the Park to the Cathedral of Light. Nara Meideros sends you to High Priestess Laurena for further instruction. In Stormwind’s Park, Nara Meideros keeps faith with Elune. The city’s spiritual guides maintain ties across their traditions. So when the Cathedral seeks a promising student, Nara sends you across the canals with quiet encouragement. The message brings good tidings, not alarm. At the Cathedral of Light in Cathedral Square, you report to High Priestess Laurena. One of Stormwind’s senior clerical leaders, she guides young acolytes beyond their first prayers. Laurena teaches the sacred invocation called Desperate Prayer, a personal plea for divine aid. Near death, a servant of the Light can use it to mend grievous wounds in an instant.

quest:5639.text: Desperate Prayer. High Priest Rohan sends you from Ironforge to Stormwind to learn healing and survival. There, High Priestess Laurena teaches dwarven acolytes the deeper mysteries of the Church. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Rohan guides dwarven initiates devoted to the Holy Light. Seeing your discipline and faith, he sends you southwest to Stormwind. Human and dwarven clerics share close spiritual ties, and the city's grand halls hold advanced teaching. You reach Stormwind by the Deeprun Tram and climb to Cathedral Square. In the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena tests you on the Church's behalf. She teaches the desperate prayers a priest calls upon in battle, seeking divine aid when strength fails and death draws near.

quest:5640.text: Desperate Prayer. In Darnassus, young human and dwarven priests find guidance in another faith. Priestess Alathea teaches the ways of Elune, while followers of the Holy Light are directed to Stormwind. There, High Priestess Laurena welcomes the returning acolyte to the Cathedral of Light. Alliance priests follow different sacred paths. In Darnassus, the priesthood tends to Elune, channeling the moon goddess's radiance and wrath. Priestess Alathea honors Elune and respects the Holy Light, but cannot teach another race the deeper prayers bound to a different devotion. Human and dwarven acolytes who seek those prayers must look elsewhere. Initiates of the Holy Light return home to learn its rites, including the prayer for divine aid in a moment of peril. High Priestess Laurena guides returning priests in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, beneath its marble arches.

quest:5648.text: Garments of Spirituality. In Razor Hill, Tai'jin sends new priests to prove their healing in the field. They seek Grunt Kor'ja, wounded while standing against Kul Tiras survivors, and tend her injuries. Those who succeed earn ceremonial vestments and recognition among the Horde's spiritual practitioners. South of Razor Hill, the Horde still fights remnants of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's forces. Tai'jin, the troll priest trainer, tests new priests in the work of real combat triage. She sends them to find Grunt Kor'ja, a warrior badly wounded while repelling human infiltrators. You tend her injuries and strengthen her before she succumbs. Healing Kor'ja proves a young priest is ready to serve the Horde's spiritual tradition. Tai'jin awards the Garments of Spirituality for saving a frontline defender. To orcs and Darkspear trolls alike, the robes mark their wearer as more than an apprentice of incantations: they can be trusted to keep Horde warriors alive in battle.

quest:5649.text: In Favor of Spirituality. Young Darkspear priests leave the Valley of Trials under Ken'jai's direction. They report to Tai'jin in Razor Hill and take their first steps into Durotar's wider challenges. Their path balances ancestral troll heritage with life in the Horde. Darkspear acolytes leave the Valley of Trials after learning their basic rites under Ken'jai. The paths out of the secluded training grounds lead to Razor Hill, a crossroads settlement in Durotar. For a young priest, the journey marks a step beyond basic survival drills and toward the spiritual and cultural responsibilities of the tribe. Ken'jai speaks plainly about the Darkspear's place in Thrall's Horde. The trolls value the orcs' loyalty and lessons of honor, yet some ancestral traditions sit uneasily among their allies. Darkspear spiritual leaders teach their pupils to preserve their heritage quietly while serving the Horde. At Razor Hill, Tai'jin welcomes the acolytes and guides them toward self-sufficiency and strength within the community.

quest:5650.text: Garments of Darkness. In Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl tests fledgling Forsaken priests before they delve deeper into shadow. The trial shows whether they can heal and fortify an injured Deathguard, for the priesthood calls for more than afflicting enemies. Forsaken priests draw renown and a distinct identity from shadow and darkness. Dark Cleric Beryl also teaches that understanding darkness means learning light and restoration. Those who seek only ruin are urged to study arcane magic instead. A priest's calling includes strengthening and preserving comrades as well as afflicting enemies. North of Brill's cemetery, Deathguard Kel holds the line against prowling gnoll packs and has been wounded. Beryl sends you to bind his wounds with healing spells and bolster his stamina with protective enchantments. In this way, you show you can maintain Tirisfal Glades' defenders. Beryl grants you her vestment and accepts you into the priesthood's higher mysteries.

quest:5651.text: In Favor of Darkness. Dark Cleric Duesten sends you from Deathknell to Brill in In Favor of Darkness. There, you continue your training with Dark Cleric Beryl and study the Holy Light and Shadow. Dark Cleric Duesten teaches that the Forsaken were forged in corruption and discarded like carrion. Their survival demands that they understand both Light and Shadow without sentimentality. In Tirisfal Glades, you leave Deathknell's graveyard and face the wider world beyond its walls. You follow the road northeast from Deathknell, cross a wooden covered bridge, and reach the ruined hamlet of Brill. Dark Cleric Beryl waits in the upper quarters of the local inn to test your resolve. He values ambition and cold practicality over blind devotion, and expects a Forsaken priest to wield divine power as a weapon and a tool, not a moral crutch.

quest:5654.text: Hex of Weakness. In Durotar, Hex of Weakness carries a young Darkspear priest from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Tai'jin sends an initiate north to Ur'kyo, who welcomes new students into the tribe's spiritual circle and teaches the loa's darker arts. Young Darkspear priests continue their lessons in Razor Hill's barracks under Tai'jin's watch. Once an acolyte shows command of spiritual communion and shadow magic, the first lessons end. Tai'jin sends the promising priest north, across Durotar's red dirt canyons, toward the Horde capital. There, elder practitioners guide the tribe's wider magical traditions. The Darkspear keep a distinct cultural sanctuary in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, apart from the orcs' clanging forges and warrior grounds. Ur'kyo, an elder priest, waits there for new initiates. Joining his circle means embracing the ancestral traditions of the jungle trolls: honoring the loa while learning potent curses and hexes that sap an enemy's strength in battle.

quest:5713.text: One Shot. One Kill.. On the road to Auberdine, Sentinel Aynasha needs help to survive an ambush and deliver her message. Marosh the Devious and his furbolg trackers have poisoned her, leaving her unable to travel while she mixes an antidote. Sentinel Aynasha was carrying important communications toward Auberdine when hostile furbolgs intercepted her on a northern Kalimdor trail. Marosh the Devious led the pack. Their venom left the scout unsteady and unable to continue on foot. Aynasha knows how to make natural remedies, but mixing and taking an antidote takes time. Marosh's trackers are closing in, so she needs travelers to guard her while she works. Though her strength is failing, she keeps her bow steady and fires into the brush to hold the attackers back.

quest:5722.text: Searching for the Lost Satchel. Rahauro sends you from Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise into Ragefire Chasm. Magatha Grimtotem seeks her lost emissary Maur and the unusual discovery he made among the troggs. Magatha Grimtotem hears on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise that her emissary, Maur Grimtotem, entered the cavern beneath Orgrimmar to study the troggs and try to parley with them. He never returned, and rumors say he found something unusual shortly before his death. While Warchief Thrall and his advisers focus on the Shadow Council presence in Ragefire Chasm, the Grimtotem clan follows its own interests.

quest:5723.text: Testing an Enemy's Strength. Magatha Grimtotem seeks retribution after troggs slaughter her emissaries beneath Orgrimmar. Rahauro on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise sends warriors into Ragefire Chasm to cull the troggs infesting it. Magatha Grimtotem sent tauren emissaries into the fiery depths beneath Orgrimmar to make peace with the troggs. The creatures slaughtered the delegates as soon as they arrived. Magatha saw the massacre as an insult to the tauren and a growing danger to the Horde. She resolved to answer it with force. Rahauro carries out Magatha’s orders from Thunder Bluff. He directs warriors into Ragefire Chasm to find and kill trogg warriors and shamans. The Horde strikes deep into their underground home to thin their numbers before they can pour through their tunnels into Orgrimmar.

quest:5724.text: Returning the Lost Satchel. In Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, the search for Maur Grimtotem ends with his satchel. You must carry it back to Rahauro on Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Maur Grimtotem was slain by troggs in the fiery depths of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Even in death, his arms clung to his personal satchel. Freeing it from his grip is the only clue to why a member of the Grimtotem clan entered the volcanic caverns beneath Thrall's capital.

quest:5725.text: The Power to Destroy.... In the Undercity, Varimathras sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner wants two dark tomes held by the Searing Blade cult, hoping their power will aid her war against the Scourge and the Lich King. Thrall's orcs are hunting the Searing Blade cult beneath their capital, while the Forsaken covet the cult's occult stores. On Sylvanas Windrunner's orders, Varimathras sends operatives into Ragefire Chasm to seize two demonic grimoires: Spells of Shadow and Incantations from the Nether. The Dark Lady believes disciplined Forsaken will can put these demonic gifts to better use than the lesser cultists. Varimathras explains the tomes' purpose once they are secured. Their dark magic is meant to strengthen Sylvanas's campaign against the Scourge. By claiming every scrap of forbidden power, the Forsaken hope to break the Lich King's hold across Lordaeron and free the remaining undead from his mental enslavement.

quest:5726.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall begins a covert search for the Burning Blade in Durotar. He asks a promising young adventurer to recover a Lieutenant's Insignia from Skull Rock, opening a way to uncover cultists working under the Horde's nose. In Durotar, the new Horde struggles to secure a home, and Warchief Thrall faces betrayal from within. The Burning Blade has taken root just outside Orgrimmar's gates. Its cultists prey on lingering demonic corruption and hunger for dark power. Thrall needs someone to watch and listen without drawing notice. Skull Rock lies east of Orgrimmar. Its rugged caverns hold warlocks, voidwalkers, and fanatical cultists. Thrall sends you to take a Lieutenant's Insignia from one of the Burning Blade leaders. The emblem is meant to open the cult's hidden ranks, so Thrall can learn who directs its movements.

quest:5727.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you into Orgrimmar to learn what the Burning Blade knows. After cult activity is found at Skull Rock, you carry a lieutenant's insignia to Neeru Fireblade and test his loyalties. Thrall turns to cunning instead of striking at the Cleft of Shadow. He knows Neeru Fireblade pretends to serve the Horde while aiding the cultists in secret. If Thrall strikes now, Neeru's masters will be warned and the trail into the conspiracy may end. So Thrall gives you an insignia taken from the cult in Durotar and asks you to pose as an initiate, to learn what Neeru knows.

quest:5728.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you against the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. After tricking Neeru Fireblade into believing you are an ally, he sends you into Ragefire Chasm to assassinate the cult's top commanders. Orgrimmar was built as a haven for a free Orcish race, but its foundations conceal an old demonic threat. Beneath the markets, the Cleft of Shadow opens onto the tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. In those volcanic depths, remnants of the Shadow Council called the Searing Blade gather strength. They practice dark arts and scheme to seize the young Horde from within its own capital.

quest:5729.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall's watch on Hidden Enemies reaches into the Cleft of Shadow. After Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed beneath the city, Thrall sends you to win Neeru Fireblade's trust. Thrall sees a chance after Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed in Ragefire Chasm. He chooses not to expose Neeru Fireblade. Neeru has lost his underground lieutenants, leaving the local cult without its leaders. Thrall sends you back to the Cleft of Shadow to offer yourself as an ally who can fill that gap.

quest:5730.text: Hidden Enemies. Neeru Fireblade has earned your trust, and Thrall awaits your report in Orgrimmar. The Warchief needs to know how far the Burning Blade's reach extends across Kalimdor.

quest:5761.text: Slaying the Beast. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Neeru Fireblade sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm to hunt Taragaman the Hungerer. He claims Warchief Thrall ordered the hunt and demands the towering felguard’s heart as proof the demonic cult has fallen. Ragefire Chasm lies beneath Orgrimmar’s red earthen streets, a fiery fissure filled with troggs, beasts, and covert Searing Blade agents. In the Cleft of Shadow above, Neeru Fireblade presents himself as a loyal servant carrying out Thrall’s order to cleanse this demonic rot. He points to Taragaman the Hungerer, a massive felguard in the cavern’s heart, and names him as the mastermind behind the cult below the city.

quest:579.text: Stormwind Library. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those bearing library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn funds the work, opening accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars. Young King Anduin directs royal funds toward learning. They pay for copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals. In Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library preserves these accounts and copies them for those in royal service. Hand copying delicate parchment takes time, ink, and royal sanction. Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In return, he provides copies of historical works, from ancient Eastern Kingdoms histories to accounts of distant lands. These books tell of conflicts beyond the capital.

quest:59.text: Cloth and Leather Armor. In Goldshire, Cloth and Leather Armor sends a trusted traveler east for gear. Marshal Dughan issues an armor marker for Sara Timberlain at Eastvale Logging Camp. Beyond Guard Thomas's bridge, recruits seek armor for the realm's defense. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern river crossing, where murlocs and gnolls threaten the border. You carry his report to Goldshire, and Marshal Dughan marks your service with an official Stormwind Armor Marker. Goldshire's garrison has few stores, so Dughan gives you a marker instead of equipment. It is a military voucher recording your service to the crown. East of Guard Thomas's bridge lies Eastvale Logging Camp, Elwynn's main timber operation. Sara Timberlain works there under commission from the Stormwind Army, making cloth and leather gear. The kingdom's central armories are strained, so local artisans like Sara outfit troops and auxiliary scouts on the frontier.

quest:5921.text: Moonglade. In Darnassus, young night elf druids learn to reach Moonglade. Mathrengyl Bearwalker teaches novices a spell to carry themselves across the world into Moonglade, where they meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. There begins their path toward mastering bear form. Moonglade is an ancient sanctuary apart from the rest of Azeroth, devoted to the teachings of Cenarius. Keeper Remulos watches over its groves, where druids find peace and communion with nature. Young druids learn a spell that lets them carry themselves across the world into Moonglade, reaching a heart of druidic wisdom beyond mortal distances. Moonglade welcomes all who follow the wild, though the Cenarion Circle knows its share of tension. In Darnassus, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm and Keeper Remulos disagree over nature’s care and the creation of Teldrassil. Their differences do not close Nighthaven to young acolytes, who are welcomed to pursue their studies. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze guides young druids in the ways of the Claw. Before an initiate can take up the bear’s mantle, the trials teach the bear’s endurance, fury, and defense of the wild. Starblaze welcomes each student in reverence to Father Cenarius as the trials of the Great Bear Spirit begin.

quest:5922.text: Moonglade. In Moonglade, a young tauren druid learns to reach nature’s ancient keepers. Guided by Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, the initiate learns to cross the waking world and commune with them directly. Moonglade lies beyond Kalimdor’s faction struggles. Keeper Remulos, son of Cenarius, watches over the ancient valley, a neutral refuge for all who follow nature. Night elf and tauren druids enter Nighthaven as equals, beneath the Cenarion Circle’s timeless mantle. Turak Runetotem teaches you a unique transport spell bound to Moonglade, aiding your spiritual and martial growth. Through your bond with the natural world, you cross hundreds of leagues in a heartbeat. The valley offers a place to study and a lasting refuge throughout your journey.

quest:5923.text: Heeding the Call. In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker calls druids from Teldrassil and beyond to begin their training. An apprentice now faces the path toward mastering the bear aspect. Novice druids receive a personal summons when their instructors judge them ready for trials. Kal in Dolanaar, Denatharion in Darnassus, and Theridran in Stormwind carry Mathrengyl Bearwalker’s invitation to train. As Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm’s direct assistant, Mathrengyl is one of the night elves’ most respected and knowledgeable mentors. His guidance marks an apprentice as ready for true trials. Mathrengyl Bearwalker receives candidates on the upper level of Fandral Staghelm’s residence in the Cenarion Enclave. Druids must learn to embody nature’s living creatures, not merely watch them. He tells each candidate that the first great undertaking is to embrace the bear’s strength, endurance, and spirit. The path reaches far beyond Teldrassil, to sacred ancestral grounds.

quest:5926.text: Heeding the Call. A summons brings a novice druid to Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff for personal instruction. Word reaches aspiring shapeshifters through innkeepers and kin across Horde settlements, directing them to Turak Runetotem. There, the sacred trials begin, leading toward mastery of the bear's form and spirit. Across Mulgore and Orgrimmar, word reaches you that Turak Runetotem has noticed your early progress. Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Pala in Thunder Bluff, or Gennia Runetotem in Bloodhoof Village may carry the message. The Cenarion Circle does not summon practitioners lightly. Your work with herbs and simple spells has earned you a chance to deepen your bond with nature's wild spirits. On Elder Rise, Turak Runetotem guides young tauren toward their ancestral duty. He assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem and welcomes you inside the large Cenarion tent. Turak teaches that animals and plants are allies, and solemn charges. Meeting him opens a path beyond basic instruction, toward trials of body and heart and communion with the Great Bear Spirit.

quest:5931.text: Back to Darnassus. After meeting the Great Bear Spirit, a young night elf druid returns to Darnassus. The initiate has left Moonglade and now reports to Mathrengyl Bearwalker in the Cenarion Enclave for practical shapeshifting trials. Dendrite Starblaze sends the initiate from Nighthaven back to Darnassus after the meeting with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade. The journey joins two sanctuaries: Moonglade, where the young druid has communed with the spirit, and the unsettled world beyond. In Darnassus, local mentors watch over Teldrassil and guide the next stage of training. Mathrengyl Bearwalker waits in the Cenarion Enclave, where he guards nature even as its balance falters. The Great Bear Spirit's blessing is only the first step. Mathrengyl prepares the initiate for trials of body and heart, to give physical form to the spirit's fierce ancestral wisdom.

quest:5932.text: Back to Thunder Bluff. Your return from Moonglade brings you back to Elder Rise, where Turak Runetotem awaits. Dendrite Starblaze sends you home after your communion with the Great Bear Spirit, so your training can continue among your people. Moonglade brings night elf and tauren practitioners of nature magic together in the Cenarion Circle, apart from the mortal world’s factional divides. After your communion with the Great Bear Spirit, Dendrite Starblaze sends you back to your people. Night elves often see tauren as fledglings in Cenarius’s formal teachings, yet Starblaze recognizes the wisdom and balance of Turak Runetotem. You climb back to Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff and stand before Turak Runetotem, changed by your rite. Communion with ancient totemic spirits such as the Great Bear Spirit runs deep in tauren culture, but the Path of the Claw asks for serious commitment. Your spiritual bond is forged, and Turak prepares you to put your new strength and endurance into practice.

quest:6.text: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. Near Northshire Abbey, an Alliance bounty calls recruits to hunt Garrick Padfoot by the vineyards. The notorious thief and his gang threaten the valley's farmers and merchants. Northshire Valley offered a safe place to train recruits and tend its sacred vineyards. But as order falters across Elwynn, thieves have reached the valley. Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat, quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, he and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants on the roads, and threatened local farmers. Stormwind's guards are stretched thin, protecting the capital and its outer borders. So local marshals and deputies rely on volunteers to keep Northshire peaceful. Deputy Willem posts a public bounty on Garrick's head, hoping to rid the valley of his gang. Padfoot's rundown shack lies east of the river. Bringing him down there strikes at the lawlessness spreading through the human heartland.

quest:60.text: Kobold Candles. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle seeks candles from kobolds crowding Elwynn's mines. The alchemist has come from his Stormwind shop for their thick wax. His errand brings adventurers face to face with the creatures encroaching on the kingdom's gold veins. William Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary with his brother in Stormwind City's Trade District. He needs wax for the remedies, ointments, and concoctions he brews. So he turns to Elwynn's kobolds instead of buying polished candles from city merchants. They carry hefty lumps of tallow and wax on their brows, ready for an adventurer to pry loose. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. They prize their candles above almost everything. The flames guide them through dark shafts as they dig for gold and shiny trinkets. Taking the candles replenishes Pestle's alchemy stocks and weakens the vermin choking off the kingdom's precious mining claims.

quest:6001.text: Body and Heart. In Darnassus, a young night elf druid nears the end of initiation into the path of the claw. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends the initiate into Darkshore to summon Lunaclaw and prove strength of body and heart before taking the form of the bear. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends night elf druid initiates east of Auberdine, the coastal settlement in Darkshore. A natural cavern there shelters wild moonkin and an ancient Moonkin Stone. Anointing the sacred stone with Cenarion Moondust awakens Lunaclaw, its ancient defender. The guardian challenges any initiate who seeks the sacred strength of the claw.

quest:6002.text: Body and Heart. At the Moonkin Stone, you face a trial of body and heart to master Bear Form. Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids from Thunder Bluff to summon and defeat Lunaclaw near the border of Mulgore and the Barrens. Turak Runetotem tests young tauren druids who seek the path of the Druid of the Claw. After you commune with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade, your training turns to a trial of strength. Turak, the elder druid trainer atop the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, gives worthy aspirants Cenarion Lunardust. He sends you to a sacred stone near the dry frontier where Mulgore meets the Barrens. West of Camp Taurajo, the Moonkin Stone marks a rare Cenarion site in southern Kalimdor. Moonkin are not native to the sun-scorched plains of central Kalimdor, and Lunaclaw guards the stone. Scatter the lunardust across the ancient monument to call Lunaclaw into battle. Defeating the guardian proves your strength and clarity of heart, earning its blessing and awakening the bear's inner essence.

quest:6061.text: Taming the Beast. At Bloodhoof Village, Taming the Beast begins a young tauren hunter’s training with Yaw Sharpmane. The first trial takes the hunter into Mulgore to tame an adult plainstrider and begin a bond with the creatures of the Earthmother. Tauren hunters seek more than meat and hides when they hunt. Their ancestral traditions teach that meeting Mulgore’s wild creatures can bring a hunter closer to the Earthmother. Taming a companion turns a beast that might have been an adversary into a partner, joined with the hunter in the natural balance of the plains. Yaw Sharpmane starts a hunter’s training with plainstriders that roam Mulgore’s grasslands. The hunter carries an enchanted taming rod and faces an adult plainstrider, calming its wild instincts and earning its trust. This first trial tests the hunter’s resolve and prepares them to face more demanding beasts.

quest:6062.text: Taming the Beast. In Razor Hill, Taming the Beast begins a young Horde hunter’s training with a taming rod. Thotar guides aspiring hunters as they face a vicious dire mottled boar. Orc and Darkspear troll hunters in Durotar must learn to command the wild as well as survive it. Thotar, the veteran hunter trainer, gives young hunters an enchanted taming rod and sends them to face a fierce wild boar. They must subdue the beast without killing it, then make it a loyal ally. Dire mottled boars roam the dry brush around Razor Hill. Their strength and temper make them a fitting first test for young hunters. The rod can subdue a charging boar, but using it takes patience and resolve, qualities every Horde tracker needs.

quest:6063.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast begins a night elf hunter’s trials with a wild Webwood Lurker. Dazalar lends an enchanted taming rod, and the hunter must win the spider’s trust through a bond with nature. For the kaldorei, hunting means more than tracking prey or surviving in the wild. It binds a hunter to nature, which is greater than any mortal. Animals are independent creatures, not tools to bend to a hunter’s will. Dazalar teaches novice hunters to meet them with respect. Before gaining a lifelong beast companion, a hunter must master local wildlife through ancient techniques, never brute force. Giant arachnids infest Teldrassil’s boughs, and Dazalar gives the hunter a taming rod. The hunter seeks a Webwood Lurker in the shadowed thickets, facing the venomous spider and its attacks while trying to reach it through empathy. A brief mental bond proves the hunter can commune with the World Tree’s eerie, skittering predators.

quest:6064.text: Taming the Beast. In Dun Morogh, Taming the Beast sets a hunter on the first trial toward mastering companion beasts. In Kharanos, Grif Wildheart guides young trackers as they calm a Large Crag Boar with an enchanted taming rod. Dwarven mountaineers and trackers depend on guns, traps, and their wits in the wild. Yet a hunter's calling is to make a lifelong bond with a wild beast. Outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Grif Wildheart oversees this rite. He tests novices against several species native to Dun Morogh before asking them to bind any beast for good. A Large Crag Boar is the first test for a young tracker. These thick-hided swine roam Dun Morogh's snowy foothills, where their bristling fur and tough flesh make them stubborn and fierce. Grif provides an enchanted Taming Rod. The hunter faces the boar's charge and tries to calm its fury until it submits to command.

quest:6065.text: The Hunter's Path. In Mulgore, young tauren hunters are sent to Bloodhoof Village for advanced training. There, they seek Yaw Sharpmane and begin the trials of taming and bonding with wild beasts. Among the Shu'halo, hunting is sacred. A hunter learns the balance of nature, honors the spirits of the plains, and respects the animals that sustain the tribes. When young hunters prove they can survive in the wild and use a bow or gun, their elders send them to seasoned mentors. That journey marks their step beyond solitary tracking and toward adulthood in tauren culture. The road crosses Mulgore's grasslands to Bloodhoof Village, beside Stonebull Lake. There, Yaw Sharpmane teaches hunters about the local beasts. Meeting him marks a hunter's readiness for the trials of beast taming, where they learn to commune with predators as well as hunt them.

quest:6068.text: The Hunter's Path. In Durotar, The Hunter's Path sends young orc and troll hunters to Razor Hill. There, Thotar teaches them to bind wild predators. In Durotar, young hunters learn to track prey with bow and cunning. Following trails through red clay canyons and harsh scrubland teaches patience. To master the hunter's way in the Horde, they must also learn to bond with the land's wild beasts. When class trainers judge a student ready, they direct them to Razor Hill. Thotar waits at Razor Hill, where he teaches young hunters how to subdue Durotar's fierce beasts without breaking their spirit. Learning from him begins the path to traveling the wilderness with a loyal companion.

quest:6074.text: The Hunter's Path. In Dun Morogh, the trainers send ready hunters to Kharanos to begin learning how to tame wild beasts. Grif Wildheart oversees the trials there. Novice hunters cross Dun Morogh’s snowy crags alone until they learn to bond with beasts. Olmin Burningbeard and Tristane Shadowstone watch their pupils closely. They wait until a hunter can face a savage creature calmly and spare its life. Then the trainers send the disciplined novice down the mountain roads toward Kharanos. In Kharanos, Grif Wildheart oversees the final trials of dwarven huntsmanship. Taming a beast takes more than bringing it down for meat or pelt. A hunter needs patience, physical endurance, and an instinctive bond with the wild predators of the mountains. Wildheart prepares each hunter to test their will against Dun Morogh’s fiercest wildlife.

quest:6081.text: Training the Beast. In Durotar, young orc and troll hunters are sent to learn from veteran master hunter Ormak Grimshot. After proving themselves with the plains beasts, they travel from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There they learn to care for, feed, and train a lifelong animal companion. In Durotar's arid canyon lands, skill with a bow and survival in the harsh wilds are only part of a hunter's duty. Young hunters first tame the plains beasts: fierce boars, crab scavengers, and armored scorpid stalkers. Once they prove their resilience, Thotar sends them from Razor Hill north through the red clay gulches to Orgrimmar's fortified gates, ready to take responsibility for a companion. Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor is an enclave where veteran stalkers and warriors hone their craft. There, aspiring hunters seek Ormak Grimshot, one of the Horde's revered master hunters. He looks beyond their youth to judge whether they have the patience to command a beast and sustain and nurture it through famine, battle, and loss. A beast won through force remains wild until hunter and companion come to understand one another.
