Ormak teaches the sacred traditions that keep their bond: which foods nourish each creature's spirit, how discipline teaches a beast lethal techniques, and the spiritual focus needed to revive one that falls in the line of duty.

quest:6082.text: Taming the Beast. In Durotar, Taming the Beast tests a young Horde hunter's skill with wild creatures. Thotar in Razor Hill guides the hunter through one last trial: taming a dangerous armored scorpid. Success brings the ability to tame, call, and dismiss a lasting companion. Before a hunter can travel Kalimdor with an animal companion, they must prove they can command Durotar's harsh wildlife. Thotar, the hunter trainer in Razor Hill, sends trainees to subdue three kinds of creature with an enchanted taming rod. After facing dire boars and swift surf crawlers, they must now tame an armored scorpid, a venomous predator protected by heavy plates and known for resilience and speed. Taming an armored scorpid tests a hunter's focus and control under attack, not their skill at killing. Thotar urges hunters to match the beast's quick, confident strikes. Once the hunter has charmed the scorpid, they return to Razor Hill and give the taming rod back to Thotar. That return completes the trial, and Thotar then teaches the wild's innate techniques, letting the hunter seek out and bind a permanent companion of their choosing.

quest:6083.text: Taming the Beast. In Durotar, Taming the Beast sends young hunters to the coast for their second trial. Thotar, the hunter trainer in Razor Hill, directs aspiring orc and troll hunters to pacify a surf crawler near the Echo Isles and extend their bond to coastal wildlife. After mastering a dire mottled boar, you turn your attention to the sea at Thotar's direction. Durotar's harsh shores are jagged, and shallow reefs teem with armored crustaceans. A surf crawler resists intrusion into its coastal domain, so taming one calls for patience and fortitude. Thotar teaches that a bound beast must become an extension of a hunter's strength. Subduing a surf crawler with the taming rod teaches you to command creatures of different temperaments in different surroundings. It proves you are ready for permanent companions.

quest:6084.text: Taming the Beast. Grif Wildheart sends you to face a snow leopard in the second taming trial. The test reaches beyond the crag boar. Snow leopards prowl southeast of Kharanos. The crag boar tested your strength against hard blows. Now Grif expects you to face a swift, graceful predator on its own terms. Beneath its white coat lies dangerous strength, ready to strike. With an enchanted taming rod, you face a wild snow leopard and seek to turn its hunting instincts toward partnership. Its speed, agility, and sharp reflexes test you in ways the crag boar did not. Learn to work alongside a predator that strikes swiftly from the snowy crags, and you draw closer to mastering the beasts of the wild.

quest:6085.text: Taming the Beast. In Dun Morogh, Grif Wildheart tests your control of an Ice Claw Bear east of Kharanos. With an enchanted rod, you subdue the bear and learn to understand it. Then you earn the power to tame, call, and dismiss a lasting wild companion. Dun Morogh’s mountaineers and scouts depend on hardy beasts in its freezing crags. You have practiced on swift, cunning predators. Now Grif Wildheart sends you to capture an Ice Claw Bear in the snowdrifts east of Kharanos. Its strength and endurance test the control every dwarven huntsman must learn. The Taming Rod keeps the bear docile while you learn how wild instincts answer to will and calm intent. Your bond lasts only for the trial, which teaches discipline. Return the rod to Grif and the trials are complete. He then teaches you to pacify a compatible wild creature and call it throughout your life of adventure.

quest:6086.text: Training the Beast. In Dun Morogh, Grif Wildheart sends young dwarven hunters to Ironforge to learn care for a lasting animal companion. After taming the mountain’s wild predators, they learn to feed and train their beasts. Young hunters finish their trial near Kharanos under Grif Wildheart’s watch. They have tamed large crag boars, snow leopards, and sturdy ice claw bears with a taming rod. Then Grif sends them up the mountain pass to Ironforge. They seek the Hall of Arms in the military district. Belia Thundergranite teaches animal care in Ironforge’s Hall of Arms. Revered among the dwarven kingdom’s master animal trainers, she shows young hunters how to nourish their pets and teach them new battlefield skills. She also teaches them to call their spirits back if they fall defending their master. Her lessons turn a frightened wild beast into a loyal partner. Dwarven tradition asks for respect between hunter and beast, never subjugation. Belia reminds young hunters that an animal companion reflects the care it receives. Fed well, respected, and properly trained, a beast will fight loyally against troggs, frost trolls, and any threat to Khaz Modan.

quest:6087.text: Taming the Beast. In Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane sets a young tauren hunter a new trial. The hunter must master the swift prairie stalker. After mastering the adult plainstrider’s endurance, you face a different kind of hunter. Prairie stalkers rely on speed, move in packs, and attack without fear. To tame one, you must approach this cunning predator without breaking stride, matching the wolf’s decisive nature. Yaw Sharpmane teaches you that hunting beside a beast means neither servitude nor brute force. You and the predator must fight as one, joined by respect and shared rhythm. Bonding with a prairie stalker under Mulgore’s open skies teaches you to complement your companion’s attacks and move with it in battle.

quest:6088.text: Taming the Beast. In Mulgore, Taming the Beast brings a young tauren hunter to the last lesson under Yaw Sharpmane in Bloodhoof Village. A taming rod lets the hunter bond with a wild swoop and prove mastery of the air. Completing the trial grants lasting knowledge to tame, call, and dismiss a companion, with the Earthmother's trust. After you subdue predators on Mulgore's plains, Yaw Sharpmane turns your attention to the open sky. A swoop is a fierce bird of prey with a sharp beak, sweeping dives, and an intimidating air. Its talons test your reflexes and calm as you use the enchanted rod to bring its instincts into accord with your own. For the tauren, hunting and companionship with beasts are spiritual pursuits, not mere subjugation. Mastering creatures of earth and sky shows the balance and respect needed to walk the plains without disturbing nature. Yaw Sharpmane takes back his temporary taming rod and teaches you lasting techniques to call, dismiss, and permanently tame a companion of your choosing.

quest:6089.text: Training the Beast. In Mulgore, young tauren hunters learn to live and hunt beside a beast. After proving their patience and resolve by soothing the plains’ wild creatures, they travel to Thunder Bluff to learn the lasting bond of care and command. After facing plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops in Mulgore, tauren hunters are ready to take up the full mantle of the hunter. Yaw Sharpmane, their mentor in Bloodhoof Village, sends each novice to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. There, Holt Thunderhorn teaches them. The shu'halo honor him for communing with the wilds, and his reverence for the Earthmother is greater still. To the tauren, a beast is a partner joined through harmony with the natural world, never a weapon or thrall. Holt Thunderhorn teaches hunters how to sustain that bond. They learn to guide a creature's combat instincts, feed it regularly, mend its injuries, and call its spirit back if it falls defending its companion on the plains.

quest:61.text: Shipment to Stormwind. William Pestle sends a parcel from Goldshire to his brother in Stormwind. Its candles carry wax gathered from kobolds in Elwynn Forest to Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary. William Pestle gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods in Goldshire. His brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot easily leave the Lion's Pride Inn, so he trusts travelers bound for the city to carry his goods. William's parcel holds large candles gathered from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. He collects them for their wax, but does not say how the brothers use it. You carry the shipment to Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District.

quest:6101.text: Taming the Beast. Dazalar guides a night elf hunter through a second trial in Dolanaar. With an enchanted taming rod, you subdue a nightsaber stalker and learn how wild beasts differ. Dazalar teaches you that the forest's creatures do not all behave alike. Each species has its own temperament, and a hunter must learn to meet it on its own terms. Beneath Teldrassil's canopy, the next test brings you against beasts more cunning and predatory than webspinners. Kaldorei revere nightsabers as sacred predators, fierce guardians, and companions of the Sentinels. With the taming rod, you face a nightsaber stalker and must keep a steady nerve and calm authority. Winning its trust shows you can handle a predator, not only the more docile creatures of the woods.

quest:6102.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast brings a young night elf hunter to the final trial of basic training. Under Dazalar’s direction, hunters tame a predatory owl of the skies before gaining the power to choose a lifelong companion. Night elf hunters must make peace with creatures across Teldrassil before their basic beastcraft is complete. After proving their will against beasts of the underbrush, they face the spirit of the skies, the Strigid Screecher. These watchful birds of prey roost high in the boughs west of Dolanaar. Patience and a steady nerve are needed to pacify one with the enchanted Taming Rod. Taming the Strigid Screecher fulfills the ancient lessons of communion between kaldorei hunters and nature. When the apprentice returns the spent rod to Dazalar, the training exercises end. The apprentice earns the full art of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming beasts of their own choosing across Azeroth.

quest:6103.text: Training the Beast. In Teldrassil, Training the Beast sends night elf hunters from the wilds to Darnassus. After taming beasts among the boughs, they learn pet care and discipline from Jocaste. Dazalar sends you from the wilds near Dolanaar to Darnassus once you prove you can tame a beast. Before you travel Kalimdor with a loyal companion, you need to learn more than how to use a taming rod. Subduing a wild creature tests your strength and will, but an untrained beast can still be unpredictable. Jocaste teaches you the arts of caring for a companion in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. She shows you how to feed your pet, bring it back if tragedy strikes, and train it to fight. For night elves, this bond reflects reverence for nature, not simple control.

quest:6121.text: Lessons Anew. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends Alliance druids from Darnassus to Moonglade for training. There, Dendrite Starblaze begins their instruction in cleansing venom and toxins. Druids learn from Cenarius, the demigod whose teachings and blessings bind them to the living world. His gifts include the power to cleanse venom with a simple incantation. Such power is not given lightly. Before young druids can wield it, they must learn the hard, ordinary work of fighting toxins without nature's magic. Mathrengyl Bearwalker trains druids in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. He sends his student past local practice and on to Moonglade. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze coordinates the Cenarion Circle's wider efforts and has practical work for the novice.

quest:6122.text: The Principal Source. At Cliffspring Falls, a sickness among Darkshore's deer draws the Cenarion Circle's attention to the water. Dendrite Starblaze sends young druids from Moonglade to collect a sample for Auberdine naturalist Alanndarian Nightsong. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore with fresh water. When deer began to sicken with a lingering malady, the Cenarion Circle looked to the river for its cause. Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade suspects the water source is tainted and sends novice druids to gather a sample at the cavern mouth beneath the falls. Vicious naga dwell inside Cliffspring River Cave, near the falls' headwaters. Their presence threatens anyone trying to investigate the blight. The Cenarion Circle needs a sample from the cave mouth to study what is making the wilderness sick.

quest:6123.text: Gathering the Cure. In Darkshore, sick deer need a salve, and Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine shows a young druid how to make one. The remedy calls for water and healing plants gathered nearby. Alanndarian Nightsong seeks a cure for Darkshore's sick deer. A contaminated water source has harmed the local wildlife, so sampled Cliffspring water will form the salve's base. Natural ingredients with healing power must complete the mixture. The deer cannot recover alone, and the Cenarion Circle needs a remedy soon. Earthroot and Lunar Fungus lend healing power to the salve. Earthroot grows in rocky soil, where a practiced herbalist's eye helps find it. Lunar Fungus blooms in caves east of Auberdine. The moonkin there have grown territorial and agitated, making the gathering more dangerous.

quest:6124.text: Curing the Sick. Darkshore’s deer are sick, and Curing the Sick asks you to bring them relief. Alanndarian Nightsong gives you salve to treat the poisoned animals before you report to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. In Darkshore, deer fall sick from the Cliffspring River south to the border of Ashenvale. They wander the misty woods, weakened by toxins in the soil and streams. After you gather the needed reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong gives you freshly brewed animal salve to treat the afflicted deer.

quest:6125.text: Power over Poison. In Darnassus, a young druid returns to complete Power over Poison. The Cenarion Circle's trial began in Darkshore, where the initiate learned to brew a remedy by hand. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong asks young druids to gather Earthroot and Lunar Fungus by hand. They brew a salve to heal stricken wildlife. Before granting the magic to purge toxins, the Cenarion Circle wants initiates to know the hardship of treating poison without spiritual aid. The work teaches them what common folk face when venom strikes, and why a druid must meet their suffering with care. After the remedy proves effective in Auberdine, Starblaze sends the druid across the sea to Darnassus. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits in the Cenarion Enclave. Pleased with the initiate's grace under pressure, he teaches the art of cleansing toxins through nature's power. But virulent poisons in the wilds around Auberdine trouble him, for they point to an unnatural blight disturbing the land's balance.

quest:6126.text: Lessons Anew. At Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids to Moonglade to learn how to cleanse natural and unnatural poisons. The sacred haven is where apprentices begin mastering that art under Dendrite Starblaze, a night elf druid, as real poisonings demand more than practice. Cenarius gave druids the power to purge virulent toxins with an incantation, and their charge is to protect the wilds. Turak Runetotem teaches that such magic needs a firm grounding. Before a druid uses it to clear a blight, they must understand venom’s physical toll and learn to treat it by ordinary means. Turak sends promising acolytes north from Mulgore along sacred pathways to Moonglade. In its peaceful village of Nighthaven, ancient night elf mentors such as Dendrite Starblaze teach elf and tauren practitioners alike. Their shared study reflects the Cenarion Circle’s delicate truce, which rises above the political strife between Horde and Alliance.

quest:6127.text: The Principal Source. Dendrite Starblaze sends Horde druids to Dreadmist Peak for a water sample. From Moonglade, she asks them to bring it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads, where it can help explain the poison harming wildlife. Dreadmist Peak rises northwest of the Crossroads, with springs and pools high above the dry northern Barrens. Their waters shape local weather and moisture. The Burning Blade, a cult devoted to demons, has taken hold on the crags. Dendrite Starblaze fears their foul sorcery may taint the basin around this important mountain. Sick gazelles stumble across the northern savanna, north of the main east-west trail through the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem seeks help for the local tauren and turns to the Cenarion Circle to learn what is poisoning the herd. Druids who reach the peak and bring back a sample of its tainted water give Tonga what he needs to study the sickness and brew an antidote.

quest:6128.text: Gathering the Cure. At the Crossroads, young tauren druids face a sacred passage under Tonga Runetotem's guidance. You gather earthroot and sturdy kodo horns to make a salve for the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Tonga Runetotem needs raw ingredients to brew an antidote from the water sample you secured at Dreadmist Peak. Natural water forms the salve's base, earthroot supplies its medicinal qualities, and ground kodo horn gives it the strength to drive venom from a creature's system. For a young druid, gathering them means relying on the gifts of the earth and hunting local beasts. Tonga Runetotem uses the salve's preparation to teach the limits of physical medicine. Herbal lore and alchemy can counter specific toxins, but each poison usually needs its own cure. Rather than carry endless herbs and horns, druids learn to attune to nature's healing energies. That lesson leads to the druidic art of Cure Poison.

quest:6129.text: Curing the Sick. Sick gazelles are suffering across the northern Barrens. Tonga Runetotem sends young Horde druids to treat them with a freshly made herbal salve, then sends them before the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. An unnatural sickness is spreading among gazelles in the northern Barrens. You have gathered earthroot and kodo horns for a curative remedy, and Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads now entrusts the animals to your care. Search north of the main crossroads and tend to ten suffering gazelles. The salve brings them relief before the affliction takes deeper hold in the ecosystem. After you apply the salve, you travel to Moonglade’s tranquil druidic sanctuary. Dendrite Starblaze recognizes your compassion and vigilance there. He says the gazelles’ suffering points to a deeper corruption stalking Kalimdor’s wilderness. By tending even the lowliest beasts, tauren druids show that reverence for Cenarius reaches beyond tribal boundaries. They earn deeper secrets of poison cleansing and nature magic.

quest:6130.text: Power over Poison. At Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to claim the gift of Cure Poison. After healing poisoned gazelles near the Crossroads with herbal mixtures, the initiate faces Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise. Before granting a druid the power to cleanse venom, the Cenarion Circle asks them to learn what affliction feels like. Dendrite Starblaze sends the novice to the Crossroads, where Tonga Runetotem has them gather ingredients for a salve. The druid treats poisoned gazelles of the Barrens by hand, without spiritual aid, and sees the struggle ordinary creatures face against natural and unnatural toxins. After the trial, Dendrite sends the initiate to Turak Runetotem, the grand druid trainer on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Turak warns that strange, virulent poisons near the Crossroads threaten the plains' natural balance. He commends the initiate's grace under pressure and grants the spiritual art of curing poisons, placing Kalimdor's living creatures in their care.

quest:6181.text: A Swift Message. Quartermaster Lewis needs armor for Westfall's militia, and he sends an urgent note to Stormwind by gryphon. With little help from the kingdom's forces, he asks you to take the requisition to Thor at Sentinel Hill for the flight to the capital. At Sentinel Hill, the People's Militia faces Defias outlaws and gnolls with little help from Stormwind's forces. Quartermaster Lewis relies on private contacts in the capital for weapons and armor. As the militia's supplies run low, he turns to Osric Strang, an armorer in Old Town. Lewis asks travelers to carry the urgent requisition note to Thor, Westfall's gryphon master. Gryphons carry people and messages swiftly across the Kingdom of Stormwind. Thor manages the air route to the capital from Sentinel Hill. When you give him Lewis's note, he carries the requisition to Stormwind by air. This route links Westfall's frontier garrison to the capital despite the lack of official aid.

quest:62.text: The Fargodeep Mine. South of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the kobold-held Fargodeep Mine. It lies between the Stonefield and Maclure farms, and its fall points to trouble beyond its tunnels. Kobolds have taken the Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire, between the feuding Stonefield and Maclure homesteads. It once supplied stone and ore for the realm. Now shrill chattering echoes through its damp tunnels, where tallow candles burn. Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the depths and learn how bad the trouble is. When Dughan hears your report, he worries about other mineral sites, including the Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. The news adds to the Stormwind Guard's strain. Its troops are already stretched thin defending against Defias bandits and gnoll incursions, leaving too few to clear the tunnels.

quest:6261.text: Dungar Longdrink. At the roost in Stormwind's Trade District, Dungar Longdrink arranges swift gryphon flights for supplies bound to Westfall's defenders. Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems have brought Westfall close to breaking. Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia badly need provisions. Lewis sent word to the capital, and armorer Osric Strang packed the equipment they asked for. Carrying military cargo on foot through bandit-ridden Elwynn and Westfall takes precious time. Stormwind's new aerial routes offer a vital link to the frontier. In Stormwind's Trade District, the gryphon roost is where Dungar Longdrink coordinates courier and passenger flights. Wildhammer dwarves have long raised and handled these great beasts. Gryphons carry people and cargo across human lands when roosts at both ends know the route. Bringing Osric's heavy crate straight to Dungar shows how aerial transport works. It links the capital's stockpiles to frontier outposts such as Sentinel Hill.

quest:6281.text: Continue to Stormwind. You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town. Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note at Sentinel Hill. Thor, the local gryphon master, offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom’s trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and Elwynn Forest’s river border. Then the gryphon carries you over Stormwind City’s high white ramparts. You land at the capital’s trade roosts, then make your way into Old Town. There you find Osric Strang at his shop, Limited Immunity. Osric supplies the frontier, yet his grim reception shows the growing rift between Westfall’s beleaguered People’s Militia and the distracted rulers in Stormwind Keep.

quest:6285.text: Return to Lewis. A crate of armor is bound for the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill, and Dungar Longdrink sends it from Stormwind by gryphon. The flight crosses Elwynn and Westfall to reach defenders under pressure. Osric, an armorer in Stormwind's Old Town, has packed a heavy crate of armor for the People's Militia volunteers at Sentinel Hill. Defias bandits, hungry gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers threaten Westfall. A lone wagon is an easy target on those roads, so the flight master network gives the armor a safer way to the defenders. Gryphons are loyal and well trained, but they need a known destination before they carry a rider there. Dungar Longdrink explains that they instinctively return to their capital roost in Stormwind. For a remote outpost, you first meet its flight master in person. You have already checked in with Thor at Sentinel Hill, opening the skies over the frontier to swift travel. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis receives the crate and begins distributing its armor among the frontier defenders. He outfits Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteer force. Each shipment helps the militia hold its ground against the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:6321.text: Supplying the Sepulcher. At the Sepulcher, Deathguard Podrig seeks weapons for the hard-pressed garrison. He sends an order toward the Undercity as beasts, Scourge and other threats wear down its supplies. Deathguard Podrig says the Sepulcher is fairly well stocked, yet fighting in Silverpine Forest steadily drains its gear. Feral beasts, Scourge remnants and other local threats wear down weapons and armor or leave them behind after skirmishes. Acting under Executor Hadrec's orders, Podrig writes a requisition for Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer in the Undercity. Replacement arms and armor help the Forsaken hold their fragile footholds beyond Tirisfal Glades. Silverpine's roads make a slow, dangerous route for vital messages and supplies. The Forsaken send them by trained vampire bats instead. Karos Razok handles the bats at the Sepulcher, linking its soldiers to the Undercity's aerial network and the routes connecting outlying garrisons to Sylvanas's capital.

quest:6322.text: Michael Garrett. In the Undercity, Michael Garrett awaits a crate bound for the Sepulcher. Gordon Wendham packs field supplies in the Trade Quarter, and you bring them to Garrett for the Forsaken bat network to carry toward Silverpine Forest. The Forsaken send supplies from the Undercity to outposts such as the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Gordon Wendham packs field supplies in a crate in the Trade Quarter. Moving freight along the ground through blighted forests is slow and leaves it open to ambush by Scourge remnants or wild beasts. The Forsaken use captive vampire bats, bred and kept by skilled handlers, to avoid dangerous roads. Michael Garrett tends the bats from his roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. When you bring him the cargo, it can be strapped to a bat and flown over the hills toward Silverpine, linking the capital with its outposts.

quest:6323.text: Ride to the Undercity. A courier carries Podrig's weapons request from the Sepulcher to the Undercity. A dread bat bears the message over Silverpine Forest to the Forsaken capital. Karos Razok handles the dread bats at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. They carry messengers and supplies between the Forsaken capital and its frontline outposts. The roads below are dangerous, with hostile beasts, Moonrage worgen, and Scourge remnants. The bats give urgent military requests a swift route to the capital. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, the courier brings Podrig's equipment request to Gordon Wendham. The weaponsmith prepares arms for the Dark Lady's cause and keeps outposts such as the Sepulcher supplied with battle-ready weapons. Those outposts defend the young Forsaken nation against its surrounding enemies.

quest:6324.text: Return to Podrig. At the Undercity, you receive a crate of weapons for the Sepulcher after delivering a dispatch to the capital. Forsaken bats carry you across Lordaeron to Deathguard Podrig. Deathguard Podrig's garrison at the Sepulcher needs a steady supply of weapons from the Undercity. In Silverpine Forest, its sentries face worgen, Dalaran remnants, and Scourge stragglers. Fresh armaments help the Forsaken hold the region and keep the outpost ready. Bat Master Michael Garrett tends the central roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Forsaken bats know the way back to the capital, but you speak with local handlers such as Karos Razok before arranging a flight to a distant outpost. Carrying Gordon's Crate across Lordaeron links the Undercity's supplies with its scattered strongholds.

quest:6341.text: The Bounty of Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong is sending fish samples from Rut'theran Village to Auberdine for comparison. She wants to learn whether Teldrassil's fish are larger and more plentiful than those along the mainland coast. Nessa Shadowsong asks you to carry fish bones and scales to Laird in Auberdine. Fishers in Rut'theran Village bring in large, plentiful catches, and she wants to know whether the mainland waters yield the same kind of fish. The samples will let Laird compare the island catch with fish from the coast of Darkshore. Nessa Shadowsong sends you to Vesprystus, the hippogryph master in Rut'theran Village, with the collection for Auberdine. Carrying the samples to him arranges your passage across the water to Darkshore.

quest:6342.text: Flight to Auberdine. You leave Teldrassil for Auberdine with a bundle of unusual fish specimens. Vesprystus sends you from Rut'theran Village by hippogryph to deliver them to Laird. Rut'theran Village is a sanctuary at the edge of the wider world for young adventurers leaving Teldrassil. A mundane ferry crosses the strait between the island and mainland Kalimdor, while night elves also travel by bonded hippogryph. Nessa Shadowsong entrusts you with a parcel of rare fish parts, and you take wing to reach the shores of Darkshore. Laird waits for Nessa's findings at the docks of Auberdine. He finds enormous scales as large as fists and a jawbone nearly twice the size of mainland specimens. The waters around the base of the World Tree seem to produce altered or abnormally large life, a curiosity tied to Teldrassil's potent, restless nature.

quest:6343.text: Return to Nessa. You carry Laird's findings from Auberdine back to Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. The journey is an introductory errand that teaches young travelers how to cross between Kalimdor and Teldrassil. Laird sends you back across the water with his written observations. He has found stark differences between the fish caught off Darkshore and those near Teldrassil, and suspects the great World Tree changes the local marine life. You can return to Rut'theran Village by hiring a flight from Caylais Moonfeather, the hippogryph master, or by boarding the regular ferry at Auberdine's pier. Nessa Shadowsong receives Laird's reply at Rut'theran Village and is fascinated by the difference in marine life. Fish near the World Tree grow so large that they bring an immediate boon to local fishermen, though the Kaldorei still do not know why. Nessa plans to share the findings with her fellow villagers. For now, she is content to harvest the abundant sea life and watch for whatever forces may be responsible.

quest:6344.text: Nessa Shadowsong. In Darnassus, Mydrannul sends a courier to meet Nessa Shadowsong below the World Tree. The delivery runs from Rut'theran Village to Darkshore, linking the canopy city with the shore. Mydrannul watches over travelers seeking work and purpose in Darnassus. Fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong needs a package carried across the sea to Darkshore, so Mydrannul directs able couriers toward the coast. Many young night elves begin their journeys among Teldrassil's boughs; this delivery takes them beyond the tree. From the Temple Gardens, the western portal in Darnassus leads down through the World Tree to Rut'theran Village. At the ocean-level roots, fishing docks and hippogryph perches connect Teldrassil with the rest of Kalimdor. Nessa Shadowsong tends her trade there and prepares shipments for Auberdine.

quest:6361.text: A Bundle of Hides. Jahan Hawkwing sends cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff for leatherworking. The delivery takes you across central Kalimdor and introduces the Crossroads wind rider roost. Hunters bring game hides and meat to the Crossroads, where Jahan Hawkwing gathers pelts from across the Barrens. The outposts cannot process every raw hide, so he asks travelers to carry them west to Thunder Bluff. Master leatherworkers there can turn the pelts into gear for the Horde. The trail across the Barrens and into Mulgore is rough, and quilboar and predators threaten anyone carrying cargo on foot. Jahan sends you to Devrak, the Crossroads wind rider master. He can take the goods by air aboard a trained wyvern, linking the Horde’s scattered settlements.

quest:6362.text: Ride to Thunder Bluff. You carry cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff by wind rider. The flight links the Barrens to the Horde capital above the plains. Devrak carries travelers over the Barrens on the back of a wind rider. For many, this is their first flight across Kalimdor. The wyverns link the young Horde's scattered settlements and spare travelers the ground roads, where quilboar and centaur packs roam. A bundle of cured hides from the Barrens is bound for Ahanu, a craftsman at Hewa's Armory in Thunder Bluff. Ahanu works beneath the great wind rider roost on the central mesa. Supplies from hunting outposts across the plains help him outfit local warriors and hunters.

quest:6363.text: Tal the Wind Rider Master. In Thunder Bluff, Tal the Wind Rider Master awaits a parcel from Ahanu. It is bound for Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads, linking Mulgore’s leatherworkers with Barrens merchants. Ahanu, a leatherworker on Thunder Bluff’s lower rise, sends finished hides to Jahan Hawkwing’s trade stall at the Crossroads. Trade between Mulgore and the Barrens matters to the young Horde, but the journey down the bluffs and across the plains takes hours on foot. Winged couriers carry parcels over the divide. On Thunder Bluff’s highest central tier, Tal tends the city’s wind riders, also called wyverns. The winged beasts cross Kalimdor’s rugged peaks and shifting thermal drafts. Tal arranges flights to outposts such as the Crossroads, carrying messengers and cargo between the tauren capital and its orcish allies.

quest:6364.text: Return to Jahan. You carry finished leather goods from Thunder Bluff back to Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads. The trip introduces travelers to the Horde’s wind rider routes between Mulgore and the Barrens, after they bring hides to Ahanu, the skinner in Thunder Bluff. Tal, the wind rider master on Thunder Bluff’s central mesa, arranges flights across central Kalimdor. For many travelers, this is their first ride on a trained wind rider. A rider can take you to another settlement once you have met its wind rider master, such as Devrak at the Crossroads. The beasts cross leagues that would otherwise mean a dangerous journey overland through the Red Rocks and northern Barrens. Jahan Hawkwing trades from the Crossroads, where hunters, scouts, and mercenaries gather each day. The flight also carries goods between the settlements. Hides sent to Ahanu on Thunder Bluff’s high rises are made into durable armor and equipment, then flown back to the Barrens crossroads to supply the Horde’s growing frontier efforts.

quest:6365.text: Meats to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sends a parcel of Barrens meat toward Orgrimmar. He asks young orc and troll adventurers to carry it to Devrak, the wind rider master, and learn the flight route to the Horde capital. Wildlife fills the Barrens, from zhevras and plainstriders to kodos and thunder lizards. Zargh has prepared choice cuts for a personal delivery to Gryshka, the innkeeper in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Rather than risk the long, dusty trek across the Southfury River into Durotar, he sends runners from the Crossroads to the wind rider perch. Meeting Devrak gives a young Horde warrior a first look at the wind rider flight network. Wind rider masters connect remote outposts like the Crossroads to the Horde's fortified seat of power in Orgrimmar. Devrak prepares you and the cargo for a swift flight over the savannah.

quest:6384.text: Ride to Orgrimmar. A wind rider carries Horde travelers from the Crossroads to Orgrimmar. With Zargh’s fresh cuts of meat in hand, you fly to the capital’s Skytower and deliver them to Innkeeper Gryshka. Devrak sends trained wind riders between the Crossroads and Orgrimmar. The flight crosses the dry Barrens and reaches Durotar’s red cliffs, sparing travelers the hard journey on foot. From high above the dusty canyon trails, the wyverns carry messengers and travelers, along with dispatches and trade goods, straight to the capital. Zargh has prepared fresh cuts of meat for Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Strength. From the central Skytower, her inn is a short walk away. Gryshka accepts the parcel and remarks with fondness that Zargh knows how to win a lady’s heart.

quest:6385.text: Doras the Wind Rider Master. Innkeeper Gryshka needs a courier to carry her thanks to Zargh at the Crossroads. She sends travelers to Doras the Wind Rider Master at Orgrimmar's skytower to arrange the flight back to the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka sends thanks to Zargh after a shipment of meat arrives safely from the Barrens hunting grounds. With no time to travel through Durotar herself, she trusts the established aerial courier network linking major Horde settlements to carry her letter back across the frontier. At the flight tower in the Valley of Strength, Doras oversees Orgrimmar's wind rider roost. The trained wyverns carry military messages and supplies between the capital and outposts such as the Crossroads, far faster than anyone traveling by foot or kodo cart.

quest:6386.text: Return to the Crossroads.. Gryshka's reply is on its way from Orgrimmar to Zargh at the Crossroads. A wind rider carries it across the distance between Durotar and the Barrens. You carry Gryshka's written reply to Zargh after bringing her a parcel of prime meat in Orgrimmar. Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's high bluffs, provides a mount for the return to the Barrens. You have already met Devrak at the Crossroads, so the wyverns know the flight path. The ride crosses the desert sky and saves you the long march overland across the Southfury River. Zargh's courtship has won Gryshka's warm reply. Quality provisions have pleased her, and Zargh celebrates, even musing about an impending wedding. The delivery also brings you back to the Barrens' central hub for travel.

quest:6387.text: Honor Students. Brock Stoneseeker sends an order from Thelsamar to Ironforge for honorary mining picks. He asks you to enlist Thorgrum Borrelson to carry it there. Brock teaches new miners about rock composition and tunnel safety. He rewards the apprentices who distinguish themselves with honorary picks. Mining sustains Thelsamar, and dwarves take pride in the craft. Local supplies are limited, so the picks must come from Ironforge across Khaz Modan. Thorgrum tends the gryphon roost beside Thelsamar, linking the frontier to Ironforge through the kingdom's aerial courier network. Bring Brock's order to him, and he can arrange a swift courier run to the capital's foundries.

quest:6388.text: Gryth Thurden. In Ironforge, Gryth Thurden can send you back toward Loch Modan with a parcel. You carry the Honorary Picks from Golnir Bouldertoe for Brock Stoneseeker's mining apprentices, and the city's gryphon roost offers a way over the mountain roads. You have traveled from Loch Modan to the Great Forge, where Golnir Bouldertoe gives you Honorary Picks for Brock Stoneseeker's mining apprentices. He points you to Ironforge's gryphon network instead of the mountain passes on foot. Carry the bundle across the city to the master handler, who can arrange your flight back. Gryth Thurden oversees Ironforge's flight roosts in the great mountain hall. Gryphon routes link the city with dwarven settlements across Khaz Modan. After scouting the route and speaking with the local handler, you can ask Gryth to arrange transport back to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar. The picks are bound for Brock Stoneseeker's apprentices, and the route joins mountain settlements by air.

quest:6391.text: Ride to Ironforge. Brock Stoneseeker sends you from Thelsamar to Ironforge with the names of his finest mining students. You carry his list to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Great Forge. Thorgrum Borrelson carries you from Thelsamar over Dun Morogh's snowy ridges to the mountain fortress. For many young mountaineers and travelers, this is their first flight on a gryphon. At the Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe carves the students' names into ceremonial honorary picks. These honors recognize their hard work in Loch Modan's quarries and mines.

quest:6392.text: Return to Brock. You carry Brock Stoneseeker’s missive to Ironforge and receive Honorary Picks for his apprentices. Gryth Thurden can fly you back to Thelsamar. Gryth Thurden oversees Ironforge’s gryphon flights from the city’s central platform. To fly to Thelsamar, you first need to have met its handler, Thorgrum Borrelson. Then Gryth can carry you and the picks over the mountains, returning Brock’s message and tools to the Loch. Brock Stoneseeker teaches mining in Thelsamar and needs tools for his apprentices. The Honorary Picks will let young miners work the rich copper and tin veins in the hills around the Loch.

quest:6395.text: Marla's Last Wish. In Deathknell, Marla's Last Wish calls you to bring a husband and wife together in death. Novice Elreth asks you to find Samuel Fipps, still bound to the Scourge, so he can be buried beside his wife, Marla. The Forsaken seek to honor the ties they had in life and to set themselves apart from the Scourge. Marla and Samuel Fipps were husband and wife in Lordaeron before the Third War devastated their home. When the plague swept through their lands, Samuel succumbed and rose as a mindless thrall of the Scourge. Marla escaped undeath, but not her husband. In his frenzy, Samuel killed her. Even then, Marla bore him no hatred. Novice Elreth remembers her final wish: to rest beside Samuel in the Deathknell graveyard. Novice Elreth sends you northeast of Deathknell to find Samuel Fipps, who still wanders among a ruined campsite. Ending his torment would remove a Scourge minion from the valley and let his remains be carried back to Marla's resting place. Elreth believes that honoring the dead and their final wishes sets the newly freed Forsaken apart from the Scourge.

quest:64.text: The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, The Forgotten Heirloom is a pocket watch left behind as the Furlbrows fled their farm. Recovering it gives them a chance to reclaim something personal amid the chaos. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts from the pumpkin patches woke them in the night, leaving little time to gather what they could carry. In their flight, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse. Defias thugs and thieves, including Benny Blaanco, now pick through the abandoned Furlbrow farm. Returning for a keepsake could mean death for ordinary folk. You can take the pocket watch from the wardrobe and restore a measure of dignity to a family that has lost nearly everything to Westfall's lawlessness.

quest:6401.text: Kaya's Alive. In Stonetalon, Kaya Flathoof has survived the Grimtotem attack and reached safety. Makaba Flathoof sends you to Sun Rock Retreat with the news for her worried aunt, Tammra Windfield. The Grimtotem strike along Stonetalon's contested trails. After their village fell under attack, young Kaya Flathoof was feared dead or captured by the renegades. Her rescue brings relief amid the fighting between tribes in the crags. Makaba Flathoof sends you from Kaya to Sun Rock Retreat with word of her safety. Kaya's aunt, Tammra Windfield, waits there anxiously for news from the trails. Your message brings comfort to the family and keeps the remote Horde outpost connected.

quest:6421.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Kobolds dig furiously for Resonite in Boulderslide Ravine, deep in the Stonetalon Mountains. From Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal sends Horde scouts into the caves for samples, troubled by a growing tension in the earth. At Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal watches the Stonetalon peaks with concern. The earth feels disturbed, with an unnatural agitation rising from the southeast. In Boulderslide Ravine, kobolds have left their usual foraging to dig aggressively for Resonite, a rare mineral found beneath the surface. Mor'rogal sends Horde scouts past the kobolds and into the cave's deepest reaches to learn why they mine with such frenzy. He asks them to bring back raw samples.

quest:6441.text: Satyr Horns. At Splintertree Post, Pixel hires Horde adventurers to gather satyr horns for Ratchet. The traveling goblin sees a chance to trade them in the port town. Pixel, a traveling goblin, sees a chance to profit while resting at Splintertree Post. Satyr horns are in high demand in Ratchet, and Pixel wants them for the journey back south to the port town. Rather than risk facing the corrupted creatures, Pixel hires passing adventurers to bring back sixteen intact horns. Demonic satyrs haunt scattered, fel-tainted ruins across Ashenvale, remnants of their betrayal during the ancient sundering. Hunters can search their strongholds at Night Run, the fortified camp of Satyrnaar, and the shadowed groves of Xavian. Horns gathered from any of these places are the trophies Pixel seeks for Ratchet's merchant wharves.

quest:6442.text: Naga at the Zoram Strand. At Zoram Strand, Naga threaten the Horde's hold on Ashenvale's coast. From Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai seeks to drive the Wrathtail away from the sunken ruins of ancient Zoram. The Horde's hold on Zoram Strand is fragile. Hostile night elf territory and bitter woodland fighting surround the outpost, whose coast links the Horde to the sea. Aggressive naga have now crawled ashore. They could cut off that link and overwhelm the small garrison before its defenses are ready. Zoram Strand's sandy shoals hide the shattered remains of Zoram, an ancient elven city swallowed by the Great Sundering thousands of years ago. Marukai and the outpost's defenders do not know why the Wrathtail have come out of the deep trenches now. Their sudden interest in the sunken ruins threatens anyone walking above them. Marukai sees a simple fight for survival. With swords and tridents drawn, reason matters little. She demands twenty severed heads from the Wrathtail, hoping force will drive the naga back into the depths and secure the shore for the Horde.

quest:6461.text: Blood Feeders. In Malaka'jin, Blood Feeders begin with butchered game drawing Deepmoss spiders toward the trolls' camps. Xen'Zilla asks the Horde to drive the predators back from the settlement. The trolls founded Malaka'jin as a frontier outpost in southeastern Stonetalon Mountains, where they could hunt. The craggy slopes offer plenty of game, but its meat draws nocturnal predators into camp. Deepmoss spiders are aggressive arachnids native to the crags and canyons to the north. Under cover of darkness, they slip in to scavenge the trolls' stores or hunt the hunters themselves. Xen'Zilla asks you to track the predators north into the mountain passes. That will help keep Malaka'jin safe and protect its supplies. Deepmoss Creepers and Venomspitters gather thickest around the rocky ravines and webs of Sishir Canyon. Thin their numbers, and the brood will retreat from the settlement. Then the hunters can rest without fearing an ambush from the shadows.

quest:6462.text: Troll Charm. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Mitsuwa seeks sacred charms stolen from his kin. A traveling party of Darkspear trolls was ambushed and slaughtered by the Thistlefur furbolgs, who took the talismans into their den. Zoram'gar Outpost is a remote Horde refuge on Ashenvale's western coast. Woodland paths make travel there dangerous. A party of Darkspear trolls never reached the post after the Thistlefur furbolgs ambushed them. Mitsuwa accepts that his kin have died and will one day meet him in the afterlife. Their sacred charms were stolen from the dead, however, and he cannot abide that insult. Troll charms and talismans mark identity, offer spiritual protection, and bind their bearers to the Loa. Mitsuwa sees a troll without her charm as hollow and worthless, like an orc without battle scars. The Thistlefur furbolgs carried the stolen charms to Thistlefur Hold, deep in the caves beyond Thistlefur Village. They hid the talismans in chests, far from their rightful owners.

quest:65.text: The Defias Brotherhood. From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle sends you east to Lakeshire, where a contact may know where the Defias Brotherhood hides. The People's Militia cannot find who directs the bandits. Gryan Stoutmantle needs the cartel's inner circle and its commander exposed before the thieves can be stopped. Wiley the Black waits upstairs at the Lakeshire inn. Stoutmantle trusts the rogue's underworld ties to reveal the Brotherhood's hideouts. Whether Wiley can offer a lead is still uncertain.

quest:6523.text: Protect Kaya. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Kaya Flathoof is found captive among hostile Grimtotem tauren. Horde adventurers guide her along dangerous mountain trails to Camp Aparaje, then bring word of her survival to her anxious father, Makaba Flathoof. Kaya Flathoof was captured and held prisoner deep in Grimtotem territory in the Stonetalon Mountains. The tauren clans are divided by bitter rivalries, and few are sharper than the hostility surrounding the Grimtotem. Kaya has escaped captivity, but reaching friendly ground on foot means winding through trails watched by enemies and predators. An armed escort is her best hope of getting through. Camp Aparaje lies in the eastern Stonetalon Mountains, and Kaya knows the way home from there. She aims for the camp, where she can continue on her own. You guide her through paths where ambushes threaten, helping her avoid recapture on the way to safety.

quest:6541.text: Report to Kadrak. At the Crossroads, Thork sends proven Horde fighters north to report to Kadrak. The orc holds a watch tower near the Ashenvale border and prepares recruits for the fighting ahead. The Crossroads faces quilboar, centaur, and local brigands, while the Horde looks north to Ashenvale's thick forests. Thork directs fighters who have proved themselves in the central Barrens to the northern border tower, where Kadrak is stationed. Kadrak oversees the southern approach to Ashenvale and organizes reinforcements for the Horde's foothold across the border. Splintertree Post and an outpost along the Zoram Strand help the Horde strengthen its presence in the timber-rich woodlands, where native night elves resist them fiercely.

quest:6542.text: Report to Kadrak. At Malaka'jin, Darn Talongrip sends Horde warriors north to Kadrak's watch post. The dispatch carries them from defending Stonetalon's crags to the campaign in Ashenvale, where the Horde holds outposts at Splintertree Post and the Zoram Strand. Darn Talongrip watches the Horde's southern and mountain frontiers from Malaka'jin. The orc sees capable fighters passing through Stonetalon and directs them toward the northern Barrens watch tower. Ashenvale is the greater pressure point, where night elf sentinels clash with Warsong lumber gatherers. The Horde needs fighters there as the struggle over the forest continues. Kadrak oversees Horde troop movements from a watch tower in the northern Barrens, where the savannah meets Ashenvale. The Horde holds outposts at the Zoram Strand in the west and Splintertree Post to the north. Kadrak coordinates supplies, troops, and urgent reports across the contested forest.

quest:6543.text: The Warsong Reports. Kadrak sends couriers from the northern Barrens to gather reports across Ashenvale. The Warsong Reports carry orders and field observations from outriders near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand. Kadrak watches the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale from a fortified tower. The Horde needs the pass because the Barrens cannot supply the timber Orgrimmar requires. The Warsong clan has pushed into the ancient elven forest to reach those supplies. Couriers carry orders between scattered patrols and help keep them in step, while night elf ambushes threaten the wilderness trails. Warsong scouts watch three parts of Ashenvale. On the western coast, a runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches naga activity and other coastal threats along the Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, a scout coordinates defense against Sentinel raids. Farther east, an outrider watches the road toward the shattered ruins of Azshara. Their reports give Kadrak a view of night elf movements and weaknesses along the frontier.

quest:6544.text: Torek's Assault. From Ashenvale's wilds, Torek's Assault strikes Silverwing Outpost. Under orders from Splintertree Post, the orc raider Torek leads a brazen, bloody skirmish to crush Sentinel resistance and slay their commander, Duriel Moonfire, in the war for Ashenvale's borders. The Horde's lumber camps and the native night elves are locked in an escalating border war across Ashenvale. Torek gathers a pack of Splintertree raiders just outside Silverwing Outpost to break the Alliance's defensive perimeter. He leads a head-on charge before the night elves can counterattack or mount a reinforced campaign against Splintertree Post. Silverwing Outpost is a fortified woodland garrison held by vigilant Silverwing Sentinels and fierce elven warriors. Torek targets their leader, Duriel Moonfire. Bringing Duriel down decapitates the local night elf military hierarchy, allowing the raiders to report a bloody victory to their commander, Ertog Ragetusk, at Splintertree Post.

quest:6545.text: Warsong Runner Update. Across Ashenvale, Warsong Runner Update warns of mounting pressure on the Warsong Clan's border. The report alerts commanders to increasingly bold naga attacks on Horde outposts. Across Ashenvale, Warsong scouts and runners watch the fighting and keep supply lines open. Night elf sentinels and the forest make their work dangerous, so frontier commanders need news quickly. Couriers carry dispatches to remote garrisons and to commanders such as Kadrak at the Mor'shan Rampart. Horde defenders expect night elves among the trees, yet outpost sentries report bolder naga attacks. The serpentine invaders strike from waterways and ancient ruins, testing barricades and drawing defenders from forest and border patrols. A dispatch to the Mor'shan Rampart warns of these coordinated assaults from the water.

quest:6548.text: Avenge My Village. Makaba Flathoof asks Horde travelers to answer the Grimtotem assault on his village in southeastern Stonetalon. He barely survived, cut off from his kin and surrounded by the dead, and now seeks vengeance at the ruffians’ and hired sellswords’ encampment. Near the Barrens border, Makaba Flathoof is the lone survivor of a massacre in the red stone passes of Stonetalon. Grimtotem raiders descended without warning and slaughtered nearly everyone in his settlement. Makaba fought back and brought down several attackers, but they drove him into hiding with little more than his life and his wrath. The Grimtotem have long troubled the tauren tribes united under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Unlike the peaceful nomads of Mulgore, their warbands use ruthless ruffians and opportunistic mercenaries to seize territory and strike isolated settlements. Makaba has no thought of diplomacy or tribal kinship now. Only blood repaid with blood can answer his grief.

quest:6608.text: You Too Good.. Lumak sends you from Orgrimmar to find his friend Nat Pagle. Your skill has outgrown ordinary lessons, and Nat camps on a distant islet south of Theramore Isle. Lumak trains fishers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He sees that you have learned all he can teach about rod and reel, and admits you are too good for ordinary lessons. To learn the art of artisan fishing, you must seek knowledge beyond the city and the Horde. Lumak sends you to find his human friend, Nat Pagle. He warns you not to harm or eat Nat, despite the friction between the Horde and Alliance across Kalimdor. Nat camps on an islet south of Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh. He keeps clear of politics and cares only whether the fish are biting.

quest:6611.text: To Gadgetzan You Go!. In Orgrimmar, Zamja sends Horde cooks south to learn from an eccentric goblin butcher. Zamja trains cooks in the Drag, where she feeds warriors and travelers passing through Durotar. When a cook has learned every recipe and technique she can teach, Zamja admits she has imparted all her culinary mojo. She sends her seasoned pupil to Tanaris, saying only a master of strange and exotic meats can help a talented cook advance further. In Tanaris, Gadgetzan is a steam-powered trading hub run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Dirge Quikcleave works inside the town tavern. The eccentric goblin butcher has an unconventional palate and no squeamishness about food. Across Kalimdor, he is known for turning monstrous desert creatures, and sometimes scraps of leather, into hearty meals for hardened adventurers.

quest:6623.text: Horde Trauma. At Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Horde Trauma calls skilled medics into front-line surgery. Doctor Gregory Victor, chief physician of the Horde's trauma division, seeks hands able to save lives under extreme pressure. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, the orc first aid trainer Arnok tells proficient healers that they have caught Doctor Gregory Victor's attention. Victor oversees Horde Trauma from Hammerfall, tucked away in the contested hills of the Arathi Highlands. Arnok regards the summons as the pinnacle of professional advancement for a battlefield surgeon. At Hammerfall, constant skirmishes with Stromgarde's forces and local hostile factions leave Victor inundated with wounded grunts, raiders, and scouts. The chief physician wastes no time welcoming recruits with pleasantries. Instead, he orders newcomers into their scrubs to prove their worth in brutal, fast-paced emergency triage.

quest:6625.text:
Alliance Trauma. Across the Alliance, accomplished medics are sent to Theramore Isle for service. There, you study under Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen, chief physician of the Alliance's elite medical corps. Your skill with needle, cloth, and triage has drawn Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen's notice. From Theramore Isle, he leads Alliance Trauma, caring for the wounded in Kalimdor's fiercest warzones and beyond. In Ironforge, Nissa Firestone treats VanHowzen's personal summons as a rare privilege. Theramore Isle faces regional threats, skirmishes, and harsh wilderness, so grievously wounded soldiers arrive in a steady stream.

You cross the sea to Dustwallow Marsh. There, VanHowzen tests how calmly you assess the wounded against his rigorous triage standards.

quest:6629.text: Kill Grundig Darkcloud. At Grimtotem Post, Grundig Darkcloud leads the Grimtotem force that sacked Makaba Flathoof's home. After you strike down the ruffians and mercenaries, Makaba sends you after Grundig and his brutes. Makaba Flathoof survived the assault on his settlement along the Stonetalon trail, but his grief is still raw. After you prove yourself against Grimtotem foot soldiers, he points you toward Grundig Darkcloud, the one behind the bloodshed. Grundig commands a devoted band of brutes and led the slaughter that leveled the village. Grundig camps at Grimtotem Post, farther up the mountain road to the west. To avenge Makaba's kin and protect the pass from more violence, you climb to the stronghold, fight through Grundig's brutes, and kill him before his raiders can descend on other vulnerable camps.

quest:6641.text: Vorsha the Lasher. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Vorsha the Lasher terrorizes the Horde's foothold on Ashenvale's coast. The nearby naga honor the hydra's ferocity with an offering brazier on an offshore island. Muglash plans to extinguish its flame, drawing Vorsha ashore to end her attacks. Northwestern Ashenvale's Zoram Strand is among the most dangerous stretches of coast. Zoram'gar Outpost holds a narrow strip there, beset by hostile wildlife, night elves, and serpentine invaders. Among the strand's most destructive threats is Vorsha the Lasher, a gargantuan hydra known for brutal, unprovoked strikes against the outpost. She surges from the surf to crush its defenses and butcher its warriors, then vanishes into the deep tides. The nearby naga venerate Vorsha's ravenous violence. On a rocky outcrop offshore, they keep an offering brazier burning in her honor. Muglash, an orc determined to end the outpost's constant harassment, has realized that defiling the ritual flame will enrage both the naga guardians and the hydra. Vorsha will surge to the surface in fury, giving the defenders a chance to draw her into an ambush instead of waiting for another surprise slaughter.

quest:6962.text: Treats for Great-father Winter. At the Smokywood Pastures display in Orgrimmar, the Greatfather Winter performer is worn out from hearing holiday wishes. He asks you for gingerbread cookies and milk. The Greatfather Winter who greets visitors in the Valley of Strength works for Smokywood Pastures. Long hours listening to citizens speak of festive treats leave him hungry. He turns to passing travelers for warm baking and a cold drink. You can bake the cookies with Holiday Spices sold by Smokywood Pastures peddlers and Small Eggs gathered from wild birds. Bring them together with Ice Cold Milk from a local tavern, and the feast's organizers offer you festive cheer and a small token of gratitude.

quest:6984.text: A Smokywood Pastures' Thank You!. Great-father Winter waits in Orgrimmar to thank those who recovered Smokywood Pastures' stolen holiday treats. Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive a token of appreciation for bringing the supplies back. In Orgrimmar, Smokywood Pastures sells treats, recipes, and seasonal cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. Their shipment was stolen in the snowy hills of the Alterac Mountains, and business stalled. With the treats recovered and the Abominable Greench dealt with, Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive the company's thanks. Great-father Winter waits beside the holiday tree in the Valley of Strength. The goblins have arranged for him to honor those who rescued the holiday supplies with a seasonal blessing and a Smokywood Pastures Special Gift.

quest:7.text: Kobold Camp Cleanup. In Northshire's northern woods, kobold numbers threaten the abbey grounds. Marshal McBride needs the camps cleared, and the valley's defense depends on fresh volunteers. Marshal McBride directs the valley's defense from Northshire Abbey, but he has too few soldiers. So he depends on fresh volunteers like you. Each threat he cannot answer could disrupt the abbey's work or spread into the vineyards nearby. The kobold camps cannot wait. Kobolds are timid, candle-obsessed cave-dwellers who usually pick at underground seams, away from direct sunlight. Now an entire clan has reached the northern timberline. Left alone, their numbers could turn scavenging into open raids. McBride sends you to thin their vanguard and test your resolve to defend the realm.

quest:7025.text: Treats for Greatfather Winter. In Ironforge, the dwarf playing Greatfather Winter asks you for a holiday treat. Bring five freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk, and he thanks you with a festive gift. Smokywood Pastures sponsors the Winter Veil festivities in Ironforge. By the holiday tree in the Commons, a performer sits dressed as Greatfather Winter. For hours, he hears holiday wishes from citizens and eager children. He wears the guise of an immortal figure from ancient titan lore and dwarven myth. After hearing requests for gifts all day, the performer grows hungry. He asks for five freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk. The simple meal gives the exhausted festival worker a moment of relief. Your kindness spreads goodwill through Ironforge.

quest:730.text: Trouble in Darkshore?. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker seeks help for his missing crew. His introductory appeal sends travelers across the sea to Auberdine, where the dwarven expedition met Darkshore's wild, shadowy coast. Darnassus, the grand night elven capital, is home to dwarven researchers from Ironforge studying Kalimdor's ancient mysteries. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sent an excavation party across the water to Darkshore to unearth artifacts of antiquity. Weeks have passed without a message or progress report, and Greywhisker fears his field crew has met dangers they could not survive alone. Greywhisker laments that many in the Alliance dismiss dwarven archaeology as an eccentric hobby. Findings in Khaz Modan have convinced his colleagues that an ancient, terrifying force threatens Azeroth from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. The work in Darkshore's ruins is more than scholarship: it seeks to understand historic cataclysms and the deep-seated menaces buried beneath ancient soil.

quest:743.text: Dangers of the Windfury. Ruul Eagletalon asks you to test your readiness against the Windfury harpies in Mulgore. The hunt takes you to the southeastern cliffs, where their speed and claws put your skill to the test before you leave the tauren homeland. In Bloodhoof Village, Ruul Eagletalon watches travelers pass through Mulgore. He asks those coming of age or preparing for wider travels to prove their combat instincts. Beyond Mulgore's sheltered valleys, survival demands poise against cunning foes, and Ruul measures your mettle against the land's fiercest native predators. The Windfury harpies roost along Mulgore's southeastern mountain rim, away from the beaten trails. They threaten wandering wildlife and isolated travelers, diving swiftly and striking with razor-sharp claws as they hunt for fresh flesh. Defeating them and bringing back their talons proves you can overcome a settled threat and react quickly to aerial attackers.

quest:745.text: Sharing the Land. In Mulgore, Baine Bloodhoof calls you to stop Palemane gnolls from killing the plains' wildlife. By striking their hunters, you help protect the herds and the tauren way of living with the Earth Mother. The tauren take from the land only what they need and honor the Earth Mother in all things. Palemane gnolls have settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, where they slaughter wildlife across the plains. Their hunting leaves carcasses behind and harms the balance of the grasslands. The tauren are building a peaceful home in Mulgore, but the gnolls' wasteful killing threatens it. Baine Bloodhoof tried to speak with the Palemane gnolls and settle the matter peacefully. They rejected every attempt and kept killing wildlife. Now Baine sends young braves to their hunting camps to put down the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer lasting harm. When you return, Baine teaches that taking life is never for malice, but may be needed to keep harmony. Life and death form a circle, and every guardian of Mulgore must carry that truth.

quest:746.text: Dwarven Digging. At Bloodhoof Village, Baine Bloodhoof fears the dwarves' digging will anger Mulgore's beasts and scar its sacred earth. He asks young Horde defenders to break the prospectors' picks and halt their work. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have marked out a dig site in Mulgore's hills. The Explorer's League searches Kalimdor for titan relics and secrets of the earthen, often without regard for the lands or customs of those who live there. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother, worthy of reverence rather than excavation for stone and metal. Baine Bloodhoof sees the dwarves' machines and blasting as a threat to the plains' fragile balance. Their noise agitates the local wildlife and stirs the kodos into frenzy. The tauren mean to smash the prospectors' picks at the forges, sending a blunt warning and stopping the digging before it causes lasting harm.

quest:747.text: The Hunt Begins. Young hunters at Camp Narache gather food and feathers for their people. Grull Hawkwind asks you to hunt plainstriders on Red Cloud Mesa, where the village depends on what the young can provide. On Red Cloud Mesa, the tauren hunt to feed and clothe their people. They also value the stalk and chase as a test of discipline and a sport. When Camp Narache's stores run low, the young hunters gather plainstrider meat for cooking and feathers for tribal garments. Grull Hawkwind judges the newcomers who hope to leave Red Cloud Mesa for the wider plains of Mulgore. Before they can meet his father, Chief Hawkwind, he asks them to prove their ability. A successful hunt shows self-reliance and helps support the tribe.

quest:748.text: Poison Water. In Mulgore, tainted wells threaten the water that sustains the tauren and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village asks young Horde defenders to gather parts from the plains for a cleansing totem. Goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted Mulgore's wells, threatening the water that sustains the tauren tribes and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder in Bloodhoof Village, has discovered the pollution. For the tauren, who recently settled here, the wells are vital to life on these sacred plains. Mull turns to tauren shamanism to cleanse the Winterhoof Water Well. He needs a ritual totem made with the strength of Mulgore's native beasts. You gather paws from prairie wolves and talons from mature plainstriders on the southwestern plains, bringing the land's own strength to bear against the pollution.

quest:749.text: The Ravaged Caravan. Near Stonebull Lake, The Ravaged Caravan still draws Venture Company salvagers. Morin Cloudstalker sends travelers to inspect the wreckage after tauren warriors burned the convoy in retribution for lost companions. Intact crates reveal the industrial scale of Venture Company operations in Mulgore. Tauren warriors burned a Venture Company convoy after an earlier skirmish cost them two companions. Morin Cloudstalker and his warriors struck swiftly, then torched the wagons to drive out the armed intruders. They left the smoking wreckage, believing the fire would consume whatever the goblins had come to haul. Venture Company salvagers returned to the blackened wreckage, suggesting the fire had failed to destroy the most crucial cargo. Morin now sends scouts to inspect the remains rather than risk more lives blindly. Intact crates among the soot-stained debris bear the Venture Company Mining Division insignia. They are packed for shipment to central processing facilities.

quest:7493.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. After Onyxia's fall, skilled leatherworkers in Orgrimmar learn how her scales can guard against the black dragonflight. Overlord Runthak recognizes their craft and teaches a rare technique for making protective cloaks, needed against the flames of Blackrock Spire. Onyxia's fall is a triumph for the Horde, yet the black dragonflight remains a threat. The broodmother's scaled hide resists draconic flame. Horde leaders seek craftsmen who can turn the dragon's remains into defensive armor rather than let them go to waste.

quest:7497.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly honors the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft of making a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can work her hide. When a master leatherworker comes to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer sees how much that skill may matter in battles ahead.

quest:751.text: The Ravaged Caravan. In Mulgore, The Ravaged Caravan leaves the Bloodhoof Outrunners with proof of an illegal foothold in tauren territory. The Venture Company is stripping the land's mineral wealth, and the Outrunners prepare to defend their ancestral plains. East of Bloodhoof Village, a ravaged caravan lies beside the road. Inside a sealed supply crate are mined ore and minerals, along with a bound sheaf of Venture Company documents. The papers prove the company has begun mining deep in Mulgore's tranquil valleys without permission. Morin Cloudstalker and his fellow Outrunners watch Mulgore's borders with care. They fear outside factions will exploit their peaceful homeland. When Morin receives the recovered documents, they confirm his worst fears. Smoke rising over the eastern foothills signals an escalating commercial invasion. The tauren must push back against the defilers before their hills are gutted entirely.

quest:752.text: A Humble Task. On the Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind asks a young adventurer to check on his mother. His pressing tribal concerns keep him at Camp Narache, so he sends you southeast to the well where Greatmother Hawkwind went for water. Every member of the tribe is expected to share in its harmony and do their part. For young tauren, duty begins with care for the community, not only prowess against quilboars or predators. Chief Hawkwind is bound to his post by the work of leading and defending the camp. So he trusts young adventurers to watch over the elders. The wells beyond the encampment provide water for the Red Cloud Mesa. Greatmother Hawkwind left Camp Narache early in the morning to fetch fresh water from a spring southeast of the encampment. Territorial wildlife and Bristleback quilboars range across the land. When an elder is away for hours, Chief Hawkwind grows concerned and sends you to make sure she is unharmed.

quest:753.text: A Humble Task. In Red Cloud Mesa, A Humble Task sends young tauren to carry well water to Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks for this service, a first lesson in humility and care for the tribe. Greatmother Hawkwind has walked many trails, though age has slowed her across the plains. She tends to her duties beside the well on Red Cloud Mesa's southern edge. When young tauren with hopes of defending their people meet her, she turns their energy toward the needs of the community. Service gives them a chance to prove themselves through care for others. You carry a filled pitcher northwest to Camp Narache and give it to Chief Hawkwind, the settlement's leader and Greatmother Hawkwind's son. Life across Mulgore's dry plains depends on shared labor and steady supplies of fresh water. By carrying a burden for an elder, you show respect for the people whose care holds the tribe together. When you bring his mother's water to Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sees more than a chore completed. Tauren custom asks those who would champion their people across distant lands to begin with humility and a ready hand. Your quiet discipline catches the chief's eye, and he recommends you for the Rites of the Earthmother, spiritual tests that open the gates to Thunder Bluff.

quest:754.text: Winterhoof Cleansing. The Winterhoof Water Well in Mulgore has been fouled. Mull Thunderhorn gives you a consecrated totem in Bloodhoof Village to cleanse it. Goblin operations have tainted the nearby springs, and clearing this well is the first step toward healing central Mulgore’s waters. Mulgore’s grassy plains rely on ancestral wells to sustain wild game and scattered tauren tribes. The Venture Company has recently brought its industrial mercenaries into the hills southeast of Bloodhoof Village. Their work has contaminated local aquifers and left the Winterhoof Water Well toxic. Wild beasts avoid its water, and nearby camps face danger if the corruption spreads through the earth. Mull Thunderhorn carves a cleansing totem and blesses it in the name of the Earth Mother. Armed Venture Company goons have claimed the spring, so you must brave them to reach the well. Set the totem at its head, and it will drive out the foul runoff. Then clean water can rise from deep within the earth.

quest:756.text: Thunderhorn Totem. In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn asks young Horde champions to help make a sacred cleansing totem. Goblin pollution is spreading through Mulgore's water wells, and natural predator claws will bind the land's primal strength into ritual wood. Mull Thunderhorn needs natural claws to make a cleansing totem. The Venture Company is poisoning Mulgore's water sources through its industrial exploitation, and he works to craft a remedy. Prairie stalkers and flatland cougars roam east and west of Bloodhoof Village. Their claws carry the plains predators' natural essences, channeling their raw, uncorrupted predatory vigor directly into the totem. Tauren tradition distinguishes hunting for sustenance or spiritual balance from the goblins' wholesale plunder. Mull says the native predators' pure way of hunting can help purify corrupted earth. Goblin machinery fouls the springs with oil and industrial waste, while the beasts' natural strength provides the spiritual catalyst to restore the Thunderhorn Water Well.

quest:757.text: Rite of Strength. At Camp Narache, young tauren face the Rite of Strength against Bristleback quilboar. They bring their belts to Chief Hawkwind to prove their courage and defend the tribe. Seer Graytongue calls young tauren to begin the Rites of the Earthmother with the Rite of Strength. Those who seek recognition from the tribal elders and acceptance in Thunder Bluff must face this duty. The trial tests whether an initiate can meet the tribe's mortal foes with courage and act to defend Red Cloud Mesa. East of Camp Narache, Brambleblade Ravine is home to Bristleback quilboar. The quilboar trespass on ancestral lands, ambush hunting parties, and raid camp supplies under cover of darkness. You are asked to slay them and bring back their belts. The proof shows your valor and helps keep the settlement secure.

quest:758.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing. In Mulgore, Thunderhorn Cleansing calls you to purify the Thunderhorn Water Well. Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem for the rite, and the Thunderhorn ancestors give their thanks when the spring is clean. Water wells sustain the tauren tribes who have settled Mulgore's grasslands. When poison taints an underground spring, the wildlife and nearby settlements suffer. The Thunderhorn Water Well lies north of Bloodhoof Village, and its waters need spiritual cleansing. Mull Thunderhorn makes a Cleansing Totem for the rite. Carry it to the poisoned spring and channel ancestral power through it to drive out the toxins. When the cleansing succeeds, the Thunderhorn ancestors visit Mull in a dream and give thanks.

quest:759.text: Wildmane Totem. At the Wildmane Well, Mull Thunderhorn seeks to heal Mulgore's last poisoned waters. He needs prairie wolf alpha teeth for a totem that can cleanse them. The Wildmane Well is the last poisoned source in central Mulgore. Mull Thunderhorn has gathered what he needs for the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, yet poisoned water still harms migrating wildlife and settlements across the plains. Powerful ingredients from the land are needed to restore its balance. Prairie wolf alphas roam Mulgore's grasslands, especially beneath the high bluffs below Thunder Bluff. Mull Thunderhorn needs their teeth for a cleansing totem meant for the northern waters. Their strength and endurance will lend the totem the power of these fierce hunters. For tauren, taking from the land's creatures carries solemn weight. Mull Thunderhorn sees the alpha teeth as a necessity, not a conquest. The predators' sacrifice may help heal the Earth Mother's poisoned waters.

quest:76.text: The Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have overrun the Jasperlode Mine in eastern Elwynn. Marshal Dughan sends scouts to learn how far the infestation has spread. After kobolds swarmed the Fargodeep tunnels south of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan feared they had reached other mines. Jasperlode lies in the rocky foothills northeast of the Tower of Azora and supplies raw stone and metal to the kingdom.
