Dughan cannot spare Stormwind guards from their town patrols, so he sends independent adventurers east to see whether kobolds have taken this mine too. Scouts who reach Jasperlode's chambers find kobolds have driven out the human miners and fortified the dark passages. Marshal Dughan faces another blow as the crisis grows. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and royal troops are withheld from outlying territories. The local garrison has too few soldiers to clear the mines, leaving the kingdom's heart short of minerals and hemmed in by threats.

quest:760.text:
Wildmane Cleansing. In Mulgore, the tauren's cleansing work reaches its final well. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village sends you north with the completed Wildmane Totem to cleanse the poisoned water and protect the tauren's way of life. Mulgore's wells sustain the herds, the soil, and the tauren tribes gathered around Thunder Bluff. The Venture Company and encroaching goblins have fouled them with toxic industrial runoff. The tauren elders see the danger to their people and their land.

The Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are purified. Now the Wildmane Water Well remains, the third and final corrupted site. Its waters still need spiritual cleansing. The Wildmane Cleansing Totem is made from elements gathered across the region. It draws on the restoring power of ancestral spirits and elemental earth. Plant it beside the foul waters north of Thunder Bluff. The ritual disperses chemicals, draws out toxins, and revives the natural flow.

The cleansing guards the tauren against disease. It also makes clear they will not tolerate the despoiling of their sacred ground.

quest:761.text: Swoop Hunting. Harken Windtotem asks you to track swoops across Mulgore. Their quills test patience, cleverness, and marksmanship, and honor the trials of the Earth Mother. Across Mulgore's open grasslands, swoops test a hunter's eye. These large birds blend into sky and plain, wheeling overhead or skimming low through tall grass. They demand focus and swift feet, unlike lumbering plainstriders or grazing kodo. Young hunters pursue them to prove their skill and earn standing among the tribes. Harken Windtotem asks for trophy quills to teach discipline, not to cull wildlife. Tauren carry tokens from a hard-won stalk as signs of cleverness and perseverance. Unblemished quills presented to the elders in Bloodhoof Village show a hunter can sustain and defend the community. Swift hooves and sharp senses prepare them for the wider world.

quest:763.text: Rites of the Earthmother. At Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sends you beyond Red Cloud Mesa to continue the Rites of the Earthmother. After the first trials, you carry a carved totem north to Bloodhoof Village and Baine Bloodhoof. Young tauren have tested their strength at Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa for generations. The first trials teach discipline and resolve. Yet the sacred Rites of the Earthmother reach beyond surviving the mesa's wildlife. Chief Hawkwind knows when an initiate is ready to leave the sheltered hunting grounds and join the wider community. Chief Hawkwind gives you a hand-carved totem to introduce you on the road from Narache to the central settlements. Carry it down the winding path to Bloodhoof Village and present yourself to Baine Bloodhoof, the young chieftain and son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. The totem is your credential and seal of approval. It marks your readiness for the rites of spirit and wisdom ahead.

quest:764.text: The Venture Co.. In Mulgore's eastern hills, goblins dig despite the tauren's refusal. The Venture Co. brings them in force to quarry the Earth Mother's soil, and Morin Cloudstalker calls for a lethal answer. The tauren honor Mulgore as part of the Earth Mother. They value its open plains and the balance of its wildlife. When the Venture Company asks to blast and excavate the hills for ore, the tribes refuse. The company ignores them and brings machinery, laborers, and overseers into the eastern ridges to mine without permission. Morin Cloudstalker and the other tauren scouts see no use in further appeals once the mining begins. Documents from a ravaged Venture Co. caravan confirm the operation. Morin sends you against the overseers who crack the whips and the laborers who drive the drills. He means for the company to pay dearly for trespassing.

quest:765.text: Supervisor Fizsprocket. In Mulgore, Morin Cloudstalker calls for help against the Venture Company mine. Documents from a ruined caravan show a plan to drive the tauren from their homeland, and Morin needs Supervisor Fizsprocket's clipboard. A Venture Company caravan lies destroyed, and its documents reveal a plan to drive the tauren from Mulgore. The company wants the plains and the veins beneath them for itself. It means to take their resources without the tauren in its way.

quest:766.text: Mazzranache. In Bloodhoof Village, Mazzranache's bite leaves Maur Raincaller feverish and near death. A generation ago, the plainstrider haunted his grandfather's tales. Now Maur suffers delirious nightmares as the venom threatens his life. Maur Raincaller knew Mazzranache only through his grandfather's tales. The elder tauren spoke of a savage plainstrider with glowing red eyes, razor-sharp talons, and a toxic bite unlike that of most Mulgore wildlife. Then Maur met the beast on the open grass. His grandfather's warning came true, and the bite left him badly wounded as he struggled to reach safety. Mazzranache's venom brings Maur a high fever and nightmarish delirium. He needs a remedy before the infection turns fatal. Traditional tauren medicine draws on the vitality of local beasts, so Maur needs a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, a plainstrider scale, and a swoop gizzard. Together, these parts can make a brew to halt the necrotic spread and nurse him back to health.

quest:767.text: Rite of Vision. Baine Bloodhoof sends travelers across Mulgore to seek Zarlman Two-Moons before the Rite of Vision. The trial belongs to the Rites of the Earthmother, and elders on the rises of Thunder Bluff regard it as a sign of spiritual readiness. For generations, the nomadic tauren have followed the Earthmother’s guidance across Kalimdor’s plains. Now they have gathered within Mulgore’s safe borders, where spiritual traditions remain at the heart of their society. Earlier trials test an initiate’s strength and bond with the hunt. The Rite of Vision turns inward, calling young tauren and honored allies to commune with the spirits. Before seeking a vision, an initiate needs guidance in the ancient ways. In Bloodhoof Village, the revered shaman Zarlman Two-Moons offers that counsel. Baine Bloodhoof entrusts travelers to his care. Zarlman recognizes those who walk the ancestors’ path, then gives them the first rites and sacred preparations to look beyond the physical world.

quest:768.text: Gathering Leather. On Thunder Bluff, Veren Tallstrider asks hunters to bring light leather for the capital. He trades crafted goods for the hides, following the tauren way of making clothing and armor from the plains hunt. Thunder Bluff needs skilled hands to make clothing and armor for its growing population. Veren Tallstrider works skins into useful goods and asks young hunters returning from the plains to bring him their quarry. Their hunts help supply the capital and feed the tribe. Tauren hunt across the grasslands to feed, clothe, and shelter the tribe. Veren Tallstrider asks hunters who would bring honor to their clan for light leather from local wildlife. In return, he trades crafted goods for twelve well-kept hides, sustaining the ties that bind tauren society.

quest:769.text: Kodo Hide Bag. Veren Tallstrider teaches Thunder Bluff's apprentice leatherworkers a craft drawn from the plains. He asks for cured light leather and sturdy thread. Veren Tallstrider teaches leatherworking on Thunder Bluff's crafting rises. He follows the nomadic way of wasting nothing from the hunt. Bring cured light leather and sturdy thread, and he will teach you. With these basic materials, apprentices show they can make goods to carry survival gear across Kalimdor's rugged expanses. To the tauren, the kodo is a sign of endurance, strength, and steady resolve. Its thick hide guards against brambles, biting wind, and beast claws. Making bags and garments from kodo hide is useful work, and it honors the animal that has fed and carried the Shu'halo across Mulgore's plains for generations.

quest:770.text: The Demon Scarred Cloak. In Mulgore, The Demon Scarred Cloak carries the wounds of Ghost Howl's torment. The hide came from a legendary white wolf scarred by the Burning Legion. Its arrival in Bloodhoof Village brings the beast's troubled story to a close. Ghost Howl is a legendary white wolf whose sorrowful howl carries across Mulgore. The hide left by the beast bears the scars of demonic corruption. Those marks came from desperate battles against the invading demons of the Burning Legion. The wounds lingered in Ghost Howl's flesh and spirit long after the Third War. Mulgore's tauren revere the wild beasts of their homeland as children of the Earth Mother. In Bloodhoof Village, Skorn Whitecloud receives the scarred cloak as proof that the tormented predator is dead. He recognizes the skill it took to track and defeat Ghost Howl. Somberly, he hopes the wolf's tortured spirit has found peace.

quest:771.text: Rite of Vision. Across Mulgore, young tauren gather offerings for the Rite of Vision. In Bloodhoof Village, Zarlman Two-Moons guides them as they brew the Water of the Seers and seek counsel from ancestral spirits. Zarlman Two-Moons sends you across Mulgore for well stones and ambercorn. The stones rest near sacred communal wells, while ambercorn falls beneath the roots of ancient trees. To the tauren, these are more than gifts from the land. They carry the Earth Mother's latent magic and lifeblood, ready for the rite. Zarlman combines the well stones and ambercorn to brew the Water of the Seers. You drink it beside the village's tribal flame. The draught clears your mind and summons an ethereal guide. Then you follow the guide across the plains, testing whether you can walk between the physical world and the land's spiritual whispers.

quest:772.text: Rite of Vision. At Bloodhoof Village, young tauren drink the Water of the Seers and glimpse the path before them. A spectral guide rises beside the tribal bonfire. After gathering the ritual herbs and passing the first trials of faith, you receive the Water of the Seers from Zarlman Two-Moons. You drink it before the tribal fire at the heart of Bloodhoof Village. Keep your mind focused and respectful, and the sacred water opens your sight beyond the physical world. It joins the material and spiritual realms. Once you drink the brew, an ancestral ghost wolf appears in the flames. It neither speaks nor fights, but lopes northwest across Mulgore's rolling plains. Follow its quiet path away from the village and into the rocky hills. There, the hermit Seer Wiserunner waits in secluded meditation. The vision ends when you reach Seer Wiserunner at the mouth of his mountain cavern. The walk across grassy hills tests your patience, your trust in ancestral guidance, and your attunement to the Earth Mother. Pass the rite, and you earn the right to face the Rite of Wisdom, the ultimate test of adulthood.

quest:773.text: Rite of Wisdom. At Red Rocks, the Rite of Wisdom brings the Rites of the Earthmother to their final trial. After the Rite of Vision clears your sight, you travel to commune with an Ancestral Spirit and seek the dead’s blessing. After the Rite of Vision clears your sight, you travel east of Thunder Bluff to Red Rocks. Those buried here fought and died so Mulgore could know peace, and their spirits still linger. Approach their resting place with reverence and seek communion. The hills are guarded by threats as you seek counsel from the honored dead. At Red Rocks’ summit, you commune with an Ancestral Spirit. The meeting tests your spiritual readiness and your place in the generations, not your strength in battle. These spirits fought beside Cairne Bloodhoof to establish Thunder Bluff and protect the tribes. Their blessing marks you as an adult and defender. You are charged with protecting the city and may enter Thunder Bluff with pride.

quest:775.text: Journey into Thunder Bluff. The spirits send you from Mulgore to Thunder Bluff after the Rites of the Earthmother. Cairne Bloodhoof, High Chieftain of the tauren, awaits you there. Across Mulgore, the Rites of the Earthmother test your strength, vision, and wisdom. The trials lead across the plains and through the land’s ancestral sites. When the Ancestral Spirit acknowledges your final rite, you have proved yourself worthy to enter Thunder Bluff as a defender of the tauren people. From the sacred ground where spirits wander, you travel upward to Thunder Bluff. The city crowns red stone mesas, joined by rope bridges and great wooden elevators. Cairne Bloodhoof, High Chieftain of the tauren, awaits you on the High Rise, ready to greet those who have followed the ancestors’ path.

quest:776.text: Rites of the Earthmother. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof sends you across Mulgore to track down the great kodo Arra'chea. Even after the old rites, he asks his people to prove their strength, tracking, and devotion anew. Arra'chea's horn shows Cairne you are ready to serve the wider Horde. In Thunder Bluff, a young tauren's childhood gives way to duty. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof asks young hunters to keep proving themselves. Reaching the high bluffs begins a life of service to the United Tauren Tribes. Cairne asks for more than a hunt for small pests: he wants proof of fieldcraft, shown by tracking and cleanly harvesting one of Mulgore's renowned wandering beasts. Arra'chea is a massive, legendary kodo whose looping path crosses the golden grasses northeast of Thunder Bluff. Bringing down this great beast takes patient stalking across the open savannah, not brute force alone. Return Arra'chea's horn to the high rise, and Cairne sends skinners and gatherers to use every part of the sacred beast for the city's provisions.

quest:7781.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head reaches Stormwind Keep after his defeat in Blackwing Lair. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives it as proof that the master of Blackrock Mountain has fallen. The victory ranks among the Alliance's greatest military triumphs in recent history. Nefarian, brood-master of the Black Dragonflight and ruler of Upper Blackrock Spire, has long threatened the surrounding human kingdoms. His defeat ends his twisted experiments and schemes. His battle-scarred head is carried back to Stormwind, proof that the Alliance's greatest heroes have brought down the Lord of Blackrock. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs the kingdom from Stormwind Keep's throne room. The dragon's severed head shocks the royal court and commands reverence. The kingdom faces internal political strife and threats from beyond. This victory lifts morale and earns a place in Alliance history.

quest:7782.text: The Lord of Blackrock. At Stormwind's gates, the Alliance gathers to honor its victory over Blackrock. After you report to Grand Admiral Jes-Tereth in Stormwind Keep, the heroes make for the Valley of Heroes. Field Marshal Stonebridge is ready to lead the city's public commemoration. Field Marshal Stonebridge raises Nefarian's severed head above the great arches at Stormwind's main entrance. The sight carries across the city, and the Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer inspires defenders, visiting dignitaries, and citizens. They know Deathwing's brood has suffered a crushing blow.

quest:7783.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head is carried from Blackrock Mountain to Orgrimmar as proof of victory. Presented to Warchief Thrall, it marks the fall of a great enemy of the Horde. Nefarian has fallen at last. He masterminded Blackwing Lair and led the black dragon brood in the Eastern Kingdoms. His colossal, battle-scarred head proves his death. For Horde warriors, carrying the prize from the burning heights of Blackrock Mountain across the Great Sea to Durotar brings great honor. The trophy is brought before Warchief Thrall. He knows the corruption of Blackrock Mountain well. He freed his people from the internment camps and led them away from the old Horde's demonic bloodlust. The son of Deathwing has fallen, and the Blackrock orcs are free of the dark dragon's cruel dominion.

quest:7784.text: The Lord of Blackrock. In Orgrimmar, Nefarian's severed head is brought before the Horde. After Thrall confirms the black dragon's death, he sends the victor to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength to show the trophy to all. Nefarian's head reaches Orgrimmar after the black dragon is slain atop Blackwing Lair. Warchief Thrall confirms that Deathwing's son has fallen, then sends the victor to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength. There, the remains are prepared for public display, a warning to enemies and a rallying cry for the true Horde.

quest:780.text: The Battleboars. At Camp Narache, young tauren hunt battleboars to guard their lands and feed the tribe's youth. East of Red Cloud Mesa, Brambleblade Ravine lies in Bristleback quilboar hands. Tensions between the Shu'halo and the quilboar have grown into open war. The Bristlebacks train vicious battleboars to test tauren borders and trouble their old hunting grounds. Left unchecked, the beasts endanger game trails and Camp Narache alike. Hunting keeps the tauren safe and feeds the tribe. Grull Hawkwind asks the young hunters to bring back the battleboars' snouts and flanks. Even these beasts, trained by quilboar hands, are put to use. Their meat and gristle go into stew for the tribe's youth, turning a quilboar weapon into food for the next generation of tauren defenders.

quest:781.text: Attack on Camp Narache. At Camp Narache, you carry a warning that could give the tauren time to call for aid. The Bristleback quilboar are planning a siege, and Chief Hawkwind needs to know. In Brambleblade Ravine, you find a crude map on the cavern floor. Its dirt-stained markings reveal the Bristleback quilboar plan a long siege against Camp Narache. This is more than a string of scattered attacks. You bring the attack plans to Chief Hawkwind at Camp Narache. Few defenders guard the camp, which shelters young initiates, so Hawkwind prepares to send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements. Your warning gives the camp time to prepare for the siege.

quest:783.text: A Threat Within. In Northshire Valley, volunteers answer Stormwind's call as local defenses falter. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride directs the response, and you begin serving on the threatened grounds. Northshire Valley once gave people quiet for prayer, farming, and monastic study. Now it is Elwynn Forest's first defense against unrest at home. Few guards remain nearby, so the Stormwind Guard calls on each willing volunteer who reaches the abbey. Trouble spreads across the surrounding countryside. From Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride directs the valley's defenses as danger grows. Bandits, vermin, and pests from below ground threaten the people nearby. You begin by clearing the ground around the abbey, where these threats press close to the valley's defenders and the place they protect.

quest:784.text: Vanquish the Betrayers. At Tiragarde Keep, Kul Tiran forces hold a coastal foothold in Durotar. Gar'Thok has ordered a Horde strike against Lieutenant Benedict's garrison, whose presence breaks the fragile peace with Theramore. Thrall led the Horde across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, where he joined Lady Jaina Proudmoore against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Peace broke when Jaina's estranged father, Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, brought Kul Tiras's navy to Durotar. He blamed all orcs for the Old Horde's atrocities and seized coastal footholds, including Tiragarde Keep. Daelin died at Theramore, but remnants of his fleet still refuse any pact or surrender their hatred. Tiragarde Keep fell briefly after the Grand Admiral's defeat, then Kul Tiras reserves under Lieutenant Benedict retook it. The fortress lies between Razor Hill and Sen'jin Village. From there, sailors and marines harass travelers and threaten Durotar's eastern sea approaches. Gar'Thok sees their position as an immediate danger to Durotar's security and calls on Horde warriors to strike at Benedict's command.

quest:786.text: Thwarting Kolkar Aggression. Lar Prowltusk has found invasion plans in Kolkar Crag, west of Sen'jin Village. The Kolkar centaurs plan to strike Durotar's settlements and Orgrimmar. Lar Prowltusk, a troll tracker scouting western Durotar, slipped into Kolkar Crag under cover of night. There he found the Kolkar centaurs planning more than scattered coastal raids. Three centaur leaders had divided the invasion plans among them, with attacks aimed at the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village, and the gates of Orgrimmar. You are sent into Kolkar Crag to destroy the three attack scrolls before the centaurs can strike. The dry canyons hold their camps, and each scroll belongs to a different leader. Lar Prowltusk believes the Horde would defeat a full invasion, but burning the plans can spare Durotar's defenders costly fighting while their young nation finds its footing.

quest:787.text: The New Horde. In the Valley of Trials, veteran warrior Eitrigg calls new recruits to the Den. He sends you to Gornek to begin training and shares why he returned to the Horde and what Thrall hopes it can become. Eitrigg stands in the Valley of Trials under Warchief Thrall's orders, ready to evaluate and mentor the Horde's newest hopefuls. After the Second War, he abandoned the Old Horde, disillusioned by its corruption by the Burning Legion. He lived in quiet exile until humans captured him. Thrall rescued Eitrigg, and the veteran chose to return after learning of the young Warchief's dream: an honorable Horde rooted in ancestral shamanism and entirely free of demonic masters. Before you venture beyond the harsh canyons of the Valley of Trials, Eitrigg sends you into the shaded cavern called the Den to speak with Gornek. Gornek rarely minces words about the crude state of new aspirants. His oversight ensures that only those who master discipline and survival enter the wider reaches of Durotar.

quest:791.text: Carry Your Weight. Atop the watchtower overlooking Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow asks young Horde adventurers to gather canvas from human and centaur hostiles. Too old for the front lines, the scarred veteran will make supplies to aid their journey. Furl Scornbrow fought beside Warchief Thrall in Durotar and at Mount Hyjal. Age and old injuries have slowed the veteran, and he no longer wields his axe in battle. From the Razor Hill watchtower, Furl keeps a steady vigil and sounds the alarm against incursions. He supports the next generation of defenders from his post. As the Horde's grip on the region tightens, signal horn alerts grow less frequent, leaving Furl more hours to craft practical gear. Sturdy canvas is scarce in Durotar's arid canyons, but the Kul Tiran interlopers along the eastern shore and the nomadic Kolkar centaur roaming the plains carry it in abundance. Canvas scavenged from these hostile forces gives Furl cloth to stitch utility bags for active scouts.

quest:792.text: Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Vile Familiars are creeping out of a nearby cavern. Zureetha Fargaze found a hidden Burning Blade coven while watching over the valley's trials. Recruits are sent to hunt the familiars spreading across Durotar's red earth. The Valley of Trials tests young orcs and Darkspear trolls in strength, discipline, and loyalty to Thrall's Horde. Its trials were meant to pit recruits against scorpids and boars, not demonic corruption. Yet a cave to the northeast shelters agents of the Burning Blade, who have formed a secret coven beneath the valley overseers' watch. Zureetha Fargaze, an instructor guiding newcomers near the Den, spotted the taint before it could overrun the canyon. Vile Familiars now pour from the cave mouth, hurling fire at anyone who wanders too close. Before the Horde can root out the masters in hiding, young recruits are sent to cut down these lesser servants and keep the valley secure.

quest:794.text: Burning Blade Medallion. Zureetha Fargaze sends young Horde initiates into the Burning Blade Coven cave in the Valley of Trials. They face a hidden cultist and seek a dark relic, the Burning Blade Medallion. Its presence points to demonic corruption taking root near the Horde. Young orcs and trolls face trials of combat and survival in the Valley of Trials, while a menace gathers nearby. The warlock Zureetha Fargaze senses through divination that the vile familiars on the northern bluffs are only the vanguard of a darker presence. Deep in a nearby cavern, the Burning Blade cult has made a hidden coven, where its followers practice dark arts and keep dangerous relics of demonic power.

quest:8.text: A Rogue's Deal. In Deathknell, Calvin Montague asks you to carry an unmarked message to Brill. He calls it a simple delivery and promises generous coin. Calvin Montague lounges among Deathknell's graves and ruined chapels. He says Scourge zombies and creeping spiders have worn him down, then asks you to carry an unmarked letter to Brill. He promises generous coin. For a newly awakened Forsaken, it seems a simple way to reach the region's main town.

quest:804.text: Sarkoth. In the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua waits for help after Sarkoth's venom leaves him stranded. You have slain the scorpid that wounded him; now Gornek needs word at the Den so aid can reach the scout. Hana'zua, a Darkspear scout, lies stranded on the high bluffs of the Valley of Trials. Sarkoth's venom has left him too weak to descend the treacherous paths alone. You have avenged him by slaying the scorpid, but he still cannot cross the arid stones without help. A passing initiate must carry word down to the training encampment. Gornek waits at the Den for your report. Once he hears of Hana'zua's plight, he recognizes the danger from Sarkoth and organizes aid for the scout. Horde commanders honor those who set aside their own training to defend and rescue a fallen stranger. Such conduct proves an initiate's worth before they march into Durotar proper.

quest:805.text: Report to Sen'jin Village. Zureetha Fargaze sends word from the Valley of Trials to Sen'jin Village. Burning Blade cultists have been active in the valley, and she asks young initiates to warn the Darkspear trolls. Master Gadrin tells them dark magic threatens the nearby Echo Isles. Young initiates leave the Valley of Trials after proving their combat mettle and recovering dark medallions from the Burning Blade Coven. Zureetha Fargaze sees that the demons in the sacred proving grounds are no isolated nuisance; they point to a blight spreading across Durotar. She sends the proven fighters east past the ravine's mouth, then south toward the coast, to warn the Darkspear tribe.

quest:806.text: Dark Storms. In Durotar, Burning Blade cultists corrupt the land from Thunder Ridge. Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill has learned that the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm leads them, and asks you to end his threat. Orgnil Soulscar has learned that dark magic has taken hold in Thunder Ridge, northwest of Razor Hill. Burning Blade cultists prowl the ravine while young Horde defenders patrol Durotar’s borders. Their presence brings ruin to the wildlife and land. Fizzle Darkstorm, a goblin warlock allied with the Burning Blade, directs the cultists in Thunder Ridge. He wields fel power for the cult rather than serving commerce or cartel interests. Slaying him and bringing back his twisted claw will show Orgnil that the cult’s leaders in the ravine have been struck down.

quest:808.text: Minshina's Skull. In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin hears the desperate cries of his dead brother, Minshina. Zalazane slew Minshina on the Echo Isles and bound his soul with dark magic to his own severed skull. To free him from torment, you must reclaim the skull from Zalazane's ritual grounds. Master Gadrin is one of the Darkspear tribe's spiritual anchors in Sen'jin Village, yet dark visions torment him. His brother Minshina fell when Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized control of the Echo Isles. Minshina died in the conflict, but death has brought him no peace. In troll tradition and voodoo mysticism, the body can die while the spirit remains bound. Now Minshina's tormented voice reaches Gadrin in his dreams, pleading to be saved from a fate worse than death. Zalazane does more than kill his former brethren; he traps their souls to fuel his dark sorcery. He bound Minshina's spirit to his own skull, now set within a blasphemous circle of power on the largest of the Echo Isles. Hexed trolls guard the circle, where candles burn through the rites and the skull focuses Zalazane's twisted mojo. While it remains there, Minshina is captive to the witch doctor's will.

quest:809.text: Ak'Zeloth. Neeru Fireblade sends you from Orgrimmar into the Barrens after signs of demonic corruption emerge. His contact waits near the border. Neeru Fireblade says the Burning Blade still threatens the Horde with demonic corruption. After you bring him a Burning Blade insignia collar from Durotar, he sends you into the Barrens. A cult gathers around the Demon Seed, an artifact of vile power, and Neeru wants you to find his contact near the border.

quest:812.text: Need for a Cure. Rhinag lies poisoned on Durotar’s northwestern cliffs, far from the cure he needs. The Darkspear troll has little time before the venom kills him, so he sends a passing courier to Orgrimmar for Kor'ghan’s remedy. Rhinag was fighting venomtail scorpids near Durotar’s border when one stung him. Their venom can kill in less than an hour. The poison keeps him from walking to Orgrimmar, so his survival depends on a traveler reaching his remote camp in time. Rhinag sends travelers beneath Orgrimmar to the Cleft of Shadow, where Kor'ghan knows how to counter the poisons of Durotar’s wastes. Kor'ghan can brew a cure, though he rarely helps those who have not proved themselves.

quest:813.text: Finding the Antidote. Kor'ghan in Orgrimmar races to brew a cure for the poisoned hunter Rhinag. You gather venomtail poison sacs from scorpids outside the city walls before their venom proves fatal. Durotar's wildlife is unforgiving, and survival depends on wilderness preparation. Rhinag, a Darkspear troll, was hunting in Durotar when he faced venomtail scorpids without an antidote. Their potent venom struck quickly, leaving him in need of immediate aid. Kor'ghan, an experienced hunter in Orgrimmar, must mix a draught before the poison kills him. Mature venomtail scorpids outside Orgrimmar's gates carry the sacs Kor'ghan needs to make an antidote. He says there will be time to chastise Rhinag for going unprepared, but every moment matters now. Bring the sacs back into the city, and Kor'ghan can brew the draught for the dying hunter.

quest:816.text: Lost But Not Forgotten. Misha Tor'kren waits at her homestead for news of her son, Kron. He went west to hunt crocolisks along the Southfury River, and she fears the worst. Misha Tor'kren lives at a farmstead northwest of Razor Hill in Durotar. Days ago, her son Kron set out west toward the Southfury River, along the Barrens border, to hunt its fierce crocolisks. Misha warned him how deadly the beasts were, but pride drove him to leave and prove his strength. No one has seen him since.

quest:817.text: Practical Prey. Vel'rin Fang needs hunters to bring tiger hides from the Echo Isles to Sen'jin Village. The Darkspear need the supplies as their numbers grow and their stores run low. The Darkspear in Sen'jin Village have to make every resource last along Durotar's harsh coast. Tiger pelts can be made into tents, blankets and armor. As refugees arrive and scouts return, the village's stores have thinned, and leatherworker Vel'rin Fang has sent hunters out for more hides. The Darkspear leave the tigers of Durotar largely undisturbed, hunting them only when the tribe needs more supplies. Hunters cross the water to the Echo Isles to track the predators. For the trolls, the hunt also tests patience, discipline and skill in the wild.

quest:818.text: A Solvent Spirit. Master Vornal tests would-be pupils in Sen'jin Village as his eyesight fades. He asks them to gather makrura eyes and crawler mucus along Durotar's coast. Though he scoffs at taking an apprentice, the work tests patience and resolve. Master Vornal lives in Sen'jin Village, where age has dimmed his sight. Primal magic once came readily to his fingertips, but now he relies on alchemy to sharpen his perceptions and weave his arts. Though his body weakens, the stubborn troll refuses an apprentice. He says neither the Darkspear nor Durotar's orcs have produced anyone worthy of his teaching. Vornal asks for raw materials from the harsh coast: intact makrura eyes and vials of crawler mucus. Taking undamaged eyes from armored, snapping makrura calls for careful strikes. Gathering enough mucus tests whether a would-be pupil can endure tedious work. For Vornal, hunting these coastal beasts is less about the reagents than finding out who can keep their focus. For Master Vornal, time and patience measure strength. He expects brash youths to grow frustrated or abandon the work. Bringing pristine ingredients back to Sen'jin Village shows survival skills along the dangerous reefs of the Echo Isles channel, and the discipline needed to master alchemy's subtle arts.

quest:819.text: Chen's Empty Keg. A keg bearing Chen Stormstout’s mark lies abandoned in the Barrens. Its discovery points toward the wandering brewmaster’s old ties to Durotar. Travelers sometimes find an abandoned wooden barrel across the dry Barrens. Razormane quilboar and Kolkar centaur leave ordinary casks behind, but this barrel is carefully made and bears a plaque: “Chen Stormstout - May your spirit be raised and always raise your spirits.” It is an odd relic beneath Kalimdor’s sun. To learn how it came to the Barrens, you seek someone who knows brewing. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet recognizes the keg’s craftsmanship and names Chen Stormstout as its owner. Chen, a wandering Pandaren, traveled with Rexxar during the battles that secured Durotar for Thrall’s Horde. Years have passed since Chen walked Kalimdor’s red earth, yet seasoned brewers still remember his recipes and wandering spirit.

quest:821.text: Chen's Empty Keg. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn hopes to revive Chen Stormstout's potent brew with wild ingredients from the Barrens. A marked keg brings Chen Stormstout to mind for Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet. Chen passed the secrets of his namesake brew to Drohn's mentor, who entrusted them to Drohn. The recipe calls for raw, potent elements taken straight from the Barrens' fierce wildlife, an unusual choice to those outside the brewing trade.

quest:823.text: Report to Orgnil. Master Gadrin sends word from Sen'jin Village to Razor Hill about the Burning Blade. This early Horde dispatch carries a warning of demonic corruption spreading through Durotar. Sen'jin Village faces its own troubles, especially Zalazane's treachery on the Echo Isles. Yet reports of the Burning Blade point to a danger far wider than the village's local woes. Demonic corruption was uncovered in the Valley of Trials, and Master Gadrin knows the threat cannot be met in isolation. He sends you north along the road to Razor Hill, where orc authorities watch over Durotar. Orgnil Soulscar is stationed at Razor Hill's military encampment, charged with rooting out evils within Durotar and guarding its central lands. When you bring Gadrin's warning, Orgnil combines reports from Sen'jin Village and the Valley of Trials. The Burning Blade's reach is dangerously close, so he quickly mobilizes forces to break up the cultists before their rituals can unseat the young nation.

quest:825.text: From The Wreckage..... Gar'Thok sends Horde scouts to the wrecks off the Scuttle Coast for Gnomish Tools. The Horde hopes to study Alliance engineering and turn its advantage to their own use. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore brought Kul Tiras's fleet to Kalimdor, where its ships crowded the shore near Tiragarde Keep. After his defeat, broken hulls sank along the Scuttle Coast. Kul Tiran soldiers who survived fortify the keep, while the fleet's wreckage lies scattered on the shoals beneath the tide. The Horde knows Alliance ingenuity can give its enemies an edge over orcish strength, iron, and blood. Gnomish technicians sailed with the expeditionary fleet and equipped its ships with complex machinery and precise tools. Gar'Thok wants those tools recovered from the wrecks so the Horde can learn how they work. Gar'Thok sends the salvaged tools by caravan from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Horde craftspeople and tacticians hope to study the gnomish instruments and better counter Alliance devices in future conflicts, while strengthening their own industries.

quest:826.text: Zalazane. On the Echo Isles, Zalazane's treachery has driven the Darkspear from their home. Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village sends Horde champions to end the witch doctor's rule. Dark magic drove Zalazane mad, and he enslaved his fellow tribesmen, seizing the Darkspear trolls' rightful home and forcing them into exile on Durotar's coast. The Darkspear made a home on the Echo Isles after fleeing their sunken island and following Thrall across the Great Sea. The isles lie just off Durotar's southeast coast. Zalazane, once a respected and powerful witch doctor of the tribe, hungered for power. He used hexes to enslave the minds of his kin and began a violent uprising. Vol'jin led the Darkspear who remained free, but they were driven from their ancestral camps across the water. They had to build a temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village. Zalazane still sends raiding parties from his hilltop stronghold on the largest Echo Isle. They cross the channel to seize more Darkspear and drag them under his control. The captured trolls become mindless voodoo and hexed thralls, lost to their tribe. Master Gadrin sees more than an occupation of Darkspear land: Zalazane threatens the tribe's survival. Until his severed head is brought before the elders, no Darkspear can be safe.

quest:827.text: Skull Rock. Margoz sends you into Skull Rock, east of Orgrimmar. Burning Blade cultists have overrun the cave and use painful demonic devices to bind themselves to dark magic. Margoz needs the cursed artifacts to study the cult's presence near the capital. In northeastern Durotar, cultists gather close to Orgrimmar's gates. The cave lies among the hills, far from the open roads, yet near the Warchief's seat. The Burning Blade, a demonic cult that has long plagued orcish society, has made its home in the tunnels. Its followers perform rituals there while the Warchief's scouts watch nearby. Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars around their necks, metal bands that scorch and brand their flesh. Margoz believes the pain and fel sorcery in the collars attune their wearers to demonic power. He asks you to recover the collars so he can study the spells and bindings that empower the cultists.

quest:828.text: Margoz. In northern Durotar, Margoz watches for the Burning Blade's growing threat. After the clash with fel corruption at Thunder Ridge, Orgnil Soulscar sends champions to seek the isolated orc shaman before they strike a nearby cultist stronghold. Margoz's counsel reveals Skull Rock, the Burning Blade's concealed cavern base. After Thunder Ridge revealed the depth of fel taint, Orgnil Soulscar sees that strength alone cannot cleanse Durotar. He sends champions to Margoz, an experienced orc shaman keeping a lonely camp in the crags northeast of Razor Hill. Between Drygulch Ravine and the eastern sea, Margoz watches the northern reaches for dark omens that Orgrimmar's busy warriors often miss. Margoz knows the Burning Blade's power base in northern Durotar: Skull Rock, a concealed cavern system carved into the mountain cliffs outside Orgrimmar's southern gates. The cultists are closer to Thrall's capital than the Warchief's guards realize, and Skull Rock's hidden passages can conceal a demonic ambush. Margoz gives those sent against the coven counsel so they do not enter blindly.

quest:829.text: Neeru Fireblade. In Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade studies dark arts he says can protect the Horde. Margoz sends you from Durotar with a Searing Collar taken from the Burning Blade cult, hoping the warlock can explain its demonic power. Margoz has found the limit of shamanic arts. The collars taken from Burning Blade cultists at Skull Rock carry demonic sorcery, beyond what he can unravel. Shamans draw on the elements and ancestral spirits, so Margoz sends you to a warlock in the capital to learn what the collars do. Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow lies beneath its red cliffs. Warlocks and other practitioners of forbidden magic work there under Thrall's wary eye. Neeru Fireblade lives in the cavern and says he studies fel power to thwart demonic threats. When you bring him the collar, his curiosity turns Durotar's investigation toward the warlock enclave.

quest:83.text: Red Linen Goods. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs linen for her tailoring. She asks you to recover bandanas from Defias bandits so she can keep making goods for travelers. Across Elwynn, Defias bandits wear red linen bandanas. Their less organized kin in Northshire make do with cheap burlap masks. The linen gives Sara workable cloth for her tailoring. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs textiles for her trade. Taking bandanas from Defias camps scattered through the woods supplies her with cloth and helps check the bandits' encroachment.

quest:830.text: The Admiral's Orders. On Durotar’s coast, the Admiral’s Orders carry word of a threat to the young Horde. Sealed by the late Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, they show that the Kul Tiran garrison is organized and entrenched. Gar'Thok in Razor Hill needs to know what they contain. On the upper floors of Tiragarde Keep, a heavy chest holds an aged envelope under Lieutenant Benedict’s watch. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore sealed it with his crest. Its parchment gives naval commands from Kul Tiras’s bloody invasion of Durotar. Though the Grand Admiral fell at Theramore, his officers still hold their fortifications and cling to their mission against the Horde settlement.

quest:8311.text: Hallow's End Treats for Jesper!. During Hallow's End, Jesper lies sick in Stormwind and longs for treats and fun beyond the orphanage. Too ill to go out, he asks Alliance adventurers to gather sweets for him. Jesper lies sick in Stormwind's orphanage in Cathedral Square during Hallow's End. While the children gather sweets across Azeroth, he must stay inside. So he hopes passing adventurers will share the holiday spirit and bring him treats. To bring Jesper the sweets he hopes for, you travel beyond Elwynn Forest. You visit the innkeepers of Stormwind, Ironforge, and Darnassus, then the gnome exile Talvash del Kissel. Each asks you to perform before giving you a treat. You cluck like a chicken, dance, flex, or chug like a train, and earn regional sweets such as Stormwind Nougat and Gnomeregan Gumdrops.

quest:832.text: Burning Shadows. In Skull Rock, the Eye of Burning Shadow carries warnings from the Burning Blade. Its voice threatens Gazz'uz with Neeru Fireblade's wrath. After Gazz'uz falls deep within Skull Rock, the Eye of Burning Shadow is found among his remains. The stone carries a voice into the mind of anyone who holds it. The speaker demands a report from Gazz'uz. His secret work east of Orgrimmar has been compromised.

quest:833.text: A Sacred Burial. At Red Rocks in eastern Mulgore, Lorekeeper Raintotem calls on Horde adventurers to protect the sacred burial grounds. Bristleback quilboar have overrun the graves of tauren warriors who gave their lives founding and defending Thunder Bluff. Red Rocks is among Mulgore's most revered sanctuaries, set in the crags beneath the eastern mountains. Only the most valiant tauren are laid to rest there. These legendary warriors shed blood to protect their tribes and their chieftains, and to carve out a lasting homeland atop Thunder Bluff's mesas. To the Shu'halo, disturbing their rest insults both tradition and the Earth Mother. The nomadic Bristleback quilboar have long contested tauren control over central Kalimdor. Their recent push into Red Rocks is a grave escalation. Bands of Bristleback Interlopers have crept onto the holy grounds, ravaging the earth and disturbing the resting places. Lorekeeper Raintotem is too aged to drive them away alone, so young Horde champions must take up arms and defend the honored dead.

quest:834.text: Winds in the Desert. A stolen supply caravan leaves Rezlak waiting in Durotar. Dustwind harpies ambushed it in Razorwind Canyon, scattering the construction materials among the cliffs. Rezlak came directly from Ratchet, sent by Chief Engineer Gazlowe to help the Horde build across Durotar. The harsh, barren land already makes fortification work hard. Now shipments keep vanishing before they reach the building sites, and without the cargo, work stops. The irritable goblin supervisor has nothing to build with. Dustwind harpies ambushed the latest supply run in Razorwind Canyon. They roost along the high ravines beside the road from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, then swoop on passing wagons. These scavengers do not eat or destroy the freight. They hoard the crates and sacks near their nests, where the supplies remain for anyone willing to fight through their territory.

quest:835.text: Securing the Lines. Near Razorwind Canyon, Rezlak needs the goblin supply routes through Durotar protected. Harpies in Drygulch Ravine keep intercepting and plundering caravans, so he hires help to drive them out. Dustwind harpies make travel through Durotar’s dry valleys dangerous. Rezlak watches over regional supply operations for his boss, Gazlowe. The harpies roosting in Drygulch Ravine raid caravans in Razorwind Canyon and seize shipments before they reach their destinations. Rezlak believes the right price can get anything done. Rather than enter the canyon himself, he hires adventurers to break the roost by eliminating Dustwind Savages and Dustwind Storm Witches. Clearing the harpies keeps trade corridors open, secures shipments of engineering gadgets, and points helpful travelers toward greater opportunities in Ratchet.

quest:8353.text: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. At Hallow's End, Innkeeper Firebrew asks Ironforge visitors to cluck for a mint for Jesper, a young orphan in Stormwind. Alliance champions gather sweets from their capitals to bring him cheer. Jesper is sick, orphaned in Stormwind, and longs for Hallow's End sweets. Alliance champions gather treats for him from innkeepers in their capitals. So seasoned adventurers have reason to go door to door during the harvest-to-winter celebration. Innkeeper Firebrew keeps the Ironforge Mints at the Stonefire Tavern in Ironforge's Commons. A polite request won't do. Visitors flap their arms and cluck like chickens before he parts with one. The performance gives the tavern's patrons a laugh, and the mint helps bring holiday cheer to Jesper.

quest:8354.text: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. At Hallow's End, Innkeeper Norman of the Undercity offers a sweet to travelers helping an ailing child. Earn the Undercity Mint by setting dignity aside and flapping like a chicken. Laughter is scarce in the Undercity, built beneath Lordaeron's ruins by the liberated Forsaken. Yet when Hallow's End comes, even the grim folk of the Trade Quarter join the revelry. Innkeeper Norman keeps Undercity Mints for travelers gathering treats for Spoops, a sick orphan who needs holiday cheer. Innkeeper Norman will not hand a treat to seasoned adventurers without a show. He believes grown warriors and spellcasters should earn their sweets. So the petitioner must mimic a barnyard chicken right before his counter.

quest:8355.text: Incoming Gumdrop. Talvash del Kissel keeps a Gnomeregan Gumdrop in Ironforge for a sick child in Stormwind. To earn it, you must give him a convincing train impression. At Hallow’s End, trick-or-treaters visit the Alliance strongholds for treats. In Ironforge’s Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel keeps the Gnomeregan Gumdrop. He feels for the young orphan who hopes to receive it. Yet Talvash asks you to bring some mischief to the holiday with a convincing train impression. Jesper is an ailing orphan in Stormwind City, hoping for four treats from across the Alliance. He wants nougat from Stormwind, a mint from Ironforge, marzipan from Darnassus, and a gumdrop from Gnomeregan. Your locomotive impression entertains Talvash and earns you the gumdrop. It brings Jesper closer to his holiday wish.

quest:8356.text: Flexing for Nougat. At the Gilded Rose, Innkeeper Allison asks you to flex before she gives you Stormwind Nougat. During Hallow's End, you gather festive sweets for Jesper, an orphan in Stormwind. Hallow's End brings a lighter mood to Stormwind. The holiday marks the turn of the seasons and guards against dark spirits. Common folk celebrate with disguises, revelry and trick-or-treating. Alliance innkeepers offer traditional sweets to those who perform a harmless trick. At the Gilded Rose in the Trade District, Innkeeper Allison asks for a show before handing out holiday candy. You are gathering sweets for Jesper, an orphaned boy. Allison playfully comments on your physique and asks you to flex your muscles. When you do, she gives you a piece of chewy Stormwind Nougat.

quest:8357.text: Dancing for Marzipan. During Hallow's End, travelers in Darnassus gather sweets for Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the trick-or-treat custom: a dance comes before her Darnassus Marzipan. Hallow's End brings a lighter spirit to Darnassus, the sacred forest city of the long-lived night elves. You come seeking sweets for Jesper, a sick child recovering in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the season's custom, even when the treat is meant for a child in need. First, she asks for a trick. Saelienne asks you to dance on the inn floor before she gives you Darnassus Marzipan. The performance earns the sweet needed for the holiday care package bound for Jesper.

quest:8359.text: Flexing for Nougat. In Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka offers nougat to those who play along. During Hallow's End, she asks you to flex for a piece meant to cheer Spoops, a bedridden child. Hallow's End brings pranks and sweet-gathering to Azeroth's capitals. In Orgrimmar's inn, Innkeeper Gryshka keeps holiday sweets for those who take part in the season's custom. You face dragons and dark sorcery in your travels, but here the bargain is simple: perform a trick or leave without a treat. Innkeeper Gryshka wants a display of Orcish strength before she gives you Orgrimmar Nougat for young Spoops. Whatever disguise or armor you wear, she asks you to strike a muscular pose. Even the Horde's feared combatants can be made to entertain the common folk for candy.

quest:8360.text: Dancing for Marzipan. Innkeeper Pala asks Dancing for Marzipan visitors to dance during Hallow's End in Thunder Bluff. The treat is meant for a sick orphan, and the custom brings holiday cheer to Mulgore's high mesas. During Hallow's End, Innkeeper Pala keeps the trick-or-treat custom in Thunder Bluff. Even when you come for an ailing child, she asks for a festive dance before giving up her Thunder Bluff Marzipan. For Pala, the custom is simple: step forward and dance to earn a sweet. When you have entertained her, she gives you the marzipan and warm wishes for the sick youth waiting for it.

quest:84.text: Back to Billy. Bernice Stonefield sends you across the road with a pork belly pie for Billy Maclure. He has information about her missing necklace, and the delivery carries on the feud between their families in central Elwynn Forest. The feud between the Stonefields and Maclures leaves little room for kindness. Auntie Bernice Stonefield baked a pork belly pie because Billy Maclure would not share what he knew about her family heirloom without one. She hands you the pie with plain irritation. Bernice hopes Billy chokes on every bite.

quest:840.text: Conscript of the Horde. Along Durotar’s western road, Conscript of the Horde sends recruits toward the Barrens. Takrin Pathseeker watches beyond Razor Hill and gives them a letter for Kargal Battlescar, whose outpost guards the crossing. After proving your strength around Razor Hill, you are called west to serve the wider Horde. Takrin Pathseeker watches the road out of Durotar for his friend, veteran Kargal Battlescar. He gives capable travelers a recruitment letter to carry across the Southfury River. For a recruit, the letter marks a first formal assignment beyond the orcs’ new homeland. Kargal Battlescar holds the outpost beyond the bridge, between Durotar’s red canyons and the dry Barrens. He gathers recruits to guard the frontier, where centaur, quilboar, and Alliance expeditions test the border. The Horde needs more than guards there: raw manpower is being sent to the settlement of the Crossroads.

quest:842.text: Crossroads Conscription. Recruits leave the Far Watch Post for duty at Crossroads Conscription. Carrying Kargal Battlescar’s signed letter, you report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Barrens’ central hub. Kargal Battlescar sends you west from the Far Watch Post after you prove your worth. He gives you a signed recruitment letter to carry along the packed dirt road through the Barrens’ arid brush. The road reaches a central junction, where the Crossroads links northern Kalimdor with the southern wilderness. Sergra Darkthorn receives new arrivals at the Crossroads. Warchief Thrall chose the sharp-tongued orc shaman to oversee its operations. Kargal Battlescar grumbles that she is difficult and talks too much, but Thrall holds her in high esteem. Sergra is fierce and unyielding. She reminds recruits, especially arrogant men, that female warriors and leaders stand as equals in Thrall’s Horde, and she will tolerate no insolence.

quest:844.text: Plainstrider Menace. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends new Horde adventurers after plainstriders east of the outpost. The birds threaten its food supplies, and the hunt gives newcomers a first measure of the Barrens. The Crossroads coordinates supplies across Kalimdor, but plainstriders east of the outpost have begun picking at its food crates. Sergra Darkthorn, an orc shaman, sends newly arrived Horde adventurers to hunt the birds before they damage the stores. Their attacks threaten provisions the settlement depends on. Sergra Darkthorn uses the hunt to measure newcomers as well as protect supplies. She sees the plainstriders as simple prey, fit to teach young hunters to endure the elements and track quarry across the sun-baked plains. Bringing back their sharp beaks shows a hunter has patience and the basic martial skill needed to face fiercer beasts of the Barrens.

quest:845.text: The Zhevra. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde warriors after the zhevra. Their hunt tests the skills needed to face the Barrens' more dangerous beasts. After the plainstriders, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after tougher prey. Zhevras run in herds across the northern and southern Barrens. They are not the savanna's fiercest beasts, but they are swift and stubborn, and their kicks can break bone. Sergra uses the hunt to test your growing skill. She asks for four intact hooves as proof of the kill and warns that a zhevra's rear kick can knock a grown tauren onto their haunches. Passing this trial brings you closer to facing the plains' predatory prowlers.

quest:848.text: Fungal Spores. At the Barrens oases, Horde adventurers gather Fungal Spores for Apothecary Helbrim of the Royal Apothecary Society. Strange, mutative energies flow through the springs and alter the local plants into potent reagents. Helbrim seeks the specimens to brew concoctions for his colleague in Thunder Bluff. The Barrens is a dry savanna, but the Forgotten Pools, Lushwater Oasis, and Stagnant Oasis brim with unnatural vitality. A curious surge of life energy flows from their waters, warping and invigorating plants and beasts that drink there. Laden mushrooms grow along the muddy banks, absorbing those currents. Their spores hold rare properties that draw the curiosity of passing alchemists. Apothecary Helbrim works at the Crossroads, far from the Undercity, yet remains devoted to the Royal Apothecary Society's research. He gathers the altered spores because Kalimdor's native reagents have strange potency, and he uses them to craft powerful mixtures. The specimens are destined for Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, part of the Forsaken's scientific work across allied lands.

quest:85.text: Lost Necklace. In southern Elwynn, Bernice Stonefield looks for her missing necklace. She suspects Billy Maclure, the young son of the family across the road, and asks you to find him. The Stonefields and Maclures live on adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but goodwill between them is scarce. When “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield finds her cherished necklace missing, she blames the youngest Maclure. Certain Billy Maclure came onto her farm and took it, the bitter widow asks you to cross the road to the vineyards, find the boy, and demand its return.

quest:850.text: Kolkar Leaders. Regthar Deathgate moves against Kolkar leaders gathering strength in the Barrens. The nomadic centaur have plagued the tauren for generations. Now new chieftains are uniting scattered bands into a military threat, and Regthar sends Horde champions against Barak Kodobane at the Forgotten Pools before his influence spreads. Centaur have terrorized Kalimdor for countless years. Before Thrall's Horde arrived and turned the tide, they drove the nomadic tauren nearly to extinction. In the Barrens, the dominant Kolkar tribe usually roams in scattered marauding bands. Now aggressive chieftains are joining those bands together, making raiders strong enough to challenge the Horde's fortified outposts. Regthar Deathgate, an orc warrior, is stationed in an encampment west of the Crossroads. He knows boldness and brute force hold the Kolkar together. Without strong commanders, their raiders fall to infighting. So Regthar sends Horde champions against the leaders to blunt their advance. Barak Kodobane, an ambitious chieftain, is the first target. He is camped near the waters of the Forgotten Pools.

quest:851.text: Verog the Dervish. Across the southern Barrens, Verog the Dervish keeps moving, and Regthar Deathgate seeks to draw him out. The orc directs Horde champions to attack the Kolkar command tent at the Stagnant Oasis, hoping to force the nomadic leader into the open. After Barak Kodobane fell, Regthar Deathgate turned to the remaining Kolkar warlords. Barak had stayed near the northern waters of the Forgotten Pools, but Verog the Dervish roams the sun-baked plains and rarely lingers in one camp. Horde scouts cannot easily track him across that wide territory. Their chance is to make the commander come to them. Verog operates from the Kolkar command post at the Stagnant Oasis, southeast of the Crossroads. Regthar sends you against the camp, where you strike the Kolkar warriors near their command tent. Their alarm calls Verog back to defend the outpost, bringing him within reach of the Horde blades.

quest:852.text: Hezrul Bloodmark. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark directs the Kolkar incursions across the Barrens. Regthar Deathgate sends you to end his command and break the centaur's hold on the region. After Barak Kodobane and Verog the Dervish fall, Hezrul Bloodmark remains the Barrens Kolkar's paramount chieftain. Regthar Deathgate calls him brutal and cunning, the spearhead behind the centaur incursions across the savanna. The Horde hopes his death will sow chaos and fracture the Kolkar ranks beyond recovery, before they can overwhelm Horde settlements. Hezrul commands his warbands from Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. The few watering holes in the Barrens are vital to survival, making this oasis a strategic hub and a staging ground for Kolkar raiders. On Hezrul's own ground, you deny the centaur their most vital stronghold and sever their hold on the southern trails.

quest:853.text: Apothecary Zamah. Apothecary Helbrim needs his volatile fungal emulsion carried from the Barrens to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. The mixture must reach her laboratory beneath Spirit Rise before it loses its potency. Apothecary Helbrim has cooked fungal blooms from the Barrens oases into a delicate emulsion. The brew quickly loses strength once prepared. Helbrim cannot travel to Mulgore in time, so he entrusts the flask to a reliable runner bound for Thunder Bluff. Apothecary Zamah works in the Pools of Vision, a cavern beneath the sacred heights of Spirit Rise. Forsaken mages and priests share the underground refuge. Beneath the tauren sanctuary, the Royal Apothecary Society quietly studies raw materials gathered across the continent.

quest:854.text: Journey to the Crossroads. At Camp Taurajo, Kirge Sternhorn sends travelers north to aid Thork at the Crossroads. The journey carries them from Mulgore into the Barrens and the wider struggles of the Horde. Camp Taurajo is where many tauren first face the Barrens beyond Mulgore. Just past the mountain pass, mystic Kirge Sternhorn watches travelers descend into the dry grasslands. When Sternhorn sees that a traveler is ready to go farther, Kirge points north along the dusty trade route toward the Crossroads. The tauren of Thunder Bluff and Thrall's new Horde now share their fortunes. Kirge says the two peoples' fates are bound together, and orcs at the Crossroads need reinforcements as they struggle to establish an outpost. At the settlement, Thork welcomes travelers from even the high bluffs, ready to test their strength against the dangers of the savanna.

quest:855.text: Centaur Bracers. West of the Crossroads, Regthar Deathgate calls for Centaur Bracers. Kolkar centaurs contest the central Barrens, threatening Horde control of the plains. The young Horde is fighting to secure territory across Kalimdor. The Barrens lie between Durotar and Mulgore, but Kolkar centaurs contest its watering holes and open plains. They attack supply trains and scouting parties. Regthar Deathgate, an orc warrior, directs the defense from his bunker west of the Crossroads. Regthar asks for proof that Kolkar warriors have fallen. Soldiers who enter Kolkar territory bring back bracers taken from slain centaurs. The trophies verify claims for Horde bounties and are meant to frighten surviving Kolkar raiders.

quest:8569.text: Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch. In Warsong Gulch, soldiers hold Ashenvale’s southern border while commanders honor their sacrifices. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks steadfast service, even when battle brings no clear victory. Along Ashenvale’s southern border, the Silverwing Sentinels and Warsong Outriders fight brutal skirmishes. Many battles end without a clear victory. Stormwind, Orgrimmar and other capitals honor those who hold their ground against the odds. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks fighters who gave themselves to the struggle. Far from the front, Alliance Brigadier Generals and Horde Warbringers oversee their forces. Recruiters send new fighters to Warsong Gulch, while quartermasters and tacticians account for veterans returning from hard campaigns. By honoring courage in stalemate or defeat, leaders help keep soldiers committed to holding Ashenvale.

quest:858.text: Ignition. At a Venture Company camp in the northern Barrens, a trapped pilot needs an ignition key before their cover fails. The operative hijacked a shredder without its key and needs someone to fetch it from the site supervisor. A spy sent by Sputtervalve has slipped into a Venture Company shredder at the northern Barrens drilling grounds. The operative means to seize the machine and study how it works. But the steering and movement column stays locked without its ignition key. A goblin worker has noticed the shredder sitting idle, so the hijacker bluffs that its engine has failed. Trapped beneath the glass canopy with workers nearby, the operative points you toward the central derrick. The supervisor keeps spare ignition keys in the upper control office, the only way out before the bluff fails.

quest:86.text: Pie for Billy. In Elwynn, you gather meat for Bernice's pie while Billy holds back what he knows about her necklace. Bernice agrees to bake, though she believes Billy stole her family's jewelry. Billy Maclure gives no apology when you ask about the necklace. He will neither return it nor name who has it until he gets a freshly baked pork belly pie. He knows Bernice is the finest cook in the valley, and means to enjoy the bargain. Bernice is furious at the thought of feeding the boy she believes stole her family's jewelry. Still, she agrees to bake before you gather the meat. You bring her meat from wild boars roaming nearby pastures. She sets aside her pride, hoping to get her prized necklace back.

quest:860.text:
Sergra Darkthorn. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits tauren hunters leaving Mulgore behind. Melor Stonehoof sends them north into the Barrens, where danger grows harsher and the Horde's lands reach beyond their home. When their first trials are done, Melor Stonehoof sends young tauren hunters east from Mulgore. Bloodhoof Village and its valleys are familiar ground, where patient tracking has prepared them for what comes next. Now he tells them to pack their gear and cross the mountain pass into the Barrens, leaving their homeland's safety for harsher country. The road winds through red rock canyons before opening onto the Barrens' broad, sun-scorched savanna. There, where Kalimdor's central trade routes meet, the Crossroads is a fortified settlement shared by orcs, trolls, and tauren.

Sergra Darkthorn waits on its eastern side. The experienced orc shaman demands much of the hunters she guides. She teaches those who come to stalk the Barrens' fierce wildlife, testing their eagerness against the discipline the wilderness requires.

quest:861.text: The Hunter's Way. In Mulgore, Skorn Whitecloud guides aspiring trackers through the Hunter's Way. To prove their skill and respect for the wild, you hunt flatland prowlers and bring their claws to Melor Stonehoof on Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise. For the tauren, hunting is among the highest honors. It calls for patience, attention to the Earth Mother's balance, and respect for the beasts across the plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud has spent decades tracking across Kalimdor and now rests in Mulgore. He sees young adventurers eager to roam and gives them a traditional trial to shape their ambition into discipline. Flatland prowlers test a candidate's tracking skill. These great cats move swiftly and quietly, hiding in Mulgore's high grass before ambushing their prey. Bring four sets of claws to show you can spot a predator before it catches you, then turn its ferocity against it. After gathering the claws, you climb the wooden towers and bridges to Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise. Melor Stonehoof receives the trophies there. A master tracker who values Skorn Whitecloud's ancient wisdom, Melor accepts them as proof that you have the spirit to learn more of Kalimdor's hunting ways.

quest:863.text: The Escape. You help Wizzlecrank flee the Venture Company drill site at the Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. Trapped in a stolen prototype shredder, the goblin pilot needs protection from company mercenaries as he climbs from the industrial pit. Afterward, you report to his contact, Sputtervalve, in Ratchet. Wizzlecrank struggles to control the stolen shredder at the Sludge Fen. He has lit the prototype deep inside the Venture Company drill site, but knows little of its levers and switches. The heavy machine lurches across the muddy quarry floor, and its erratic driving and roaring joints alert nearby laborers and armed guards. A stealthy escape becomes a running battle up the excavation pit’s western ramp. The Venture Company sends mercenaries to stop the stolen prototype. As the machine claws up the slope toward open ground, squads move to intercept and disable it. The shredder lashes out, but cannot withstand their sabotage without your protection. It clears the rim and staggers from the main drilling depression, though the machine soon suffers a critical failure.

quest:8642.text: Silvervein the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers find Silvervein the Elder on the hills above Thelsamar in Loch Modan. They honor him and the ancient ties among Azeroth’s elder peoples, and he grants them an ancestral blessing. Above Thelsamar, Silvervein keeps watch as travelers honor him. He holds memories from ages past. Though trogg invasions and local disputes trouble Loch Modan, the elder spirit remains peaceful on his overlook. Silvervein welcomes travelers who honor Azeroth’s olden races. His greeting carries ancestral appreciation. To those who pay homage, he offers a commemorative token.

quest:8646.text: Hammershout the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, you meet Hammershout the Elder in Stormwind's Park and honor the old races with a ceremonial token. Ancestor spirits walk Azeroth for the festival, offering wisdom and blessings to travelers who pay their respects. In Stormwind's Park, Hammershout the Elder recalls the ancient races who walked the land before today's kingdoms rose. Hammershout the Elder asks only that you acknowledge the past. He is relieved and grateful when people still honor the old races. In return, he gives you a ceremonial token, binding the living to the spirits who came before.

quest:8648.text: Darkcore the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers find Darkcore the Elder in the Undercity and honor Azeroth's ancient spirits. In return, they receive a Coin of Ancestry. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient night elven and earthen ancestors appear across the continents. They offer wisdom and blessings to those who seek them. Elder Darkcore dwells in the Undercity's shadowed halls, watching the world as it is now and remembering those who sought its roots. Approaching Elder Darkcore honors an ancient custom. It shows respect for the venerable dead and Azeroth's timeless wardens. In return for the pilgrimage, the spirit gives travelers a Coin of Ancestry, a token of goodwill and enduring memory.

quest:8649.text: Stormbrow the Elder. Near Goldshire, Stormbrow the Elder greets travelers during the Lunar Festival. They honor Azeroth’s ancient traditions and olden races, and receive a commemorative coin in return. Behind Goldshire’s smithy, a quiet pond lies beneath the forest canopy. There Stormbrow the Elder appears as an honored spirit. Guards, tradesfolk, and travelers pass through the town as visitors come to honor the realm’s long history. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of great ancestors return to walk among the living. Stormbrow commends travelers who remember those who came before. For honoring the elder peoples’ wisdom and legacy, visitors receive a blessing and a commemorative coin.

quest:865.text: Raptor Horns. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix wants intact raptor horns for a scheme of his own. The goblin believes the cunning of Barrens raptors lies in their horns and hires travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws. Mebok Mizzyrix looks for fortune in Ratchet, where goblins chase one scheme after another. He has watched the Barrens raptors act with unusual craft and coordination compared with beasts elsewhere. Mebok decided their intelligence must be held in their horns. He has no formal inquiry in mind; he wants to put this idea to profit. Mebok wants undamaged horns from Sunscale Scytheclaws, among the Barrens' deadliest predators. They prowl the southern stretches of the Barrens and the northern borders near Ashenvale. The raptors hunt in packs and defend their territory fiercely, so bringing down one and taking its horns intact calls for considerable skill in battle.

quest:8652.text: Graveborn the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Graveborn the Elder waits near Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Travelers seek him among the blighted groves to honor Azeroth’s ancient forebears, and receive his blessing and a holiday token. In Tirisfal Glades, the Forsaken live among ruined manors and grave sites. During the Lunar Festival, a spirit from ancient times appears just outside Brill. Elder Graveborn welcomes pilgrims who pause to honor the old ways, even in a land shattered by the Scourge and reclaimed by the undead. During the Lunar Festival, spirits from long-past eras return with wisdom and gratitude. When you approach Elder Graveborn, he says it heartens him that Tirisfal’s people still honor their ancestors despite the land’s decay. He gives a Coin of Ancestry to those who greet him.

quest:8653.text: Goldwell the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Goldwell welcomes travelers in Kharanos and invites them to honor the ancestors. Your visit keeps their memory alive across the snowy dwarven lands. Beside the Thunderbrew Distillery, Elder Goldwell greets those who follow the trade path to Ironforge's gates. Weary travelers, adventurers, and locals all pass before him. He remembers the ancient days when the first mortals walked beneath Azeroth's stars. Goldwell is glad that mortals still remember the ancient races and their deeds. He thanks you for pausing to honor them. Then he gives you a Coin of Ancestry as a sign of his blessing.

quest:867.text: Harpy Raiders. Witchwing harpies strike supply caravans on the northwestern trails of the Barrens. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads sends you to hunt their raiders and roguefeathers, taking their talons as proof. Witchwing harpies strike caravans crossing the Barrens. From rocky crags in the northwest, they swoop on merchant trains and supply wagons. They kill pack animals and seize goods bound for orcish outposts, making each journey through the region dangerous. Darsok Swiftdagger, an orc rogue, has spent days watching the flock's habits and ranks. He believes an unfocused assault on their mountain roosts would scatter them. His plan is to break the Witchwing from the lowest rank upward, starting with the raiders before turning to their commanders.

quest:8670.text: Runetotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers in Durotar can honor Runetotem the Elder, an ancestral spirit. She waits in Razor Hill beneath a beam of heavenly light, offering blessings and festival tokens to those who remember the past. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient elders appear across Azeroth to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem waits inside Razor Hill, just past the southern entrance. A beam of starlight falls on her as she watches over the orcish settlement. Travelers can pause there to honor the wisdom of those who came before. When you pay Elder Runetotem homage, she gives you a festival token of fortune and tells you where other spirits can be found. Her directions point toward Elder Darkhorn and Elder High Mountain elsewhere across the continent.

quest:8673.text: Bloodhoof the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bloodhoof the Elder just north of Bloodhoof Village. The ancestral spirit appears near the bridge and offers a Coin of Ancestry in return. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village, near the bridge. Travelers honor the sacrifices of the past by approaching the elder, who offers words of encouragement and a Coin of Ancestry. On Mulgore's ancestral lands, Elder Bloodhoof links the living tauren tribes with the memory of their forebears. Honoring the dead is central to tauren spiritual life. It keeps the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those walking the plains in harmony.

quest:8675.text: Skychaser the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skychaser the Elder watches over Westfall from Sentinel Tower. Travelers climb to honor her as an ancestral spirit, and she recognizes the living with a blessing. Sentinel Hill is Westfall's lone fortified redoubt. Below, weary soldiers and settlers face threats from Defias raiders and roving scavengers across the scrublands. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Skychaser appears on the open platform atop Sentinel Tower, watching from above the dust and wind. Anyone may climb and pay her respect. Across Azeroth, the Lunar Festival honors wisdom, heritage, and the deeds of ancient spirits. When you approach, Elder Skychaser recognizes the living spark within you and accepts your homage. She gives you a token of her favor, binding the living to the honored dead.

quest:8677.text: Darkhorn the Elder. At the Lunar Festival, Darkhorn the Elder receives travelers in Orgrimmar. Honored among the ancestors, she embodies age, survival, and ancestral pride. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestors appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within Orgrimmar’s fortified ramparts, watching the young warrior city. You can approach her to honor those who walked the earth generations ago, whether you fight for the Horde or brave the gates as an Alliance traveler. Travelers greet Elder Darkhorn and pay her reverence, and she recognizes the spark of life in them. For honoring the old ways, you receive a Coin of Ancestry and her blessing. The tokens celebrate victory over ancient perils and remind the living to cherish the strength handed down through unbroken bloodlines.

quest:8678.text: Proudhorn the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder receives visitors atop Thunder Bluff. Tauren honor him as an ancestral spirit and pay respect to the wisdom of those who watch over Mulgore and the Horde. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder appears high on Thunder Bluff's windblown mesas. Tauren hold their ancestors' voices in the highest regard. They believe ancient leaders and sages remain as spirits, offering guidance and strength to the living. Travelers who climb Thunder Bluff's heights to honor Elder Proudhorn are welcomed as vital flames of life. In return for their homage, he gives them a Coin of Ancestry, a sign of communion between the enduring past and the living champions who fight for the world's future.

quest:86784.text: Sticks and Bones. Deathguard Bartholomew asks travelers in Tirisfal Glades to gather dry branches for Eleanor Shackleton. The experienced survivalist camps in the western hills, far from the settlements. Deathguard Bartholomew pauses between patrols to help an acquaintance in Tirisfal Glades. Deathguards guard against the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders, but Bartholomew also looks out for Eleanor Shackleton. She spends her unlife in the harsh elements, so he asks you to gather dry branches for her campfire. Eleanor Shackleton survives alone in Tirisfal's blighted wilderness. Though undead, the Forsaken still feel the damp, bitter chill rolling off the northern moors. Eleanor's rule for gathering wood is simple: when you think you have enough firewood, gather five times more. Grateful for the extra timber, she lets you keep Bartholomew's basket and shares the warmth of her fire.

quest:8680.text: Windtotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder receives travelers on a bluff above Ratchet.
