She welcomes those who honor the wisdom of ages past and offers an ancestral blessing and guidance to other elders across Kalimdor. On a grassy hill just northwest of Ratchet’s flight master, Windtotem the Elder watches over the goblin docks and open sea. Iron, gunpowder, and coin pass through the harbor below, while quiet Barrens winds and a shaft of celestial light reach the elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder guides wandering mortals, as do the other ancestral spirits. Those who seek her receive her blessing and a token of her favor, along with whispers pointing to nearby elders across the continent, including Elder Runetotem and Elder Bloodhoof.

quest:869.text: Raptor Thieves. A raptor has stolen the guards' payroll from the Crossroads tower, leaving the defenders baffled. Gazrog calls for a cull to keep the beasts from striking again. The Crossroads depends on mercenary and grunt guards to keep trade routes open across the Barrens. Their pay matters to morale and discipline. When silver vanished from the guard tower, leaders expected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, a raptor was caught stealing in the dead of night, leaving the settlement stunned and short of coin. Gazrog does not know why wild beasts would hoard shiny coins, and he has no interest in studying their behavior. The guards are restless without their pay, so he calls for blood and deterrence. He sends hunters to take a dozen raptor heads from across the savannah, hoping to curb the predators' boldness before a full search for the silver begins.

quest:87.text: Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Billy Maclure's careless play has set the Stonefield and Maclure families against each other. His trail leads you to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt. He says he found the necklace before a creature snatched it away. Billy says a large kobold with gleaming fangs took the shiny necklace and fled to a den above Fargodeep Mine. Yet Goldtooth lurks on the mine's lower level. Slaying the kobold returns Bernice's necklace and settles the families' dispute. Bernice also gives you an old campaign keepsake left by her late husband.

quest:870.text: The Forgotten Pools. At the Forgotten Pools, life surges through the dry Barrens for reasons the Cenarion Circle cannot explain. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads sends Horde adventurers to inspect the oasis northwest of the settlement, where druids sense unseen forces beneath the earth. The Barrens once flourished as fertile land before ages of war and the Sundering shattered the continent. The region became sun-baked scrubland, but lush oases have recently begun taking root in its dry basin. Druids of the Cenarion Circle find this sudden growth unnatural. They sense powers beneath the earth pressing upward, stirring vegetation and wildlife into life in scattered pockets across the wastes.

quest:871.text: Disrupt the Attacks. Thork needs the Crossroads defended as Razormane quilboar cut its supply roads. Their ambushes have halted caravans from Durotar, and the outpost is running short on food and gear. You strike at the quilboar while scouts search for the one directing their warband. The Crossroads guards a key junction for Horde traffic through central Kalimdor. Freight wagons and caravans bring food, iron, and equipment west from Durotar, and the outpost depends on those supplies. Razormane ambushes along the northeast trails have stopped the deliveries. Stores are running low, and Thork cannot wait for peaceful talks. Thork sends you against the quilboar bramble dens northeast of the settlement before they can assault the town walls. Striking their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Hunters weakens the Razormane scouting perimeter and deprives raiding parties of magical and logistical support. These skirmishes buy time while Horde trackers search the brush for the one organizing the raids.

quest:8717.text: Moonwarden the Elder. At the Crossroads, Moonwarden the Elder receives travelers beneath a beam of light. During the Lunar Festival, people honor ancestral spirits and seek his wisdom and directions to elders across Kalimdor. At the Crossroads, a column of light falls around Elder Moonwarden. He is one of the ancient spirits honored during the Lunar Festival, when mortals set aside their conflicts to seek the wisdom of generations past. Elder Moonwarden looks to the stars for answers to earthly mysteries. He offers ancestral blessings and directs seekers to other elders across Kalimdor, including Elder Bloodhoof, Elder High Mountain, Elder Morningdew, and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8718.text: Bladeswift the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Bladeswift the Elder's ancient spirit is honored in Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, travelers seek his wisdom beneath the stars and a blessing tied to night elven tradition. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth to share wisdom and bless travelers. In Darnassus, Bladeswift the Elder appears among the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave. This ancient spirit turns his gaze to the night sky and its mysteries, while the living face the trials of the present. Night elves have long looked to the heavens as reflections of Elune and signs of deeper truths. Bladeswift urges the wise and fortunate to seek answers among the stars. Those who honor him receive a Coin of Ancestry and join a ceremony that links the living with spirits of the past.

quest:872.text: The Disruption Ends. Thork orders a strike against the Razormane raids on the Horde road. Kreenig Snarlsnout leads the attacks from the northern Barrens, and his death is meant to break the warband's hold on the route between Durotar and the Crossroads. The road between Durotar and the Crossroads carries provisions and reinforcements through the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar ambushes have kept it under threat. Scout reports name their leader as Kreenig Snarlsnout, whose raiding party organizes the attacks. Thork orders a strike against Kreenig, hoping to break the warband's unity and secure the road. Kreenig's war party is entrenched in craggy hills northeast of the Crossroads. Hardy Razormane Defenders and geomancers who manipulate the arid earth shield his position. Thork's order is to break through that guard and strike Kreenig in his redoubt, sending a warning across the plains. His tusk will prove the leader's death and show that the Horde will not accept attacks on its lifelines.

quest:8721.text: Starweave the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave receives visitors in Auberdine. Travelers come to honor Kalimdor's ancestral spirits and seek her wisdom and blessing. During the Lunar Festival, ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth beneath pillars of celestial light. Elder Starweave joins the night elves in Auberdine, a harbor on Darkshore's coast. Travelers come to honor her and seek guidance from ages past. Elder Starweave looks to the heavens above Kalimdor. She tells visitors that the stars hold answers to mortal doubts and worldly riddles. Those who seek her counsel are urged to look skyward for truth and receive ancestral favor, along with tidings of other wandering spirits across the wild frontier.

quest:8725.text: Riversong the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, pilgrims seek Riversong the Elder beneath a shrine in Astranaar. The night elf spirit offers wisdom and points them toward other honored ancestors across Kalimdor. In Astranaar, Riversong the Elder waits beneath an open night elf shrine. A shaft of light falls through the Ashenvale canopy onto her spirit. During the Lunar Festival, pilgrims gather there to honor those who came before. Riversong the Elder recalls how night elves read truth and mystery in the stars. She urges patience and contemplation, then guides pilgrims toward other spirits, including Elder Starweave.

quest:875.text: Harpy Lieutenants. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger sends Horde champions against the Witchwing coven in the northern Barrens. In the Dry Hills, the aim is to kill the flock’s front-line officers and break its chain of command. After the first clashes with Witchwing raiders, Darsok Swiftdagger turns the offensive toward the harpies roosting in the Dry Hills. Horde scouts are sent after the Witchwing Slayers who lead the flock. These officers keep the lesser harpies in line and coordinate raids against Horde supply paths. Their deaths are critical to securing the northern approaches of the Barrens. Witchwing Slayers lead through strength and dominance, and only the most vicious among them carry ornate rings that mark their authority within the matriarchy. Taking the rings proves the lieutenants are dead, disrupts the roost’s coordination, and sends the coven a clear message: attacks on Horde territory will meet decisive retribution.

quest:877.text: The Stagnant Oasis. Tonga Runetotem sends you southeast from the Crossroads to search the Stagnant Oasis. He wants to know if the hidden fissure beneath the Forgotten Pools has a match in its murky waters. Tonga Runetotem sends you to the Stagnant Oasis after a strange fissure is found beneath the Forgotten Pools. He suspects the sudden patches of lush growth across the Barrens have a cause beneath the earth. You search the oasis's murky shallows for another opening, among predators that haunt the water.

quest:88.text: Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield asks you to kill Princess before the sow ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning pig from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, putting the family’s crops at risk. The sow belongs to the Brackwells. She grew enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots. Ma has had enough of Princess eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants the pig put down before the season’s yield is lost. Princess stays at Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, east beyond the Maclure homestead. Protective boars surround her. Get past her guards and bring Ma the distinctive brass collar from Princess’s neck. It will prove the sow can trouble the Stonefield fields no more.

quest:880.text: Altered Beings. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem studies strange changes in the Barrens' oasis waters. Fissures beneath the pools may be changing the creatures that live there, and he asks you to bring him shells from altered snapjaws. Tonga Runetotem is searching for the cause of strange changes in the Barrens' oases. Though the savanna is dry, a handful of pools support fertile ground. Tonga found peculiar fissures beneath those waters, sending out potent energies. He does not know whether the force came from outside or rose from deep within the earth. Now he studies the creatures that drink from and live in the pools, hoping to learn what the fissures are doing to them. You are sent to the Lushwater Oasis and the Stagnant Oasis to gather altered snapjaw shells. Snapjaws live in the shallows, where they take in the strange essence through food and exposure. Their carapaces have changed, offering Tonga a sign of how the fissures affect local wildlife. He hopes the shells will help him understand the disturbance before it spreads farther across Kalimdor.

quest:881.text: Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, hunters prepare to face Whitemist in the northern Barrens. Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde hunters to summon the legendary white lion and test their strength. Across the central plains, a white-maned lion rules the savannah cats. Taur-ahe speakers call him Echeyakee, or Whitemist. Legend says he moves so silently that he seems like morning mist gliding over the red earth. His strikes come swiftly, leaving prey no time for fear or suffering. Local hunters revere him as a sign of mercy and swift death. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn trains fledgling warriors. The experienced orc shaman sends her pupils to challenge the king of beasts after they have proven themselves against lesser savannah prowlers. With a special horn, you travel northeast past the mountain ridges to a graveyard of massive kodo bones. Sound the horn to challenge Echeyakee and draw the elusive predator from hiding for a test of strength and cunning.

quest:882.text: Ishamuhale. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sends you to face Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor in the Barrens. The hunt tests your skill and respect for nature's deadliest predators. Sunscale raptors hunt the Barrens in cunning, vicious packs, but none inspires more dread than Speartooth. Jorn Skyseer says Ishamuhale kills by instinct and passion, not for food or territory. He hunts because killing is his nature. To face him is to test whether you can withstand a predator's unbridled ferocity. Ishamuhale will not be found resting in a nest. To draw him out, you follow the plains' natural rhythm. Jorn tells you to kill a fresh zhevra and carry its carcass to a lone, withered dead tree on the plains northwest of Ratchet. The scent of blood on the arid wind brings Ishamuhale swiftly to claim his prey. When you bring Ishamuhale's fang back to Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sees it as a profound spiritual milestone, not merely a sign of victory. Tauren belief holds that overcoming so fierce a predator lets you absorb some of its raw strength. The test then turns inward: you must carry that might with temperance, honor, and restraint, rather than surrender to blind bloodlust.

quest:8827.text: Winter's Presents. In Ironforge, revelers gather for the Feast of Winter Veil. They direct travelers to Greatfather Winter beside the Smokywood Pastures stalls, where gifts wait beneath the holiday tree. Winter settles over Khaz Modan, and Ironforge fills with cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. Revelers and holiday enthusiasts point passersby toward the decorated tree near the Smokywood Pastures vendors. Smokywood Pastures, a goblin enterprise, shares the season with Greatfather Winter. He greets visitors as goblin merchants remind gift recipients that festive treats and seasonal wares make gifts for friends and family.

quest:8828.text: Winter's Presents. In Orgrimmar, Winter's Presents await beneath the festive tree during the Feast of Winter Veil. Holiday organizers and goblin apparatus tenders direct Horde heroes to Great-father Winter, where gifts have been prepared for them. The Feast of Winter Veil brings a pause for celebration to Orgrimmar as the chill winds of late year sweep across Durotar. Promoters from Smokywood Pastures and holiday enthusiasts spread word through the capital that gifts wait beneath the decorated tree. Warriors, hunters, and wanderers resting in the city are all invited to share in the season’s generosity. Great-father Winter sits among holiday ribbons and packaged cartons near the Smokywood Pastures market. The ancient figure marks the season’s renewal, while goblin merchants nearby offer seasonal wares and festive treats to visitors.

quest:8846.text: Five Signets for War Supplies. In Ironforge, Field Marshal Snowfall trades commendation signets for supplies bound for the Grand Alliance’s war effort. You can exchange them for field rations, bandages, and combat gear to keep those serving on the home front equipped for the conflicts ahead. Couriers and heroes bring Snowfall commendation signets earned through civic service. He trades them for survival rations and tactical gear bound for the fronts. Armies there need steady supplies as much as courage. Royal heralds offer public honor and civic standing for commendation signets. Snowfall offers another choice: five signets buy field gear, without pomp, glory, or official recognition. These goods help soldiers and volunteers stay alive as they march into hostile lands.

quest:8851.text: Five Signets for War Supplies. Orgrimmar's stores gather supplies for the Horde's campaign across Kalimdor. Workers earn commendation signets for their contributions, and Warlord Gorchuk exchanges them for supplies to equip the fighters. Across Kalimdor, the Horde gathers raw goods, weapons, and provisions for a vast campaign. Gatherers and tradesfolk bring bandages, metals, and herbs into the cities, where military overseers award commendation signets for their work. The tokens mark each contribution to the stockpile growing along Orgrimmar's central avenues. Warlord Gorchuk knows the wider war effort needs supplies, but each warrior also needs gear and provisions to survive the march into battle. Fighters can trade their commendation signets back into the Horde's stores for field supplies and surplus materiel, giving up personal recognition for what they need on the front.

quest:886.text: The Barrens Oases. Beneath the Barrens, strange power stirs, and Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem takes heed from Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. He sends travelers east through Mulgore to meet Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads and investigate the new waters. For generations, the Barrens have known drought while Mulgore flourishes under the Earth Mother's care. Now tauren druids on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise feel strange currents waking beneath the plains. Life stirs where it should not, and the Cenarion Circle fears the power behind it may endanger the land and its creatures. Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem sends Tonga Runetotem to investigate the strange stirrings. The wilderness is too dangerous for one investigator, so Hamuul asks travelers leaving Mulgore to follow. Go east past Bloodhoof Village and through the mountain passes to the Crossroads, where Tonga waits for news. There, in the Barrens, stands the Horde's busy heart.

quest:8866.text: Bronzebeard the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bronzebeard the Elder beneath Ironforge. His greeting offers wisdom and a token of esteem. Across Khaz Modan, people revere their forebears and their long-lived heritage. During the Lunar Festival, spirits and venerable elders appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with travelers who honor the past. In Ironforge, Elder Bronzebeard carries the Bronzebeard clan’s stalwart resilience. He is quietly pleased when travelers come to pay their respects and the people honor the lineage of the old races. No great trial or perilous journey is needed. Travelers pause to greet Elder Bronzebeard and offer their good wishes. He returns the greeting with a Coin of Ancestry, a festival token recalling the living bond between the present and the generations who forged Khaz Modan from stone and fire.

quest:887.text: Southsea Freebooters. Along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, Southsea Freebooters strike goblin trading vessels. Gazlowe hires adventurers to attack their camp and curb the raids. Ratchet's trade suffers from pirates on the Merchant Coast. The port sits in central Kalimdor, where merchant vessels travel between Kalimdor and the eastern continents. South of town, Southsea Freebooters hold a fortified beach camp. From there, they attack goblin cargo ships arriving and departing, cutting into profits and disrupting local shipping lanes. Gazlowe blames the pirates and the Steamwheedle Cartel's naval leaders. The Trade Princes have spent immense sums on defensive fleets, yet Vice Admiral Grezzlik has failed to patrol the waters effectively. Frustrated by Undermine's slow response, Gazlowe hires independent mercenaries to thin the pirate brigands and cannoneers.

quest:888.text: Stolen Booty. Pirate cargo off Ratchet’s coast has left Gazlowe choosing what matters most. Stolen Booty brings him two vital goods: boots for local laborers and a delicate telescopic lens needed to complete his observatory. The Southsea Freebooters have troubled merchant lanes across the Great Sea for years. Their fortified camp just south of Ratchet brought them into direct conflict with Gazlowe. Pirates intercepted merchant vessels bound for the port and took valuable supplies from the Steamwheedle Cartel. Some goods could be written off as a cost of shipping. Specialized cargo mattered enough for Gazlowe to hire mercenaries to break into the pirate stronghold. Gazlowe has two practical priorities. Drizzlik sent a needed shipment of boots from Booty Bay for local laborers. The other item is specialized: a ground telescopic lens made for the observatory tower overlooking Ratchet. Its twin arrived safely by caravan through Durotar, but pirates seized this lens at sea. Until it is recovered, the observatory remains an empty frame.

quest:890.text: The Missing Shipment. In Ratchet, Gazlowe waits for goods sent from Booty Bay across the Great Sea. He sends couriers to Wharfmaster Dizzywig to check the dock records, while the Southsea Freebooters remain a possible cause of the delay. Ratchet is the Steamwheedle Cartel's trading port on Kalimdor. Ships cross the Great Sea from Booty Bay with manufactured goods, exotic supplies, and heavy freight for the town's building and trade. When cargo goes missing, business suffers. Chief Engineer Gazlowe keeps close track of every crate brought into port. The Southsea Freebooters haunt the coast south of Ratchet and often intercept merchant ships. Gazlowe checks his records before accusing the pirates or sending anyone into a fight. He sends his inventory ledger to Wharfmaster Dizzywig at the docks. Dizzywig oversees the unloading and storage of ship cargo, and can check whether goods were lost at sea or misplaced in a warehouse.

quest:892.text: The Missing Shipment. At Ratchet’s docks, Dizzywig’s ledger points away from harbor graft and toward the Southsea Freebooters. Gazlowe receives the records and prepares to reclaim his lost cargo. Ratchet’s trade and its port bring constant logistical headaches. When a shipment fails to arrive, Gazlowe suspects bad harbor accounts or foul play on the piers. Wharfmaster Dizzywig examines the manifest and insists his books are clean. The intake records account for everything, so the missing merchandise never made it onto the dock.

quest:894.text: Samophlange. At a Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve wants a device called a samophlange. He sends you southwest of the Sludge Fen to find it. In the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve cannot explain what the Venture Company is building. The goblin engineer and tinker works in Ratchet, while the rival company experiments southwest of the Sludge Fen. Its people call one device a samophlange. Sputtervalve does not know its purpose or value, but wants to study its design before his competitors can profit from it. The Venture Company guards its research site with armed overseers, deforesters, and machinery. Sputtervalve gives you an intercepted operating manual to help shut down the rig safely. At the central control station, you find a locked console with levers, lights, and gauges. Three control valves keep the rig's pressure in order.

quest:895.text: WANTED: Baron Longshore. On Ratchet's docks, Chief Engineer Gazlowe posts a bounty for Baron Longshore. The pirate captain hails from Gilneas and commands vessels of the Southsea Freebooters. His presence along the Merchant Coast threatens goblin merchant shipping across the region. South of Ratchet, the Southsea Freebooters hold fortified camps along the Merchant Coast. Their pirates harass merchant vessels and disrupt the sea lanes the Steamwheedle Cartel relies on between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and points beyond. Under captains such as Baron Longshore, the raids drain the local goblin administration and threaten trade along the coast. Baron Longshore comes from Gilneas, the isolated human kingdom across the sea. On Kalimdor, he commands the pirate vessel Heedless and leads crews ashore just north of Northwatch Hold. Chief Engineer Gazlowe answers with a bounty, calling for Longshore's identifiable head.

quest:896.text: Miner's Fortune. Wharfmaster Dizzywig has heard of a fist-sized emerald at the Venture Company's Boulder Lode Mine. He hires you to take the Cats Eye Emerald from the mine's supervisors and share the profits. Wharfmaster Dizzywig hears the merchants who pass through Ratchet's harbor on the routes between Ratchet and Booty Bay. Word reaches him of a huge gem found deep in the Boulder Lode Mine. The Venture Company strips the northern Barrens for its own gain, so few are likely to ask questions if its finest recent find disappears. Northeast of the Sludge Fen, laborers fill the Boulder Lode Mine's rocky shaft. The Venture Co. Overseers and Enforcers have taken the Cats Eye Emerald, and an ordinary digger cannot claim a prize so rare. You need to face the armed managers, secure the stone, and bring it to Dizzywig. He can judge its value against the market in Undermine.

quest:9.text: The Killing Fields. In Westfall, The Killing Fields begins with Farmer Saldean's crops under threat. Rogue Harvest Watchers overrun his fields and neighboring farms, while the Defias Brotherhood's disruption has left local agriculture in ruin. Many Westfall farmers abandoned their land when bandits and outlaws swept through. Farmer Saldean and his family chose to stay. Thieves are not the only danger on their farm. Harvest Watchers built to tend and guard the grain have run wild, pacing the furrows and attacking anyone who comes near. Farmer Saldean asks passing travelers to dismantle twenty hostile Harvest Watchers across his fields and the adjoining plots. Clearing them gives his harvest a little relief. For now, his farm remains one stubborn hope that Westfall's breadbasket can be reclaimed.

quest:900.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, Samophlange machinery keeps the Venture Company's digging rig running. Three valves must be sealed before the central apparatus can be shut down safely. At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company's machinery is complex and dangerous. The central console makes clear that the core cannot be stopped with a single switch. Its feed lines must be handled by hand first, or the apparatus could fail or explode. Three valves control the flow into the rig: the Main Control Valve, the Fuel Control Valve, and the Regulator Valve. Each must be sealed by hand against high pressure. As they close, the console's green indicators fade to yellow, making it safe to engage the central shutoff.

quest:901.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company’s machinery waits with its valves shut and its pressure relieved. Tinkerer Sniggles holds the key to open the control unit and free the samophlange within. You have relieved the pressure by turning the auxiliary valves, and the dials and gauges have settled. The housing remains locked against tampering. Its key rests with the goblin engineer overseeing the drilling site. Tinkerer Sniggles oversees the Venture Company’s equipment at the Sludge Fen. He keeps the console key in a hut just northeast of the main rig. You need that key to open the housing and reach the samophlange.

quest:902.text: Samophlange. At the Venture Company console, you uncover the elusive samophlange and carry it to Ratchet. You have shut down the controls and their defenses; now the delicate device is ready for Sputtervalve to examine. Behind the Venture Company console's faceplate, wiring and purposeless tubing crowd around strange engineering. Deep inside lies the samophlange, a core component that has baffled engineers across the region. With a firm tug, you free the device from its housing and carry it back to the goblin who began the recovery effort.

quest:903.text: Prowlers of the Barrens. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after the savannah prowlers. Their claws will show whether you can face the Barrens' greatest beasts. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters who have already faced the plainstriders and zhevras. Southwest of the Crossroads, savannah prowlers vanish into the central Barrens' gold and ochre scrub. These great cats hunt instead of grazing with the herds. They wait in tall grass, then ambush their prey, and unwary travelers can fall to them. Sergra warns you that prowlers know how to hunt. Read the grasses and strike before a cat leaps if you mean to claim its paws and claws. Bring back seven prowler claws to show you have the cunning and quick reflexes to survive against Kalimdor's deadliest wildlife.

quest:905.text: The Angry Scytheclaws. South of the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends hunters to face the savage scytheclaws stalking the Barrens. Bring sunscale raptor feathers to their breeding nests, and prove your courage in a land that gives little quarter. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters against the beasts of the Barrens. After lesser trials, she sends you south of the Crossroads to hunt vicious sunscale raptors and take their feathers. Then you carry those feathers southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, into the heart of raptor territory. Placing them in the nests is the true test: it shows you can face the scytheclaws without fear. Three raptor nests lie southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, near the Gold Road. Red, blue, and yellow eggs mark the separate clutches. Scytheclaws defend their nests fiercely against anything that comes near. Place the feathers of fallen raptors among the eggs, and you make your challenge clear to the beasts. Return to the Crossroads after entering the nests, and Sergra can see you have faced the danger and lived. Walking out of a raptor den takes raw courage. The Barrens test every hunter; each fight may harden you, or leave your bones among the kodo ribs scattered across the dirt.

quest:907.text: Enraged Thunder Lizards. In the southern Barrens, thunder lizards roam the plains around Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer calls hunters to face the great beasts and bring back their blood as part of a wider rite of passage. After defeating the raptor Ishamuhale, you return to Camp Taurajo. The tauren elder Jorn Skyseer now tests your strength against the largest grazers of the land. Stormsnouts and Thunderheads roam the southern Barrens, their heavy strides able to crush an unwary hunter beneath them. Tauren and orc hunters prize poise, position, and strength when facing a thunder lizard. Jorn asks you to bring back samples of their potent blood, proof that you stood in the path of the rumbling beasts and survived with your bones unbroken. The trophy opens the way to Jorn's final quarry in the skies.

quest:90902.text: Rediscovering the Light. In Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken paladins face the pain of calling on the Holy Light. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them to heal wounded Deathguards through the burning agony. Newly risen Forsaken paladins must face a hard truth: the Holy Light still answers them, but burns their withered bodies. Many were champions of the Silver Hand or knights of Lordaeron before they fell. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them that powers once used without thought now bring fierce pain. The Light clashes with the foul magic that sustains undeath, so calling on it takes resolve and endurance. Deathguards in Deathknell suffer grievous wounds fighting mindless zombies, and Forsaken paladins are called to heal them. Aramis teaches that pushing through the burning pain is like exercising an atrophied muscle. The paladins treat that agony as a badge of honor and proof that the Light has not forsaken them.

quest:91208.text: Coming to Terms. A frightened former paladin has fled into the hills west of the chapel. Aramis Hammerhand asks a newly risen knight to reach her with compassion. The Silver Hand's former paladins wake among the Forsaken in shock. In life, they served the Holy Light and fought the undead. Now their souls are bound to decomposing flesh. Aramis Hammerhand guides some through this change, while others flee into the Tirisfal wilderness, unable to face their new existence.

quest:91209.text: Continue Your Training. Newly risen Forsaken paladins leave Deathknell for instruction in Brill. Aramis Hammerhand sends them east into Tirisfal Glades, where dangers and distrust await those who wield the Holy Light. After learning martial combat and channeling holy power in Deathknell's graveyard, you are sent east into Tirisfal Glades. Your destination is Brill, the regional outpost and administrative hub for central Tirisfal. There, Shari Stilwell oversees the training of those who follow the path of the paladin in undeath. Aramis offers parting advice about the peril of being an undead paladin. Lordaeron still needs defenders against threats from beyond, yet wielding the Holy Light under Sylvanas Windrunner's banner draws suspicion. Many Forsaken suffered agony or death at the hands of holy zealots, and the Light's presence breeds distrust among their undead kin.

quest:916.text: Webwood Venom. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the giant webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. He asks young night elves to gather venom sacs so he can learn how Teldrassil's growth has affected the forest's wildlife. Gilshalan Windwalker has come to Shadowglen to study the webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave. They are far larger and more aggressive than their cousins elsewhere. He suspects Teldrassil's immense magical energies are changing the local wildlife. He asks for venom sacs to compare with those of ordinary spiders and learn what has changed. Webwood spiders live in and around Shadowthread Cave, where they threaten young night elves in the glen. Gathering their venom can help thin their numbers and give Darnassian researchers evidence of Teldrassil's effect on the wild.

quest:917.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker seeks an unhatched Webwood Egg for his study of Teldrassil’s wildlife. After gathering venom samples, he needs a living specimen to examine the unnatural aggression afflicting the forest’s creatures. An egg can be studied safely without subduing a full-grown spider. Gilshalan Windwalker needs live subjects to understand the unnatural corruption affecting the Webwood spiders around Shadowglen. You have secured raw venom from the aggressive spiders, but carrying a thrashing giant out of the depths would be deadly for a novice. Gilshalan asks you to bring back an unhatched egg from the brooding clutches inside Shadowthread Cave. Webwood spiders brood in Shadowthread Cave, where the forest’s increasingly hostile arachnids make their nests. An intact egg gives scholars a controlled subject that can hatch under containment. Gilshalan plans to bundle it with his venom samples and send both to Darnassus for examination. With his local study complete, he directs recruits toward higher duties in the boughs of Aldrassil.

quest:918.text: Timberling Seeds. At Lake Al'Ameth, botanist Denalan studies the growing hostility of Teldrassil's nature elementals. He seeks to harvest Timberling Seeds and test whether enriched soil can help them grow calmer. His work is one quiet effort by night elf herbalists to understand the subtle afflictions troubling the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to Teldrassil's boughs, closely bound to the health and vitality of the surrounding flora. They are usually peaceful reflections of the forest's balance, but their recent hostility has alarmed the local night elves, and no cause is known. Botanist Denalan hopes to learn what has stirred them rather than simply cull them. Denalan suspects the blemish lies deep in the ground. He hopes to sprout fresh timberlings, a gentler generation of elementals, in enriched and carefully treated loam. By harvesting seeds from wandering timberlings near Lake Al'Ameth, he aims to learn whether the land's corruption can be countered from the roots up.

quest:919.text: Timberling Sprouts. Around Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts are spreading across Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to uproot them before they grow into hostile timberlings. Corrupted sprouts are spreading along Lake Al'Ameth's banks. Denalan lives beside the lake and knows these young plants cannot be healed. Left alone, they quickly grow into aggressive, bark-covered timberlings that threaten wildlife and travelers. Uprooting the sprouts helps protect the grove. Denalan is troubled by how quickly new sprouts appear across Teldrassil. Their spread points to a sickness in the World Tree's roots and soil, and Denalan and the druids of Darnassus seek its cause.

quest:92.text: Redridge Goulash. In Lakeshire, Redridge Goulash helps feed a town under strain. Chef Breanna fed the active Stormwind garrison during the recent Blackrock orc uprising, emptying her pantry and leaving her to seek hearty ingredients from the mountains. Lakeshire remains under siege from Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and ferocious wild beasts. When the recent orc uprising began along the ridges, Chef Breanna took on feeding the entire brigade of Stormwind troops stationed in town. Keeping the active garrison fed quickly emptied her cupboards, though the town still had plenty of hungry mouths. With her cupboards bare, Chef Breanna looks to the dangerous wilderness beyond Lakeshire's gates. Her signature goulash calls for tough mountain condor meat, seasoned snouts from formidable Great Goretusks, and crisp leg meat from giant tarantulas that prowl the hills.

quest:920.text: Tenaron's Summons. In Shadowglen, Tenaron's Summons calls you to Aldrassil. After helping Gilshalan Windwalker with woodland dangers, you are asked to meet Tenaron Stormgrip high in the great tree. The call draws you from local troubles toward the spiritual afflictions touching Teldrassil. Your work against the venomous spiders and corrupted wildlife in the glen has reached Tenaron Stormgrip. Gilshalan Windwalker tells you the elder has asked for your presence. Even night elves, with their long lives, know better than to keep an elder waiting atop Aldrassil. Tenaron waits in Aldrassil's highest chamber, looking across Shadowglen's boughs. Meeting him brings you into wider concerns of stewardship, including the cleansing of Teldrassil's moonwells and the corruption spreading through the young World Tree's ecosystem.

quest:921.text: Crown of the Earth. At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to draw sacred water before they leave Shadowglen. The rite recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people gave up there. Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast cost them their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history as he gives novices a rite, preparing them with humility and purpose for a changing world. To complete the rite, you draw water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil with a crystal phial. Moonwell waters carry remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids channel their restorative power into the wild, while Sentinels honor the wells as tranquil shrines to Elune. The kaldorei remain wary: arcane sorcery is forbidden, and the wellspring that sustains their land recalls the reckless magic that nearly broke the world.

quest:92124.text: Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton needs help finding missing books. He sends young adventurers to Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, to count the library's archives. But Daniel's thoughts turn to local tradeskills, making a clear answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey keeps scholarly works, spiritual writings, and records of Stormwind's history that survived the First War. Brother Paxton, a careful monk, takes pride in the collection. Now books are missing from the shelves, and he needs a clear count to learn how many are gone. He has little patience for chasing his daydreaming helper. Daniel assists Brother Paxton in the abbey library, but his thoughts stray from parchment and catalog numbers. He is fascinated by the practical trades and professions of Elwynn Forest, including smithing, leatherworking, tailoring, and herbal craft. So when Paxton asks him to count the books, Daniel rambles about local crafters instead of looking for lost scriptures.

quest:922.text: Rellian Greenspyre. At Denalan's lakeside retreat in Teldrassil, you carry a timberling seed to Rellian Greenspyre in Darnassus. The handoff brings news of trouble spreading through the World Tree's boughs. Denalan has studied the plants and elemental life around Lake Al'Ameth. After gathering seeds from the local timberlings, he sends you to Darnassus with a sample for his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian is a druid who walks the Cenarion Enclave's terraces. He had shown interest in Denalan's research and hopes to grow a timberling of his own.

quest:923.text: Tumors. In Darnassus, the Cenarion Circle seeks to contain the sickness spreading through Teldrassil. You are sent to Wellspring Lake to gather mossy tumors from afflicted timberlings, so druids can study the poison and burn the growths safely. Teldrassil’s native plants and animals are being twisted by a strange affliction. Its timberlings, usually placid nature spirits with bark for skin, have grown hostile and erratic. Grotesque mossy tumors spread across their living wood, pulsing with unnatural poison. Cenarion scholars Denalan and Rellian Greenspyre search for the cause, while timberlings already lost to the sickness must be culled to protect the rest of the boughs. Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil has become a focal point of the outbreak, and its timberlings are among the most tainted on the World Tree. Rellian Greenspyre asks you to kill these corrupted guardians and cut away their tumors. Bring the growths to the druids in Darnassus, where they can be burned safely. The night elves hope this will slow the contagion while they search for the disease’s source.

quest:924.text: The Demon Seed. Neeru Fireblade's orders reach Ak'Zeloth, who sends Horde travelers to destroy the Demon Seed atop Dreadmist Peak. An unstable Flawed Power Stone can break the Burning Legion's conduit before its influence spreads farther through the Barrens. High in a cave on Dreadmist Peak, the Demon Seed hangs above an altar of fire. The artifact anchors demonic power in the heart of the Barrens for the Burning Legion. The orc Ak'Zeloth prepares specialized power stones to break its link to the Nether. One must reach the peak before the stone's unstable energy runs out.

quest:92481.text: A Student of the Arcane. On Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker calls novice spellcasters to A Student of the Arcane. After newcomers prove their mettle, they review a Glowing Recall Crystal and report to Dorii Brightwhisper, the local mentor. After helping with the troublesome vuldren near Thendal Grove, fledgling mages receive a curious artifact: a Glowing Recall Crystal. Dorii Brightwhisper, the island’s arcane instructor, left it behind. Its recorded message tests an initiate’s aptitude and welcomes them into deeper study of magic. Dorii Brightwhisper says arcane mastery has slowly faded among their people. For millennia, they lived secluded high in the clouds. So Dorii sees each new practitioner as a pioneer who can recover lost knowledge and restore their people’s once-mighty magical heritage.

quest:92485.text: A Student of Nature. On Zephras Isle, A Student of Nature begins with a summons to novice druids. After they help restore local harmony, Xyton Silverwind calls them beneath the boughs of Thendal Grove to learn the isle's natural balance. After local disturbances caused by overzealous wildlife are resolved, Rorian the Dayseeker brings a personal summons to young initiates. The folded parchment was left by Xyton Silverwind. It invites aspiring druids to step forward and study the deeper mysteries of the wild, for their natural talents have caught the grove elders' attention. Meeting Xyton Silverwind on the lower level of the great tree in Thendal Grove marks a novice's first step in their calling. To Silverwind, Zephras Isle's plants and animals form an intricate living whole that needs constant care and watchful balance. The path of fang, claw, feather, and branch calls for lasting mentorship, and this meeting begins a lifetime of stewardship.

quest:926.text: Flawed Power Stone. Across the Barrens, Flawed Power Stone rests on arcane tables, charged with arcane energy. Its makers left it fatally flawed, so it consumes its own power soon after it is moved. In the Barrens, flawed power stones hold arcane essence within compromised structures. Their makers deliberately left them unstable, so they decay into inert matter moments after someone handles them. A stone begins consuming its power as soon as it leaves the ritual table where it rests. Its energy burns away too quickly for anyone to carry it far.

quest:9260.text: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. Lieutenant Orrin calls Stormwind's defenders to drive back Scourge forces pressing against the city. Necropolises loom beyond its walls, and he asks them to gather Necrotic Stones and study the runes around enemy camps. Scourge forces have reached the outskirts of Stormwind City. Necropolises float overhead as undead and cultists take hold near the kingdom’s greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin gathers defenders outside the city to drive them back before they threaten the capital. Glowing runes mark the dirt around Scourge camps, but their purpose remains unclear. The circles crackle with magic like that of the necropolises and carry eerie whispers. Lieutenant Orrin can only guess who, if anyone, hears those unnatural voices.

quest:9261.text: Investigate the Scourge of Ironforge. The Scourge presses against Ironforge’s gates, and Lieutenant Nevell calls for defenders. Undead troops gather beneath a hovering necropolis while glowing runic circles mark their camps. Lieutenant Nevell and the Argent Dawn watch the undead at Ironforge’s mountain entrance. Necropolises hover above Dun Morogh’s frigid heights, far from Lordaeron and the plagued lands of the north. They mean to stop the Scourge before it reaches the Bronzebeard fortress.

quest:9262.text: Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus. Lieutenant Beitha calls for help as the Scourge encampments press close to Darnassus. The Argent Dawn needs defenders to strike the undead and learn what the runes outside the gates are for. The Scourge has reached Teldrassil, and floating necropolises loom above the invasion camps near Darnassus. Ghouls, skeletons, and other undead horrors spill from them. Lieutenant Beitha of the Argent Dawn coordinates the city's defense, calling on volunteers to slow the attack and gather information before the undead overwhelm the night elven homeland.

quest:9263.text: Investigate the Scourge of Orgrimmar. Outside Orgrimmar, the Scourge has raised a camp beneath a floating necropolis. Lieutenant Dagel calls on defenders to repel the undead, recover necrotic stones, and examine runic circles charged with necromantic energy. The attack brings the Lich King's reach to Durotar. The Scourge now threatens lands far from Lordaeron and the northern ice. Floating necropolises cast their shadows across Azeroth, even over Durotar. Undead forces have gathered at Orgrimmar's threshold, raising camps that threaten the Horde capital. Lieutenant Dagel and the Argent Dawn coordinate the defense, calling on local champions to drive the invaders back before they can secure a siege.

quest:927.text: The Moss-twined Heart. Near Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies a strange heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid. Dark, oily moss covers the core, yet it keeps beating after being cut from the timberling. Blackmoss the Fetid's heart still pulses after being cut from the timberling. Dark, oily moss hides nearly all of the timberling's core, but a slow rhythm continues within it. That pulse points to a corruption reaching beyond ordinary rot in Teldrassil's wild plants. Denalan, a researcher of local flora near Lake Al'Ameth, takes a keen interest in the heart and recognizes its troubling corruption. Timberlings should be gentle beings tied to the boughs of the World Tree, yet this core bears a virulent blight. Troubled by what he sees and eager to understand it, Denalan plans to plant and study the organ, hoping to learn how foul moss takes root in the island's soil.

quest:92742.text: Testing the Wells. Across Westfall, Alba Fairmoon sends you to test the farm wells. Their samples may show what is poisoning the soil and groundwater. Alba Fairmoon asks you to test the water beneath Westfall. Neglect and banditry have already harmed the open plains. Now poison below the earth threatens the farmland that remains. You gather samples from farm wells so Alba can learn what is tainting the soil and water. You gather samples from the wells at Jansen Stead and Molsen Farm. These homesteads lie among scattered farms, exposed to Defias outlaws and feral wildlife. Their water may show whether the blight rises from the ground, comes from magic, or was put there deliberately.

quest:92744.text: Murloc Gills. At Westfall's Longshore, Alba Fairmoon seeks murloc gills to test the sea. She fears the crop blight may reach the Great Sea, and the gills could show whether the coastal waters are tainted. Westfall is close to ruin. Crops fail, farmers leave their homes, and bandits roam the roads. Alba Fairmoon fears the blight may drain from inland fields into the Great Sea. If it taints the coast, fish that feed Westfall's poor and fill Stormwind City's tables could vanish. Then an already strained kingdom may face famine. Murlocs are stubborn and violent, but their amphibious bodies can reveal the water's condition. As they breathe, their gills filter seawater and readily take in poisons, blight, and unnatural pollutants. Alba Fairmoon hopes fresh gills from murlocs prowling the Longshore will show how far the contamination has spread.

quest:92745.text: The State of the Mines. Toxic metals are turning up in Westfall's wells, and Alba Fairmoon fears for the farmland. She suspects the Defias mines and warns that the soil could fail for decades. You head to Jangolode Mine and Gold Coast Quarry to disrupt the mining. Alba Fairmoon finds dangerous levels of toxic metals in Westfall's wells. Once Stormwind's main breadbasket, the region now faces a threat to its crops. Alba suspects the Defias Brotherhood is poisoning the water through the mines it seized. If the contamination continues, the surrounding earth could lie barren for decades. The Defias put local creatures to work alongside their highwaymen, stripping Westfall of its resources. Riverpaw gnolls dig for stone and minerals at Gold Coast Quarry, while kobold diggers tunnel through Jangolode Mine. Disrupting their labor weakens the Defias' ability to process and distribute contaminated minerals.

quest:92747.text: Moonbrook Espionage. In Moonbrook, Alba Fairmoon follows signs of industry trouble in Westfall. The poison found across the region does not seem to come from the smaller mines, so the Deadmines beneath the town draw her attention. The mines already searched across Westfall have yielded no answer to the poison spreading through the region. No known surface excavation seems to be its source. One great site remains unexplored: the Deadmines, whose vast shafts lie beneath Moonbrook’s ruined streets.

quest:92748.text: Explosive Consultation. Alba Fairmoon sends you to find a way to stop the poison spreading from the Deadmines into Westfall's fields. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, you seek an engineer who can make the heavy explosives the work requires. Westfall's poisoned fields lead back to caustic toxins and industrial refuse in the Deadmines. Reinforced machinery guards the underground works, and ordinary weapons cannot disable it. Heavy explosives could break through that machinery and halt the poisoning. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, you seek Sprite Jumpsprocket, an engineer able to devise the needed explosives. Roaring forges, tinkerers, and merchants selling blasting powder fill the district. Its craftsmen may know how to stop the Deadmines operation.

quest:92749.text: A Dynamite Plan. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Sprite Jumpsprocket is eager to begin a plan sparked by talk of industrial sabotage. She wants ten sticks of coarse dynamite. Sprite Jumpsprocket is a gnome engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. She welcomes talk of industrial sabotage and asks passing mercenaries to bring her a bundle of coarse dynamite. You can make coarse dynamite at an engineering workbench or trade with the city's craftsmen. Sprite asks for ten sticks, enough to disrupt industrial schemes unfolding in the surrounding territories. Her plan shows the practical, perilous methods gnomes favor when facing mechanical and political disruptions.

quest:92750.text: Detonation at a Distance. Sprite Jumpsprocket needs a safer way to set off explosives, and sends you to Stormwind Intelligence for a remote detonator. Volatile chemicals are handled recklessly by goblins and gnomes, though some blasts call for care. A standard fuse can put you in danger. Ordinary tinkerers do not keep the special trigger Sprite needs for a controlled explosion. Sprite sends you to Stormwind Intelligence in Old Town, rather than to local dwarven blasters or ordinary engineering suppliers. Its agents, known as SI:7, work in sabotage, stealth, and targeted demolitions. Jasper Fel serves among them in the capital and can provide discreet, dangerous equipment.

quest:92751.text: Detonation at a Distance. In Moonbrook, blasts beneath Westfall have drawn SI:7's attention. Jasper Fel, a Stormwind operative, sends a remote detonator kit to let you handle the work from a safe distance. Jasper Fel and SI:7 watch events across Stormwind's lands, including Westfall's troubled border. When word reaches him of explosive work in Moonbrook, Fel already knows what is happening in the abandoned mining tunnels beneath the countryside.

quest:92752.text: Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, Sprite Jumpsprocket sends a volatile charge to Alba Fairmoon. The primed explosives must reach her safely, with the detonator undisturbed. Sprite Jumpsprocket has finished a bundle of Extra-Destructive Explosives for Alba Fairmoon. In wartime Westfall, the road is already threatened by Defias bandits and feral beasts. Carrying a live charge makes the journey more dangerous. Sprite Jumpsprocket warns you to guard the detonator. The explosives are meant to destroy the hidden industrial operation in the Deadmines, which is poisoning Westfall's farmland. Alba Fairmoon needs the explosives intact before she can use them.

quest:92753.text: Destruction in Deadmines. In the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, Defias industry blights the land. Alba Fairmoon suspects their metallurgical forge is the source and sends you to destroy it with explosives. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines hold a fortified complex that powers the Defias Brotherhood. Its heavy forge smelts metal and builds machinery. Alba Fairmoon believes the forge is the likely origin of the contamination blighting the area. She wants it destroyed.

quest:928.text: Crown of the Earth. In Shadowglen, you set out with moonwell water for Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. The journey carries you from secluded training into the wider work of protecting Teldrassil. After tasting the enchanted water of Shadowglen's moonwell, you meet Tenaron Stormgrip at the crown of Aldrassil. He seals the gathered water in a larger vessel and sends you beyond the sheltered glade. The road runs south toward Dolanaar, through woods where danger has grown harder to predict. Dolanaar is the first major village beyond Shadowglen, along the cobblestone paths through central Teldrassil. Its own moonwell lies at the heart of the village. Corithras Moonrage, an elder who oversees preservation across the boughs, waits there. The vessel you bring places you in the wider effort to protect the World Tree.

quest:92819.text: Destruction in Deadmines. Alba Fairmoon sends you against the Defias forge beneath Westfall. The explosives are planted, and she waits in the hills behind Moonbrook with the detonator. Beneath Westfall, the Deadmines hold the Defias Brotherhood's strength. Alba Fairmoon sends you to sabotage the forge hidden in the mines. The explosives are planted beside it. You return to Alba in the hills behind Moonbrook, where you can set them off from a safe distance. She hopes the blast will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal. Deep in the Deadmines, the charge waits beside the forge. After you rejoin Alba Fairmoon in the hills behind Moonbrook, a remote detonator lets you set it off from outside the caves. She hopes the destroyed forge will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal.

quest:929.text: Crown of the Earth. Near Starbreeze Village, you draw sacred water for Darnassus. Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar asks young night elves to replenish the city's moonwell, and the work teaches the history behind their care for Teldrassil's great boughs. You carry a jade phial made by druids to Starbreeze Village, where a lesser moonwell holds sanctified water. Its refined craft lets you draw and carry the luminous water without disturbing its purity. Darnassus's central moonwell depends on these scattered fonts, and the elders send initiates on foot so the city's fountains stay full of Elune's grace. The journey also teaches the young what it takes to nourish Teldrassil. Corithras Moonrage tells you of the sorrow that followed the Battle of Mount Hyjal. The sacrifice of Nordrassil, the ancestral World Tree, cost the night elves their immortality. Illidan Stormrage was unleashed amid the ruin, while Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared. Grief and isolation marked the days that followed, as the kaldorei turned to Teldrassil.

quest:930.text: The Glowing Fruit. A strange fruit shines among Teldrassil's trees, and its growth troubles those who find it. You carry it to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, where the herbalist can study the unfamiliar plant. In Teldrassil's misty boughs, you may find plants bearing large, round fruit that shine with their own light. The World Tree's balance is delicate, and its wildlife has behaved strangely of late. So unusual plants call for care. You gather the glowing fruit to bring it to someone who knows the wild flora.

quest:931.text: The Shimmering Frond. Across Teldrassil, a curious plant shimmers among the roots and canopy. Travelers bring a cutting to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, hoping the botanist can explain its origin. In Teldrassil's boughs, a strange plant catches the light. Its fronds twist with a pulsing shimmer unlike the island's usual foliage. The glow draws the eye amid Teldrassil's young forest life.

quest:932.text: Twisted Hatred. Tallonkai Swiftroot sends trusted champions into Fel Rock to stop Lord Melenas. The satyr has rallied the cave’s grell into an organized force, threatening night elf settlements near Teldrassil. Satyrs recall an ancient betrayal that still stains kaldorei history. They were Highborne who gave themselves to the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Now one has made a foothold on Teldrassil, the young World Tree meant to be a sanctuary. For defenders like Tallonkai Swiftroot, that presence is a bitter disgrace. Fel Rock lies north of the nearby paths, its corrupted caverns crawling with feral grell. Lord Melenas has gathered the chaotic creatures into a hostile force under his will. Tallonkai fears what the satyr may unleash on the World Tree’s boughs, and demands a swift, quiet end. He wants Melenas eliminated and his severed head brought back.

quest:933.text: Crown of the Earth. Corithras Moonrage sends you to the Pools of Arlithrien for water as Gnarlpine furbolgs turn violent. His account of Teldrassil begins with Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance after the Third War. Corithras Moonrage sends you with a tourmaline phial to a moonwell southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the Pools of Arlithrien. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, once peaceful, now lash out with sudden violence. They ambush travelers and harry Sentinel patrols across the region. What seemed like isolated skirmishes has become a threat to the night elves' new home. When you return with the filled phial, Corithras tells you how Teldrassil came to be. After the Third War, Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage vanished, leaving the Cenarion druids without a leader and divided. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm took the mantle of leadership in his absence. He urged the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore to set aside their mourning. The night elves, he argued, had to regain their lost immortality and heal their civilization by planting a vast new World Tree.

quest:934.text: Crown of the Earth. At the Oracle Glade, Corithras Moonrage sends you to gather water from Teldrassil’s sacred moonwell. The journey reveals the truth behind the World Tree’s creation. Corithras Moonrage sends you northwest across Teldrassil to the Oracle Glade. Beneath the Oracle Tree’s great boughs lies the first and most powerful moonwell raised on the island. You draw water into an Amethyst Phial from its sacred pool. The moonwell is the sanctuary where druids and the tree itself watch over the health of their new homeland.

quest:935.text: Crown of the Earth. In Teldrassil, moonwell waters are gathered to tend the World Tree’s sickness. The rites lead to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus, where concern grows over a tree raised without blessings. Teldrassil rose after the Third War to give the night elves a new home and restore their lost immortality. The Great Aspects Alexstrasza and Nozdormu withheld their blessings and refused to sanction its creation. Without their divine protection, sickness spreads through the tree. Strange creatures emerge from its boughs, and once-peaceful furbolg tribes fall into madness.

quest:937.text: The Enchanted Glade. Bloodfeather harpies threaten the Oracle Glade on northwestern Teldrassil, where Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak guards the ancient Oracle Tree. After harpies kill a runner bound for Darnassus, Arynia calls for their nests to be thinned and their belts brought back as proof. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak watches over the Oracle Glade with an escort of warriors. The sacred retreat centers on the colossal Oracle Tree, an ancient rooted among Teldrassil's boughs. Bloodfeather harpies have spread through the surrounding canopy, nesting in the hollows and threatening anyone who comes near. A runner carrying an urgent report from the Oracle Tree never reaches Darnassus. Bloodfeather harpies ambush and kill the messenger before the runner can leave the glade. Arynia calls on you to thin their flock and bring back Bloodfeather belts as proof that their nests have been weakened.

quest:938.text: Mist. In Teldrassil's shaded boughs, Mist lies wounded and separated from her companion. She needs a safe path back to Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak at a nearby moon well. A gray sabercat named Mist lies wounded among Teldrassil's undergrowth. Deep slashes mark her back and belly. Her blue eyes are bright, and she stays calm rather than acting like a feral beast. She looks to friendly travelers for guidance and protection.

quest:93963.text: Exploring the Alliance. In Stormwind Keep, you begin a journey to meet the rulers of Ironforge and Darnassus. Their lands show you the breadth of the Alliance before you turn toward Westfall. Randal Emerson, an attendant in Stormwind Keep’s southern antechamber, sends you beyond the human capital. Newly arrived on Azeroth, you are invited to see the Alliance’s allied peoples firsthand. The journey takes you beyond the keep to learn the distinct cultures, traditions, and strength of those who stand with Stormwind. Your travels cross land and sea to the leaders of the Alliance. In Ironforge, you meet King Magni Bronzebeard in the mountain halls and High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, leader of the displaced gnomes. In Darnassus atop Teldrassil, you meet High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Their cities and peoples reveal the ties among humans, dwarves, gnomes, and night elves. After the long journey, you return to Stormwind. Knowing more of Azeroth helps you aid your own people, while your order prepares to establish itself in Dalaran. For now, the troubled territories near the capital need help, beginning with Westfall’s struggling farmlands.

quest:940.text: Teldrassil. After the harpies are driven back, Arynia Cloudsbreak sends you with a report to Darnassus. The inscribed bark tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm about the boughs and the corruption still troubling the World Tree. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak entrusts you with a piece of inscribed bark after you clear the harpies from their nests in the Oracle Glade. The Oracle Tree watches over the forest, and with the harpies gone, Arynia can send word to the kaldorei leadership. You carry her report through the wilderness to Darnassus, the great forest of stone, and deliver it to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Fandral Staghelm receives the report with mixed feelings. He is grateful to hear that the harpies have been pushed back, but the report shows how one threat gives way to another across Teldrassil. Staghelm championed the planting of the new World Tree to reclaim the night elves' lost immortality. The afflictions in its boughs remind him that his work remains far from finished.

quest:941.text: Planting the Heart. At Lake Al'Ameth, you help Denalan tend a wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling. After clearing away its moss, he asks you to place it in his planter and see whether it can be healed. Denalan has scraped the foul moss from the wooden heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling. Yet an unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. Trusting his years of botany and soil tending, the herbalist asks you to bury the heart directly in his personal planter. He hopes the rich nutrients he blended can draw its remaining natural vitality back toward health.

quest:944.text: The Master's Glaive. In southern Darkshore, Onu sends Alliance scouts to investigate the Master's Glaive. He fears the Twilight's Hammer cult may have reached the fallen ancient horror. Along Darkshore, Onu sees corruption linger and wildlife driven from its homes. The naga on the coast trouble him, but signs of the Twilight's Hammer are worse. Its followers worship primal lords who ruled the world before they were overthrown in ages past. South of Onu, the Master's Glaive is a grim excavation around a colossal creature pierced by a great stone weapon. Onu gives you a Phial of Scrying and asks you to enter the pit and learn whether the cultists have gathered there. The behemoth has been dead for eons, yet corruptive power still clings to its bones. The Twilight's Hammer may seek to claim it.

quest:945.text: Therylune's Escape. Therylune is cornered by cultists at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. She wandered into its dig sites, and you are needed to guide her to safety and tell her worried sister, Therysil, at the Shrine of Aessina that she survived. At the Master's Glaive, Therylune is pinned down by Twilight's Hammer cultists. The ravine is dominated by the skull of an ancient monstrosity, pierced by a huge stone blade. Therylune wandered into the heart of the valley despite the dread surrounding it. She survives by reacting quickly and hiding among the rough terrain. Therysil waits far to the south at the Shrine of Aessina. Her adventurous sister Therylune rarely minds getting dirt on her clothes, but even Therysil was shocked to learn she had ventured into the unwholesome excavations at the Master's Glaive. Word that Therylune is safe will ease her worry. Therysil knows the dark forces digging through Darkshore's ancient earth.

quest:947.text: Cave Mushrooms. Barithras Moonshade sends you behind Cliffspring Falls for rare fungi. In Auberdine, the night elf prepares a specialized potion and asks you to investigate troubling warnings from the Grove of the Ancients. Barithras Moonshade needs scaber stalks and a death cap for a potent mixture. Both grow in a damp cavern hidden behind Cliffspring Falls in northeastern Darkshore. Gathering these fungi is more dangerous than picking ordinary woodland herbs.

quest:948.text: Onu. Barithras Moonshade sends you south from Auberdine to speak with Onu. Your findings in Cliffspring Falls have drawn the attention of one of Darkshore's oldest guardians. Barithras Moonshade sees more than strange fungi in the samples you brought back to Auberdine. The caves beneath Cliffspring Falls are tainted, and word of them reaches Onu, an Ancient of Lore in the Grove of the Ancients south of town. The corruption in Darkshore's waterways may reach beyond anything a naturalist can explain. Onu wants counsel, and even an Ancient's patient nature cannot hide the weight of that summons. The road south from Auberdine turns inland, away from the coastal ruins and toward the mountain slopes. The Grove of the Ancients shelters an old refuge of nature, set apart from the decay along the shore. Onu waits among stone barrows and kindred spirits, ready to guide allies toward the blights stirring at the edge of the wilderness.

quest:949.text: The Twilight Camp. Cultists gather around the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, and Alliance scouts seek to learn why. A scrying bowl has shown their ritual site; now you enter the excavation to discover what the Twilight's Hammer seeks beneath the earth. The Twilight's Hammer has made the Master's Glaive an active threat. After a scrying bowl reveals the cultists' fortifications, you enter their camp to learn their designs before the Alliance can prepare its defenses.

quest:950.text: Return to Onu. You carry a page from the Twilight Tome back to Onu in Darkshore. The scribbles are all you could bear to take from the cultists’ book. The Twilight Tome overwhelms anyone who tries to read it. Its words swim across the page, and its ornate scrollwork twists into grotesque figures. You tear out a single page of scribbles before the strain brings on vertigo.

quest:95041.text: Data Hoarders. Outside Gnomeregan, Jemma Quikswitch searches the snow for lost punch cards. The exiled gnome lives in Ironforge, and the cards hold her family's archives, from submarine designs to family recipes. Without them, the records she still has remain unreadable. When troggs invaded Gnomeregan and radiation struck, thousands of gnomes fled with what they could carry. A damaged satchel spilled several of Jemma's cards into the snow around the fallen city. Without them, her surviving records read as gibberish, and her family's knowledge risks being lost. The Quikswitch archives hold arcanotechnical field equations and submarine hull blueprints from the Second War. They also preserve Grandma Quikswitch's secret chili recipe. For refugees in Ironforge, the comforts of home matter as much as engineering marvels.

quest:95065.text: Fishin' Time. At Stormwind harbor, Gilbert Gray keeps to his fishing line while the fish are biting. His supplies run low, so he asks passersby to fetch nightcrawlers and a shiny bauble from a shop along the city canals. Gilbert Gray watches his bobber dance on the water. The elderly angler will not leave his prized perch while the fish are biting. His supplies have run out, and he needs help so he can stay at his line instead of returning to the city. Catherine Leland runs a tackle shop beside Stormwind's stone canals, just west of the Trade District. Fishermen across the city come to her for lures and bait. Her shop can replenish what Gilbert Gray needs to keep fishing.

quest:952.text: Grove of the Ancients. A dispatch carries you from Darnassus to Darkshore, where Onu waits in the Grove of the Ancients. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm sends you across the sea with correspondence for the Ancient of Lore, who lives south of Auberdine. After you help with matters at the Oracle Glade atop Teldrassil, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm summons you for another duty. He sends you across the sea to Darkshore with an urgent dispatch for Onu. From Darnassus, you can book a flight aboard a hippogryph. South of Auberdine, you reach the Grove of the Ancients and deliver the missive to Onu. The towering Ancient of Lore accepts it quietly and remarks on Staghelm's impatience. Onu and the forest's ancient keepers believe all things unfold in their proper time. Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage embodied that patient wisdom, while Staghelm lacks it.

quest:953.text: The Fall of Ameth'Aran. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade sends you to explore Ameth'Aran's ruins in Darkshore and read its ancient stone tablets. Their inscriptions tell of the Highborne city's ruin during the Sundering, preserving history largely lost in the War of the Ancients for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine. Ameth'Aran was a flourishing settlement of Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers, who practiced powerful arcane magic. After the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the city lay in broken marble and cracked pillars. Restless, anguished spirits of the Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins. Few written accounts survived the Great Sundering intact, as the War of the Ancients drove night elves into a struggle for survival. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade surveyed the ruins and found two large engraved tablets, the Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran. Ghostly Highborne specters forced her to retreat. The readings can carry the ancient disaster's history to the scholars of the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

quest:95314.text: That Shadowvale Green Elixir. In Brill, Carolai Anise seeks bottles of Shadowvale's green elixir. The secluded village once distilled Whispering Elixir from local herbs, and buyers still prize the banned brew. Before the Scourge came, Shadowvale's secluded villagers brewed Whispering Elixir from rare herbs found only in Tirisfal Glades. The draught became known across northern Lordaeron. Though the Capital City outlawed it, mystics, poisoners, and apothecaries still sought its unusual properties, even at the risk of defying royal decrees. Shadowvale lies deep in the Whispering Forest of western Tirisfal. Its people were insular and distrustful, and rarely welcomed outsiders. The Scourge invasion left the settlement in ruins, but forgotten stores of aged green elixir remain among the wreckage. Carolai Anise works from Brill, where she answers the underworld's lasting demand by paying adventurers willing to brave the forest's unsettling silence.

quest:954.text: Bashal'Aran. Demonic satyrs and grells shun one shrine in Bashal'Aran, where an unearthly blue aura burns. Thundris Windweaver, Auberdine's elder, sends you to find its source. Bashal'Aran once flourished under the ancient Kaldorei Empire. Now demonic taint fills its broken marble halls and overgrown arches. Twisted satyrs and corrupt grells feed on the ruins' lingering magic, growing more malicious by the day. Yet Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine has noticed a mystery: atop a western bluff, a blue aura shines above a shrine that no demon will approach.

quest:955.text: Bashal'Aran. At Bashal'Aran, Asterion seeks release from the magic binding his ghostly form. He suspects the grells have touched the seal that holds him, and asks travelers to gather their earrings so he can trace its lingering magic. Asterion waits among Bashal'Aran's shattered marble, bound there for centuries. The ancient night elf spirit is trapped between life and true death beneath Darkshore's canopy. Arcane craft ties him to the ruined settlement, and he cannot break free alone. Solitude and despair have worn down his mind through all those years. Asterion believes an ancient seal hidden in the ruins may hold the key to his release. Though he cannot search the brush and fallen stones himself, the feral grells of Bashal'Aran forage there and steal small baubles. He asks travelers to gather their earrings, hoping the trinkets' lingering magic will lead him to the seal that torments his soul.

quest:956.text: Bashal'Aran. Asterion seeks release from his prison among the ruined pillars of Bashal'Aran. He has traced the binding magic to the satyrs who command the grells and asks travelers to recover the Ancient Moonstone Seal. For more than a thousand years, Asterion has remained bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran. The marble pillars around him mark the limits of his prison, beyond the reach of his fading strength and ancient magic. A cursed relic holds him here. Through the centuries, he has watched Darkshore's canopy and wondered whether the wearing stone could ever set him free. Nearby grells carried traces of the magic that binds Asterion, and he deduced that the Ancient Moonstone Seal was the source of the enchantment. The satyrs who command the grells now hold the seal. These demonic night elves wander the ancient groves, keeping watch over the relic. Asterion needs the seal recovered before its binding power can be broken.

quest:957.text: Bashal'Aran. At Bashal'Aran, Asterion's spirit remains bound by an ancient seal. You carry the seal south to Ameth'Aran, where an old flame may break his bonds. Asterion's spirit remains chained in death at Bashal'Aran by an Ancient Moonstone Seal. Highborne sorcerers forged it before the Great Sundering, and no ordinary strength can break its power. Only an ancient flame still burning among Ameth'Aran's fallen stones to the south can destroy it. Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister settlements of the kaldorei under Queen Azshara, when the Well of Eternity anchored their empire. Now both are overgrown, haunted ruins, where ghosts linger and arcane power remains volatile. In a stone gazebo at Ameth'Aran, a mystical brazier burns with cyan fire. Only this flame can consume Asterion's binding relic.

quest:960.text: Onu is meditating. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Onu enters a deep trance over a growing threat. The ancient of lore weighs the alliance and motives of the Twilight's Hammer cult and the naga. If you lose your scrying phial, you can speak to him for another. In the Grove of the Ancients, Onu is an Ancient of Lore and a living repository of Kalimdor's history. Ominous reports of dark excavations at the Master's Glaive draw his immense consciousness inward. He ponders what brings the fanatical Twilight's Hammer cultists and the naga to the petrified remains of an ancient behemoth. For adventurers carrying out his reconnaissance, Onu remains within reach and can replace a scrying phial misplaced in the wild. Onu uses nature-attuned divination to watch the ruins without risking his physical presence. He entrusts adventurers with a phial of scrying, which conjures a scrying bowl at the excavation site so he can commune from afar. The journey south through Darkshore is perilous, with hostile wildlife and cultist patrols, so mishaps can happen. Onu's trance is an attentive vigil, not unbroken slumber. He readily offers another vial of sacred waters so the investigation of the Master's Glaive can continue.

quest:96047.text: Camping 101: First Aid. In Kharanos, Thamner Pol teaches you to prepare First Aid Kits for camps in Dun Morogh. With these supplies, travelers can stay alive in the field. You can build on your basic bandaging skills by learning to prepare supplies for a resting site. Thamner Pol shows you how raw medical supplies become complete kits, ready for use at camp when travelers need care far from shelter. Thamner Pol teaches you practical ways to outfit expedition sites with emergency supplies. A proper field kit lets a group bind wounds and regain strength together by the hearth before heading back into the cold.
