quest:96139.text: The Valor Family. In Darkshire, Sirra Von'Indi seeks records of Raven Hill's lost people. The village remembers their courage, but her library holds little of Raven Hill's history. Sirra Von'Indi says brave people helped Darkshire endure. Lady Althea was among them, as were those who died at Raven Hill. You are asked to search for anything that might preserve their memory.

quest:963.text: For Love Eternal. In Auberdine, Cerellean Whiteclaw asks you to free Anaya Dawnrunner's spirit from torment in Ameth'Aran. His grief has endured since the city's fall. Ten thousand years ago, the War of the Ancients tore ancient Kalimdor apart around the Well of Eternity. The catastrophe destroyed Ameth'Aran and took Anaya Dawnrunner from Cerellean Whiteclaw. Stricken with grief, Cerellean followed Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage into the druids' long hibernation. He hoped that walking the Emerald Dream through the ages would quiet his aching heart, but sorrow remained with him. After awakening, Cerellean wandered Darkshore in a stupor until he reached Ameth'Aran's melancholy ruins. Among the ancient stones, he saw Anaya's tortured ghost. He cannot raise a weapon against the woman he loved, so he asks passing travelers to destroy her tormented form, retrieve her pendant, and grant her troubled soul peace.

quest:96390.text: Nip 'Em in the Bud. Dark Iron spies move through Dun Morogh, and Earthseer Farsen calls for help. Near Ironband's Compound, their presence threatens the Bronzebeard homeland. Dark Iron spies have crossed Dun Morogh's high passes and snowy crags. They hide near settlements and excavations, where even a few watchers may signal a strike. Earthseer Farsen sees the danger and calls on Alliance defenders to find them before their plans advance.

quest:96391.text: Underground Map. Near Ironband's Compound, the Underground Map points toward chambers beneath Ironforge. Recovered from Dark Iron spies, its runes trace a hidden route piercing toward ancient halls beneath the mountain. You bring it to Earthseer Farsen to begin learning what lies below. You find the parchment near Ironband's Compound after dealing with Dark Iron spies. Its diagrams lay out an intricate maze of roads beneath the earth. Harsh, jagged runes mark passages that run deep underground and converge beneath Ironforge. Their course suggests a possible threat beneath the Bronzebeard capital, though the Dark Iron notes remain uncertain.

quest:96392.text: Farsen's Watch. Near Gol'Bolar Quarry, Earthseer Farsen watches for Dark Iron movement close to Ironforge. The Wildhammer shaman lends you his farsight, revealing a threat that calls for swift action. From his post above Gol'Bolar Quarry, Farsen watches the lower reaches of Dun Morogh. He came south from the crags of Aerie Peak, bringing a Wildhammer's spiritual awareness with him. His clan's old arts let him sense tremors underground and watch for sudden movement along the hillsides. Farsen lends you his farsight, a shamanic gift that carries sight across great distances. Through it, you see danger beyond troggs and wild beasts. Dark Iron dwarves have drawn close to Ironforge's industrial center and are digging in. Their foothold must be confronted before it takes root.

quest:96393.text: Old Ironforge Incursion. Beneath Ironforge, Earthseer Farsen sends you to the Hall of Thanes for the last part of the investigation. There, you face the Dark Iron threat and report to King Magni Bronzebeard. The underground map reveals Dark Iron movements, and Earthseer Farsen identifies the mastermind behind the intrusion. The entrance to the Hall of Thanes lies deep within Old Ironforge's ancient stone halls. While the upper city tends to matters on the surface, Dark Iron forces slip into caverns that lie dormant beneath the kingdom.

quest:96408.text: A Visitor to Dun Morogh. Beldin Steelgrill sends you to learn who has lit a fire above Gol'Bolar Quarry. The camp overlooks the excavation, and the dwarves fear its visitor may mean them harm. High on the snowy ridges east of Kharanos, a stranger's campfire burns above the quarry. The unfamiliar fire has worried the folk of Kharanos. There, the Mountaineers watch the heights for danger.

quest:965.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. North of Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze fears trouble at an ancient ruin. She sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the Tower of Althalaxx, but he has missed his report. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze watches for danger around Auberdine. Suspicious activity near the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore drew her notice, so she sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the ancient ruin. Days have passed without word from him. Elissa asks you to travel north, find Balthule, and make sure he has not met an untimely end.

quest:966.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Warlocks gather at the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, drawing the scout Balthule Shadowstrike’s attention. He asks travelers to recover parchment scraps from the fanatics camped outside the ruins, hoping to learn who they are and what they seek. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the misty shore of northern Darkshore, keeping sight of the ancient Tower of Althalaxx. Auberdine sent him to monitor the ruin and warn Delgren the Purifier if danger grew. But leaving his post to report might mean missing the dark spellcasters moving among the stones. So Balthule asks passing travelers to scout the camps around the tower.

quest:96607.text: The Great Outdoors. Beyond city walls, The Great Outdoors teaches you to meet the wild with care. Seasoned travelers begin with a campfire and the habits that make each journey safer. A sharp blade or potent magic will not save you if you neglect the basics. Near roadside clearings, seasoned wanderers teach travelers leaving their home valleys to rest by a campfire. Its warmth eases sore boots, settles the mind, and prepares you for the harsh road ahead. Rest and preparation improve your chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory. Your instructors also send you to town tradesfolk, because a field camp needs more than an ember and a bedroll. You can forge replacement rivets, cook trail rations, or stitch torn gear beneath the stars. Each profession offers camp fixtures that help turn a bare hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

quest:96627.text: The Adventurer. From Northshire Valley, Marshal McBride sends you toward Goldshire to find Sam Sarsaparilla. You have proved your skill defending the abbey, and now he wants you to look into a newcomer. With the Defias and vermin threats easing, McBride turns his attention to the road beyond the valley. His garrison needs promising fighters to watch travelers and wanderers in the surrounding woods. Marshal McBride asks you to check on Sam Sarsaparilla, who was spotted near Goldshire. This is neither a military order nor a hunt for a bounty. The newcomer draws you from Northshire’s secluded valley into Elwynn’s wider wilds.

quest:96628.text: The Adventurer. At Dun Morogh’s southern gate, The Adventurer carries supplies toward Kharanos. Mountaineer Thalos asks travelers to bring provisions to Eric Brighthammer, a newcomer camped just outside the village. Mountaineer Thalos keeps watch at Dun Morogh’s southern gate, where the trail leaves Coldridge Valley. Guarding the high passes and tunnels keeps the Mountaineers busy. Thalos also watches for dangers and travelers on the road. When a lone adventurer arrives near Kharanos, he asks trusted passersby to carry supplies onward. The bundle is meant to help newcomers venturing into the frozen crags. The road from the southern pass winds down to Kharanos, a center of dwarven craft and travel in central Dun Morogh. Eric Brighthammer has recently made camp just outside the village. Carrying the Mountaineers’ provisions to him links the sentries on the ridge with those walking the wilderness.

quest:96630.text: The Adventurer. In Teldrassil, a lost journal waits to be carried to Lyreena Duskblade near Dolanaar. Its pages record an unknown traveler's simple journeys and camping outings. You find a journal among Teldrassil's boughs and roots. Its nameless writer records modest wanderings and the simple pleasure of making camp beneath the twilight canopy. The journal can be carried toward Dolanaar instead of left in the wilderness. Lyreena Duskblade waits near the night elf settlement to receive the lost pages.

quest:96652.text: The Adventurer. In Durotar, The Adventurer finds a lost journal among the red wastes. Its pages tell of quiet travels and nights beneath the stars, and it is meant for Brakk near Razor Hill. A lost journal lies in Durotar's red dirt, far from the bloody battles and grand campaigns that mark the land. Its unknown writer fills the pages with day-to-day travels and the simple pleasure of making camp beneath the open sky. The book offers a quiet glimpse of life on the road through a harsh country. The journal is meant for Brakk, an adventurer camped near Razor Hill. Its pages connect an unknown traveler to someone watching the dusty roads, and carrying it to Brakk may help keep the writer's travels remembered.

quest:96656.text: The Adventurer. Near Deathknell, The Adventurer is sent to investigate a stranger by the road to Brill. Scarlet Crusaders threaten the region, but the stranger is Eleanor Shackleton, a Forsaken traveler with wilderness skills to share. Executor Arren watches Deathknell and the roads around it. Scarlet Crusaders spy on the region and infiltrate northern Lordaeron, so an unfamiliar figure near Brill draws suspicion. You have proved your dedication by striking at Crusader threats along the border. Now Arren asks you to investigate the stranger quietly and learn whether she threatens the Forsaken. You find Eleanor Shackleton by the roadside near Brill. She is a Forsaken traveler, pausing before another journey into the wilds, with no Crusader plot or Scourge necromancy in mind. Eleanor sees a fellow adventurer in those sent to check on her. She offers to teach you how to survive in open country and make camp.

quest:96658.text: Camping 101: Cooking. As you learn to cook, a basic campfire gives you a hearth for camping beyond fortified walls. Across Alliance and Horde lands, cooking trainers show new adventurers how to kindle one and prepare for life in the wild. Beyond fortified walls, a campfire boils water and roasts meat. Its flames give you a hearth when you travel through unfamiliar country and make camp. Apprentice cooks kindle small fires with few surroundings. As your cooking grows, you can light larger fires for more elaborate campsites. Other practical trades teach you to make useful furnishings.

quest:96659.text: The Adventurer. Chief Hawkwind sends young travelers from Red Cloud Mesa with supplies for Kaga Wildhoof near Bloodhoof Village. She once aided him, and he means to repay that favor. Chief Hawkwind asks you to carry provisions to Kaga Wildhoof near Bloodhoof Village. Long ago, Wildhoof aided him when he needed help, and he remembers that kindness. Now she has made camp outside the village. As young travelers leave the mesa, Hawkwind entrusts them with supplies for his old benefactor. The trail leads from Red Cloud Mesa toward Bloodhoof Village, across the plains of Mulgore. Carrying Hawkwind's bundle takes you beyond Camp Narache, where young tauren have trained, and into the wider lands of the United Tauren Tribes.

quest:967.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Dark Strand cultists are gathering, and Balthule Shadowstrike needs help. He sends an Alliance courier to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale with a warning for his mentor, Delgren the Purifier. Balthule Shadowstrike sees that the Dark Strand threat is too great for one scout to face alone. After clashing with cultists near the Tower of Althalaxx, he writes a report and entrusts it to an Alliance messenger bound for his master, Delgren the Purifier. The cult's summoners are growing bolder, and Balthule needs seasoned leaders to direct a response. Balthule's dispatch takes you south along Darkshore's coastal road, then across the wooded border into Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier is stationed at Maestra's Post, beside the western road. The human paladin works to cleanse demons and undead from the woodland. Though night elven customs were once unfamiliar to him, he has earned the Sentinels' deep respect as an indispensable ally.

quest:968.text: Tools of the Highborne. Thundris Windweaver sends help from Auberdine to the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Restless Highborne spirits still carry enchanted relics through the shattered settlement, and he wants them taken away. South of Auberdine and east of the coastal highway, Ameth'Aran's stone foundations lie overgrown. Ten thousand years ago, the settlement was a stronghold of the Highborne, the privileged aristocracy of the ancient night elven empire. Their unchecked use of arcane magic helped bring about the Sundering, which shattered Ameth'Aran. The inhabitants never truly left. Sentinels patrolling Darkshore report that the Highborne ghosts still haunt the sunken plazas, clutching the enchanted tools and trinkets they held in life. For the kaldorei, arcane magic carries the memory of a danger that nearly destroyed life on Azeroth. Thundris Windweaver fears that leaving the Highborne implements in ghostly hands could invite corruption. He sends adventurers to wrest the relics from the restless spirits, intending to have them destroyed so their tainted magic cannot fuel another disaster.

quest:97279.text: Wayward Weapons. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends new recruits to recover weapons for the encampment. With young warriors arriving to serve the Horde, supplies run thin, and the weaponsmith needs old arms returned to use. New recruits face harsh trials in Durotar's red wastes. Many arrive ready to pledge their blades to the warchief, straining the encampment's weapon stocks. Weaponsmith Kzan Thornslash struggles to meet demand, especially when early lessons prove fatal or humiliating for the unready. Overseer Gornek makes the shortage a practical trial. He sends fresh arrivals to recover abandoned blades and blunt training weapons left by recruits who fell or fled. Bring the recovered arms to Kzan, and he can repair and temper them for the next wave. New recruits learn that survival in the Horde calls for scavenging as well as swinging steel.

quest:97558.text: Hides for the Forsaken. In Tirisfal, the Forsaken gather animal skins to mend their ruined flesh. Shelene Rhobart asks you to bring darkhound hides, duskbat wing membranes, and murloc skin. Forsaken flesh cannot heal on its own. A wound leaves a rotting gap, and the body cannot close it through natural means. To keep their forms intact, the Forsaken stitch living tissue over their injuries and keep their corpses working. Different materials mend different parts of the body. Thick darkhound hide suits broad repairs that need to hold firm. Duskbat wing membranes are thin and pliable, covering faces and fingers without making them stiff. Vile Fin murloc skin lines inner membranes and sensitive places such as cheeks and mouths.

quest:97894.text: Business in Auberdine. In Stormwind, Borgus Steelhand waits for news of his brother Gorbold in Auberdine. You can reach Gorbold by sailing west from Stormwind Harbor to northern Kalimdor. Gorbold crossed the Great Sea to keep a merchant stall in auberdine. He hoped to profit by supplying ships that call at Darkshore. Weeks have passed without word, and Borgus worries for his brother so far from Ironforge and Stormwind. The passage to Kalimdor once led through Menethil Harbor or neutral goblin ports such as Booty Bay. Borgus sends you to the vessel at stormwind harbor's southern-most dock. Its direct sailing ends at Auberdine's long wooden piers.

quest:97914.text: Expanding Horizons. Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine to Stormwind. He wants the settlement's work and its home known beyond Darkshore. Auberdine's sea passage now joins Darkshore directly to Stormwind. Its leaders want the shipping route kept safe and the coastal settlement linked to the wider Alliance. Nearby, the ruined cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran have long drawn more notice than Auberdine and its living people. Baros Alexston oversees Stormwind's construction and infrastructure. His duties include public works and logistics. Thundris Windweaver's letter crosses the Great Sea to the official charged with the human capital's building needs.

quest:97919.text: Camping 101: First Aid. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Michelle Belle shows you how to prepare First Aid Kits for camping. You need enough First Aid skill to learn how to ready these supplies for the road ahead. Travel through Elwynn can leave you wounded, far from a town healer or inn. First Aid lets you tend your own injuries without relying on anyone else. Bandages help with bleeding and trauma, without arcane rites or holy prayers. At Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn, Michelle Belle teaches skilled practitioners to assemble First Aid Kits. Keep medical supplies at camp so a weary party can treat injuries and regain strength before facing the dangers ahead.

quest:97920.text: Camping 101: Fishing. Lee Brown teaches novice anglers near Goldshire how to use their fishing skill around camp. With simple catches and basic materials, they can make useful additions for a campsite. Fishing can feed you on the road and add comfort to camp. A fish bowl lifts the spirits of weary travelers between excursions. A sound mind and high spirits help make formidable fighters. Lee Brown waits beside the waters outside Goldshire for fishermen ready to broaden their craft. Show him your skill with rod and line, and he can teach you to make useful additions for camp.

quest:97926.text: Making Do. Auberdine waits for word from Stormwind, but no aid is coming. Making Do carries Alexston's Reply across the sea to Elder Thundris Windweaver. You carry Alexston's Reply across the sea to Elder Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. The letter brings no troops or relief. Stormwind's representative explains that the kingdom's treasury is nearly empty. What wealth remains must stretch across its own struggling territories.

quest:97957.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. In Tirisfal, Eleanor Shackleton sends new herbalists to Faruza in Brill to learn a useful craft. Incense Candles give spellcasters help as they rest at camps in the wild. Herbalism gives alchemists their first materials, but travelers also depend on gathered roots and blossoms. Regional master herbalists teach aspiring foragers to prepare Incense Candles. In Tirisfal Glades, Eleanor Shackleton points promising foragers toward Faruza in Brill once they show basic skill. Long travel wears on spellcasters and spiritualists. Incense Candles release restorative fragrances to lift spirits and soothe tired minds. Gatherers infuse dried plants into the candles, helping healers and mages whose magical reserves falter on the road.

quest:97960.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Tirisfal Glades, new skinners learn how to make a chair for camp from harvested hides. The lesson points them toward craftsmen who teach the trade across Azeroth. A sharp blade is not enough to last in the wilds; you also need to know how to save your strength between trials. Adventurers can build basic skill in the field and use treated skins to make camp chairs. Those comforts give weary travelers a place to rest and recover before facing danger again. Young Forsaken skinners in Tirisfal Glades who reach their first measure of skill are sent to Rand Rhobart. He works along the road between Brill and the Capital ruins of the Undercity. Rhobart teaches practical ways to turn rough leather into a seat for camp. Skinning masters across the lands of the Horde and Alliance teach the same craft.

quest:982.text: Deep Ocean, Vast Sea. North of Auberdine, the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil lie beneath the waves. Murlocs ambushed both night elf vessels as they sailed into port, and their surviving crews seek a way to mourn their lost captains. Murlocs overwhelmed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as the ships approached Auberdine. Both vessels sank in the shallows north of the settlement. Their surviving crews reached shore, but the loss of the ships and their captains weighs on the port. Gorbold Steelhand, a dwarf in Auberdine, seeks to honor the fallen night elf captains. Murlocs now occupy the underwater wrecks, but the captains' lockboxes remain in the flooded holds. Their logs and personal effects could help the surviving sailors mourn their commanders and lay their spirits to rest.

quest:98219.text: The Shamed Lieutenant. A Stormwind guard asks you to check on Lieutenant Farren Orinelle in Southshore. His reassignment is meant to teach him a lesson, but the guard hopes he can still succeed. You've safely delivered the statuette. Now your contact asks you to speak with Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, a city guard sent to Southshore in Hillsbrad Foothills. Farren's father was a friend of the guard, who believes he could benefit from help. If you are passing through, a boat bound for Southshore leaves from Menethil Harbor.

quest:98247.text: Shipping Label. A damaged Shipping Label points toward the Azeroth Commerce Authority's trade hub at Three Corners in the Redridge Mountains. It marks a supply crate as the authority's property and shows travelers where to report it. A damaged label marks a stocked supply crate as freight belonging to the Azeroth Commerce Authority. The destination and recipient have been torn away, but the label tells anyone who finds the cargo to return it or report to the authority's trade outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Beside the formal text, a rough map sketches the roads toward the Three Corners intersection. At Three Corners, representatives of the Azeroth Commerce Authority enlist travelers as independent couriers. The authority does not bind haulers to strict merchant contracts. Instead, it runs an informal network that compensates them with Merchant's Favor for recovering missing cargo and completing abandoned deliveries along the highway.

quest:983.text: Buzzbox 827. Along Darkshore's coast, Buzzbox 827 waits silent for repairs. Wizbang Cranktoggle built it as the first of a chain of voice relays, each made to use parts from local wildlife. Restoring it lets Wizbang test his network from Auberdine. In Auberdine, gnomish engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle is trying to bridge Darkshore's wild coast with a chain of voice relays called Buzzboxes. Their levers and gears carry speech across great distances, a sharp contrast with the ancient ruins and somber forests around them. The machines break down often, and each needs constant care to keep working. Buzzbox 827 lies on the misty shore just south of Auberdine. Wizbang built each relay to use parts from nearby wildlife, so repairs do not depend on carrying refined iron gears and copper pins through the wilderness. This unit takes the sturdy, jointed legs of local tide and reef crawlers. Put the legs in its receiver hopper, and the machine assembles itself and carries Wizbang's voice through its speakers.

quest:98386.text: Alther's Mill. Workers at Alther's Mill cannot send timber to Lakeshire while giant spiders overrun the eastern lumberyard. Foreman Oslow needs the wood to finish the town bridge. Foreman Oslow is trying to keep bridge repairs on schedule in Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs, gnoll packs, and murlocs along Lake Everstill already strain his workforce. Now giant tarantulas have overrun Alther's Mill to the east, stopping the timber shipments the bridge needs. Spiders lurk among the timber stacks, leaving the mill useless. Foreman Oslow cannot risk sending laborers into a nest of greater tarantulas, so he hires capable adventurers to clear the spiders and destroy their egg clutches. He is irritated that Alther let the mill fall into disarray, but Lakeshire needs the lumber before the bridge work can continue.

quest:98389.text: A Light in the Darkness. In Deathknell, Aramis Hammerhand asks you to save newly raised Forsaken from Night's Web Hollow. Your aid can show that wielders of the Holy Light remain loyal to Sylvanas and their people. Some Forsaken still wield the Holy Light they knew in life, though its power brings pain to the undead. In Deathknell, Aramis Hammerhand and others seek to prove their faith has not turned them against their own people. They use their gifts to protect the Forsaken and ease fears that holy wielders see their kin as monsters. Northwest of Deathknell, Night's Web Hollow is a dank cavern crawling with vicious spiders. Newly raised Forsaken often stumble inside, disoriented and unable to defend themselves, and become trapped in sticky webbing. Saving them brings new recruits to the Dark Lady and may convince Executor Arren that wielders of the Light serve the Forsaken faithfully.

quest:984.text: How Big a Threat?. Terenthis asks scouts in Auberdine to learn whether furbolg corruption has reached Darkshore. After madness takes hold among furbolgs in Teldrassil, the night elf druid sends them to inspect mainland settlements across the sea. Night elves across northern Kalimdor have long lived peacefully with the furbolg tribes. Since the Third War, strange corruption has unhinged furbolg minds in Teldrassil. They have kidnapped and attacked their former allies. Terenthis, a druid stationed in Auberdine, fears the affliction has spread beyond the World Tree to the mainland tribes along Darkshore’s coast.

quest:98407.text: Show of Force. Deputy Feldon sends you to drive gnoll packs back from Lakeshire. The Redridge guards need proof that the thrashers have been beaten. Gnoll packs have grown bolder in the Redridge Mountains. Their camps now lie close to Lakeshire and the human homesteads beyond it. Stormwind has too few soldiers to spare for the borderlands, so local authorities depend on travelers to hold the perimeter. The gnolls have not yet struck the town, but their camps bring them within reach of its homes. Deputy Feldon knows the gnolls respect strength above all. He wants you to hunt their fiercest fighters, the gnoll thrashers, and bring back their spiked collars as proof of defeat. By breaking the front line and showing the trophies, Lakeshire's defenders hope to frighten the surviving packs into retreating to the highlands.

quest:985.text: How Big a Threat?. Terenthis in Auberdine sends you against the Blackwood furbolgs south of town. Their corrupted camp threatens the settlement, and the Sentinels want its pathfinders and windtalkers culled. The Sentinels see the Blackwood furbolgs as an immediate danger to Darkshore’s refugees and defenders. After you scout south of Auberdine, Terenthis sends you to strike their camp. Killing Blackwood Pathfinders and Windtalkers may break their attack before it reaches the settlement. Night elves have long regarded furbolgs as spiritual kin and allies of the wilderness. Fel moss and demonic taint have spread across northern Kalimdor, driving the Blackwood tribe mad. No known remedy can restore their minds, so Auberdine’s defenders see a grim choice: stop them before innocent people die.

quest:98576.text: Glyphic Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Glyphic Parchment points young mages toward their first lessons. Gornek delivers the runed notice, which sends them to Mai'ah near the Den to begin learning the arcane. New recruits test their strength against Durotar's local pests, but those drawn to magic need more than brute force. Gornek passes along a notice marked with runes. It directs novice spellcasters to Mai'ah, who guides the Horde's newest recruits through their first lessons in magic. Mai'ah waits just outside the Den, where she teaches young spellweavers to temper ambition with patience and thought. She urges them to choose their moment instead of hurling raw sorcery without care. In her lessons, novices learn to weave delicate strands of the cosmos rather than unleash an unruly tempest.

quest:98601.text: A Difficult Path. In Deathknell, a newly awakened Forsaken paladin begins training with the Light. After facing the undead outside the crypt, you are sent to the village church to meet Aramis Hammerhand and learn what holy power demands of the Forsaken. After you clear feral undead from outside the crypt, Shadow Priest Sarvis gives you an unexpected delivery. The Consecrated Scroll shines with holy energy, and Sarvis recoils before asking you to step aside. For one devoted to shadow and decay, the Holy Light burns like an open flame. Aramis Hammerhand waits inside Deathknell’s desecrated church to train Forsaken paladins. Other races may wield the Light with ease and joy, but the undead endure searing agony when they call upon it. Aramis speaks plainly: channeling holy power through a rotting body is torment. He expects his disciples to face that pain instead of shrinking from it, and let it temper their resolve.

quest:99.text: Arugal's Folly. In Pyrewood Village, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks the magic binding its people to a curse. He needs enchanted shackles from the villagers to study Archmage Arugal's work and understand the worgen transformation. South of the Sepulcher, Pyrewood Village lives two lives. In daylight, its fearful, insular residents appear to be ordinary human peasants. At twilight, their human forms tear apart and become savage Moonrage worgen, roaming the streets under Arugal's sway. Dalar Dawnweaver seeks to learn what arcane bindings cause this horror.

quest:990.text: Trek to Ashenvale. Sentinel Selarin sends travelers south from Auberdine into Ashenvale. There, you report to Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar, where the Sentinels face spreading corruption. Sentinel Selarin's call for aid brings you from Auberdine, on Darkshore's somber gray coast, toward the night elf lands to the south. The Sentinel trusts capable fighters and scouts to make the journey into the heart of that territory. With local threats in Darkshore handled, the greater perils of Ashenvale now demand attention. An ancient night elf road winds south beneath Ashenvale's dense canopy. Raene Wolfrunner, who leads the Sentinels in Astranaar, has urgently called for reinforcements. Demonic taints, rampant wildlife, and incursions from beyond ancestral lands have stretched the defenders thin. They need outside aid to hold the sacred forest.

quest:991.text: Raene's Cleansing. In Ashenvale, Raene Wolfrunner asks you to find Teronis in Raene's Cleansing. He set out toward Lake Falathim to recover a magic gemstone and find a way to halt the furbolgs' growing aggression. Raene Wolfrunner serves with the Sentinels in Astranaar, defending Ashenvale from mounting threats. Teronis was among her closest companions. He set out to find a strong defense against the furbolg tribes as they grew more violent. Days passed without his return, and Raene feared the worst while duty kept her at her post. Teronis followed rumors of a powerful rod forged by a wicked wizard who had died. He believed its magic could calm the furbolg fury. To restore the rod, he needed an enchanted gem hidden in an elven shrine at Lake Falathim, near the mountains to the west. Yet aggressive murloc tribes had recently taken the lake's once-tranquil waters.

quest:99134.text: Discipline. Executor Zygand turns to outsiders in Tirisfal Glades to keep his Deathguard sentries alert. He has little faith in the garrison and orders physical punishment for those who slacken. The Deathguard guard the Forsaken across Lordaeron. Freedom from the Lich King's control has brought its own troubles: apathy, fatigue, and neglect. Executor Zygand has little patience for sentries who let their discipline slip. The Scarlet Crusade and Scourge prowl Tirisfal's borders, and the garrison must stay ready. Its officers use force and close oversight to keep the troops alert. Executor Zygand chooses outsiders to punish negligent Deathguards instead of using soldiers from his own garrison. With the Executor's Motivator, you remind sentries that service to the Dark Lady demands constant vigilance. Even in undeath, they cannot escape the consequences of neglecting their duties.

quest:99141.text: Patience. In Tirisfal Glades, Executor Zygand waits for overdue field reports. He sends you to gather updates from Deathguards near Brill and a sentry by Stillwater Pond. Executor Zygand commands local security in Tirisfal Glades and allows no lapse in vigilance. Serving Lady Sylvanas, he expects every duty done without fail. When scheduled field reports do not reach his post, he treats the delay as a breach of duty. He stays at his post and sends Forsaken agents to find the tardy subordinates and keep the borders secure. Sentries at key points around Brill owe Zygand their reports. Deathguard Dillinger watches the graveyard west of town, where rogue undead and Scourge remnants stir. East of Brill, Deathguard Kristof guards a waystation on the approaches to the Capital City and the eastern roads. Gordo is the strangest sentry: a hulking abomination who wanders near Stillwater Pond, where military record-keeping seems a poor fit for his simple mind.

quest:99142.text: Tomb Weed. At Balnir Farmstead, Holland's altered doom weed now draws the Scourge. The crop has become a new specimen called tomb weed, and Holland wants it for his experiments. Junior Apothecary Holland wants more than a place among the Royal Apothecary Society. He gathers doom weed, makes small alchemical changes, and replants it in the soil of Balnir Farmstead. There, he has cultivated a new strain he calls tomb weed. Holland sees the hybrid as the heart of his work and a sign of the future he seeks for himself. Holland expected his altered plants to gain alchemical potency, but the Scourge wandering Balnir Farmstead have taken an unexpected interest in them. He now depends on travelers to push past the undead and gather the mature crop, so his experiments can continue.

quest:99156.text: Rear Guard Patrol. Deathguard Linnea calls patrollers to defend Tirisfal Glades. She sends them after Riptear, an abomination roaming near Venomweb Vale that should never have passed the Bulwark. The Bulwark is the sole fortified barrier between Tirisfal Glades and the horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Forsaken military strategy depends on fighting on one front. If mindless undead slip behind the lines, they can choke the supply routes feeding the front. Stray spirits or ghouls sometimes bypass the barricades, but an abomination roaming the glades signals a grave failure of containment.

quest:997.text: Denalan's Earth. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf sends a late shipment of rare earth south to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth. The night elf researcher studies Teldrassil's young plants. Syral Bladeleaf stops travelers in Dolanaar with a special shipment of rare earth for Denalan. The soil came from Darnassus to support his botanical studies, but delays kept it from reaching Dolanaar until now. Syral seeks a courier to carry the parcel south along the forest trail to Denalan's campsite by Lake Al'Ameth. Denalan works alone at a station on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, watching Teldrassil's young ecosystem take root. The tree grew quickly after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and its plants behave in unexpected ways. Denalan tests the vitality and behavior of timberlings and native plants with unique soil mixtures and specimens. The rare earth shipment will support those experiments.

quest:cutting-teeth.text: Cutting Teeth. In the Valley of Trials, fresh recruits face a first test against mottled boars. Overseer Gornek sends aspiring warriors and spellcasters to thin the boars around the cactus dirt farms, where they can prove their fighting skill and readiness to serve the Horde. The Valley of Trials leaves little room for grand dreams. Young recruits may imagine hunting great beasts in the Barrens or winning glory on a battlefield, but overseer Gornek begins with the farms. Thinning the mottled boars is a grounded test of a recruit’s first skills with a weapon or spell. It shows whether they can face a wild attacker and have the sense to survive their first skirmish. Feral swine roam the red desert settlement’s dirt farms north and northeast of camp. They root through cactus patches and threaten the few supplies grown in Durotar’s harsh soil. Sending aspirants to clear them keeps local pests in check while shaping young orcs and trolls into defenders of the new nation.

quest:galgar-s-cactus-apple-surprise.text: Galgar's Cactus Apple Surprise. In the Valley of Trials, Galgar sends fresh recruits to gather cactus apples for his cooling treat. The work teaches them to forage and survive in Durotar's arid land. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls take their first steps as defenders of the Horde in the Valley of Trials. Combat drills and fierce trials against native beasts quickly bring exhaustion and thirst. Learning to live off the land matters as much as learning to swing an axe. Cacti across the valley bear ripe, water-rich apples that offer relief from the desert sun. Galgar tends his cooking in the training grounds, where he has made an art of foraging. His Cactus Apple Surprise is known among the valley's people for cooling a person faster than a plunge into river water. He sends eager recruits to gather prickly fruit from nearby cacti, keeping his kitchen stocked and ensuring new wanderers do not set out into Durotar hungry.

quest:lazy-peons.text: Lazy Peons. Foreman Thazz'ril sends new Horde recruits across the Valley of Trials to wake sleeping peons. Their work keeps lumber moving to Durotar's settlements. Durotar's new homes need timber, stone, and hard labor. Peons, orcs with little skill in battle, carry much of that burden and keep the Horde supplied with workers. In the Valley of Trials, the heat and grueling work leave Foreman Thazz'ril's crews seeking shade beneath trees for unauthorized naps. Foreman Thazz'ril gives new Horde recruits his blackjack and sends them across the valley to wake the sleeping workers. The startled peons return to chopping wood, keeping lumber flowing for Durotar's survival.

quest:sarkoth.text: Sarkoth. On a southern plateau in the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth has left a young Darkspear hunter near death. Wounded beneath a tree, Hana'zua asks a passing warrior to kill the scorpid and bring back its mangled claw, so his last strike will count for something. In the Valley of Trials, the Horde tests aspiring warriors against Durotar's harsh desert. While hunting the valley's venomous creatures, young troll scout Hana'zua met a scorpid far larger and deadlier than the rest. He struck hard enough to mangle one pincer, but Sarkoth drove its tail into his chest. Now Hana'zua bleeds in the red dirt, fearing his life is near its end. He wants the beast dead before it can outlive him. Sarkoth roams a high mesa above the southern Valley of Trials. Hana'zua's blow left one claw shattered, but the scorpid still rules the ridge and attacks anyone who climbs the rocky path. Bring the scarred claw back to the wounded scout, and he will have proof that his last strike weakened the monster enough for someone to bring it down.

quest:your-place-in-the-world.text: Your Place In The World. In the Valley of Trials, untested recruits take their first steps toward honor and survival in Durotar. Kaltunk sends them straight to Gornek for basic combat training, beginning their service to the Horde. In Durotar's arid Valley of Trials, young orcs and Darkspear trolls prove their worth before entering the wider world. Under Warchief Thrall, life demands strength, vigilance, and discipline. Kaltunk evaluates every eager recruit, tempering dreams of wrestling demons and dragons with the practical duties ahead. Training begins in the canyon, where recruits learn humility before claiming glory. Gornek waits beside the camp fire, only steps away from Kaltunk. The gruff veteran regards fresh arrivals with a skeptical eye and often grumbles about the meager stock reaching camp. His duty is to harden these young fighters through trials, starting with the vermin that threaten the encampment's supplies.
